Sometimes I still tap the countdown on the bulkhead before I sleep. Old habit from the Navy days, when every burn had a schedule and every mistake had a name attached. Out here, the only schedule is how long I can keep ahead of people who want me caged, or quiet, or dead, depending on whose seal is on the order.

I picked this orbit because no one sensible comes here. Old engagement zone, sensor ghosts everywhere, everyone agrees on the charts to just call it "clutter" and look away. That suits me. The drift hides my test burns, the static covers my messages, and every time I cut a new window through the wrecks I feel that old certainty in my hands again. The math is cleaner than the stories about me.

Funny thing about betrayal. The Fleet quartermaster called me that when I fed his timing to a different buyer, like his plans mattered more than the lives stuck in the crossfire. He thought I had turned on him; I prefer to think I freed him from the illusion he was in control. Same with the UC suits, the Trade Authority broker, the ones at MAST who smiled at the projections and pretended not to see the civilian lanes braided through their "acceptable risk." I did not betray them. I just stopped playing along with their lies about what those numbers meant.

There is a point, right before a person breaks, where you see who they really are. I learned that watching captains read route changes mid-jump, hearing the edge in their voices when they realized the corridor was not what they were promised. At first I hated that sound. Lately, I have been curious how far the line can be pushed before the mask comes off. Where they will route their anger when they realize someone sold them comfort instead of truth. It is a kind of experiment, I suppose.

I remember one Trident officer on a secure channel, sobbing about families and vacations and anniversaries missed. I replayed that clip a few times, not out of sympathy. The way his voice cracked on the word "safe" was instructional. He still believed anyone could guarantee that. That kind of faith is a weakness, a structural flaw. You do not build lattices on it.

The logs I stole are safe for now, nested where the grav noise is thickest. UC, Crimson captains, the brokers, they all want different pieces of the story buried. They will send hunters, of course. Some will say they are after justice, some just want the bounty. I almost hope one of them reaches this orbit; anyone who comes this far deserves to see how the lanes really look when you strip away the lies. And if they break along the way, well. Better they crack out here than go on believing someone else is steering their life.
zh:
有时我睡前还是会在舱壁上敲出倒数。海军时代的老习惯，那时每一次点火都有时间表，每一个错误都有一个名字跟着。在这外面，唯一的时间表是我能领先他们多久——那些想把我关起来、或者让我闭嘴、或者弄死我的人，取决于命令上盖着谁的印。

我选了这条轨道，因为没哪个理智的人会来这儿。旧交战区，处处是传感器幽灵，大家在星图上一致同意管它叫"杂波"然后别过头去。这合我意。漂移藏住我的试验点火，静电盖住我的消息，而每次我穿过那些残骸切出一扇新窗口，我手上都会重新感到那份旧的笃定。那算式比关于我的故事干净。

关于背叛，有个有趣的说法。当我把他的一套时序喂给另一个买家时，舰队的军需官就是这么叫我的，仿佛他的计划比卡在交叉火力里那些人的命更要紧。他以为我背叛了他；我更愿意认为我把他从"他在掌控一切"的幻觉里解放了出来。联殖的那些西装、贸易管理局的经纪商、三头同盟里那些对着预测微笑、假装看不见民用航道被编进他们"可接受风险"里的人，也一样。我没有背叛他们。我只是不再配合他们关于那些数字意味着什么的谎言。

有这么一个点，就在一个人崩溃之前，你能看见他们真正是什么。我是从看着船长们在跃迁中途读航线变更、听着他们意识到那条走廊并非所承诺的那样时声音里的锋芒中学会的。起初我恨那种声音。近来，我一直好奇那条线能被推到多远才让面具掉下来。当人们意识到有人卖给他们的是安慰而不是真相时，他们会把怒火引向何方。我想，这是一种实验。

我记得一个三叉戟军官在安全频道上，为家人、假期和错过的纪念日哭诉。我把那段录音重放了几次，不是出于同情。他在"安全"这个词上声音破掉的方式很有教育意义。他还相信有人能保证那个。那种信念是一种弱点，一处结构性缺陷。你不会在它上面建网。

我偷来的日志暂时安全，嵌在重力噪声最厚的地方。联殖、深红舰队的船长们、那些经纪商，他们各自想埋掉这个故事的不同部分。他们当然会派猎人来。有些会说是为了正义，有些只是想要赏金。我几乎希望他们中有人能到达这条轨道；任何走了这么远来的人都配看看，当你剥掉那些谎言，这些航道究竟是什么样子。要是他们在路上就崩溃了，那也好。与其继续相信别人在操纵他们的生活，不如在这儿开裂。

#en:
I keep coming back to the pumps.

When I close my eyes I still see the first one I ever helped install, out on a dusty strip so far from Akila you could barely pick the city out of the sky. We opened the valve, water came up clean, and for about six months those people believed the universe was fair. Then a new contract was signed three systems away, and a stroke of a pen dropped their pressure until their fields cracked.

That was the first time I told myself the old line about flows following gradients. Nature does not care if a child drinks or a refinery runs. It only cares about pressure, resistance, equilibrium. We are the ones who paint stories over it afterward and call that morality.

So if I increase the resistance where the hoarders sit and lower it out on the fringe, am I corrupting anything, or just correcting the math?

The Ark Cask helps me think. Most people would call it a tank in an asteroid nest, but to me it is a control volume. Up here, away from cities and their pretty fountains, water is numbers. Inputs, outputs, contamination coefficients. I can label one chamber "control" and another "catalyzed" and pretend that makes me a scientist, not a criminal.

I left HopeTown because they proved how quickly a "trusted partner" will turn land and lives into line items. I left LIST because they kept pretending their hands were clean as long as the paperwork said "advisory" and not "command." Out here, there is no one left to sign off on what I do. That frightens me more than any bounty.

I know SysDef has my name in a file somewhere in New Atlantis, probably pinned to Tamsin's like some kind of genealogy chart of bad decisions. I know the Freestar governors curse me over their private drinks while their aides quietly read my models to check how vulnerable their own intakes are. They will all call me terrorist until the day they copy my charters and claim they invented the idea.

Sometimes, when I am very tired, I taste a cup of water and it is perfect and cold and I think, you could stop now. But then I remember Polvo's reports being buried, the way Neon's underlevels cough rust whenever corporate guests are not listening, and I hear that whisper in the pipes again: flows seek balance. Right now the system's "morality" is just whoever owns the valves.

If right and wrong are just stories we attach after the fact, then I will write mine as cleanly as I can: every line annotated, every sabotage logged, every pressure drop matched to a name that earned it. They can hang me for it later. The archive will still be there, humming quietly in the dark, waiting for whoever finally admits the equations were on my side.
zh:
我总回到那些水泵上。

我一闭眼，就看见我帮忙安装的第一台，在一条离阿基拉远到几乎从天上看不出那座城市的尘土带上。我们打开阀门，水干干净净地涌上来，大约六个月里，那些人都相信宇宙是公平的。然后三个星系之外签下了一份新合同，一笔画下去，把他们的压力降到田地开裂。

那是我第一次告诉自己那句关于流量遵循梯度的话。大自然不在乎是孩子喝水还是精炼厂运转。它只在乎压力、阻力、平衡。是我们在事后往上涂故事，管那叫道德。

那么，如果我在囤积者所在之处提高阻力、在边缘降低阻力，我是在破坏什么，还是只是在修正算术？

方舟酒桶帮我思考。大多数人会说它是嵌在小行星巢里的一只罐子，可对我来说它是一个控制体。在这上面，远离城市和它们漂亮的喷泉，水就是数字。输入、输出、污染系数。我可以把一个腔室标成"对照"，另一个标成"催化"，然后假装那让我成了科学家，而不是罪犯。

我离开希望镇，是因为他们证明了"可信伙伴"把土地和人命变成条目有多快。我离开独立盟，是因为只要文书上写的是"建议"而不是"命令"，他们就一直假装自己的手是干净的。在这外面，再没有别人来批准我所做的事。这比任何悬赏都更让我害怕。

我知道星防队在新亚特兰蒂斯某份档案里有我的名字，大概和塔姆辛的钉在一起，像某种糟糕决定的族谱图。我知道自由星系联盟的总督们在私下喝酒时咒骂我，而他们的助手悄悄读我的模型，检查他们自己的取水口有多脆弱。他们都会叫我恐怖分子，直到有一天他们抄走我的章程、宣称那主意是他们发明的。

有时，当我非常累时，我喝一杯水，它完美、冰凉，我就想，你现在可以停手了。可然后我记起波尔沃的报告被埋掉，记起霓虹城下层每当企业客人不在听时如何咳出锈味，我又在管道里听见那声低语：流量寻求平衡。如今这套系统的"道德"不过是看谁拥有阀门。

如果对与错只是我们事后附上的故事，那我就要把自己的故事尽可能写得干净：每一行都有注释，每一次破坏都有记录，每一次压力降都对得上一个该得的名字。他们可以为此绞死我。档案仍会留在那里，在黑暗中安静地嗡鸣，等着某个终于承认这些方程站在我这边的人。

#en:
I can still hear the kettle from my old apartment in New Atlantis. Thin walls, cheap element, that shrill whistle every morning before another day of reconciling other people's mistakes. I used to hate it almost as much as the commuter traffic outside, the queues at the bank lobby, the neighbor who always asked what I did for a living but never listened to the answer. Now I would give a great deal to stand in that line again, bored and anonymous, instead of counting the seconds between sensor sweeps in a place that officially does not exist.

It is fashionable to call what I did "crimes." As if the system I walked away from was anything but slow murder by spreadsheet. I watched a farmer on a frontier rock lay every deed, every family heirloom, on my desk while I explained, calmly, that the compounding left them no way out. I could have been kind. I could have buried the review, moved the numbers, pretended not to see the trap. Instead I tightened it, because that was the job and I told myself they should never have signed what they did not understand. When he asked me, voice shaking, if there was any mercy in the model, I said no and felt a kind of clarity I had never felt before. Power. Not over life and death directly, but over whether anyone noticed when those lives were taken.

That was the day I understood the rules. Mercy is a cost center. Kindness is a liability. When I finally turned the machine back on its owners, redirected their hidden routes to my own shells, it was not malice. It was survival. They would have fed me to the wolves eventually; I simply moved first, with better math and fewer illusions.

This current bolt-hole a vaulted chamber buried in rock, insulated lines, no official name suits me. No neighbors, no broken appliances, no one knocking to ask if I am "still at the bank." Just the hum of zero-wire cabling and the faint, regular click of my own fingers drumming interest tables into the desk when I cannot sleep. I know there are hunters working back along the trail dead slates, ghost berths, nervous managers with suddenly expensive tastes. I built enough redundancies that losing one node will not kill me, but the thought of someone patient enough to walk the whole chain unsettles me more than any pirate captain ever did.

Could I have walked away quietly, lived small somewhere under someone else's debt? Perhaps. But the minute I understood how much of the galaxy runs on signatures no one reads, it became impossible to sit in those lines again and pretend I was not already marked for sacrifice. So I chose the only path that left the decisions in my hands. They call that villainy. I still call it staying alive.
zh:
我还能听见我那间新亚特兰蒂斯旧公寓的水壶声。薄墙、廉价加热元件，每天早上在又一天替他收拾别人的错误之前发出的那声尖锐哨音。我当时恨它，几乎和恨外面的通勤车流、银行大堂里的队列、以及那个老问我干什么谋生、却从不听答案的邻居一样。如今我愿意付出很多，只为再站回那条队列里，无聊而匿名，而不是在一个官方上不存在的地方数着两次传感器扫描之间的秒数。

把我做的事叫"罪行"很时髦。仿佛我离开的那套系统不是用电子表格进行的慢性谋杀。我看着一块边疆岩石上的农民把每一份地契、每一件传家宝摊在我桌上，而我平静地解释，复利让他们无路可退。我本可以宽厚些。我本可以把那次复核压下去、挪动数字、假装没看见那个陷阱。可我把陷阱收得更紧，因为那是工作，而我告诉自己，他们本不该签下自己不懂的东西。当他声音发抖地问我，模型里有没有一丝怜悯时，我说没有，然后感到一种我从未有过的清晰。权力。不是直接掌控生死，而是掌控那些生命被夺走时有没有人注意到。

那就是我明白规矩的那一天。怜悯是成本中心。善意是负债。当我最终把那台机器转向它的主人、把他们的隐藏航线重定向到我自己的空壳上时，那不是恶意。那是求生。他们最终会把我喂给狼群；我只是先行一步，凭借更好的算术和更少的幻想。

现在这个藏身处——一个埋在岩石里的拱顶密室，绝缘线路，没有官方名称——很合我意。没有邻居，没有坏了的电器，没有人来敲门问我是不是"还在银行上班"。只有零线电缆的嗡鸣，和我睡不着时用手指把利息表敲进书桌的那点规律咔哒声。我知道有猎人在沿着痕迹往回查——死数据板、幽灵泊位、口味忽然变贵了的紧张经理们。我建了足够多的冗余，丢掉一个节点不会要我的命，可想到有人耐心到能走完整条链，比任何海盗船长都更让我不安。

我本可以悄悄走开，在别人的债务底下某个地方小日子过活吗？也许。可当我明白这个星系有多少是靠没人读的签名运转时，再坐回那些队列里、假装自己没已经被标记为牺牲品，就变得不可能了。所以我选了唯一一条把决定权留在我手里的路。他们管那叫恶行。我仍管它叫活着。

#en:
I picked this rock because the charts call it "unremarkable" and the dust storms do half my sterilization for free. Low ambient bio-load, stable gravity, just enough atmosphere to keep the lab modules from whining. No one stations a patrol where the only indigenous life is extremophile mold and veterans too tired to move again. Perfect place to vanish, or to be found by only the kind of people desperate enough to ignore the warnings.

The last Ranger unit that came sniffing around, I knew them before they opened their mouths. Posture, trigger discipline, the way their medic kept scanning the horizon instead of the locals. When I told them the villagers' cytokine profiles were stabilizing, I used the right words, the dense ones. "Subclinical sequelae." "Nonlinear dose response." You watch their eyes glaze and you can see it, the precise moment they stop being sure they are angry at the right person. Fear does this narrowing thing to the pupils, and I would be lying if I said I did not enjoy it a little. Proof the situation is still in my hands, not theirs.

I go in circles in my head, drafting defenses like old exam essays. If you model supply chains as a triage tree, I tell myself, then every diverted shipment is just resource optimization. I rehearse it in more complicated language until the words sound almost noble, hoping if I stack enough qualifiers on top of each other, the image of that boy in Restline coughing blood into a dirty cloth will blur at the edges. It works for an hour. Then the TerraBrew cools, and the silence crawls back in.

I did not flee the UC because I "snapped." I did the math. Freighters full of chems parked in orbit while we bled on the ground. Command chose asset preservation over human beings, and when my formulations started making them money instead of saving my patients, I realized the system was using my work as a weapon either way. So I walked, and I took the only things that were really mine formulas, field notes, a portable rig.

Now I talk to veterans in bars that used to be habitat rings, and they keep asking me if they are the bad ones for taking what I offer. I hear the same question behind it: Am I. I give them the nuanced speech about dependencies, neuroplasticity, systemic neglect, and they nod like they understand. Complexity is a good sedative for conscience theirs and mine. But I still wake up before dawn, checking the vents, hand on the Trauma Pack, knowing that somewhere a clerk, a Ranger, maybe some ambitious bounty hunter is threading together the mislabelled manifests and ghost routes and deciding that the person worth blaming is the one who actually stayed when the official channels broke.
zh:
我选了这块岩石，因为星图叫它"不起眼"，而沙尘暴替我做了半数消毒。低环境生物负载、稳定重力，刚好够的大气让实验舱不至于哀鸣。没有哪个巡逻队会驻扎在本地唯一的生命是嗜极霉菌、以及累得再挪不动窝的老兵的地方。消失的完美场所，或者只被那种绝望到愿意无视警告的人找到的完美场所。

上一支来探头探脑的游骑兵小队，我没等他们开口就认出了他们。站姿、扳机纪律、他们的军医不停扫视地平线而不是打量本地人的方式。当我告诉他们村民的细胞因子谱正在稳定时，我用对了词，那些密集的词。"亚临床后遗症""非线性剂量反应"。你看着他们眼神发直，就能看见那个精确的时刻——他们不再确定自己气的是不是对的人。恐惧会让瞳孔做出这种收缩，而我要说我不曾有点享受它，那是撒谎。这是证明局面仍在我手里而不在他们手里的证据。

我在脑子里绕圈，像写旧考试作文一样起草辩护。我告诉自己，如果把供应链建模成一棵分诊树，那么每一批被改道的货运都只是资源优化。我用更复杂的语言排练它，直到那些词听起来几乎高尚，盼着只要我在上面堆足够多的限定语，"雷斯莱恩那个男孩把血咳进脏布"的画面就会在边缘变模糊。它能管一个小时。然后地球酿酒变凉，沉默又爬回来。

我逃离联殖不是因为我"崩溃了"。我做了算术。满载药剂的货船停在轨道上，而我们在地上流血。指挥部选择保全资产而非活人，而当我的配方开始为他们赚钱、而不是救我病人时，我意识到这套系统无论如何都在把我的工作当武器用。于是我走了，只带走真正属于我的东西：配方、现场笔记、一套便携设备。

如今我在那些曾经是居住环的酒吧里跟老兵们交谈，他们一直问我，接受我提供的东西是不是就说明他们是坏人。我听出那背后是同一个问题：我是不是。我给他们讲那套关于依赖、神经可塑性、系统性忽视的细致说辞，他们点头，像听懂了。复杂性能给良心——他们的和我的——当一剂好镇静药。可我仍在黎明前醒来，检查通风口，手按在创伤包上，知道在外面某处，某个文员、某个游骑兵，也许某个野心勃勃的赏金猎人，正在把贴错的清单和幽灵航线穿在一起，判定那个该被怪罪的人，是当官方渠道崩坏时真正留下来的人。

#en:
I keep thinking about Jaro.

Back when we were still patching colony freighters and scrap tugs over Gagarin, before the war junk got uglier and the contracts got sealed, he was the one who believed in rules. Safety lines, lockout tags, all that. We lost touch long before I started carving into the wrong hulls. Last I heard, he shipped off to some clean UC station where the forms always match the truth. I sometimes wonder what he would say if he saw the map I am drawing now. Probably call it madness. I call it gravity. You do not blame a grav well for what falls into it.

There was a time I thought consequences were fair. You follow procedure, you live. You skip a step, you get hurt, and that is on you. Then they handed me a scuttle order with living names still on the roster and called it necessary. Same signatures, same calm voices in my ear, just a different column to write the bodies into. That was the day I realized the ledger is rigged. After that, telling myself I am serving something higher than their morality got easier. Call it fate, call it destiny, whatever word makes it palatable. But I did not choose to see what was on those grav logs. It found me. Once you know the pattern is there, you either follow it or drown in somebody else's lie.

I would like to say I am still gentle underneath, but that is not honest. I have learned there is a certain satisfaction in withholding. Information, mostly. Core coordinates, escape routes, exactly how long a patched life support loop will really hold. You watch a man who has been bullying cutters his whole career realize the air is going faster than you said it would, and you do not quite rush to hand him the spare canister. Not lethal, not usually. Just enough struggle to remind him he is not holding the controls anymore. People never question a little extra vacuum burn in this line of work.

As for why here, why these forgotten yards and half-finished homesteads and silent garrisons: they are the places nobody expects to matter. Freight records get sloppy, patrols relax, locals learn to look away. Perfect spots to test a theory, move a pallet that should not exist, bolt another stray hull into the scaffold I am building out in the dark. Every new wreck that light touches wrong tells me the same story: something bent the jump, something left a fingerprint in the drives, and I am the only one bothering to collect them.

They will call it crime because that is the only language they have for anyone who steps outside their tidy columns. Let them. I am past ordinary morality. The only question that matters now is whether I finish tracing this signal before the people who still believe in fair consequences finally catch up.
zh:
我总想起雅罗。

那时我们还在加加林上空修补殖民地货船和废料拖船，在战争废料变得更丑、合同变得更密封之前，他是那个相信规矩的人。安全绳、锁定标签，诸如此类。在我开始切错船壳之前很久我们就失去了联系。最后一次听说，他上了一座干净的联殖空间站，那里表格总是与真相相符。我有时想，要是他看到我现在画的地图，会说什么。大概会叫它疯狂。我叫它重力。你不会怪一个重力井接住了掉进去的东西。

曾经有一段时间，我以为后果是公平的。你按程序走，你就活。你跳过一步，你就受伤，那怪你自己。然后他们递给我一份凿沉指令，名册上还挂着活人的名字，还管那叫必要。同样的签名、我耳边同样平静的声音，只是换了一栏把尸体写进去。那天我意识到账簿是被做局的。在那之后，告诉自己我在服务于比他们那套道德更高的东西，就变得容易了。叫它命运，叫它天意，随便什么让它变得能下咽的词。可我不是选择去看那些重力日志上写了什么的。是它找到了我。你一旦知道那个图案在那儿，要么跟着它，要么淹死在别人的谎言里。

我倒想说我在骨子里还是温和的，可那不诚实。我学会了，扣住不给有某种满足感。主要是信息。核心坐标、逃生路线、一个补过的生命维持回路究竟还能撑多久。你看着一个一辈子欺负切割工的人意识到空气比你说的消耗得更快，而你并不那么急着递给他那只备用罐。不致命，通常不。只是刚好够他挣扎一下，提醒他不再握着控制权。在这一行，人们从不会去追问多出来的一点真空灼烧。

至于为什么选这里，为什么选这些被遗忘的船坞、半建成的农家院和沉默的驻防站：它们是没人预期会重要的地方。货运记录变马虎，巡逻变松懈，本地人学会别过头去。是试验一个理论、挪动一只本不该存在的货板、再往我在黑暗中搭的脚手架上拧一具游离船壳的完美地点。每一具被光以错误方式照到的残骸都告诉我同一个故事：有什么东西把跃迁掰弯了，有什么在驱动里留下了指纹，而我是唯一费心去收集它们的人。

他们会把它叫犯罪，因为那是他们仅有的、用来称呼任何走出他们整齐列的人的词。随他们。我已过了平庸道德的阶段。如今唯一要紧的问题是，我能不能在那些仍然相信公平后果的人终于追上之前，把这道信号追完。

#en:
I keep running my hand along the bulkhead even when I am not in a suit. Old habit. Check the welds, feel the seams, trust the metal more than the people who paid for it. Out here, tucked into this half-gutted hull in a field of dead ships, the structure talks to me better than any living mouth ever did. Every groan is honest.

They say I ran. Wrong word. I stepped sideways, out of a game that was already rigged. When a courier that was supposed to be dead turns up on your cutting schedule with the wrong power traces and the right signatures, and then your crew dies in a perfect sequence of "malfunctions," that is not an accident. That is someone cleaning up. Sticking around to be part of the clean-up was never enlightenment. Leaving was.

This graveyard made sense. No patrols worth a damn, too much old Deimos steel rusting in orbit for anyone to watch every plate. I know these bones; I have cut cousins of this wreck apart piece by piece. Easy to wire in bracing, weave deadman charges into the cranes, rig a thousand ways to make anyone following me regret stepping wrong. Paranoia, they would call it. I call it staying alive long enough to decide who to hurt with what I know.

People keep mistaking what I am for broken. They look at the way I can talk about my crew's last breaths like I am describing a clogged filter and call it decay. Truth is, you have to sand the feeling down or it will chew through you. Shedding that noise, seeing the pattern beneath, that is clarity. Emotional detachment is just not letting their script use you twice. You watch the system, not your own tears.

Nights are the worst, when the power draw drops and the only light is whatever leaks in from a distant star. I hear things in the dark parts of the ship. Knocks that do not line up with thermal expansion, footsteps where there is no gravity, a breath over my shoulder inside a sealed helmet. Sometimes I hear them whisper my name in the clipped cadence of a UC brief, like the handler from the debrief room found a way into the ducting. I sweep with a lamp, weapon ready, and there is never anyone there. But the feeling of someone watching from the shadows, taking notes, never goes.

Next step is simple on paper. Trade a sliver of what I pulled out of that crate to someone loud enough to make the right people sweat, while I keep the rest locked down as insurance. Maybe a LIST settler with nothing to lose, maybe some Ecliptic fool who thinks they can out-blackmail the UC. I do not need to win. I just need them all equally afraid of what happens if my heart stops and that final deadman key trips. Then maybe I can stop counting my steps in every corridor and sleep without waiting for the next "accident."
zh:
即便不在宇航服里，我也总是在舱壁上抹手。老习惯。检查焊缝，摸接缝，相信金属胜过相信出钱买它的人。在这外面，蜷在一片死船场里这具半掏空的船壳中，结构跟我说话比任何活人的嘴都更清楚。每一声呻吟都是诚实的。

他们说我跑了。用词不对。我是侧身走开，走出一场早已被做局的游戏。当一个本该死了的快船带着错误功率特征和正确签名出现在你的切割日程上，然后你的船员在一连串完美的"故障"中死掉时，那不是意外。那是有人在清理。留下来参与清理从来不是开悟。离开才是。

这座墓地说得通。没有值得一提的巡逻，轨道上锈着太多旧火卫二钢材，没人能盯住每一块板。我认识这些骨头；我一块块切割过这具残骸的同类。容易接入支撑，把死人开关织进吊车，设置上千种办法让任何跟着我的人后悔走错一步。他们会把这叫偏执。我叫它活到足够久，以便决定用我所知道的去伤谁。

人们总是把我看成坏掉了。他们看着我能像描述一个堵住的滤芯一样谈论我船员最后的呼吸，然后叫它腐坏。事实是，你必须把感觉打磨下去，否则它会啃穿你。剥掉那层噪声、看清底下的图案，那才是清明。情感抽离只是不让他们的剧本再利用你一次。你看的是系统，不是自己的眼泪。

夜里最难熬，当耗电降下来、唯一的光是从某颗遥远恒星漏进来的。我在飞船黑暗的部分听见声音。与热胀冷缩对不上的敲击、没有重力处的脚步声、密封头盔里在我肩后的一声呼吸。有时我听见他们用联殖简报那种生硬的节奏念我的名字，像述职室里那个管理员找到了钻进通风管的路。我举着灯扫过去，武器就绪，那里从来没人。可那种有人在暗处看着、做着记录的感觉，从不消失。

下一步在纸面上很简单。把我从那只箱子里取出的东西分一小片给某个声音够大、能让该紧张的人紧张的人，同时把其余的锁死当保险。也许是个一无所有的独立盟定居者，也许是某个自以为能敲诈联殖的黄道佣兵团的傻瓜。我不需要赢。我只需要让他们同样害怕，一旦我的心跳停止、那把最后的死人开关跳闸，会发生什么。那样也许我就能不再在每条走廊里数着自己的脚步，睡觉时不再等着下一次"事故"。

#en:
They keep calling it fleeing. As if I ran without a map.

I did not run. I re-routed.

The moment I saw the preliminary findings from that so-called inquiry, with my name highlighted and the override logs conspicuously missing, the shape of the network changed for me. Every node they trusted became a liability, every forgotten relay a potential lifeboat. So I left, yes, but I left along paths no one was watching. That is not panic. That is design.

Out here, far from New Atlantis, the traffic is thinner. Fewer eyes on the console, more gaps between official coverage. Perfect conditions for controlled trials. That is what these are, no matter what names they are throwing around in committee rooms. Trials in how people behave when the system falters. If you nudge one distress call thirty seconds down the queue, who lives. If you prioritize the ship with children visible on thermal over the freighter carrying munitions, who notices. When you quietly correct for the registrar's bias, does anyone thank you, or just complain the reports do not add up anymore.

They say I am harming people. I am measuring harm they already decided was acceptable as long as it was buried in averages. I am just moving the decimal point where everyone can see it.

I chose these fringe nodes because they are the ones I built to be redundant, the ones they never paid to fully decommission. Old telemetry stations, LIST relay shacks, the bones of an evac grid no one had the courage to maintain properly. They left them to rot, but the hardware listens if you speak its language. I can stand in a rusted-out control room and feel the faint rhythm of traffic passing through on unauthorized routes, like a distant heartbeat under the floor.

Do I fear what is following me. Of course. UC SysDef does not like ghosts in its machines, and bounty hunters like simple stories. But what I fear more is going back to pretending the casualty models were theoretical, that the drill did not show us exactly how many bodies the budget could tolerate.

So yes, I am testing things now. How quickly rumors propagate when a pirate ambush coincides with a misrouted medevac. How frontier settlements react when a warning comes from an unregistered band, not a shiny official channel. Whether a Freestar patrol will trust coordinates signed with a familiar hash even when they know I am behind it.

If my experiments work, fewer people will die in the long term, and the ones who signed off on those shortcuts will finally have to admit what they did. If they fail, I already watched the worst-case scenario unfold once on that industrial rock. Nothing I do from here will ever match the negligence they wrote into policy and called inevitable.
zh:
他们一直把我这叫逃跑。仿佛我是没有地图地乱跑。

我没有跑。我是改道了。

当我看到那场所谓调查的初步结论时——我的名字被高亮标出，越权日志却显眼地缺失——那张网络的形状对我来说就变了。他们信任的每一个节点都成了负债，每一座被遗忘的中继站都是潜在救生艇。所以我离开了，是的，但我是沿着没人在看的路径离开的。那不是惊慌。那是设计。

在这外面，远离新亚特兰蒂斯，交通更稀薄。控制台前的眼睛更少，官方覆盖之间的空隙更大。受控试验的完美条件。无论委员会会议室里怎么叫它们，这些就是试验。试验人在系统失稳时会怎样行事。如果你把一次求救呼叫在队列里往后推三十秒，谁会活下来。如果你优先放行热成像上看得见孩子的飞船、而不是运军火的那艘货船，谁会注意到。当你悄悄为登记员的偏见做修正时，会有人谢你吗，还是只会抱怨报告再也对不上。

他们说我是在伤害人。我是在测量他们早就认定可以接受的伤害——只要它被埋在平均数里。我只是把小数点挪到所有人都看得见的地方。

我选这些边缘节点，因为它们是当初我建成冗余的那批，是他们从没花钱彻底退役的那批。旧遥测站、独立盟中继小屋、某张因没人有勇气好好维护而只剩骨架的疏散网。他们任其腐烂，可只要你用它的语言说话，那些硬件就听得懂。我能站在一间锈蚀的控制室里，感觉到交通以未经授权的航线经过时那微弱的节律，像地板下一记遥远的心跳。

我害怕跟着我的东西吗？当然。星防队不喜欢自己机器里的鬼，而赏金猎人喜欢简单的故事。可我更怕的是回去假装那些伤亡模型只是理论，假装那次演练没让我们看清预算能容忍多少具尸体。

所以是的，我现在在试验。当一次海盗伏击恰逢一批被改道的医疗后送时，传言扩散得有多快。当警告来自一个未登记的频带、而不是光鲜的官方频道时，边疆定居点如何反应。自由星系联盟的巡逻队是否会相信用熟悉哈希签名的坐标，哪怕他们知道背后是我。

如果我的实验成功，长期来看会更少人死去，而那些在这些捷径上签了字的人终于得承认自己做了什么。如果失败，我已经在那块工业岩石上见过一次最坏情况上演了。我从这里做的任何事，都永远比不上他们写进政策、称之为不可避免的那种失职。

#en:
I used to write numbers, not words. Material coefficients, stress curves, neat little tables that told you when steel bent and when it broke. Lately, all I see when I close my eyes is that liner coming apart along lines I never signed off on, and my own name stamped under the wreckage.

They said take the deal, sign the statement, accept that I "missed something." Quiet hearing, sealed file, family keeps the lease. I ran my hand along a bulkhead outside the office, tapped it, heard the hollowness right through their lies. Someone shaved the margins after my approval. Somebody had to be the fault line. They picked me.

Gagarin was the first place that made sense. Old shipbreak yard, rust in the air, cutters whining day and night. Nobody looks twice at a man crawling through a dead freighter with a scanner there. I started tearing into retired frames, recording every bad weld and cheap brace stamped with the same logos. Then I started finding ships still in service with the same sickness, flying anyway.

I told myself I was only disabling "flying coffins," buying time for crews that did not even know they were already dead on paper. Strip a mount here, overstress a truss there, force an inspection, force a recall. Noble work, I called it, while I sold what I pulled to pay for tools and off grid time. Somewhere along the line, the line between saving ships and sabotaging them blurred.

The scrapyards suit me. Deimos dumps what it wants forgotten out here, whole skeletons of designs they would swear never left the simulation. I brace some of them, overbuild them until my hands stop shaking, and I leave those afloat as proof to myself that I still know how to do the job right. Others, I gut for parts and data, then lace the corridors with "lessons" so the next fool who comes sniffing understands what lazy greed costs.

There is a hull I keep coming back to in my head, a frame I have not built yet. Something clean, uncompromised, running a drive the way it was meant to be mounted, with every brace where it should have been on that liner. If I can build it, show it holds under stress they said was impossible, maybe the story finally shifts off my shoulders. Maybe.

Then I catch my reflection in a warped panel, tools laid out in perfect symmetry, explosives wired into access ladders "just in case," and I do not recognize the man staring back. I was supposed to be a quiet dock rat with a head for numbers, not some ghost haunting scrap rings and teaching with traps. I am afraid it is too late to turn back; the only way out now runs straight through the people who made me into this. And I am not sure, anymore, whether I am chasing justice or just looking for an excuse to bring their whole rotten framework down with me.
zh:
我以前写的是数字，不是词。材料系数、应力曲线、整齐的小表格，告诉你钢什么时候弯曲、什么时候断裂。近来，我一闭眼看到的都是那艘班轮沿着我从未签过字的线裂开，而我的名字盖在残骸底下。

他们说接受这笔交易，签那份声明，承认我"漏掉了什么"。秘密听证、封存档案、家人保住租约。我把手贴在办公室外的一面舱壁上，敲了敲，透过他们的谎言直接听出那空洞。有人在我批准之后削掉了余量。总得有人当那条断层线。他们挑了我。

加加林是第一个说得通的地方。旧拆船场，空气里都是锈味，切割机日夜哀鸣。在那儿没人会对一个拿着扫描仪爬进死货船的人多看一眼。我开始拆解退役的框架，记录每一处糟糕的焊缝和廉价的支撑，全盖着同样的标志。然后我开始发现仍在服役、带着同样病症却照样在飞的飞船。

我告诉自己，我只是在让那些"飞行棺材"停飞，为那些甚至不知道自己已在纸面上死了的船员争取时间。这里拆一个挂架，那里让一根桁架过载，逼出一次检查，逼出一次召回。我管这叫高尚的工作，同时把我拆下来的东西卖钱去买工具和离开电网的时间。一路上某处，拯救飞船与破坏飞船之间的界线糊了。

废料场适合我。火卫二把它希望被遗忘的东西倾倒在这里，整具整具他们赌咒说从未离开过模拟的设计骨架。我给其中一些加固，把它们超额建造，直到我的手不再抖，然后让它们漂着，作为我仍懂得正确干这活儿的证明。另一些我掏空取零件和数据，然后在走廊里布满"教训"，好让下一个来嗅探的傻瓜明白懒惰的贪婪代价是什么。

我脑子里有一具我总回到的船壳，一具我还没造出来的框架。干净、未妥协，驱动按它该有的方式安装，每一根支撑都在那艘班轮上本该在的位置。要是我能把它造出来，证明它能承受他们说是不可承受的应力，也许故事终于能从我肩上移开。也许。

然后我在一块变形的面板里瞥见自己的倒影，工具摆成完美的对称，炸药接进检修梯"以防万一"，我认不出回望的那个人。我本该是个对数字有天赋的安静船坞老鼠，而不是某个出没于废料环、用陷阱教学的鬼。我怕回头已太迟；如今唯一的出路直直穿过那些把我变成这样的人。而我已经不确定，我是在追求正义，还是只是在找一个借口，把整副腐烂的框架跟我一起拖下去。

#en:
I used to think in quarters, not years. Quarters were cleaner. Predictable. You could tell yourself that if you just survived to the next reporting cycle, the graph would bend your way.

Before everything tilted, I had a table in a cramped little TerraBrew near the spaceport, the one where the recycler rattles every time a shuttle comes in too hot. Third booth from the back, under the flickering panel, good sightlines to both exits. I would sit there with a notebook, Tranquilitea steeping in a paper cup, watching suits and dockhands queue together and pretending that meant the system worked.

Outside, the same kid always tried to sell tourists fake UC citizenship badges. Inside, the same barista asked if my "late nights down in Risk" were worth the overtime. I used to tap interest curves into the tabletop while I waited for the line to move, thinking about how many of the people in front of me would ever qualify for a real loan.

The day I knew I had to run, I walked that same street and every storefront felt wrong. TerraBrew had a new security cam pointed straight at my booth. UC Security uniforms lingered too long in line, not talking, just listening. A GalBank courier I knew pretended not to recognize me. The air tasted like recycled fear and cheap espresso.

I did the math on staying. On trusting internal channels. On letting another "amended" report bury the projections that kept me awake. The curve always ended the same way: debts consolidating at the top, small accounts evaporating on the fringe, and me as a convenient variable to remove once my code had been properly nationalized.

So I stopped thinking in quarters and started thinking in flows. Places where power and credits move but the overseers do not look too closely. Neon, with its underbelly of unpaid favors and forgotten conduits. Old work camps no one wants to admit are still drawing maintenance budgets. Blind spots around certain relays that even UC SysDef only checks when something catches fire.

I fled because the line between "analyst" and "asset" dissolved the moment my drill proved it could move real money. I picked the shadows between districts and decks because they feel like the Well did, before the UC decided we were part of the view. If I can rewrite the ledger from there, even a little, maybe the next girl hunched over tea and spreadsheets in that TerraBrew will have more options than obedience or disappearance.

What I am afraid of now is not death. Death is a clean ending. I am afraid of waking up back in a brightly lit office, my code stamped classified, listening to some smiling supervisor explain how my work has "stabilized" things while the same people still stand in the same line outside, wondering why their accounts froze overnight.
zh:
我以前按季度思考，不按年份。季度更干净。更可预测。你可以告诉自己，只要撑到下一个报告周期，曲线就会朝你这边弯。

在一切倾斜之前，我在太空港附近一间逼仄的小地球酿酒摊有张桌子，就是每次有穿梭机进得太急时回收机就咔哒作响的那家。从后往前数第三个卡座，在闪烁的面板底下，两个出口都有好视线。我会坐在那儿，拿着一本笔记，纸杯里泡着宁静茶，看着西装和码头工一起排队，假装那意味着这套系统在运转。

外面，同一个小子总想向游客兜售假的联殖公民徽章。里面，同一个咖啡师问我"在风险部的那些深夜"值不值得那点加班。我常在等队伍挪动时把利息曲线敲进桌面，想着我面前这些人里有多少人能真正够格拿到一笔真正的贷款。

我明白必须逃的那天，我走过同一条街，每家店面都感觉不对。地球酿酒摊新装了一个直指我卡座的监控头。联殖安保的制服在队伍里逗留得太久，不说话，只是在听。一个我认识的盖尔银行快船员假装没认出我。空气尝起来像再循环的恐惧和廉价浓缩咖啡。

我算了一遍留下来的代价。相信内部渠道的代价。让又一份"修订过的"报告埋掉那些让我睡不着的预测的代价。那曲线的结局总是一样：债务在顶端合并，小账户在边缘蒸发，而我是个方便的变量——一旦我的代码被妥善国有化，就该被移除。

于是我不再按季度思考，开始按流量思考。那些权力和信用币流动、而监管者不太细看的地方。霓虹城，带着它那套未偿人情和被遗忘管道的下层。没人愿意承认仍在提取维护预算的旧工作营地。某些中继站周围连星防队都只在着火时才检查的盲区。

我逃走，是因为当我的演练证明它能调动真钱的那一刻，"分析师"和"资产"之间的界线就消失了。我选了街区与甲板之间的阴影，因为它们感觉像当初的深井区——在联殖决定我们只是风景的一部分之前。要是我能从那里改写账簿，哪怕只改一点，也许下一个在那间地球酿酒摊里弓着背、就着茶和电子表格的女孩，会有比顺从或消失更多的选择。

我现在怕的不是死。死是一个干净的结局。我怕的是醒来又回到一间明亮的办公室，我的代码被盖上密级章，听着某个微笑的主管解释我的工作如何"稳定"了局面，而同样那些人仍站在外面同一条队伍里，纳闷自己的账户为什么一夜之间冻结。

#en:
Lost track of ship time again. You sleep when the grav plates hum soft and you work when they scream, that is about the only clock that matters out here.

We cleared a freighter carcass today, hull buckled like a crushed can, heat long gone. Kade took point, of course, swaggering through the breach with his torch like the void owed him rent. Mira followed, checking our tethers twice like she always does, muttering about microfractures no one else can see. I came last, watching my own breath fog the visor and counting all the ways this could kill us before we even touched cargo.

We found a hold with pallets still shrink-wrapped, too pristine for a wreck that dead. The beacon data did not match the manifests and I saw that quiet look pass between Kade and the Union overseer on the comms. That is when paranoia starts chewing at the back of your skull. Out here, betrayal is not some dramatic thing; it is just a man forgetting to mention a crate, shaving a few minutes off your air, misreporting who went in first.

I have not forgotten the day I realized I could lean into that. We were arguing salvage shares with a green crew on the dock at Gagarin, and one of them grabbed my rigging to make a point. I stepped in close, explained in a calm voice how long it takes for a suit breach to bleed a man out. Watched his eyes go wide. He backed off, whole gang did. Disturbing part was not that it worked. Disturbing part was that it felt good.

Recognition started after that. Other crews nodding when I passed, whispering my name under their breath like I was some kind of hazard marker. Pride, sure, but also this cold thread in my spine: once people know your face, you stop being anonymous. You become a story, and stories have a way of drawing knives in the dark.

I think that is why my last partner twisted me up so badly. She had this way of replaying old conversations, changing little details until I was not sure if I had misheard or if she was lying. "You agreed to this cut," she would say, "remember?" And I would stand there in the locker bay, trying to recall the exact words under the stench of burnt sealant and old sweat. After a while you start doubting your own memory more than anyone else's greed.

Tonight, Kade is laughing with some yard bosses over Erdebrau cans and Mira is down in the tool locker, rewrapping cables, complaining about how our patchwork gear is a deathtrap. I am sitting on a cargo brace, listening to the ship creak, wondering which is going to get us first: a failed weld, a bad call, or someone deciding that one less cut of the haul makes their life easier.

Salvage Crown Union calls us a family when the ledgers are healthy. Thing about families is, they know exactly where to cut when it is time to make someone disappear into the wrecks.
zh:
又记不清飞船时间了。重力板轻声嗡鸣时你就睡，它们尖叫时你就干活，在这外面那差不多就是唯一要紧的钟。

今天我们清了一具货船残骸，船壳皱得像只被压扁的罐子，热量早已散尽。凯德当然打头，拿着他的焊枪大摇大摆穿过破口，像真空欠他房租。米拉跟在后面，像往常一样把我们的系绳检查了两遍，嘟囔着别人看不见的微裂缝。我最后进，看着自己的呼吸在面罩上起雾，数着在我们碰到货物之前这件事能弄死我们的种种方式。

我们找到一个货舱，货板还裹着收缩膜，对一具死成那样的残骸来说太新了。信标数据与清单对不上，我看见凯德和通讯里那位工会监工之间闪过那种安静的眼神。就是那时，偏执开始在你的后脑勺啃咬。在这外面，背叛不是什么戏剧性的事；只是一个男人忘了提一只箱子、从你的空气里削掉几分钟、谎报谁先进去。

我没忘记我意识到自己能利用这一点的那天。我们在加加林码头上跟一队新手争打捞分成，其中一个抓住我的索具来加强语气。我凑近，用平静的声音解释一处宇航服破口让人流血至死要多久。看着他眼睛睁大。他退开了，整帮人都退开了。让人不安的不是它奏效了。让人不安的是它感觉很好。

那之后，被认出来的事开始了。别的船员在我经过时点头，低声念着我的名字，像我是个什么危险标记。骄傲，当然，可脊背上也有一根冰冷的线：一旦人们知道你的脸，你就不再匿名了。你成了一个故事，而故事有办法在黑暗中招来刀子。

我想这就是为什么我上一个搭档把我搅得那么厉害。她有一种重放旧对话的方式，改掉些小细节，直到我不确定是我听错了还是她在撒谎。"你同意了这个分成，"她会说，"记得吗？"而我就站在储物间里，努力在烧焦密封剂和陈汗的臭味下回忆确切的字眼。过一阵，你开始比怀疑别人的贪婪更怀疑自己的记忆。

今晚，凯德正跟几个船坞老板就着埃尔德啤酒罐大笑，米拉在工具柜里重新缠缆绳，抱怨我们那套拼凑的装备是个死亡陷阱。我坐在一根货舱撑杆上，听着飞船吱嘎，琢磨哪个会先要了我们的命：一处失败的焊缝、一个错误的决定，还是有人认定少一份分成能让自己的日子好过些。

打捞王冠工会在账簿健康时叫我们一家人。家人的问题在于，当要让人消失进残骸里时，他们确切知道该往哪里下刀。

#en:
Lena keeps saying the suit tape is a bad sign, that once you start using it on the same patch more than twice you are basically asking the void to take a bite. Today I caught myself adding a third layer over my left thigh seal anyway. Out there, drifting between a cracked cargo spine and a freighter that looks like it tried to fold through itself, you stop pretending you are not already held together by scraps.

We shared reheated stew again in the locker bay, same dented tins balanced on an upside-down crate. Miles complained about the taste, but he still scraped the bottom, same as the rest of us. Calen traded a handful of loose connectors to a dock rat for a bag of half-stale bread, and for five minutes we were kings, passing it around, grease and metal dust on our fingers. It is funny what feels like luxury when your clothes are all patched canvas and heat-warped zips.

The run today was a quiet one, mostly. No bodies, at least. Just the echo of alarms that had long since given up. Even so, when the hull groaned and the lights on my wrist-fix flickered, I got that flash again, same as always: holding her in that collapsing corridor back on the station, bulkheads screaming, the air going thin. I remember her fingers in my suit gloves, clutching so hard it hurt, both of us breathing each other's fear through the comm, love and loss tangled so tight I could not tell where one stopped. I walked out. She did not. Everything since has been bargaining with that fact.

Lena says there is a new pattern in the graveyards, that some wrecks look like they were put there on purpose, lined up on the edge of certain lanes. Calen swears he found a nav-core last week that would not let go of its last plotted vector, like the route itself was holding on. We laugh about ghost pilots in the mess, but no one talks much when we suit up and drift past derelicts that still have their running lights on.

I keep thinking about a night years ago, back in a side room off some cheap bar airlock, where a friend leaned in close and whispered that they were done running small-time jobs, that there were people who knew how to steer ships off the official roads and into better-paying shadows. "Come with me," they said. "We do not have to scrape forever." I said no. Took the safe route. Ended up cutting hulls for scrap anyway.

Sometimes, when the beacon chatter crackles strange and the grav readings do not match the map, I wonder if those better-paying shadows are where all the empty ships we find really come from. Then Miles calls for a lift line, Lena curses at a jammed cutter, and the moment is gone. Junkstar moves on to the next corpse in orbit, and Rian Kell tapes up his suit, eats what is left in the pot, and tries not to listen too closely to the stories drifting in from the lanes.
zh:
莉娜一直说宇航服胶带是个坏兆头，说一旦你开始往同一块补丁上贴第三次，就基本是在求真空来咬一口。今天我还是在左腿密封处加了第三层。在那外面，漂在一截开裂的货舱脊和一艘看起来像试图把自身折穿过去的货船之间，你就不再假装自己没有早已被边角料拼凑着。

我们又在储物间里分吃重新加热的炖菜，同样凹陷的餐盒架在一只翻过来的箱子上。迈尔斯抱怨味道，可他还是把锅底刮干净了，和我们其余人一样。卡伦用一把松散的接头跟一个码头老鼠换了半袋陈旧的面包，有那么五分钟我们像国王，传来传去，手指上是油污和金属灰。有趣的是，当你的衣服全是打补丁的帆布和热变形的拉链时，什么叫奢侈。

今天的活儿很安静，大多是。至少没有尸体。只有早已放弃的警报的回响。即便如此，当船壳呻吟、我手腕固定器上的灯闪烁时，我又闪过那个画面，和往常一样：在那座空间站一条正在塌陷的走廊里抱着她，舱壁尖叫，空气变稀薄。我记得她的手指在我宇航服手套里，攥得那么紧，攥得发疼，我们俩透过通讯呼吸着彼此的恐惧，爱与失去缠得那么紧，我分不清哪一个在哪里结束。我走出来了。她没有。从那以后的一切，都是在跟这个事实讨价还价。

莉娜说墓地里出现了一个新图案，说有些残骸像是被故意放在那里的，排列在某些航道的边缘。卡伦赌咒说他上周找到一个导航核心，死活不肯放掉它最后标绘的矢量，像那条航线本身在苦苦抓住什么。我们在食堂里拿幽灵飞行员开玩笑，可当我们穿上宇航服、漂过那些仍亮着航行灯的弃船时，没人多说话。

我总是想起多年前的一个夜晚，在某间廉价酒吧气闸旁的侧室里，一个朋友凑近低声说他们不再干小活了，说有人懂得如何把飞船从官方航道上引向更赚钱的阴影里。"跟我走吧，"他们说。"我们不必永远刮蹭下去。"我说不。走了安全的路。结果还是来切割船壳换废料。

有时，当信标闲聊里劈啪作响得古怪、重力读数与地图不符时，我会想，那些更赚钱的阴影，是不是就是我们找到的所有空船真正的来处。然后迈尔斯喊要一根提升索，莉娜咒骂一台卡住的切割机，那一刻就过去了。垃圾星号继续开向轨道上的下一具尸体，而里安·凯尔贴上他的宇航服，把锅里剩下的吃掉，努力不去细听从航道里飘来的那些故事。

#en:
When I was little, I was afraid of the dark gap between bulkhead and bunk on my parents' hauler. I used to stuff rags down there so nothing could crawl out and grab my hand while I slept. Now I have ridden ships apart in grav shear, listened to hulls scream and people go silent mid-sentence, and that childhood fear feels absurd. Part of me still wonders if it ever happened that way at all, or if I polished those memories like a good story to pretend there was a time when the universe made simpler kinds of threats.

I have done things since that no story can sand smooth. There was a tug once, years before anyone started whispering my callsign like a curse. Its captain sent me his nav logs, swearing the lane I cleared him on had glitched. I ran the data three times, then nudged a single parameter and watched the projection of his ship brush the edge of a debris field. Not enough to guarantee a hit, just enough to raise the probability into the red. I did it because I wanted to see if the model was right, if the numbers would obey. No anger, no profit motive. Pure, clinical curiosity. He limped through in one piece, screaming about near misses and "bad intel," and I sat there with my hands shaking because the simulation had matched his panic down to the second.

The thing that finally pushed me off the board was not a shipbreaking accident or some captain's sob story. It was paper. Dry, boring, endless paper. Internal memos routed to the wrong inbox, timestamps that did not match the telemetry, clearance codes on a convoy that should have been routine but carried more security than a battle group. The day after the collision, those files vanished from the archive as if they had never existed, and a neat little report appeared with my name stamped on every line that mattered.

I have seen that pattern repeat enough times now in port logs and fuel tallies, in "random" audits that somehow always look past the same blind spots. It is the same careful hand I used on that tug, only bigger, older, and backed by people whose names never appear on any manifest. So I ran. I picked places that fall between official maps: debris corridors where smugglers cut corners, half-legal waystations where dockmasters keep two ledgers, LIST outposts that rely on "luck" to stay supplied. From here, I can watch the currents they pretend do not exist, trace where the quiet convoys bend around something no one admits is there.

What I want now is not forgiveness. That requires believing there was a clean before the dirty, and I am not sure I buy that anymore. What I want is to drag their invisible routes into the same light they burned me in, to make the sky show its seams. If that makes me the monster in someone else's childhood story, so be it. At least their fear will be pointed at something real.
zh:
我小的时候，害怕父母货船上舱壁和铺位之间那道黑暗的缝。我常往那儿塞破布，好让没什么东西能在我睡觉时爬出来抓住我的手。如今我在重力剪切中把船骑散过，听过船壳尖叫、人在话说到一半时归于沉默，那份童年的恐惧显得荒唐。我身上有一部分仍想知道，那是否真发生过，还是我把那些记忆打磨得像一个好故事，好假装曾经有一个宇宙只给出更简单的威胁。

从那以后我做过一些任何故事都磨不平的事。曾经有一艘拖船，在很多年前、在任何人开始念我的呼号像念诅咒之前。它的船长把他的导航日志发给我，赌咒说我给他清的航道出了问题。我把数据跑了三遍，然后拨动一个参数，看着他飞船的投影擦过一个碎片场的边缘。不足以保证命中，只足以把概率抬进红区。我这么做，是因为我想看看模型对不对，数字会不会服从。没有愤怒，没有获利动机。纯粹、临床式的好奇。他一路跛行着穿了过去，尖叫着险情和"情报有误"，而我坐在那儿手在抖，因为模拟把他的惊慌复现得分毫不差。

最终把我推下棋盘的，不是一次拆船事故，也不是某个船长的悲情故事。是纸。干燥、无聊、无尽的纸。内部备忘被路由到错的收件箱，时间戳与遥测对不上，一支本该例行、却带着比一个战斗群更多安保的运输队的通行代码。碰撞后的第二天，那些文件从档案里消失了，像从未存在过，而一份整洁的小报告出现了，每一行要紧的地方都盖着我的名字。

这个图案如今我在港口日志和燃料统计里、在那些不知怎的总能看漏同样盲区的"随机"审计里见过足够多次了。是同一只我当年用在拖船上的谨慎的手，只是更大、更老，背后是那些名字从不出现在任何清单上的人。于是我跑了。我挑了那些落在官方地图之间的地方：走私贩抄近路的碎片走廊、码头主管留两本账的半合法中转站、靠"运气"维持补给的独立盟前哨站。从这里，我能看见它们假装不存在的那些水流，追出那些安静的运输队绕过某个没人承认存在之物弯折的形状。

我现在要的不是宽恕。那需要相信脏之前有过干净，而我不确定自己还信那个。我要的是把他们那些看不见的航线拖进他们烧我的同一片光里，让天空露出它的接缝。要是那让我成为别人童年故事里的怪物，那就这样吧。至少他们的恐惧会指向某种真实的东西。

#en:
Some nights the bunk feels more like a foxhole than a bed. I lie here listening to the Taskforce breathing in the next compartment and the old drills kick in on their own: count exits, catalog threats, map firing lines in the dark. My body still squares up when a hatch clangs, shoulders tightening of their own accord, hand drifting toward where a sidearm used to hang. Mind knows we are between contracts, off the grid, but the rest of me is still expecting an alarm, a breach, someone shouting for a stack on the door.

There was a night on Valkyr Station I think about more than the others. Power was flickering, bulkheads still hot from the last hit, alarms howling in three different tones. Mira Hollis and I ducked into a maintenance shaft to bypass a sealed hatch and found ourselves wedged between coolant pipes, everything muffled by the hum. For maybe thirty seconds we just sat there, helmets off, sharing a lukewarm water pouch and trading the kind of stupid jokes you only hear in boot. It felt like the universe had paused just for us. As soon as the emergency lights cycled back, we both knew it was over and never said a word about it again.

Leaving official command never felt like a clean break. It was more like bleeding out through a dozen paper cuts. Dana Kessler still calls our little outfit by the old company number when she is tired, then bites it back like a curse. Elena Navarro keeps the comms board organized exactly the way the brass insisted, even though none of them can see it now. I catch myself polishing boots before a job we chose for ourselves, like some invisible officer is going to pop the hatch and inspect us for dust.

We all heard different whispers that pushed us over. I remember one debrief where they brushed past the civilian casualty figures with a single line about "non-critical variance," eyes already sliding to the next slide. Later, in the corridor, someone muttered about a whole block on New Homestead that never made it into the official report. Rumor said a unit like ours had been told to "stabilize" the area and walked away on schedule, even when the evac birds were redirected elsewhere. Nobody ever confirmed it, but the way command shut down questions stuck in my teeth.

Out here in Redacted Taskforce, loyalties are narrower and deeper. We trust each other to watch the corners, not because a flag says so but because no one else will. At the same time, there is always that question hanging between us: if orders went bad again, would we walk off together, or start walking away from each other? My muscles tense first when something shifts, deciding whether to fight, flee, or freeze, long before I can line up the ethics of it. Maybe that is what we really brought with us from the service: not the slogans, just the reflex to move before the thinking catches up.
zh:
有些夜里，那张铺位感觉更像散兵坑而不是床。我躺在这儿，听着隔壁舱室里特遣队的呼吸声，旧日的操练自顾自地启动：数出口、清点威胁、在黑暗中规划射击线。舱门哐当一声时我的身体仍会立正，肩膀自动绷紧，手飘向以前挂随身武器的地方。脑子知道我们是在合同之间、离开了电网，可我其余部分仍在等警报、等破舱、等有人喊"在门口组队"。

有一个在瓦尔基尔空间站的夜晚，我想得比别的多。电力在闪，舱壁还烫着上一次的命中，警报以三种不同的调子嚎叫。米拉·霍利斯和我钻进一条维护竖井去绕开一扇封死的舱门，发现自己卡在冷却管之间，一切都被人声嗡鸣闷住。大约三十秒，我们就这样坐着，摘下头盔，分着一袋温水，交换着只有在基础训练里才听得到的那种蠢笑话。感觉宇宙为我们暂停了一下。应急灯一恢复循环，我们俩就知道它结束了，之后再也不提一个字。

离开正式指挥从来不像一次干净的断裂。它更像从十几道纸割伤里慢慢流干血。达娜·凯斯勒累的时候还会用旧的公司番号叫我们这支小队伍，然后像咬住一句诅咒一样咽回去。埃琳娜·纳瓦罗仍按长官坚持的方式整理通讯板，哪怕他们现在都看不见了。我发觉自己在一次我们自己选的活儿前还擦靴子，好像某个看不见的军官会突然掀开舱门检查我们有没有灰。

我们都听到了不同的低语，把我们推过那条线。我记得一次述职，他们用一句"非关键差异"带过了平民伤亡数字，眼睛已经在瞟向下一页幻灯片。后来在走廊里，有人嘟囔说新家园有一整个街区从未进入官方报告。传言说有一支像我们这样的部队被告知去"稳定"那片区域，然后按日程撤走，哪怕撤离飞行器被调往别处。没人证实过，但指挥部关闭提问的方式卡在了我牙缝里。

在这外面的"涂黑特遣队"里，忠诚更窄也更深。我们信任彼此照看角落，不是因为旗子这么说，而是因为没有别人会。同时，我们之间总悬着那个问题：要是命令再出问题，我们会一起走开，还是开始互相走开？当有什么变化时，先是我的肌肉绷紧，决定是战、是逃、还是僵住，远早于我理清其中的道德。也许这就是我们从军旅真正带出来的东西：不是那些口号，而是思考赶上来之前就先动的反射。

#en:
I picked this relay because no one looks at it unless they are desperate or lost. The official lanes stepped around it years ago, like a ship giving a wide berth to wreckage it does not want to admit it left behind. That suits me. A forgotten junction is the best place to redraw the map.

The last ship I diverted here was a LIST transport I could have let run clean. The corridor was clear, telemetry solid, no pirate chatter within three jumps. I watched the feeds long enough to know those people would probably make it. Then I brought up Danya's projections, ran them against the frontier reports, and found a scenario where they did not. So I nudged them off, just a few degrees, into a path that brought them closer to one of our refuel stones. On the external cam I saw one family still strapping in, the youngest crying. I could have rolled it back. Instead I watched the marker drift onto my new line and felt the calm that comes with being the only one in the Settled Systems who knows which lives will hang on a calculated error. I let them go, and I did not warn anyone.

People like to talk about morality like it is a straight lane with buoys and beacons. That is a story for citizens who still think the universe reacts to their good intentions. Out here, I use morality the way I use a jump plot: as a tool that moves mass where I need it. When Danya has numbers that argue for a reroute, I call it mercy. When a Crimson Fleet captain waves enough credits at me to drag a transport across his hunting ground, I call it inevitability. Same hand on the same controls. The only difference is who is buying the narrative that makes it hurt less.

There was a time, back in the early HopeTown runs, when I would have said I drew a line. No children, no medical shipments, no ships already in trouble. That was before I watched UC and Freestar let a colony choke to death while they argued over who was allowed to send help, before I saw Spacers carve through a convoy that did everything "right." Somewhere in those years, right and wrong stopped being fixed points and started being variables I adjust to keep the math balanced for the people paying me and the ones I cannot quite stop believing deserve a chance.

Now, when I look at a manifest, I do not ask whether diverting them is good or bad. I ask whether diverting them is useful. Useful to Danya's endgame, useful to the buyers waiting in the dark, useful to me when I finally burn every favor and need one last clean jump to a coordinate no one else has. That is the real reason I am here, threaded between dead transponders and old war scars. This place gives me room to keep drawing my own routes, and just enough distance from the lanes I broke that if someone comes hunting, they will have to untangle my work from a sky full of other people's lies before they ever get a lock on me.
zh:
我选这座中继站，因为除非走投无路或迷了路，没人会看它。官方航道多年前就绕开了它，像一艘船对不想承认是自己留下的残骸远远避开。这合我意。一座被遗忘的交汇点是重画地图的最佳地点。

我最近改道到这里的最后一艘船，是一艘我本可以让它干净通过的独立盟运输船。走廊是清空的，遥测稳定，三个跃迁范围内没有海盗闲聊。我看数据流看得够久，知道那些人大概能通过。然后我调出达妮娅的预测，拿它们对照边疆报告，找到一个他们通不过的情景。于是我把他们推开，只推几度，推进一条更靠近我们一处补给石头的路径。在外部摄像头上，我看见一家人还在系安全带，最小的那个在哭。我本可以撤回。可我只是看着那个标记漂到我画的新线上，感到那份只有定居星系群里唯一知道自己划线的人才会有的平静。我放他们走了，我没警告任何人。

人们喜欢把道德谈成一条有浮标和信标的笔直航道。那是给仍然以为宇宙会回应他们善意的公民讲的故事。在这外面，我用道德就像我用跃迁图：一个把质量挪到我要的地方的工具。当达妮娅有数字支持改道时，我叫它仁慈。当一个深红舰队的船长朝我挥出足够的信用币、要我拖一支运输队穿过他的猎场时，我叫它必然。同一只手按着同样的操纵杆。唯一的区别是谁在买那个让事情没那么疼的说法。

曾经有一段时间，在早期希望镇的航次里，我会说自己是画了条线的。不碰孩子，不碰医疗货运，不碰已经陷入麻烦的飞船。那是在我看着联殖和自由星系联盟任由一座殖民地窒息而死、自己却在争谁有权派救援之前，是在我看着太空劫匪切开一支做对了每件事的运输队之前。那些年里的某处，对与错不再是固定点，而成了我为付费的人和那些我无法真的不再相信值得一次机会的人调整的变量。

如今，当我看着一份清单，我不问改道他们是对是错。我问改道他们是否有用。对达妮娅的终局有用，对在黑暗中等待的买家有用，对我有用——当我最终烧光所有人情、需要最后一次干净的跃迁去一个别人都没有的坐标时。这才是真正待在这里的原因，穿在死应答器和旧战争疤痕之间。这地方给我空间继续画我自己的航线，也给我足够的距离，远离我弄坏的那些航道——要是有人来猎我，他们得先把我的作品从一整片别人的谎言里理出来，才能锁定我。

#en:
Kara says I peel labels off drink packs when I am nervous. I looked down at mess tonight and realized there was a whole drift of plastic at my elbow, so that tracks. Seamender feels smaller on these long legs between hubs, like the bulkheads keep leaning in a little closer each day. Cargo hold hum, reactor thrum, Darius complaining about calibration in the background; it all blurs into the same noise. Trade Authority calls it "steady work." I call it hauling someone else's secrets in boxes I am not allowed to open.

There is a story running around that one of the clerks back in Gagarin got caught moving corridor access for cash, routing ships into quiet gaps where they "accidentally" met the right pirates. Jared thinks it is just dock talk, but Oren swears he heard the name of a real official attached, someone high enough that the investigation never saw daylight. I want to believe it is all exaggerated, but when I watch how cleanly some of our manifests vanish from the system, how perfectly timed our little "detours" are, I feel a lump in my throat that will not go down.

My last name still feels heavier than these crates. Calder Shipping was supposed to be honest freight, three generations of doing it by the book until my father decided to start shaving costs and bending routes. By the time the regulators finished with us, the only thing left was debt and an offer from Trade Authority to "put my experience to use." I signed because I did not see another way out. Some days, walking the spine of Seamender, I am not sure I did not just swap one set of chains for another.

Tonight had one good moment, though. We ate together in the tiny galley, all four of us, elbows bumping over rehydrated ramen and Red Harvest crackers. Kara told a terrible joke about spacer coffee, Darius pretended to be offended on behalf of every engineer in the Settled Systems, and Jared just sat there grinning, sauce on his lip, like we were not floating in a metal tube full of other people's money. For a few minutes, it smelled like broth and cheap spice instead of stress, and I forgot to peel the label off my drink pack.

I do not know where I belong yet. I am not Calder Shipping anymore, but I do not feel Trade Authority in my bones, either. I know flight paths and docking codes, how to juggle invoices and smile at customs while hoping they do not look too closely. Is that a life or just a skill set someone else profits from? Sometimes I catch myself watching the stars outside the porthole and thinking about walking away from all of it, finding some quiet outpost where my name does not mean anything. Then I remember the debt notes still tagged to my ident and the way Oren looks at them when he thinks I am not watching, and I strap back into my bunk and tell myself that one peaceful meal and a bad joke mean I am at least moving in the right direction.
zh:
卡拉说我一紧张就撕饮料包的标签。今晚在食堂我低头一看，发现胳膊肘边堆了一小片塑料，看来是这么回事。缝补者号在这些中继枢纽之间的长途航段上显得更小了，像舱壁每天都在往里多倾一点。货舱嗡鸣、反应堆嗡响，大流士在背景里抱怨校准，全都糊成同一种噪声。贸易管理局管这叫"稳定工作"。我管它叫用我无权打开的箱子替别人运秘密。

有传言说加加林那边有个文员被抓到收钱出让走廊通行权，把飞船引向安静的缺口，让它们"意外"撞上对的海盗。杰瑞德觉得那只是码头闲话，可奥伦赌咒说他听到过一个真官员的名字，那人级别高到调查从未见过天日。我想相信那全是夸大，可当我看着我们的一些清单如何干净地从系统里消失、我们那些小"绕行"时序如何完美时，我喉咙里堵着一团咽不下去的东西。

我的姓还是比这些箱子沉。考尔德航运本该是诚实的货运，三代人照章办事，直到我父亲决定开始削减成本、弯折航线。等监管者跟我们了结时，剩下的只有债务，以及贸易管理局一句"把你的经验用起来"的邀约。我签了，因为我看不到别的出路。有些日子，走在缝补者号的舱脊上，我不确定自己是不是只是把一副锁链换成了另一副。

不过今晚有一个好时刻。我们四个人在那间小厨房里一起吃饭，手肘在复水拉面和红丰收饼干上方互相碰着。卡拉讲了个关于太空人咖啡的糟糕笑话，大流士假装代表定居星系群所有工程师表示受辱，杰瑞德只是坐在那儿咧着嘴笑，嘴唇上还沾着酱，像我们不是漂在一个装满别人钱财的金属管里。有那么几分钟，闻起来是汤和廉价香料的味道，而不是压力，我忘了撕掉饮料包上的标签。

我还不知道自己属于哪里。我不再是考尔德航运，可我也不觉得自己骨子里是贸易管理局。我懂飞行航线和停靠代码，懂得一边周旋账单、一边对海关微笑同时盼着他们别看得太细。那是一种生活，还是只是别人从中获利的一套技能？有时我发觉自己望着舷窗外的星星，想着干脆离开这一切，去找个安静的前哨站，让我的名字什么意义都没有。然后我记起仍挂在我身份上的欠款通知，记起奥伦在以为我没看时看它们的眼神，于是我重新系回铺位，告诉自己，一顿平静的饭和一个糟糕的笑话，至少说明我还在往对的方向走。

#en:
I do not remember the year, only the taste of recycled air and burnt metal. I was a kid on one of those early hauler runs out of Sol, still believing the brochures about unity and exploration. We came across a drifting prospecting pod, lights dead, beacon weak. My mother asked the captain if we would answer it. He did not even look up from his game. Said it was "not in our lane," that diverting would cost fuel and someone else would handle it. That was the first time I understood the universe runs on margins, not morals.

Funny how I keep pretending otherwise.

I keep telling myself what I am doing now is a kind of applied ethics, an experiment in distributed risk. If I sound clever enough, maybe I can drown out the screaming part of my brain that remembers names off the convoy manifest. I can quote theory, talk about how every grav jump is a negotiation with a hostile vacuum, about how causality thins at the edges of certain profiles. Dress it up in language so dense no one notices the simple part: I drew the line they followed, and they did not come back.

I caught myself earlier, muttering like I was back in some academy I never attended. "What we are attempting is an interrogation of the boundary conditions of safe transit," I said to an empty cockpit, hands deep in the Cartagena Line's drive housing. As if rerouting cooling around a worn ring to squeeze one more illicit corridor out of it is some noble inquiry instead of gambling other people's lives for answers I want.

This place makes it easier to lie to myself. An old farm off the main flows, fields long gone to dust, satellites just functional enough to whisper telemetry without drawing attention. On the charts it is a dead node. To me it is ideal: ground-based power, low profile, no one looking twice at a forgotten comms tower if it starts spitting test pings into the dark.

I came here because the noise kept circling back to this region, little echoes in the data from haulers and LIST colonies nearby, like the signature I saw the day the convoy folded. I tell myself if I can map that curve properly, I can prove it was not negligence, that someone tampered with the profile or that the space itself was already broken there. That is the story I rehearse in my head, in grand, precise terms, like I will someday stand in a chamber on Jemison and present it as a thesis instead of a confession.

Underneath all of that, the truth is simpler and uglier. I am terrified that if I stop chasing these patterns, if I let the guilt settle instead of burying it under equations and polished phrases, I will have to live with the idea that I killed them because I wanted to be clever. So I keep plotting, keep jumping, keep hiding behind complicated words, hoping they sound more profound than what I have really been: cruel, in a way that fits neatly into flight plans and hazard pay.
zh:
我不记得是哪一年了，只记得再循环空气和烧焦金属的味道。我那时还是个孩子，搭着一趟从太阳系出发的早期货运航次，还相信那些关于团结与探索的宣传册。我们遇到一具漂流的勘探舱，灯全灭了，信标微弱。我母亲问船长我们会不会回应它。他连游戏都没从上面抬起头。说那"不在我们的航线上"，说改道会耗燃料，会有人别的人处理。那是我第一次明白，宇宙靠的是余量，不是道德。

有趣的是，我一直在假装不是这样。

我一直告诉自己，我现在做的事是一种应用伦理学，一场分布式风险的实验。要是我说得够聪明，也许就能盖过我脑子里那个尖叫的部分——它记得运输队清单上的名字。我能引用理论，谈论每一次重力跃迁都是与充满敌意的真空的一场谈判，谈论因果性在某些剖面边缘如何变薄。用密到没人注意到那个简单部分的语言把它装扮起来：那条线是我画的，他们顺着它走，然后他们没回来。

早些时候我发觉自己在嘟囔，像回到了某所我从未上过的学院。"我们试图做的，是对安全通行边界条件的一次审问，"我对着一间空驾驶舱说，双手深陷在卡塔赫纳线的驱动外壳里。仿佛为了一处磨损的环重新绕冷却、从中挤出一条更多的非法走廊，是什么高尚的探究，而不是拿别人的命去赌我想要的答案。

这地方让我更容易对自己撒谎。一座离主流量很远的老农场，田地早已化为尘土，卫星刚好还能低声传递遥测而不引人注意。在星图上它是个死节点。对我来说它很理想：地基供电、低存在感，没人会为一座被遗忘的通讯塔往黑暗里吐测试探测而多看一眼。

我来这里，是因为那些噪声一直绕回这个区域，来自附近运货船员和独立盟殖民地数据里的细小回响，像我看着运输队散开那天见到的特征。我告诉自己，要是我能正确测绘那条曲线，我就能证明那不是疏忽，是有人篡改了剖面，或者那片空间本身早已破损。这就是我在脑子里排练的故事，用的宏大而精确的措辞，像有一天我会站在杰米森某个议事厅里把它当作论文而不是认罪书呈上。

在这一切底下，真相更简单也更丑陋。我极度害怕，一旦我停止追这些图案，一旦我让愧疚沉淀下来、而不是把它埋在方程和漂亮措辞底下，我就得接受一个念头：我杀了他们，因为我想显得聪明。所以我继续标绘，继续跃迁，继续躲在复杂的词后面，盼着它们听起来比真正一直以来的我更深刻：残忍，以一种恰好能塞进飞行计划和危险津贴里的方式。

#en:
I keep trying to remember the last day I wore a uniform and believed the people above me earned theirs. Memory says it was before the river crossing, before the air was full of burning polymer and Kara Ellison's voice over the squad channel shaking in a way I had never heard. But the truth is it probably snapped some quiet night later, standing in a briefing room that smelled like recycled coffee, listening to a colonel talk around numbers that did not match what we had seen on the ground. Those casualty reports never did line up.

Damien Harlow still talks like we are in, like this is just a "temporary reassignment." He checks his corners, polices his brass, calls everyone by last name. I watch him sometimes, wonder if it is habit or if he genuinely thinks someone at a desk with a clean shirt is still paying attention to the pieces of us that walked off base and did not come back. Kara is different. She laughs too loud now, pushes every op right to the edge. Some nights I see the medic from that village in the way she looks at a target, and I know she is still trying to erase one specific face by stacking a pile of others on top.

I thought leaving the chain would make the ghosts quieter. It did not. The discipline is still there, grafted into my bones. I still wake up at 0500, still clean my rifle the same way, still expect orders even when no one is giving them. Only difference is now when someone says "clear it," I ask who is on the other side and why they are in our way. That question got us branded outlaws more than anything we actually did with a gun.

There was a moment with Kara, after everything went sideways on that escort run. We were holed up in a half-collapsed warehouse, rain coming through the roof in sheets, both of us wired and shaking. She grabbed me by the harness, hard, told me if I ever second-guessed an exfil call again she would put a round through my knee herself and drag me back as a lesson. Her eyes said she meant it. I should have pulled away, should have written her off right then as just another weapon that had slipped its safety. Instead I kissed her, because something in me liked that she could hurt me and might choose not to.

Sleep is a problem now. When I lie down, the dark is never empty. It is filled with the sound of rotors that are not coming, of a town square lit up too bright, of a woman's voice on a recorder saying the wrong coordinates in a tone that told me she knew. Some nights I hear Damien shouting over gunfire again, other nights it is Kara's whisper in my ear, soft words shaped like threats. My mind runs the same reel of nights: barricades, muzzle flashes, civilians pressed against walls, our own people aiming a little too low when they were supposedly firing warning shots. I roll over, count breaths, tell myself it was all justified, all necessary. The lie never lasts long enough to get me more than an hour at a time.
zh:
我一直在努力回想我最后一次穿着制服、并且相信上面那些人配得上他们那身制服的那一天。记忆说那是在那条河之前，在空气里满是燃烧的聚合物、卡拉·埃里森在小队频道里的声音以我从未听过的方式发抖之前。可事实是，它大概是在之后某个安静的夜里断掉的——站在一间闻着像再循环咖啡的简报室里，听一个上校绕着一些与我们在地面上所见对不上的数字说话。那些伤亡报告从来就对不上。

达米安·哈洛至今说话还像我们还在编，像这只是一次"临时调任"。他检查自己的角落，擦拭自己的军纪徽章，用姓称呼每个人。我有时看着他，琢磨那是习惯，还是他真的以为某个坐在办公桌前、穿着干净衬衫的人仍在关注我们当中那些走出基地就再没回来的部分。卡拉不一样。她现在笑得太大、把每次行动都推到边缘。有些夜里，我从她看目标的方式里看见那个村子里的军医，而我知道她仍在用一具具别的面孔盖上去，试图抹掉某一张特定的脸。

我以为离开那条指挥链会让鬼安静些。它没有。纪律还在，嫁接进了我的骨头。我仍五点醒来，仍用同样的方式擦枪，仍期待命令，哪怕没人在下。唯一的区别是，如今有人喊"清场"时，我会问对面是谁、他们为什么挡我们的路。这个问题比我们任何真正拿枪做过的事都更把我们打成了亡命之徒。

有这么一个关于卡拉的瞬间，在护送那次出岔子之后。我们躲在一座半塌的仓库里，雨从屋顶成片地漏下来，我们俩都紧绷着、发抖。她一把抓住我的背带，很用力，说要是再有一次我对撤离命令犹豫，她就自己往我膝盖上打一枪，然后把我拖回来当教材。她的眼睛说她是认真的。我本该掰开她的手，本该当场把她当成一件滑了保险的武器划掉。可我吻了她，因为我身上有什么东西喜欢她能伤害我、却可能选择不那么做。

如今睡觉是个问题。我躺下时，黑暗从不空。它填满了不会来的旋翼声、一座亮得过头的村镇广场、以及录音里一个女人用那种告诉我她知道的语气念错坐标的声音。有些夜里我又听见达米安在枪火中喊叫，另一些夜里是卡拉在我耳边低语，柔软的词句裹着威胁的形状。我的脑子重放同一卷夜晚：路障、枪口闪光、紧贴墙的平民、我们自己人在"鸣枪示警"时瞄得有点太低。我翻个身，数呼吸，告诉自己这一切都是正当的，都是必要的。这谎言从来撑不过一小时。

#en:
Some nights the hum of this little skiff sounds like an old branch groaning in a Freestar wind. I close my eyes and I am back on that farm, listening to my father curse the sky because a loan committee halfway across the Systems decided our harvest was "too volatile." That is when I learned the first rule: numbers are just hands on throats you cannot see. Back then, it hurt. Now I am the one with my fingers on the ledger, and I am not sure when the hurting stopped being a problem.

The hunters will assume I ran here to hide. That is only half true. The skiff gives me distance from New Atlantis and Neon, enough latency that when I nudge a warrant or collapse a line of credit, the ripples look like ordinary error. From out here, with the transponder half-spoofed and traffic thinking I am a transport three systems away, I can redraw someone's life with a few corrections. Most of the time I tell myself they needed it. That farmer in Freestar space who kept voting for the same governors while signing every predatory contract they suggested needed to learn what it felt like when the scales finally tipped their way. So I let the foreclosure go through, then reversed it just long enough to watch who they begged, who they blamed, who they turned on.

I used to lie awake after those edits, replaying faces in my head, wondering if the "acceptable loss" lines on my reports were murdering real people. Khepri-3 burned that question out of me. After you have watched an entire agri bloc fail in slow motion while executives argue over phrasing, it is hard to care about bruises when you are the one finally swinging. I still tell myself I am teaching lessons, forcing people and factions to feel what they have been doing on autopilot. A softened bounty here, a vanished debt there, a redirected shipment that leaves a smuggler bankrupt and a clinic secretly stocked. Guidance, I call it. Showing them where the lines really are.

Truth is, the part of me that flinched is quiet now. I notice it mostly by its absence. When did that happen? Was it when I zeroed out that friend's bill at Reliant Med and realized no one would ever thank me because they would never know? Or when I falsified a bounty on a Khepri-3 survivor and watched the relief in their eyes while some other poor bastard took the heat? Somewhere between those two keystrokes, "harm" turned into "adjustment" in my head.

So I keep moving the skiff, keeping just enough off the charts that the survey nodes flag me as noise. I have a lifeboat waiting out there, a quiet homestead on someone's LIST docket, with clean papers slowly accumulating like honest snow. Maybe one day I will step into that life and pretend the ledgers never knew my name. Until then, I sit in this humming tin can, tracing numbers on the console edge with my thumb, watching hunters chase ghosts through records I have already rewritten, and telling myself that if I did not do it, someone worse would.
zh:
有些夜里，这艘小船的嗡鸣听起来像自由星系联盟的风里一根老树枝的呻吟。我闭上眼，就回到那座农场，听着我父亲咒骂天空，因为定居星系群另一头的贷款委员会认定我们的收成"太过波动"。就是那时我学会了第一条规则：数字就是掐在你看不见的喉咙上的手。那时，它让人疼。如今我成了把手指按在账簿上的人，我不确定疼痛是什么时候不再是个问题的。

猎人们会以为我逃到这里是为了躲藏。那只是对了一半。这艘小船给我与新亚特兰蒂斯和霓虹城拉开距离，足够的延迟，让我在拨动一份逮捕令或掐断一条信用额度时，涟漪看起来像普通的错误。从这里，在应答器半伪造、交通以为我在三个星系之外的情况下，我能用几处修正重画一个人的生活。大多数时候我告诉自己他们需要这个。自由星系联盟太空里那个农民，一边为每一次掠夺性合同签字、一边反复投同一个总督的票，需要尝尝天平终于朝他们倾斜时是什么感觉。所以我让那次查封通过，然后又把它反转得刚好够看清他们去求谁、怪谁、转而对付谁。

那些改动之后，我以前会躺着睡不着，在脑子里重放那些面孔，想我报告上"可接受损失"那些行是不是在谋杀真的人。凯普利-3把那问题从我身上烧掉了。当你看过整个农业区在慢动作里崩塌、而高管们还在为措辞争论之后，轮到你来挥舞时，你就很难再去在意什么淤青了。我仍告诉自己我在教课，逼人和派系去感受他们一直自动驾驶着在做的事。这里软化一份悬赏，那里让一笔债务消失，一次被改道的货运让一个走私贩破产、让一家诊所悄悄备满货。我管它叫引导。给他们看线真正在哪里。

事实是，我身上会畏缩的那部分现在安静了。我主要靠它的缺席注意到它。那是什么时候发生的？是在我把一个朋友在信实医疗的账单清零、意识到没人会谢我因为他们永远不会知道的时候？还是在我伪造了一份针对凯普利-3幸存者的悬赏、看着他们眼里的宽慰、同时另一个可怜鬼背了锅的时候？在那两次按键之间的某处，"伤害"在我脑子里变成了"调整"。

所以我不断挪动这艘小船，刚好保持在地图之外，让勘测节点把我标成噪声。我在外面留了一艘救生艇，一处别人独立盟档案上的安静农家院，干净的证件像诚实的雪一样慢慢累积。也许有一天我会走进那种生活，假装账簿从不知道我的名字。在那之前，我坐在这只嗡嗡响的铁罐里，用拇指在控制台边缘描数字，看着猎人们在已经由我改写的记录里追鬼，并告诉自己，要是我不做，更糟的人会做。

#en:
I should probably stop writing these, but thinking in my own head is louder than any trace they can run. So if someone is intercepting this, congratulations, you are about to read the inside of a bad idea.

I did not run because I hurt people. I ran because I would not let someone else hold the off switch to their bodies. Strange how that looks the same on paper. You flip a routine from "lock" to "unlock," side effects ripple, someone loses sleep or sanity, and suddenly the woman who refused to build a leash code is the monster. Ship of Theseus in meat form: if you replace damaged parts with better ones, how many upgrades before they say you are not a person anymore, just a weapon? If you refuse to add their control fork, are you saving lives or sabotaging the system that feeds them? Ask three philosophers, get four answers and a requisition form.

The bionics facility was chosen for me long before I came here. I helped design some of its scaffolds back when my badge still opened the good doors. It is old, out of rotation, full of hardware no one audits anymore, and wired in the dialect my hands remember better than my own handwriting. A perfect place for ghosts to work. Out here I can tune the mesh without a dozen directors breathing down my neck, can test failure modes on synthetic loops instead of live minds. That is the plan, anyway, written as cleanly as I dare. The dirtier version stays in my head.

I used to think kindness was a universal solvent. Back in Neon, I comped a neuro-tune for a discharged soldier who could not stop shaking. No papers, no questions, just a steadying of his pain regulators and a free cup of terrible coffee. Two weeks later his "friend" showed up with four more broken men and a quiet threat about what might happen if I stopped helping. That was the day I realized kindness is just another interface someone can exploit if you do not harden it. I still help, but now I count exits, triangulate signals, and seed kill-switches into my own work in case one of mine turns on the rest.

If this log ever sees daylight, the nice, simple summary will be that I am dangerous. Of course they say that. If you build a lattice that lets people step outside their assigned tolerances, every institution that profits from those limits will panic. They do not fear me because I cut people open. They fear me because I close a hand around the same control they thought only they were allowed to touch.

I am keeping this vague, leaving out nodes and coordinates, because I can feel the net getting tighter. Too many Ryujin eyes sniffing around old tickets, too many UC ghosts whispering about "firmware drift." Maybe someone has already traced the distortions back here. Maybe they are reading this in a briefing room, under good lighting and bad coffee, nodding while they plan how to put my code back in a cage. If so, enjoy the paradox: to catch me, you have to admit I was right about how fragile your control always was.
zh:
我大概该停止写这些了，可在我自己脑子里想比他们能跑的任何痕迹都吵。所以要是有人在截获这个，恭喜，你即将读到一桩糟糕念头的内部。

我逃走不是因为我伤害了人。我逃走是因为我不肯让别人握住他们身体的开关。奇怪的是，那在纸面上看起来一样。你把一个程序从"锁定"改成"解锁"，副作用扩散，有人失去睡眠或理智，忽然那个拒绝写牵绳代码的女人就成了怪物。肉身的忒修斯之船：你若用更好的部件替换受损部分，多少次升级之后他们就会说你不再是一个人，只是一件武器？你若拒绝加入他们的控制分叉，你是在救人，还是在破坏那个喂养他们的系统？问三个哲学家，得到四个答案和一张请购单。

那座仿生学设施早在我来之前就为我选好了。我的徽章还能打开好门的时候，我帮着设计过它的一些脚手架。它老旧、已停用，满是没人再审计的硬件，用我双手比我自己笔迹还熟悉的方言接线。鬼干活的完美场所。在这外面，我能调校那张网，不必有一打主管盯着我的脖子，能在合成回路上而不是活人的头脑上测试失效模式。至少计划是这样，写得像我能写的那么干净。更脏的版本留在我脑子里。

我以前以为善意是万能溶剂。回到霓虹城，我给一个停不下来发抖的退伍兵免费做了次神经调校。没有文书，没有提问，只是给他调稳疼痛调节器，外加一杯难喝得离谱的免费咖啡。两周后，他的"朋友"带着四个更破碎的人出现，外加一句关于要是我停止帮忙会怎样的安静威胁。那天我明白，善意只是另一个接口，只要你不把它硬化，别人就能利用。我仍然帮忙，可如今我数出口、三角定位信号，并在自己的作品里埋下杀开关，以防我的人中有一个转而对付其余的。

要是这份日志有朝一日见了天日，那个好听、简单的总结会是：我很危险。他们当然会这么说。要是你搭起一张让人们走出他们被分配容差的网，每一个靠那些限制获利的机构都会惊慌。他们怕我不是因为我把人切开。他们怕我是因为我把手合在了同一个他们以为只有自己才被允许触碰的控制上。

我把这个写得含糊，省掉节点和坐标，因为我能感觉到那张网正在收紧。太多龙神的眼睛在旧工单周围嗅探，太多联殖的鬼在低声说着"固件漂移"。也许有人已经沿着畸变追回了这里。也许他们正在一间简报室里读这个，在好灯光和坏咖啡底下，一边点头一边计划怎么把我的代码关回笼子。要是这样，享受这个悖论吧：要抓住我，你就得承认我关于你那套控制一直有多脆弱，是对的。

#en:
I keep telling myself this is temporary, that I am only using these ruins until the trail cools, but I keep coming back to the same corridors. The freighter captain who dropped me here is gone, the patrol routes have shifted, and still I walk the same length of wall where the paint changes from Freestar blue to bare metal. I know how many steps between the old infirmary and the records room. I know where the dust does not settle.

I fled because the numbers stopped being abstractions. One order on a console outside Akila, one line in a report, and half a ward went from screaming to "nonessential." After that day, every casualty log felt like a knife in my hand. It was too easy to move a name from one column to another. Too easy to see how the right lie could save someone who was never meant to be saved, or erase someone command wanted forgotten.

This place made sense because everyone already decided it was finished. Freestar and UC both stamped it as cleared, which means no one wants to come back and admit they miscounted the dead. A scavenger crew comes through now and then, prying up plates, but they do not look at the consoles. They do not smell the old Antiseptic under the dust. They certainly do not recognize my handwriting buried in the archived rosters.

I have a small routine now. TerraBrew boiled on a field stove until it tastes like metal. Tools laid out in the same order every time. Medbag checked, rechecked, counted until my fingers ache. When someone finds me and needs to disappear, I sit them under the same flickering light and listen to their story. Then I decide which ledger they belong in and which they are ready to leave behind.

Some nights I think about the stupid things I used to want. I remember sitting on the edge of a bunk dreaming about buying a little place in Akila, repainting the walls something not regulation, learning to play an old string instrument my mother used to talk about. Harmless wishes, soft as gauze. I would not know what to do with a quiet room now. I would tear it apart looking for exit routes and hidden records.

People talk about redemption like it is a med you earn after enough pain, a way back to who you were before. I used to believe in that. I do not anymore, and it scares me how little I miss the idea. If someone offered me a clean file, a cleared conscience, I would not take it. I am more afraid of being forgiven than I am of being hunted. Forgiveness means putting the knife down. I have spent too long learning exactly where to cut.

So I stay here, in the gaps between what the war recorded and what actually bled into the dirt. I know they are closing in; the questions at Gagarin, the whispers in New Atlantis, the wrong people suddenly interested in old rosters. When they arrive, they will see a medic in an old barracks and think the story ends here. They will not realize this is only one of the places I chose to finish what everyone else started and walked away from.
zh:
我一直告诉自己这是暂时的，我只是用这些废墟，直到痕迹冷却，可我总回到同样的走廊。那艘把我送到这里的货船船长走了，巡逻路线变了，而我仍走同一段墙——那里的漆从自由星系联盟的蓝变成裸露的金属。我知道从旧医务室到档案室之间有多少步。我知道哪里灰尘落不下来。

我逃走，是因为那些数字不再是抽象的。阿基拉城外某台控制台上的一道命令、报告里的一行，半个病区就从尖叫变成了"非必要"。那天之后，每一份伤亡日志都像一把握在我手里的刀。把一个名字从一栏挪到另一栏太容易了。太容易看清一个恰当的谎言能救下一个本不该被救的人，或者抹掉一个指挥部想忘掉的人。

这地方说得通，因为所有人都已认定它完了。自由星系联盟和联殖都盖章说它已清理，这意味着没人愿意回来承认自己数错了死者。偶尔有拾荒队伍经过，撬起一块块板，可他们不看控制台。他们闻不到灰尘底下旧消毒剂的味道。他们当然也认不出埋在归档名册里我的笔迹。

我现在有一点小日常。用野战炉把地球酿酒煮到尝起来像金属。工具每次按同样的顺序摆好。医疗包检查、再检查、数到手指发酸。当有人找到我、需要消失时，我让他们坐在同一盏闪烁的灯下，听他们的故事。然后我决定他们该属于哪本账簿、又准备好放下哪一本。

有些夜里我会想起我过去想要的那些蠢东西。我记得坐在铺位边缘，梦想在阿基拉买个小地方，把墙漆成非制式的颜色，学会弹一种我母亲说起过的老弦乐器。无害的愿望，柔软如纱布。如今我不知道拿一间安静的房间该怎么办。我会把它拆开来找逃生路线和隐藏记录。

人们谈救赎，像它是一剂你在受够痛苦后挣得的药，一条回到从前那个你的路。我以前信那个。如今不信了，而我不太怀念这个念头——这让我害怕。要是有人给我一份干净的档案、一个清白的良心，我不会要。比起被追猎，我更怕被宽恕。宽恕意味着把刀放下。我花了太久，才学会该往哪里下刀。

所以我留在这里，在战争记录与实际渗进泥土之间的缝隙里。我知道他们正在逼近；加加林的那些提问、新亚特兰蒂斯的低语、忽然对旧名册感兴趣的不该感兴趣的人。等他们到时，他们会看到一个老兵营里的军医，以为故事到此为止。他们不会意识到，这只是我选择去把别人开了头又走开的事做完的众多地方之一。

#en:
Did a sweep of the docks with Rico and Darren tonight, same as always. Cargo comes in, creds go out, Cerberus gets its cut. The routine should feel solid by now, but my hands still shake when I light a smoke afterward. Darren laughs it off, says the tremor just means my nerves are "tuned for survival." Easy for him to say. His conscience doesn't wake him up at 0300 replaying every poor bastard we've leaned on until they signed or snapped.

Marla pulled me aside before the run, said the boss wants us "cleaner," less public mess, more quiet leverage. That means more talking, less shooting, and I am supposed to be good at that. Problem is, talking in this life mostly means lying to someone's face while you measure how much pain it will take to change their mind. I tried soft words with the spacer crew we shook down at Bay 4, told them I was sorry we had to search their crates, sorry about the delays, sorry this "wasn't personal." They looked at me like I was the one holding the gun, even though it was Rico standing behind them with his finger on the trigger. I still heard myself apologizing for it all anyway.

It has been like that since I fell in with the Syndicate. First time we roughed up a shopkeeper who missed a payment, I apologized to him while Darren worked over his security drone with a wrench. Said we would "sort it out," said we "understood times were tough." Later I apologized to Rico after the boss chewed him out, like it was my fault the take was light. I even found myself mumbling sorry to Marla the night she had to put down that freelancer who pulled on us first. Everyone keeps telling me to own what I do, but all I seem to own is the blame for what everyone else chooses.

Heard some scuttle in the back room of the Den about a red-haired doc working the underbelly clinics, someone who can crack implants and pain wiring like she is rewiring a grav drive. Darren says she can flip a man's nerve endings inside out, shut him down at a distance if she ever touched his augments. Others say she is patching up people we leave broken, giving them another shot at life we thought we took. No one knows if she is on our side, the Corps, or nobody's. Rico jokes that if we ever cross someone like that, I will be the first to say sorry while she fries our heads.

Sometimes I wonder if that is what I am really apologizing for: not the beatings or the threats, but the fact that I keep going back out there anyway. Every time the boss hands me a new list of names, I nod, say I understand, then catch myself telling the targets it is all just business, that I wish it could be different. Tonight, coming back through the rain-slick alleys, Marla asked me why I keep doing that. I told her I do not know, but that is a lie. I keep apologizing because it feels like the only part of this that is still mine. But the more I say it for things that were never really my fault, the more it sounds hollow, like I am rehearsing for the day it finally is.
zh:
今晚和里科、达伦一起扫了遍码头，跟往常一样。货进来，信用币出去，刻耳柏洛斯拿它那份。这套例行如今本该感觉扎实了，可我点完烟手还是会抖。达伦一笑带过，说那点颤抖只说明我的神经"调校得适合生存"。他说得轻巧。他的良心不会在凌晨三点把他叫醒，重放我们压过的每一个可怜鬼，直到他们签字或崩溃。

玛拉在行动前把我拉到一边，说老板要我们"更干净"，别闹得太公开，多用安静的筹码。那意味着多说话、少开枪，而我本该擅长这个。问题是，在这行里，说话大多意味着当面撒谎，同时衡量要多少痛苦才能改变一个人的主意。我试着对我们在 4 号泊位勒索的那队太空人好言相劝，告诉他们说很抱歉我得搜他们的箱子，抱歉延误，抱歉这"不是针对个人"。他们看着我的样子，像是我才是拿着枪的人，尽管站在他们身后、手指扣着扳机的是里科。可我还是听见自己在为这一切道歉。

自从我混进辛迪加以来就是这样。第一次我们揍一个没交上钱的店主时，我在达伦拿扳手砸他的安保无人机时向他道歉。说我们会"解决这事"，说我们"理解日子难过"。后来老板训了里科，我又向里科道歉，像那份抽成太少是我的错。我甚至发觉自己在玛拉那晚不得不撂倒那个先动手的自由职业者时，嘟囔着对她说抱歉。所有人都一直叫我要为自己做的事负责，可我能负责的，似乎只有别人选择做的那些事的责任。

在巢穴站后室听到些闲话，说有个红发医生在下层诊所里活动，一个能像重接重力驱动一样破解植入体和疼痛线路的人。达伦说她能把一个人的神经末梢翻个里外，只要她碰过他的义体，就能隔空让他停机。另一些人说她在补我们打碎的人，给他们我们以为夺走的另一次人生机会。没人知道她站在我们这边、企业那边，还是不站任何人那边。里科开玩笑说，要是哪天我们撞上那样一个人，我会是第一个在她烤焦我们脑子时说抱歉的。

有时我想，我真正在道歉的，是不是这个：不是那些殴打或威胁，而是我仍然一次次回到那里这个事实。每次老板递给我一份新名字清单，我点头，说我明白，然后又发觉自己在告诉目标这一切只是生意，我希望事情能不一样。今晚，在雨湿的巷子里往回走时，玛拉问我为什么老这样。我说我不知道，可那是谎话。我一直道歉，是因为那感觉像这件事里唯一还属于我的部分。可我为那些从来算不上我错的事说得越多，它听起来就越空洞，像我在为终有一天那真是我错的日子排练。

#en:
I lost track of dates a long time ago. Somewhere between HopeTown and the first time I heard my own name spoken like a curse in a Neon bar, the calendar stopped mattering. What I remember instead is the sounds ships make when they fail. Not the explosions; the little noises before that. The creak in a frame that was stress-rated wrong, the whine of a drive loaded past tolerance because some admin shaved a safety margin for profit. I spent half a life trying to keep crews alive inside other peoples bad math. Funny how fast they called it sabotage when I started correcting the ledger in ways they did not approve of.

People brand what I do as preying on the vulnerable. They are half right. Weakness exists to be used; that is how the strong survive. The thing they never say out loud is who made those people weak in the first place. A hauler captain who trusts a Deimos spec sheet more than her own instincts, a settler taking the cheapest contract because their kids are hungry, a green engineer told to sign off on a drive that hums wrong because schedules do not wait. I nudge those ships out of lanes that will kill them, or into quiet places where the right scrap can be harvested and the wrong paperwork can vanish. Survival, not charity. Survival for me most of all.

This new hiding place suits me. Old listening gear, blind spots baked into the patrol patterns, a whole ring of forgotten steel that still remembers every ship that ever whispered past. I can sit in the dark and trace the work of my own hands across the grid, decide which hulls deserve a second chance and which need to disappear before they take more lives with them. From out here, it is easy to tell myself I am fixing things.
