So far all I know is that analysts saw impossible approach curves in their feeds, then someone upstream ordered a cleanup, and the only reason any of it still exists is that past edits were lazy, leaving faint echoes of corridors that should not intersect where they do.
zh: 线索从这座安静的研究舱开始，是因为这里正是有人第一次试图抹掉她画下的线条却失败的地方。流经这些服务器的被盗航线工程并未消失，它的指纹抹在缓存的遥测、半擦除的备份，以及没人费心清除的错误日志上。若她在这里劫持了一条数据盗窃链，那么她躲开的模式与她创造的模式都擦过同一批系统，留下刚好足够的残迹，让有耐心的人重建出一个行进方向。目前为止我只知道，分析员在他们的数据流里看到了不可能的进近曲线，然后上游有人下令清理，而这一切还存在的唯一原因，是过去的编辑太懒，留下了那些本不该在彼处相交的走廊的淡淡回声。

#en: Cydonia's fringe is where the city's light thins and the dust takes over, a no-man's land of dead loaders, rusting refinery towers, and forgotten survey shacks humming with old UC telemetry. Out here Vector can splice herself into the traffic grid without too many eyes noticing when a lane bends the wrong way, and she has ringed the outskirts with portable beacons tuned to scramble every approach that relies on sanctioned charts. If she hard-burns her private atlas through those rigs, the Settled Systems inherit her routes without her, and nobody will ever agree whether that is justice or convenience. From the buried slate on that remote rock to the redacted files in New Atlantis and the orbital clue pried from an Ecliptic screen, every line has curved toward this pilot rewriting the map in her own image.
zh: 赛多尼亚的边缘，是城市灯光变稀薄、尘土接管一切的地方，一片由死掉的装载机、生锈的炼油塔，以及嗡鸣着旧联殖遥测的被遗忘勘探棚构成的无主之地。"向量"能在这里把自己接进交通网格，而不会在一条航道弯错方向时被太多眼睛注意到；她还在外围环布了便携信标，调校来扰乱每一次依赖获批星图的进近。若她通过那些设备把自己的私人地图硬烧出去，定居星系就会在没有她的情况下继承她的航线，而永远没人会就"那是正义还是便利"达成一致。从那块遥远岩石上被埋的数据板，到新亚特兰蒂斯城里的涂黑文件，再到从黄道佣兵团屏幕上撬出的轨道线索，每一条线都弯向这名按自己的模样改写星图的飞行员。

#en:
Gagarin Landing is all scaffolds and secondhand promises, a place where yesterday's industry was gutted and today's work happens in back rooms no one audits.  
If any station in the Settled Systems would quietly trial hardware built from skewed data, it would be this one, with its mix of desperate locals and cost-cutting offworld executives.  
Somewhere in these refurbished bays is the piece that proves Vector's math is not just theory, a system tuned to the same crooked pattern that keeps surfacing in wreck telemetry.  
So far all I have are fragments and ghost paperwork; a nameless slate from a forgotten outpost, misaligned jump traces off a crippled freighter, and a half-redacted log from an isolated agent, all pointing to ships dying the same strange way without a single clean record explaining why.
zh:
加加林着陆点满是脚手架与二手承诺，一个昨日工业被掏空、今日工作发生在无人审计的后室的地方。  
若说定居星系里有哪座星际站会悄悄试用由扭曲数据造出的硬件，那就是这一座——它混杂着绝望的当地人与削减成本的太空高管。  
在这些翻新的货舱里某处，是那件证明"向量"的数学不只是理论的零件：一套调校到与残骸遥测中不断浮现的同样歪斜模式的系统。  
目前为止，我只有碎片与幽灵文书：一块来自被遗忘前哨的无名数据板、一艘残废货船上错位的跃迁痕迹，以及一名孤立特工半涂黑的日志，全都指向船只以同样古怪的方式死去，却没有一份干净的记录解释原因。

#en: This lonely orbit has been a dumping ground for deferred problems for years, a quiet holding pattern where old refuel nodes, dead beacons, and forgotten contracts drift until someone remembers to clean the slate. That habit of leaving things circling, unresolved, made it the perfect anchor for a navigation construct designed to outlast memories and overwrite patrol charts in slow, invisible increments. Left intact, it keeps bending ships along the same narrow band of space, feeding Vector the predictable traffic she needs to stay ahead of every pursuit. Earlier, a stray dataslate in the black mentioned altered routes, and a gutted freighter's logs confirmed impossible course corrections; now, this orbital clue is where those stories start to intersect, pointing to a single hand quietly reshaping the lanes.
zh: 这条孤独的轨道多年来一直是延期问题的倾倒场，一个安静的滞留区——旧的补给节点、死掉的信标与被遗忘的合同在此漂着，直到有人想起要来清账。那种把东西留在轨道上、悬而不决的习惯，使它成了一座导航构造物的完美锚点；那座构造物设计来比记忆活得更久，并以缓慢、看不见的增量覆写巡逻星图。任其完好，它会继续把船只沿同一条狭窄的太空带掰弯，为"向量"提供她保持在每一次追击之前所需的可预测交通。早先，漆黑中一块散落数据板提到被改动的航线，一艘被掏空货船的日志证实了不可能的航向修正；如今，这个轨道线索正是那些故事开始交汇之处，指向一只悄悄重塑航道的单只手。

#en: The fragment of shattered drive housing drifts where no one ever meant it to matter, spinning lazily in a thin ring of junked metal and dead satellites; yet the telemetry echoing from its scorched casing ties together pressure lines, ship routes, and storm signatures that keep repeating in your files. Whatever calibration was once done here has been reused, repurposed, nudged a little further each time until this forgotten orbit became a quiet hinge between smugglers, old UC hardware, and an engineer who prefers to stand nowhere she was officially assigned. So far you have followed a trail from a lonely outpost in the dust, to a dead hunter's battered ship, to freight records in a rusting factory town and altered harvests on the frontier, each step shifting the pattern closer to this unseen axis in the sky.
zh: 那块碎裂的引擎外壳残片漂在没人曾想过它会要紧的地方，懒洋洋地旋转在一圈废旧金属与死卫星构成的细环里；可从它烧焦外壳中回荡出的遥测，却把不断在你的文件里重复的压力线、船只航线与风暴签名串在一起。这里曾经做过的无论什么校准都被重复利用、改作他用、每次都再推远一点，直到这条被遗忘的轨道成了走私者、旧联殖硬件，以及一名偏爱站在任何官方未曾指派给她之处的工程师之间一个安静的铰链。目前为止，你追着线索从尘土中一座孤独前哨，到一艘死掉猎人的破船，到一座锈蚀工厂镇的货运记录与边境上被改动的收成，每一步都把模式推得更靠近天空中这条看不见的轴。

#en: A husk like the FC-9470 Prairiefire is where bad habits go to calcify; a bounty cutter once meant for clean contracts and short-term holds, now adrift with its databanks still humming, auto-archiving side deals no one bothered to erase when the lights went out. If brokers were quietly hiring someone to bend storms around smuggling routes, this is where the first retainers would have been filed, a "temporary" workaround that became standard practice with every unreported payout. Strip those records out here and the pattern of who bought favorable weather, and where they needed it most, will finally start to show. Up to this point the trail has been fragments: a lonely stash in the dust, a wrecked hunter's half-burned log, and a frontier manifest full of shipments that somehow always sailed between the storms.
zh: 像"FC-9470 草原之火"这样的空壳，是坏习惯钙化之处；一艘赏金切割船，当初本是为干净合同与短期羁押而造，如今漂着，数据库仍在嗡鸣，自动归档着灯光熄灭时没人费心抹掉的私下交易。若掮客在悄悄雇人把风暴掰绕走私航线，这里就是最早的那批聘约被归档的地方，一种"临时"变通，随着每一笔未申报的付款变成了标准做法。在这里把这些记录剥出来，谁买了顺风天气、又最需要在哪里，这个模式终于会开始显形。到目前为止，这条线索都是碎片：尘土中一处孤独的藏匿点、一名失事猎人半烧毁的日志，以及一份满是"不知怎地总能在风暴之间航行"的货运的边境舱单。

#en: On this little cargo module clinging to a dead moon, ships only stop long enough to shed weight and disappear from questions, which makes it the one place where a nervous broker could hide records that never should have existed. The station hums with old generators and half-paid docking fees, a perfect limbo for manifests that list ships twice, captains who deny ever owning them, and routes that dead-end in empty space. Here, in the gaps between official ledgers, the pattern of a quiet auditor's hand might still be pieced together, if the fragments have not already been scrubbed. So far the trail is only a broken complaint slate from an abandoned shack and hangar gossip about underpriced hulls changing names too often, more rumor than record, with nothing yet that explains how the first ship was really taken.
zh: 在这座攀附在死卫星上的小货运舱里，船只只停留到刚好卸下重量、并从问询中消失，这让它成了某个紧张掮客唯一能藏起本不该存在之记录的地方。这座星际站因老旧发电机与付了一半的停泊费而嗡鸣，是舱单把船只列两次、船长否认曾拥有它们、航线在空荡太空中断头的完美悬置地。在这里、在官方账册之间的空隙里，一名安静审计员的手笔也许仍能被拼出来——如果那些碎片还没被擦掉。目前为止，这条线索只有一块来自废弃棚屋的损坏投诉数据板，以及机库闲话关于低价船壳换名太频的议论；传闻多于记录，还没有任何东西能解释第一艘船究竟是如何被拿走的。

#en: The signal only exists out here, in the thin static between worn orbital paths where no registry admits anything was ever parked. Whatever is broadcasting rides the same curve as old medical transports and unscheduled evac flights, too regular to be random, too quiet to be honest, as if some forgotten routing order is still echoing long after the war that birthed it was filed away. Scans disagree on how many relays are in the chain, timestamps smear across different campaigns, and every recovered log looks like it has been rewritten at least once by an uncredited hand.  \nSo far all we can pin down are fragments: a nameless cache on a backworld, a dead hulk whispering scrambled commands, a gutted UC frame with its history carved out, each pointing toward a medic who has never truly stepped off the triage line.
zh: 那道信号只存在于这里，存在于老旧轨道路径之间稀薄的静电里——任何登记册都不承认那里曾停放过任何东西。正在广播的东西与旧医疗运输船和未排期的撤离飞行走着同一条曲线，太规律不像随机，太安静不像诚实，仿佛某道被遗忘的航线路由命令在那场催生它的战争被归档很久之后仍在回响。扫描结果对这条链里有几座中继说法不一，时戳在不同战役之间糊成一片，而每一份被找回的日志都像是至少被一只未署名的手改写过一次。  \n目前为止我们能钉住的只有碎片：一穷乡星上一处无名储藏点、一具低声说着错乱指令的死残骸、一具历史被剜掉的被掏空联殖船架，每一处都指向一名从未真正走下分诊线的医疗兵。

#en: Neon Starport is the only place she could choose to finish this, a tangle of launch lanes and grav beacons where every route out of the city narrows to a handful of controlled vectors. Here, under the noise of freight traffic and tourist liners, she can hide one decisive burn inside the churn of a hundred departures, then vanish into the same anomaly that stole her squadron. UC watchers, Freestar eyes, and corporate ghosts all crowd the manifests, each waiting to see whether she escapes with what her implants remember or dies with those seconds still locked inside her skull. From a quiet corporate office you trailed erased flight plans and Ryujin drift data, then out in dead Vanguard metal you found proof that something was cut from the record; every line, every rumor, has bent you inexorably toward this dock.
zh: 霓虹城太空港是她唯一可能选择来完成此事的地方——一片由发射航道与引力信标构成的乱麻，城市每一条出港路线都收窄成少数几条受控向量。在这里，在货运交通与观光邮轮的噪声之下，她能把一次决定性的燃烧藏进上百次离港的搅动里，然后消失进那个夺走她中队的同一异常。联殖监视者、自由星系联盟的眼线，以及公司的幽灵全都挤在舱单里，各自等着看她究竟是带着她植入体记得的东西逃脱，还是带着那几秒仍锁在颅骨里死去。从一间安静的公司办公室起，你追过被抹除的飞行计划与龙神的漂移数据，然后在死掉的先锋队金属里你找到"记录中有东西被剪掉"的证据；每一条线、每一则传闻，都不可阻挡地把你推向这个船坞。

#en: Out here, the outpost sits half-forgotten above a nameless rock, humming just loud enough to pass for routine. If Torque cached the first drafts of his collapse doctrine anywhere, it would be in a place everyone thinks they already understand, where old logs roll by unchecked and no one bothers to ask why the stress models do not match the traffic. The techs who pass through argue in low voices about whether that waste ring failure years back was bad luck, bad metal, or something worse, but the talk always trails off when someone important walks in. So far I have a patchwork: a single remote station that recorded anomalous spin, a drifting cache in empty orbit crammed with tampered drive data, and a trail of "accidents" whose reports all disagree on the details but point, quietly, toward the same careful hand.
zh: 在这里，那座前哨半被遗忘地坐落在一颗无名岩石上方，嗡鸣得刚好够冒充例行公事。如果"扭矩"把他的坍缩学说最初草稿缓存在任何地方，那就会在一个所有人都以为自己已经了解的地方——旧日志不受检查地滚过，没人费心问为什么应力模型与交通对不上。路过的技师低声争论多年前那次废料环故障是霉运、坏金属、还是更糟的东西，可只要有大人物走进来，谈话总会散掉。目前为止，我有一块拼凑：一座记录了异常自旋的单独远程星际站、一处塞满被篡改引擎数据的空轨漂移储藏点，以及一连串"事故"——它们的报告在细节上全不一致，却都悄悄指向同一只谨慎的手。

#en: The Den is exactly the sort of place people forget about until they need something left off the books. UC colors on the bulkheads, Vanguard uniforms in the corridors, and a station assignment nobody fights for because nothing ever happens in this system, officially. That makes it perfect for burying the kind of paperwork that turns derelicts into ghosts and missing crews into accounting entries. Whatever someone locked away here was meant to sleep under layers of routine inspections and disinterest.  \n\nSo far it has been a string of accidents that felt like luck: a misfiled cache on a backworld rock, an offhand comment in a quiet bar, a pattern in drift data that did not match its story. One coincidence is chance. Three start to look like intent, all pointing toward a salvager who only exists in the margins.
zh: 巢穴站正是那种人们会忘记、直到他们需要某样不走账册的东西时才想起的地方。舱壁上是联殖的颜色，走廊里是先锋队的制服，还有一份没人争抢的星际站指派——因为按官方说法，这个星系从不出事。这让它成了埋葬那种"把弃船变成幽灵、把失踪船员变成会计条目"的文书的完美之地。有人锁在这里的任何东西，本都该在层层例行检查与漠不关心之下沉睡。  \n\n目前为止，它是一连串感觉像运气的意外：穷乡岩石上一处归档错误的储藏点、一家安静酒吧里的一句随口之言、一段与自身说法不符的漂移数据模式。一次巧合是偶然。三次就开始像有意为之，全都指向一名只存在于页边的打捞者。

#en: Down here, beneath Neon's gloss, the air tastes of metal and spilled Aurora, and every cable-strung corridor feels like part of a nervous system somebody rewired in a hurry. This is where off-the-books processors move through gloved hands, where nav code and storm data can be traded like street chems, and where a cautious engineer could hide the blueprint for disappearing between sensor gaps. If there is a pattern that can point the way to him, it lives in these jury-rigged stacks and smuggled thoughtware, not in any clean corporate tower. Out on that forgotten rock the first rumor surfaced; at the abandoned station, recordings cut off mid-sentence; by the time the stories reached the shadows of Neon, every retelling bent the same direction, as if the whole trail had always been sliding toward this underbelly.
zh: 在这下面、在霓虹城的亮面之下，空气尝起来有金属与洒出的极光味，每一条挂满线缆的走廊都像某个被人匆忙重接过神经系统的部位。这里正是账外处理器在戴手套的手之间流转、导航代码与风暴数据能像街头毒品一样被交易、一名谨慎工程师能藏起"在传感器空隙间消失"之蓝图的地方。若说有什么模式能指向他，它就活在这些勉强拼凑的机架与走私来的思维硬件里，而不在任何干净的公司塔楼里。在那块被遗忘的岩石上，第一则传闻浮出水面；在那座废弃星际站，录音在句子中间中断；等故事传到霓虹城的阴影里时，每一次重述都朝同一方向弯曲，仿佛整条线索一直滑向这个下腹。

#en: This forgotten Deimos scrapyard is where every missing shipment, every ghost-hauler rumor, finally stops being theory and becomes steel under your boots. The place is built for him: towers of gutted hulls wired into a single nervous system of chained drones, jury-rigged turrets, and cutter arms that only someone who lived their life in maintenance bays could truly command. From here he can vanish cargo, erase sensor echoes, and, if given a little more time, turn the surrounding trade lanes into a minefield of weaponized debris no traffic controller could ever untangle. The trail from that drifting tug in orbit to the grease-stained garage pointed the same way each time, through altered firmware and TS-? signatures, through dockside whispers about ghost salvage and workers getting quiet help from an unseen hand.
zh: 这座被遗忘的火卫二废料场，是每一笔失踪货运、每一则幽灵货船传闻终于不再是理论、而变成你靴下钢铁的地方。这地方是为他造的：一座座被掏空的船壳塔，接进由串联无人机、临时拼凑炮塔与切割臂构成的单一神经系统——只有一生都在维修舱里度过的人才真正指挥得动。从这里，他能让货物消失、抹掉传感器回声，若再多给一点时间，还能把周围的贸易航道变成一片交通控制员永远解不开的武器化残骸雷场。从轨道上那艘漂移拖船到那间油污斑斑的车库，线索每次都指向同一方向——穿过被改动的固件与 TS-? 签名，穿过码头边关于幽灵打捞与工人得到无形之手暗中帮助的低语。

#en: The Deserted Relay Station hangs in the dark like a forgotten nerve in a severed limb, still wired into the same grav-lane mesh Vector has been twisting for years. Its dishes are old enough to be ignored by modern traffic audits, yet vital enough that any signal pushed through here ripples across half a sector. This is where he has nested his final experiment, feeding stolen buoy keys and corrupted drift tables into a spine nobody bothered to decommission, preparing to bend routes until another convoy dies the way the first one did. Too many captains, too many clerks, saw the anomalies and filed them away as glitches. All I have so far are a burned buoy core in high orbit, packet ghosts from an abandoned listening post, and the same signature threaded through both, repeating like a warning nobody wanted to hear.
zh: 那座"被遗弃的中继站"像断肢上一根被遗忘的神经悬在黑暗中，仍接在"向量"多年来一直在扭动的同一张引力通道网上。它的天线盘老旧到足以被现代交通审计忽略，却又重要到任何从这里推送出去的信号都会在半个星区激起涟漪。这里就是他安放最后实验的地方：把偷来的浮标密钥与损坏的漂移表喂进一根没人费心退役的脊柱，准备掰弯航线，直到又一支车队像第一支那样死去。太多船长、太多文书看见了那些异常，却把它们当作小故障归档了事。目前为止，我只有高轨道上一枚烧毁的浮标核心、一座废弃听音哨发出的封包幽灵，以及贯穿两者的同一签名，反复着像一则没人想听的警告。

#en: The sealed monitoring pod sits deep under rock and old fear, a place built for people who watch patterns for a living and then pretend nothing is wrong. Down here, the air tastes of stale power and rerouted protocols, all those quiet updates and altered schedules that slipped in over years while no one with rank bothered to ask why. Whatever is buried in these records is where the cartographer first brushed up against someone the UC was not supposed to be running, and where their routines began to bend together.  \n\nSo far, the trail goes from a forgotten cache in the back end of nowhere to this analyst's hideaway full of half-erased telemetry, and now to a classified file that mentions the same name and an unnamed companion in the same breath, just before ship movements started to drift off their expected lines.
zh: 那座密封监控舱深埋在岩石与旧日的恐惧之下，一个为那些以观察模式为生、然后又假装一切无事的人而建的地方。在这下面，空气尝起来像陈旧的电力与被改道的协议，所有那些多年来溜进来的安静更新与改动日程，而没有一个有官阶的人费心问过为什么。埋在这些记录里的，是那位制图师第一次撞上某个联殖本不该在运作的人的地方，也是他们的例程开始彼此弯折的地方。  \n\n目前为止，这条线索从天涯之外一处被遗忘的储藏点，到这个塞满半擦除遥测的分析员藏身处，如今又到一份机密文件——它把同一个名字与一个无名同伴放在同一个呼吸里提起，就在船只活动开始偏离预期航线之前不久。

#en: Whatever the truth of the story, this is where it started to grow legs. The old recon hide still squats above a dead valley, half its arrays stripped, but the hardened recorders inside were built to see what no one was supposed to talk about. UC overwatch once watched this region for smugglers and deserters; now the only thing worth trusting is what those lenses caught when a certain navigator slipped their net. If there is any unedited glimpse of how he moves through the dark, it will be buried in this bunker. So far the trail runs from a forgotten rock with a corrupted slate, to falsified cargo logs on a wandering freighter, to war-era simulations that do not match their own summaries and every retelling in bars and briefing rooms points back to one quiet mathematician whose paths keep intersecting missing ships.
zh: 无论这故事真相如何，这里正是它开始长出腿的地方。那座旧侦察掩体仍蹲在一道死谷上方，半数阵列被剥走，可里面加固的记录仪本就是为记录没人该谈论的东西而造。联殖监视队曾在此注视走私者与逃兵；如今唯一值得信任的，是当某位领航员溜过他们的网时那些镜片捕捉到的东西。若说关于他如何在黑暗中移动还有任何未经剪辑的一瞥，它就会埋在这座掩体里。目前为止，线索从一块带着损坏数据板的被遗忘岩石，到一艘漂游货船上被伪造的货运日志，再到与自身摘要都不符的战时模拟，而酒吧与简报室里的每一次重述都指回一名安静的数学家——他的路径不断与失踪的船只相交。

#en: This lonely orbital node hangs where nobody bothers to look anymore, a forgotten cog in an old refinery network still dutifully sampling skies no one thinks to question. That is exactly why her fingerprints would linger here: spliced into legacy routines that kept running long after their operators rotated out, quietly folding her altered readings and storm tracks into every weather model downstream. Pulling the raw telemetry from this vantage is the only way to see which worlds her corrections keep bending toward, without the filters added later to hide them.  \nUp to now the trail has come from a nameless fringe tip, guarded files at a support post, and shipping records in Neon's shadows; together they suggest someone has been riding the same narrow band of routes, letting obsolete systems carry work no one officially remembers authorizing.
zh: 这座孤独的轨道节点悬在再没人费心去看的地方，一台被遗忘的齿轮，仍在一张旧炼油网络里尽职地采样着没人想着去质疑的天空。这正是她的指纹会留在这里的原因：接进那些在操作员轮岗之后仍继续运行的遗留程序，悄悄把她被改动的读数与风暴轨迹折进下游每一个天气模型。从这个视角拉取原始遥测，是看清她的修正不断朝哪些世界弯折的唯一办法——不用后来为了掩盖它们而加的过滤器。  \n目前为止，这条线索来自一条无名的边境线报、某座补给站里戒备的文件，以及霓虹城阴影中的航运记录；合在一起，它们暗示有人一直在同一条狭窄的航线上骑行，让作废的系统承载着没人正式记得批准过的工作。

#en: Out here, where a UC listening post once sifted whispers from the dark, only dead consoles and cold antennae remain, the perfect place to bury something meant to be half-forgotten. The Renegade Guard have taken to using the abandoned arrays as their own filter, catching and trimming any transmission that still dares to speak Catalyst's name, cutting and splicing casualty traffic until no one can say what really happened to the people she treated off the books. What survives is scattered across corrupted logs, half-burned debriefs, and field reports annotated in three different hands, none of them entirely honest. So far, the trail begins with a gutted courier loaded with misrouted chems and continues through a medical station's split routing codes, each fragment pointing toward a medic who keeps rewriting her own story in other people's blood.
zh: 在这里，在一座联殖听音哨曾从黑暗中筛出低语之处，只剩下死掉的控制台与冰冷的天线，是埋葬某种"注定要被半遗忘"之物的完美地点。"叛徒卫队"已习惯于把那些被弃置的阵列当作自己的过滤器，捕捉并剪切任何仍敢说出"催化剂"名字的传输，剪接伤亡播报，直到没人说得出她账外治疗过的人究竟遭遇了什么。存活下来的东西散落在损坏的日志、半烧毁的述职与三种不同笔迹批注的战地报告里，没有一份完全诚实。目前为止，这条线索始于一艘载着错投药剂的被掏空信使船，延续于一座医疗站被拆分的路由代码，每一块碎片都指向一名不断用别人的血重写自己故事的医疗兵。

#en: An abandoned farm is the one place his models were never meant to survive; here, no patrol routes or corporate scanners complicate the lines, only wind across empty plots and the echo of a life that should have been ordinary. Vector has chosen ground like this to run his last calculation, close enough to failing homesteads to hear what his numbers have done, far enough from New Atlantis and Neon that LIST, Argos, and UC analysts can still claim ignorance. Each misaligned landing pad, each stripped hab, has funneled him toward this quiet edge where he can erase the last proof of his manipulated routes or vanish into another statistical anomaly. The pattern behind these deaths is brutally straightforward, yet every dataslate, every hushed testimony from a spacer bar or a back table in the Well has somehow made that simplicity harder to pin down.
zh: 一座废弃农场，是他的模型本绝不该存活下来的地方；在这里，没有巡逻航线或公司扫描仪把线条搞复杂，只有吹过空荡地块的风与一段本该平凡之生的回声。"向量"选了这样的地面来跑他最后一次计算——离失败的农庄足够近、能听见他的数字都干了什么，又离新亚特兰蒂斯城与霓虹城足够远、让独立盟、阿戈斯与联殖分析员仍能声称不知情。每一块错位的停机坪、每一间被剥光的居所，都把他引向这道安静的边缘——在那里，他能抹掉自己操弄航线的最后证据，或消失进又一处统计异常。这些死亡背后的模式粗暴地直白，可每一块数据板、每一句来自太空劫匪酒吧或深井区后桌的低声证词，都莫名地让那种简单更难被钉住。

#en: HM-6310 drifts between beacons with its running lights dead, a Navy hull abandoned to slow tumble and the thin hiss of leaking atmosphere. Whatever was done to its comms was not an accident; relays cut clean, antenna feeds scorched, the kind of work that takes time and access codes, not raiders with bolt-cutters. If there is any trace left of when the ship went quietly dark, it will be in the records still trapped inside these bulkheads, not in the sanitized traffic summaries sitting on some desk in New Atlantis. The way the stories stack up, the blackouts did not start with explosions and screaming but with small adjustments to schedules, slight delays in escorts, a convoy reassigned here, a patrol pulled there, until ships like this ended up alone in the wrong lane at the wrong hour and no one could quite remember who signed which order when.
zh: HM-6310在信标之间漂着，航行灯熄灭，一艘被弃给缓慢翻滚与漏气舱壁细微嘶声的海军船壳。对它通讯所做的一切绝非意外：中继被干净切断、天线馈线被烧灼，那种需要时间和访问码、而不是拿着断线钳的掠夺者干的活。若说这艘船悄悄变黑的确切时刻还有任何痕迹，它就会在这具舱壁里仍被困住的记录中，而不是新亚特兰蒂斯城某张桌子上那些净化过的交通摘要里。故事这样堆叠起来看，那些黑障并非始于爆炸与尖叫，而是始于日程的小改动、护航的轻微延误、一支车队被调到这里、一支巡逻队被抽到那里，直到像这样的船在错误的时间、错误的航道上落单，而没人说得清谁在何时签了哪道命令。

#en: The Deimos yard is where old hulls come to be argued over, both in scrap value and in stories people wish they had not heard. Whatever was spilled at that Vanguard hulk has leeched into the metal here, into the residue pooled in cracked tanks and forgotten drums. The ex-military crew watching over this place walk patrols like they are still on someone else's clock, swapping versions of the same operation under their breath: some say it was a clean strike, others mutter about civilian signatures and doctored logs, but every time someone gets too close to naming names, the conversation drifts back to pay and patrol rotations. So far the trail has run from a lonely rock with a discarded record, to this graveyard of Deimos steel, each step hinting that his route through the wreck fields is tied to whatever truth those soldiers refuse to say out loud.
zh: 火卫二场区，是旧船壳被拿来争论的地方——争论拆解价值，也争论人们但愿自己没听过的故事。在那具先锋队残骸上洒出的东西，已渗进这里的金属，渗进裂开的储罐与被遗忘的油桶里积下的残留。看守这地方的老兵船员巡逻得像仍在按别人的时钟走，低声交换着同一次行动的不同版本：有人说那是一次干净打击，另一些人嘟囔着平民签名与被动过手脚的日志，可每次有人太靠近点名的边缘，谈话就漂回薪水与巡逻轮值。目前为止，线索从一块带着被丢弃记录的孤独岩石，延伸到这片火卫二钢铁的墓地，每一步都暗示他穿越残骸场的路线，与那些士兵拒绝大声说出的真相系在一起。

#en: Whoever set this run up understood how the Settled Systems look past anything wearing Trade Authority colors; a courier like this drifts through customs and crosschecks without anyone asking what rides in its data spine. Out here, with power failing and registry tags flickering, the ship is finally honest about what it became a moving splice node between corporate vaults, UC traffic, and the shadow channels Synapse favors. The hull groans in the quiet, lights stuttering over consoles that once carried routine manifests and now hum with patterns meant to be forgotten, archived in motion so no world ever held them for long. Earlier, the trail began with a burned slate in the dust, then half spoken warnings in Neon's bright center; those hints all pointed to altered records, missing routes, and a single engineering signature threaded through it all.
zh: 布置这条航线的人明白，定居星系会如何无视任何披着贸易管理局颜色的东西；像这样的信使船漂过海关与交叉核查，没人会问它数据脊柱里载着什么。在这里，电力衰竭、登记标签闪烁，这艘船终于诚实地面对自己成了什么：公司金库、联殖交通与"突触"偏爱的阴影信道之间的一个移动接驳节点。船壳在寂静中呻吟，灯光在那些曾承载例行舱单、如今嗡鸣着注定被遗忘之模式的控制台上闪烁——它们在被运动中归档，好让任何世界都无法长期持有。早先，这条线索始于尘土里一块烧毁的数据板，然后是霓虹城明亮中心里半说出口的警告；那些暗示全都指向被改动的记录、失踪的航线，以及贯穿其中一道单一的工程签名。

#en: The orbital node hangs just outside the usual traffic lanes, a quiet watcher that only a shipbreaker or surveyor would think to ask for directions. Its telemetry buffers are cluttered with half corrected coordinates and aborted course updates, the kind of messy trail that forms when different pilots, different contracts, and different lies all tug a route a few degrees off in their own favor. Buried under those minor contradictions is the composite pattern that matters a repeating arc toward the same strip of dead space where his tugs always vanish, a path no one ever meant to reveal so clearly. Up to this point, the search has chased a forgotten dataslate, carved marks in a gutted yard, buried sensor echoes in an old bunker, and a hijacked service line in Gagarin Landing all hinting that his orbit around old wrecks is neither random nor solitary.
zh: 那座轨道节点悬在寻常航道之外，一个安静的观察者，只有拆船工或勘探员才会想到向它问路。它的遥测缓冲区塞满半修正的坐标与中断的航向更新，那种当不同飞行员、不同合同与不同谎言各自把一条航线朝自己有利的方向拽偏几度时形成的凌乱痕迹。埋在这些细微矛盾下的，是那个要紧的复合模式：一段朝同一片他那些拖船总是消失的死寂太空重复弯去的弧线，一条没人曾打算透露得如此清楚的路径。到目前为止，搜寻追过一块被遗忘的数据板、被掏空场区里刻下的标记、一座旧掩体里埋着的传感器回声，以及加加林着陆点一条被劫持的服务线，全都暗示他绕着旧残骸的轨道既非随机、也非独行。

#en: Out on this forgotten pad, the robotics sheds are just shells, walls stripped for scrap and gantries hanging like broken ribs, but the acoustics are perfect for catching what should not be there. The crews working this place are grave-robbers of metal and code both, and they have staked their claim on whatever fragment of the emergency grid washed up here. If anything survived the purge of official logs, if any trace of her hand bled into test rigs or maintenance drones, it will be buried under their haul and their guns. The Claim Jumpers guard it not because they understand it, but because someone paid well to make sure it never leaves this dustbowl intact. So far all anyone really has are pieces: a scorched slate by a dead beacon, rumors of hijacked rescue calls, and a quiet pattern in UC telemetry that keeps circling the same missing architect.
zh: 在这片被遗忘的停机坪上，那些机器人棚屋只是空壳，墙壁被剥去当废料，龙门架像断肋骨一样垂着，可这里的声学特性完美适合捕捉不该存在的东西。在这地方干活的队伍既是金属的盗墓者，也是代码的盗墓者，他们已对冲到这里的任何应急网格碎片宣誓主权。若有什么在官方日志的清除中存活下来，若说她的手有任何痕迹渗进测试设备或维护无人机，它就会埋在他们的收获与枪口之下。抢矿队守着它，不是因为他们懂它，而是因为有人花了大价钱确保它永远不会完好地离开这个尘暴窝。目前为止，所有人真正拥有的都只是碎片：一座死信标旁烧焦的数据板、关于被劫持救援呼叫的传闻，以及联殖遥测里不断绕着同一名失踪设计师打转的安静模式。

#en: This maintenance garage matters because it is where the wrong kind of questions have been asked for too long, and the answers were written into metal instead of reports. Someone has been gutting old tugs and drones here, rebuilding them to run off-pattern, siphoning diagnostics and traffic data through a single buried core no official auditor ever signed off on. The Bloodied Phalanx watch the floor with veteran stillness, the kind you learn in briefing rooms where opinions stop one sentence short of insubordination; they have the look of people who were told once too often that curiosity was a liability. Crates marked for routine refit hide navigation slates and jump sequences, the same signature you first saw on the derelict in orbit and again in altered work logs, all pointing toward a single engineer who turned lane safety into a personal weapon.
zh: 这间维修车库之所以要紧，是因为这里太久以来一直在问错误的问题，而答案被写进了金属而不是报告。有人一直在把旧拖船与无人机掏空、重造来反常运行，把诊断与交通数据通过一个无人正式批准的埋藏核心抽取出去。血染方阵以老兵的沉静看着场地，那种在"意见之差一句就是抗命"的简报室里学来的沉静；他们一副被反复告知"好奇心是负担"的样子。标记为例行翻新的箱子里藏着导航数据板与跃迁序列，正是你第一次在轨道弃船上、然后又在被改动的工作日志里见过的那道签名，全都指向同一名把航道安全变成私人武器的工程师。

#en: The beacon is buried in an asteroid field the charts treat as background noise, a scattering of rock and old test debris where signal reflections knot together into something that only a pilot like her would trust. If she is splicing new corridors off the bones of a weapons range, then this is where the geometry first gets bent, where her numbers and the navy's old scars overlap in ways no official lane will ever admit. Locking onto this transmitter means choosing to believe the uglier version of the story, the one where someone has been stitching shortcuts through places that were never meant for traffic. Up to now, all you have are telemetry fragments from that quiet corporate post and a pirate relay full of half-decoded calls; every retelling of how she flies and what she wants has come secondhand, changing slightly with each mouth that repeats it.
zh: 那座信标埋在一片被星图当作背景噪声的小行星带里，一片散布的岩石与旧测试残骸，信号反射在此打结，变成只有像她那样的飞行员才会信任的东西。若她在从一座武器靶场的骨架上拼接新走廊，那么这里就是几何第一次被掰弯的地方，是她的数字与海军旧伤疤以任何官方航道都不肯承认的方式重叠之处。锁定这台发射机，意味着选择相信这个故事更丑的版本——那个有人一直在把捷径缝进从未打算让交通经过之处的版本。目前为止，你只有来自那座安静公司据点的遥测碎片，以及一座塞满半解码呼叫的走私者中继；关于她如何飞行、想要什么的每一次转述都是二手的，每换一张嘴就稍有变化。

#en: The moonside cargo relay hangs low over bare stone, a hollow bone in orbit, its traffic feeds choked with half-sanitized routes and anonymous handoffs that never appear on official charts. This is where smugglers and brokers reconcile the numbers no one wants audited, where manipulated beacons and missing freight quietly resolve into profit, and where the paths Gravline has been carving through emergency lanes finally take on shape. Buried in its local records is the pattern of his movements, a thread only someone with his training would think to weave through rescue corridors and claim cycles, and someone here clearly started tracing it before going dark midstream. All we have so far is a dead beacon shack on a forgotten rock, corrupted diagnostics from an automated plant, and a set of partial manifests tying his accidents to very deliberate payouts.
zh: 那座卫星侧货运中继低悬在赤裸岩石之上，一根轨道上的空心骨，它的交通数据流塞满半清理的航线与从不现身官方星图的匿名交接。这里正是走私者与掮客核对没人想被审计之数字的地方，是被人动手脚的信标与失踪货运悄悄化作利润的地方，也是"重力线"一直在应急航道上凿出的路径终于成形的地方。埋在它本地记录里的，是他动向的模式——一根只有受过他那种训练的人才会想到穿进救援走廊与索赔周期里的线，而这里有个人显然在追查它、追到一半就消失了。目前为止我们只有：一块被遗忘岩石上一座死掉的信标棚屋、一座自动化工厂里损坏的诊断，以及一组把他的事故与非常刻意的赔付系在一起的部分舱单。

#en: Down here the air tastes of rusted brine and old power surges, the whole underbelly humming like a grav-drive on the edge of misjump. This is where Vector would come to ground his equations, buried under neon and secrecy, splicing himself into forgotten relay trunks while gangs and corporate fixers look the other way. The maze of conduits and flooded service halls gives him proximity to the traffic he has been bending for years, and enough noise to hide the last adjustments he needs to turn Neon's lanes into another "corrected" knot in his invisible map. Freighters diverted at impossible angles, corrupted buoys around distant homesteads, half-erased telemetry from dead UC ships, and a data-runner's quiet confession beneath the city all point the same way: someone has been rewriting routes, and no one wants to admit how long the pattern has been there.
zh: 在这下面，空气尝起来像锈蚀的盐卤与旧日的电力浪涌，整个下腹嗡鸣得像一台正处在错跳边缘的引力引擎。这里正是"向量"会来落地他那些方程的地方——埋在霓虹与隐秘之下，把自己接进被遗忘的中继干线，而帮派与公司掮客都转开视线。导管与淹水服务厅构成的迷宫让他贴近自己多年来一直在掰弯的交通，也有足够噪声藏起他最后几处调整——他需要它们把霓虹城的航道变成他那张隐形地图上又一个"修正过的"结。以不可能角度被改道的货船、遥远农庄周围损坏的浮标、死掉联殖船只的半擦除遥测，以及城市下方一名数据跑腿的安静自白，全都指向同一方向：有人在改写航线，而没人愿意承认这个模式存在了多久。

#en: On the surface this bunker should be dead, just another relic the UC forgot to decommission properly, yet the walls still thrum with low-duty cycles no one logged and antennae still track a sky no one is supposed to be watching. Whatever legacy routines survived here have been quietly repurposed, turning this place into a blind mirror of the patrol grid she once helped design, catching echoes of ships that never appeared on official reports. If those echoes can be read, they will show how she has been slipping through restricted airspace, testing the same gaps her superiors once ordered her to ignore. So far the trail runs from a gutted robotics site rigged for clandestine upgrades to stolen atmospheric scans showing a single signature ghosting through secured lanes, all pointing back toward forgotten UC infrastructure where someone is still listening.
zh: 表面上，这座掩体本该是死的，不过是联殖忘了妥善退役的又一件遗物；可墙壁仍在以无人记录的低温占空比嗡鸣，天线仍在追踪一片没人该监视的天空。在这里幸存的任何遗留程序都被悄悄改作他用，把这地方变成她曾协助设计的那张巡逻网格的一面盲镜，捕捉着从未出现在官方报告里的船只回声。若那些回声能被读取，它们会显示她如何溜过受限空域，测试着她上级曾命令她忽略的同样那些空隙。目前为止，线索从一座被改装用于秘密升级的被掏空机器人场址，延伸到显示单一签名幽灵般穿过安全航道的被盗大气扫描，全都指回被遗忘的联殖基础设施——那里仍有人在聆听。

#en: Down here, beneath Neon's gloss and lightning, signals slip between dripping conduits and rusted catwalks where no official registry bothers to listen. This is where smugglers and failed technicians hide their experiments, where a nav-savant could bury something that talks to Grav Drives without ever tripping a corporate monitor. If there is a device bending lanes around patrol nets, its heartbeat will echo best in this tangle of forgotten relays and jury-rigged boosters, half-maintained by people who swear they saw "ghost jumps" flicker on backroom scanners while others laugh it off as Aurora paranoia. So far the trail has been a half-scrubbed slate on a lonely rock and guarded notes from a research team, all hinting at altered corridors, missing ships, and one vanished contractor whose fingerprints keep surfacing in the margins of other people's data.
zh: 在这下面、在霓虹城的亮面与闪电之下，信号溜进滴水的导管与锈蚀栈道之间，那里的任何官方登记册都懒得去听。这里正是走私者与失败技师藏起实验的地方，是一名导航天才能在不触发公司监控的情况下埋下某个"与引力引擎对话"之物的地方。若说有一台设备在把航道绕巡逻网掰弯，它的心跳会在这团被遗忘中继与临时拼凑升压器的乱麻里回响得最清楚——这些东西由那些发誓在后室扫描仪上见过"幽灵跃迁"闪烁、而另一些人一笑置之说是极光妄想症的人半打理着。目前为止，这条线索是一块孤独岩石上被半擦除的数据板，以及一支研究队伍里戒备的笔记，全都暗示着被改动的走廊、失踪的船只，以及一名消失的承包商——他的指纹不断在别人数据的页边浮现。

#en: The derelict hull drifting ahead once flew under UC colors, its silhouette as familiar to patrol charts as a commuter shuttle, and that is exactly why no one looked too closely when it went dark. A SysDef frame disappearing during a quiet operation is the sort of loss buried in routine, the kind of absence that lets a controller slip experiments into live traffic and blame the void when ships do not arrive. Whatever survived inside this carcass is a record of that comfort, of favors traded and anomalies waved through because the uniforms were the right shade. So far the trail runs from a forgotten dataslate on a remote rock to half-whispered rumors in Neon's upper terraces; now the missing logs and corrupted pings from this lost patrol hint that her hand has been inside military corridors as surely as civilian lanes, and none of them wanted to admit it.
zh: 前方漂着的那具弃船船壳曾挂着联殖的颜色飞行，它的轮廓对巡逻星图来说是通勤穿梭机般熟悉的，而这正是它在变黑时没人仔细看的原因。一具星防队的船架在一次安静行动中失踪，是那种被例行公事埋葬的损失，是那种能让调度员把实验溜进实时交通、并在船只未抵达时归咎于虚空的缺席。这具残骸里存活下来的任何东西，都是那份"安逸"的记录——记录了人情往来与被挥手放行的异常，只因为这些制服颜色对了。目前为止，线索从一块偏远岩石上被遗忘的数据板，延伸到霓虹城上层露台里半低语的传闻；如今，这支失踪巡逻队缺失的日志与损坏的脉冲暗示，她的手既伸进了民用航道，也肯定伸进了军用走廊，而没人愿意承认这一点。

#en: The Ranger outpost is where nervous stories go to be filed away and forgotten, unless someone bothers to read them like a weather map instead of a complaint list. Settlers passing through here talk about strange clouds and broken forecasts only in low voices, as if the wrong adjective might summon more trouble from the sky, and the liaison has been stitching those whispers together into something that looks uncomfortably like a pattern. Buried in those incident notes is the first honest record of where she has passed and how the air changed after she left.  \nSo far all I have is a vague tip from the fringe and a sense that official channels are pretending not to notice; this is the first place where people who actually watched the storms form have tried to put what they saw into words, then lowered their voices and hoped no one important was listening.
zh: 游骑兵前哨，是紧张的故事被归档并遗忘的地方——除非有人费心把它们当作天气图、而不是投诉清单来读。路过的定居者只低声谈论古怪的云与失灵的预报，仿佛用错一个形容词就会从天空招来更多麻烦；而那位联络官一直在把那些低语缝成某种看起来令人不安地像模式的东西。埋在那事件笔记里的，是她曾经过何处、以及她离开后空气如何变化的第一份诚实记录。  \n目前为止，我只有来自边境的一条模糊线报，以及一种官方信道正在假装没注意到的感觉；这是第一次，有真正看着风暴成形的人试图把他们所见写进文字，然后压低声音，希望没有要紧的人在听。

#en: The orbit here is cluttered with old traffic ghosts and discarded buoys, the kind of junk ring no one charts anymore because it is safer to give it wide berth. That is exactly why someone has been using it, stitching subtle course corrections into the noise so passing ships slide into one of two invisible lanes without ever knowing who guided them. The Crimson Fleet hull sitting watch on the edge of this debris is not here for charity; they are guarding a sliver of sky worth killing over, a tool that decides which convoys live, which vanish, and which storms arrive right on time. So far, the trail runs from a frozen lab full of twisted signals to a ranger's hut tracking twin scars in the dust, and now to a derelict Navy run that bent too close to shear, all touched by the same unseen hand before everyone involved drifted away, leaving the pattern behind.
zh: 这里的轨道塞满了旧交通幽灵与被丢弃的浮标，那种再没人测绘的垃圾环——因为它太危险，最好远远绕开。这正是有人一直在利用它的原因：把细微的航向修正缝进噪声里，让过往船只滑进两条隐形航道中的一条，而浑然不知是谁在引导。停在这片残骸边缘警戒的那具深红舰队船壳不是来做慈善的；他们守着一条值得为之杀人的天空缝隙，一件决定哪些车队活、哪些消失、哪些风暴准时抵达的工具。目前为止，线索从一座塞满扭曲信号的冰封实验室，到一座追踪尘土中两道平行伤疤的游骑兵小屋，再到一次弯得离剪切面过近的废弃海军航行，全都在所有相关者飘然离去、只留下模式之前，被同一只无形的手触碰过。

#en: Out here in thin orbit, away from ports and patrol routes, the only witnesses are dead satellites and the faint smear of exhaust on vacuum. This is where someone in a hurry would dump raw navigation work, splice it into an automated relay, and trust that nobody ever looks twice at telemetry meant for dust storms and refinery yield charts. The vectors she has been riding between storm-torn farms, old research shells, and fuel-rich rocks will only line up cleanly from this vantage, where gravity, magnetosphere, and flight paths can be seen in one sweep instead of scattered logs.  \nSo far the trail has run from a nameless backwater tip, to guarded files at a frontier post, to strange readings along a Helium-3 line, then into Neon's underlevel wiring and an abandoned raider chart; each step tighter, each rushed decision leaving a small, crooked mark behind.
zh: 在这里的稀薄轨道上，远离港口与巡逻航线，唯一的证人是死掉的卫星与真空上那抹淡淡的废气痕。这里正是一个匆忙的人会倾倒原始导航工作、把它接进自动化中继，并笃信没人会多看一眼那些本为沙尘暴与炼油产量图表准备的遥测的地方。她一直在风暴摧残的农场、旧研究空壳与富燃料岩石之间骑行的向量，只有从这个视角才能整齐对齐——在这里，引力、磁层与飞行路径能一次扫清，而不是散落在日志里。  \n目前为止，线索从一条无名穷乡线报，到某座边境哨所里戒备的文件，再到氦-3 航线沿线的古怪读数，然后钻进霓虹城下层的线路与一张废弃掠夺者星图；每一步都更紧，每一个匆忙的决定都留下一道小小的歪斜记号。

#en: Out here the sky is empty and the ground is nothing but scrub and wind, the kind of place freight captains and smugglers both use when they want their paperwork to quietly slip between jurisdictions. Whatever list was compiled here, it would have been built from a dozen minor favors and half-heard instructions, a route stitched together by dispatchers who misread storm warnings, handlers who rounded up coordinates, and pilots who logged their cargo under the wrong codes on purpose. That is why this backwater matters: it is where the little errors and quiet lies converge into a clear pattern of ships moving under engineered weather. So far the trail has run from a lonely stash in the dirt, to a bounty-hunter hulk with half its records burned out, to a derelict orbiting grid and a rusting company town whose harvests refuse to match their own climate models.
zh: 在这里，天空空空荡荡，地面只有灌木与风，货运船长与走私者想让自己文书悄悄在管辖缝隙间滑过时都会用的那种地方。无论在这里编成的是一份什么清单，它都会是由十几个小人情与半听来的指令搭成的航线，由误读风暴警告的调度员、把坐标凑整的经手人，以及故意用错误代码登记货物的飞行员缝在一起。正因如此，这片穷乡才要紧：正是在这里，小小的错误与安静的谎言汇聚成一种清晰的模式——船只在人造天气下行进。目前为止，线索从尘土中一处孤独的藏匿点，到一具记录被烧毁一半的赏金猎人残骸，再到一座废弃的轨道网格与一座丰收拒绝与自身气候模型相符的锈蚀公司镇。

#en: The beacon sits alone in high orbit, a pinprick of engineered light anchored where traffic lanes thin and patrol routes pretend not to notice. That makes this the only place a full map of those off-chart jumps could be stored without triggering alarms, and explains why a gunship like AR-1006 Warshade is babysitting empty space. Whatever pattern is encoded out here ties Navy vectors, missing freighters, and a freelance technician's wandering repairs into something more deliberate, the kind of truth that gets downgraded to "operational nuance" in briefings and quietly buried in classified archives. So far the trail runs from a forgotten slate in the dust, to jittering signals in an outpost shack, to a dead hauler with the wrong drive history, each clue delivered by people who chose their words very carefully once they understood what they were really seeing.
zh: 那座信标孤悬于高轨道，一点工程化的光，锚在航道变稀薄、巡逻路线假装没注意的地方。这让它成了唯一能存放那些偏图跃迁完整地图而不触发警报的地方，也解释了为什么像"AR-1006 战影"这样的炮舰在看护一片空荡太空。在这里编码的任何模式，都把海军向量、失踪货船与一名自由技师的漂泊维修系成某种更刻意的存在，那种在简报里被降级为"行动细节"、并被悄悄埋进机密档案的真相。目前为止，线索从尘土里一块被遗忘的数据板，到一座前哨棚屋里抖动的信号，再到一艘引擎履历不对的死掉货船，每一处线索都是由那些在明白自己真正看见的是什么之后、措辞极其谨慎的人交出的。

#en: The rocks here are thick enough to drown most signals and slow even a careful pilot, which is exactly why a man obsessed with broken orbits would hide his calculations among them; anything mapped out here was meant to be read only by those already fluent in wreckage and misalignment. The device tucked into this clutter listens to grav-wakes the way others listen to gossip, charting every ship nudged off course toward some unseen gathering point, and anyone who ever tried to talk about it in the open either fell quiet or disappeared from the flight rosters. So far the trail has given you a lonely dataslate on a backwater world, a dead relay full of mismatched pings, a gutted garrison with doctored beacons, and a deserted barracks whose logs all bent around the same engineer's careful hand, teaching everyone involved to keep their opinions carefully measured.
zh: 这里的岩石厚到足以淹没大部分信号、拖慢哪怕谨慎的飞行员，这正是为什么一个痴迷于破碎轨道的人会把他的计算藏在其间；在这里测绘出的任何东西，都只该被那些已经精通残骸与错位的人读懂。藏在这堆杂物里的设备聆听引力尾迹的方式，就像别人听闲话：标出每一艘被推离航线、朝某个看不见的聚集点驶去的船。任何曾试图公开谈论它的人，要么沉默了，要么从飞行名册上消失了。目前为止，这条线索给了你一穷乡世界上一块孤独的数据板、一座塞满对不上脉冲的死掉中继、一座带着被做手脚信标的被掏空驻军，以及一座日志全都绕同一名工程师谨慎之手弯折的废弃军营——教会了每一个相关的人把自己的意见小心拿捏。

#en: The Red Mile is the only place he can work without drawing questions about risk or missing runners; here, disappearances are entertainment, and grav anomalies can be folded into the legend of a brutal blood sport. Vector has wrapped himself in that noise, using the constant flux of contestants, wagers, and emergency medevacs to mask his last adjustment to the charts, one final attempt to bend the Silent Corridor into a predictable weapon. If he finishes here, every faction that ever touched his work gets a new way to make ships vanish and blame it on bad luck. The coincidences have stacked up until they no longer feel random: the corrupted dataslate in the wilderness, falsified manifests aboard a Trade Authority hauler, buried telemetry in an abandoned bunker, and clinical reports at the edge of legality all point to the same quiet hand reshaping the lanes.
zh: 红里是他唯一能在不引来"风险或失踪选手"追问的情况下工作的地方；在这里，失踪是娱乐，引力异常能被折进一项残酷血腥运动的传说里。"向量"把自己裹进那片噪声，利用选手、赌注与紧急医疗后送的持续流动，掩盖他对星图的最后一处调整——一次把"静默走廊"掰成可预测武器的最后尝试。若他在这里完工，每一个碰过他工作的派系都会得到一种让船只消失、并归咎于霉运的新办法。这些巧合已经堆叠到不再感觉随机：荒野中损坏的数据板、一艘贸易管理局货船上被伪造的舱单、某座废弃掩体里被埋的遥测，以及游走在合法边缘的临床报告，全都指向同一只重塑航道的安静之手。

#en: The Dogstar plant hangs in the dark like a forgotten bolt in a dead machine, conveyors idle, loader arms frozen mid-haul. This place was designed to store and sort mass for years without complaint, to hold cargo in tight orbits until someone somewhere needed it moved. Starline has turned that instinct into a weapon, nesting her prediction mesh in the factory's autonomous routines, letting them herd ships, drones, and data streams into holding patterns she alone can break. Here she is seconds from locking a whole sector's traffic in place, a test run for something far larger.  \n\nThe trail to this moment runs through a dead slate on a lonely rock, strange shipping shifts whispered over coffee in New Atlantis, a shaken family on a dusty yard still paying for a lost registry, and an orbital breadcrumb that proved her fingerprints were on every diverted route.
zh: 那座犬星工厂悬在黑暗中，像一台死掉机器里一颗被遗忘的螺栓，传送带闲置，装载臂僵在搬运中途。这地方的设计本是在多年内毫无怨言地储存与分拣质量，把货物保持在紧凑轨道上，直到某个地方的某个人需要它们移动。"星线"把那种本能变成了武器，把她的预测网格嵌进工厂的自主程序里，让它们把船只、无人机与数据流赶进只有她能打破的滞留模式。在这里，她离把整个星区的交通锁死只差几秒——一次为某个远更大之物做的试运行。  \n\n通往此刻的线索，穿过一块孤独岩石上的死数据板、新亚特兰蒂斯城咖啡桌旁低声议论的古怪航运变动、一座仍在为丢失登记册付出代价的积灰船坞上一户受惊的人家，以及一块证明她的指纹留在每一条被改道航线上的轨道面包屑。

#en: Out here, where the rock swallows every signal and the sky is just a thin crack overhead, the patterns finally have nowhere else to go; if he really wanted to end his work, he would choose a place that cannot drift, cannot burn up, cannot be quietly towed away. They say Vector picked this cave because the stone reminds him of armor plating, because he can carve his last equations straight into the walls and let the dust keep his secrets. Others mutter that UC and Deimos forced him planetside, flushing him out of his wreck-constellations until this was the only blind spot left between their sensors. Hard to tell what is true anymore: only that the first dataslate in that lonely backwater, the silent relay where echoes would not die, the gutted merc outpost, and the factory full of hijacked guidance code have all traced the same careful hand, drawing you here.
zh: 在这里，岩石吞掉每一个信号、头顶的天空只是薄薄一道裂缝，这些模式终于无处可去；若他真的想结束自己的工作，他会选一个不会漂移、不会烧毁、不会被悄悄拖走的地方。他们说"向量"选中这座洞窟，是因为石头让他想起装甲板，因为他能把最后的方程直接刻进岩壁、让尘土守住他的秘密。另一些人嘟囔说，是联殖与火卫二把他逼到了地面，把他从自己的残骸星座里冲出来，直到这里成了他们传感器之间仅剩的盲点。如今很难分辨什么是真的：只知道那座孤独穷乡里的第一块数据板、那座回声不肯死去的沉默中继、那座被掏空的佣兵据点，以及那座塞满被劫持制导代码的工厂，全都追着同一只谨慎的手，把你引到这里。

#en: This Deserted Relay Station is where the old war habits work in your favor; the place still trusts any signal wearing the right uniform, and long familiarity has dulled what few safeguards remain. Its consoles speak the same language as the cargo hulk you first boarded, the same obsolete protocols Hart once served under, which is why the routing you need would pass unnoticed anywhere else but glows here like a buried vein. Bloodied Unit holds the corridors with the casual discipline of soldiers who have guarded too many forgotten secrets, certain no one is paying attention anymore. So far the trail has given you a dead Navy freighter with surgically cut comms, scattered audit fragments hinting at non-standard blackout trials, and rumors of frontier outposts paid off in quiet, all pointing to someone higher than Hart who learned to hide malice inside routine.
zh: 这座"被遗弃的中继站"，正是旧日战争习惯对你有利的地方；这地方仍信任任何穿着正确制服的信号，而长久的熟悉磨钝了仅存的那点防护。它的控制台与你第一次登上的那具货船残骸说着同样的语言，同样"哈特"曾在其下服役的过时协议——所以你需要的那条路由在别处都会不被注意地滑过，在这里却像一条埋藏的血管一样发光。"血染单位"以那种"守过太多被遗忘机密"的士兵的随意纪律把守走廊，笃信再没人在意。目前为止，这条线索给了你一具通讯被精密切除的死掉海军货船、零散的审计片段暗示着非标准的黑障试验，以及关于边境前哨被悄悄收买的传闻，全都指向某个比哈特更高、学会了把恶意藏进例行公事里的人。

#en: Whatever he left woven into this place had to pass through a node no one watches anymore, and that makes the abandoned listening post the only place his hand would show clean. The old UC dishes still rake the sky out here, catching the faint spill from misaligned satellites and hushed transmissions that never make it into official logs. If there is a thread connecting his altered storm bands and bent grav lanes, it brushes this station first, before anyone can smooth it away. Back on that lonely rock, farmers only muttered about wrong weather when no recorders were running; in the last relay I checked, half the warning audio simply stopped mid-sentence; now even the salvagers squatting in these corridors lower their voices when they mention redirected traffic and ghost jump routes, like saying too much might be enough to make whatever is listening look back.
zh: 他留下并织进这地方的东西，必然要经过一个再没人看管的节点，这让那座废弃听音哨成了唯一能让他那只手干净显现的地方。旧联殖天线盘仍在这外面扫过天空，捕捉错位卫星与从不进入官方日志的压低传输的微弱溢出。若说有一根线把他被改动的风暴带与弯折的引力航道连起来，它会先擦过这座星际站，在任何人能把它抹平之前。在那块孤独的岩石上，农场主只在没在录音时才嘟囔天气不对；在我查过的上一座中继里，一半的警告音频干脆在句子中间断掉；如今连蹲在这些走廊里的打捞者提起被改道的交通与幽灵跃迁航线时都压低声音，仿佛说太多就足以让正在聆听的东西回头看过来。

#en:
Out here, away from the traffic lanes and official eyes, this little rock and its abandoned camp are exactly where someone would stash notes you do not want filed in any UC archive.  
The agent who was watching Vector chose distance over backup, which means whatever they wrote down never made it to a tribunal and has been fermenting in the dark ever since.  
Locals argue over the story in low voices, each version shifting blame a little, but no one ever insists on being right; the last person who pushed too hard stopped asking questions altogether.  
So far my trail is a broken chain of evidence and hearsay: strange misjump telemetry off a crippled freighter, a nameless slate in the backcountry that whispered the same skewed vectors, and now a rumor that one UC watcher tried to piece it all together out here and did not live long enough to file the report.
zh:
在这里，远离航道与官方的眼睛，这块小岩石与它废弃的营地正是有人会藏起那种"你不想让它进入任何联殖档案"之笔记的地方。  
那个监视"向量"的特工选择了距离而非后援，这意味着他们写下的无论什么从未送到法庭，此后一直在黑暗中发酵。  
当地人低声争论这个故事，每个版本都推诿一点责任，可没人坚持自己是对的；上一个追得太紧的人干脆不再问问题了。  
目前为止，我的线索是一条断裂的证据与传闻之链：一艘残废货船上古怪的错跳遥测、乡间一块低语着同样歪斜向量的无名数据板，以及如今一则传闻——某名联殖监视者试图在这里把一切拼起来，却没能活到提交报告。

#en: The remote research module hangs in the dark like a forgotten thought, power throttled back, only the faint hum of life support keeping its data banks from freezing into silence. This is where the transfer paths knot together, where half-legal experiments and quiet corporate audits once shared the same servers until priorities shifted, budgets moved on, and no one bothered to cleanly erase the past. Logs were rerouted, ownership changed hands, and what began as routine record-keeping slowly became an accidental dead drop, leaving critical traces where no one originally meant them to settle. So far the trail runs from an unmarked cache in the wilds to abandoned terminals in a shuttered lab, and now to this forgotten node where freight manifests and tampered accounts finally begin to rhyme with the stories told about a hauler who never stopped working the dust.
zh: 那座偏远研究舱像一段被遗忘的思绪悬在黑暗中，电力被压低，只有生命维持的微弱嗡鸣让它的数据库不致冻结成沉默。这里正是转运路径打结的地方，半合法的实验与安静的公司审计曾共用同一批服务器，直到优先级转移、预算挪走，而没人费心干净地抹掉过去。日志被改道、所有权几度易手，起初只是例行记录的东西慢慢变成了一个意外的死信箱，在没人原本打算让它们沉淀的地方留下关键痕迹。目前为止，线索从荒野中一处无标记的储藏点，到一座关闭实验室里被弃置的终端，如今又到这座被遗忘的节点——在这里，货运舱单与被篡改的账户终于开始与那些关于一名从未停止在尘土里干活的货船船工的故事押上韵。

#en: This husk of machinery drifting over the planet is where his pattern stops being theory and hardens into proof. Its position sits just off the main grav lanes, nested in a blind patch no navigation authority admits exists, quietly reshaping jump telemetry for anyone routed through Deadbolt's handiwork. Whatever he has been modeling in secret hinges on this node staying intact, turning shipping accidents into rehearsals and pirate raids into timed demonstrations. Bringing it down here fractures the spine of his system before it can be fully weaponized. So far the trail runs like this: a forgotten dataslate in the dark, falsified courier orders on a paid-for ship, Navy records scrubbed yet echoing the same delay codes, and now this silent construct in orbit that proves someone tried to bury the truth, but every frightened captain's story kept the whispers alive.
zh: 这具漂在行星上方的机械残骸，是他的模式不再是理论、而硬化成证据的地方。它的位置就在主引力航道外，嵌在一片没有任何导航机构承认存在的盲区里，悄悄为任何经由"死栓"手笔引导的船只重塑跃迁遥测。他暗中建模的一切都取决于这个节点保持完好——它把航运事故变成排练，把海盗袭击变成定时的演示。在这里把它打下来，就能在它被完全武器化之前折断他系统的脊柱。目前为止，线索是这样的：黑暗中一块被遗忘的数据板、一艘被买通船只上被伪造的信使命令、被擦净却仍回响着同样延迟代码的海军记录，以及如今轨道上这座沉默的构造物——它证明有人试图埋葬真相，可每一个受惊船长的故事都让低语活着。

#en: New Atlantis looks clean from orbit, a perfect holo of order and regulation, but everything that gets buried up here slides downhill somewhere. Whatever was used to carve people out of the registries would have needed access close to the heart of the system, somewhere the right kind of clearance opens doors and the wrong question closes them. That makes this city the only place where a gap in the records does not look like a glitch but a choice. You are not the first to come asking; the way clerks pause mid-sentence and security eyes wander past you says there is a shared understanding about what not to say aloud. Still, the trail started with a stray slate in the dark, led to mismatched accounts in a branch that swore nothing was wrong, then to stories in the underlevels about a second voice on old calls that made difficult cases disappear instead of resolve.
zh: 新亚特兰蒂斯城从轨道上看很干净，一幅秩序与规章的完美全息图，可在这里被埋葬的一切都会在某处滑向下坡。任何用来把人从登记册上剜掉的手段，都需要贴近系统心脏的权限——在那里，正确的许可打开门，错误的问题关上门。这让这座城市成了唯一一个"记录里的空缺不像故障、而像选择"的地方。你不是第一个来问的人；文书们在句子中间停顿、安保的目光从你身上飘过的方式，说明大家对"什么不能大声说"有着共识。不过，这条线索始于黑暗里一块散落数据板，牵出一家发誓一切正常的支行里对不上的账目，然后成了下城层关于"旧呼叫里第二个声音让棘手案件消失、而非解决"的故事。

#en: Perched on the airless rock, the cargo relay feels like a rumor given structure: a few patched hab modules, a tangle of antennae, and a petty broker who somehow knows too much about freight that never officially existed. This is where manifests are shaved, containers renamed, and whole shipments turned into ghost stories before they ever reach an insurer's desk. Somewhere in the broker's hoard is the thread that shows which vanished loads were accidents and which were quietly steered into the dark, a pattern only visible from this halfway house between lanes. So far the trail is a chorus of half-believed sightings and nervous denials: a stray dataslate on a forgotten rock, incomplete logs in a quiet lab, a relay repeating traffic no one admits to sending, and dockhands who swear a tug drifted wrong while their supervisors insist nothing unusual happened at all.
zh: 栖在无气岩石上，那座货运中继感觉像一则被赋予结构的传闻：几间打过补丁的居住舱、一团乱麻的天线，以及一个不知怎地对"从未正式存在过的货运"知之过多的小掮客。这里正是舱单被削薄、货柜被改名、整批货运在送到保险员桌上之前就变成鬼故事的地方。在掮客的囤积里某处，藏着那根显示哪些消失的货物是意外、哪些被悄悄引进黑暗的线——一种只有从这座航道之间的中转客栈才能看见的模式。目前为止，这条线索是一场合唱：半信半疑的目击与紧张的否认——被遗忘岩石上一块散落数据板、某间安静实验室里不完整的日志、一座重复着没人承认自己发送过的交通的中继，以及发誓某艘拖船漂错方向、而主管坚称毫无异常的码头工。

#en: The relay station hangs dead between stars, stripped of its ident tags and left to rust just far enough off the main lanes that no one asks why its dishes still twitch. Once it fed clean credit traffic between colonies; now its gutted halls hum with rerouted power and the thin whine of overclocked routers, the perfect place to vanish a man and the records he carries. Here, spliced into the old grid, he is trying to drag one last surge of wealth out of black accounts and bury every trace of who paid and who was saved, before GalBank and the Fleet can rewrite the story. The urgency is simple: if he finishes, the pattern of stolen foreclosures, doctored manifests on that moonside module, and impossible absolved debts on that empty farm will be scrubbed as if they never were, and the quiet effort to erase him will finally succeed after the whispers led you this far.
zh: 那座中继站死寂地悬在群星之间，身份标签被剥走，任其在离主航道刚好足够远处锈蚀，没人会问为什么它的天线盘仍在抽动。它曾为殖民地之间输送干净的信用交通；如今它被掏空的大厅因改道的电力与超频路由器的细微尖啸而嗡鸣，是让一个人与他随身携带的记录消失的完美地点。在这里，接进旧网格，他正试图从黑账户里拽出最后一波财富，并在盖尔银行与舰队改写故事之前，埋葬"谁付了钱、谁被救了"的每一丝痕迹。那种紧迫很简单：若他完工，被偷走的止赎、那座卫星侧舱室上被做手脚的舱单，以及那座空农场上一笔笔不可能被免除的债务，都会被擦得仿佛从未存在，而此前那些低语把你引到这里之后，抹掉他的那份安静努力终将成功。

#en: The moonside cargo relay was built to be invisible, just another anonymous hinge in Trade Authority's supply chain, and that is exactly why this is where the trail tightens. Years of routine traffic, rubber-stamped inventories, and bored shift rotations have turned it into a blind spot, a place where manifests could be bent and whole hulls could slide between columns without raising alarms. The broker buried here has been skimming those omissions, turning quiet discrepancies into private leverage, and somewhere in his hoard lies the pattern of ships that paid to vanish along the same shadowed paths. Familiar routes and familiar signatures lulled everyone into thinking nothing unusual was passing through, until erased vectors in that forgotten hangar and off-book chatter from nervous captains made it clear the same hand had been nudging traffic just out of sight.
zh: 那座卫星侧货运中继被造得隐形，不过是贸易管理局供应链上又一个匿名铰链——这正是线索在这里收紧的原因。多年的例行交通、盖章即过的库存清单与无聊的轮班，把它变成了一个盲点：一处舱单能被掰弯、整具船壳能在各栏之间滑过而不触发警报的地方。埋在这里的那名掮客一直在揩取那些遗漏，把安静的差异变成私人筹码；而在他的囤积里某处，藏着那些"付钱沿同一批阴影路径消失"的船只的模式。熟悉的航线与熟悉的签名让所有人都以为没有不寻常的东西经过，直到那座被遗忘机库里被抹除的向量与紧张船长们的账外闲谈说明：同一只手一直在把交通推离视线之外。

#en: If there is a place where stories warp into scripture, it is this ridge top shelter, where tired settlers trade fears over thin coffee and the wind steals half of every sentence before it reaches the next listener. Whatever was first said about the visiting engineer has already been retold, softened, sharpened, turned into warning and rumor, but here the missioner tried to catch it on a screen before it slipped away. Their notes are the only map left to those who disappeared after seeking "help" with failing air, the closest thing to a clean trace through all this speculation. So far all I know is that an unnamed fixer walks between struggling habitats, leaves systems running too hot, and moves on before the failures start, and that every frightened account eventually winds up echoed in this retreat, like all their paths are bending toward the same unseen point.
zh: 若说有一个地方会把故事扭曲成经文，那就是这座山脊顶的避难所——疲惫的定居者就着淡咖啡交换恐惧，风在每句话传到下一个听者之前就偷走一半。关于那位来访工程师最初说了什么，早已被重述、磨软、磨尖，变成警告与传闻，可在这里，那位传教士试图趁它溜走之前把它捕捉到屏幕上。他们的笔记，是那些在因空气故障寻求"帮助"后失踪的人仅剩的地图，是这一切猜测中最接近干净痕迹的东西。目前为止我只知道，一名无名的掮客在挣扎求生的聚居地之间行走，让系统过热运行，然后在故障开始之前离开；而每一份受惊的叙述最终都会在这处隐居地得到回声，仿佛他们所有的路径都弯向同一个看不见的点。

#en: Neon is where routes are born in the cracks between legal manifests and back-alley bets, and where the lines on a screen can matter more than the streets themselves. Down in Ebbside, the noise of the grid and the weight of the storms above give smugglers cover to test patterns no patrol will ever see, and Vector has been using that cover longer than most captains have been flying. If she hid the key to her curve anywhere, it would be here, buried amid routine simulations and crooked ledger work that security stopped looking at years ago. Out in the drop shelter, a pirate fixer pointed to this district when the pressure rose, and before that a dead courier's slate hinted at the same signature noise; all the fragments say the same thing, that her invisible path was refined under this city while everyone else assumed the traffic here was just more of the usual grind.
zh: 霓虹城，是航线在合法舱单与后巷赌注之间的裂缝里诞生的地方，也是屏幕上的线比街道本身更要紧的地方。在埃布赛德，网格的噪声与头顶风暴的重量给了走私者掩护，去测试任何巡逻队都永远看不到的模式，而"向量"利用这份掩护的时间比多数船长的飞行生涯都长。若她把那条曲线的钥匙藏在任何地方，就会是这里——埋在例行模拟与安保多年前就不再查看的歪斜账务活儿之间。在投放掩体里，一名海盗掮客在压力升高时指向了这个区份；而在此之前，一块死掉信使船的数据板暗示了同一道标志性噪声；所有碎片都在说同一件事：她的隐形路径正是在这座城市之下打磨出来的，而其他所有人都以为这里的交通只是寻常的苦役。

#en:
Gagarin Landing wears its new corporate gloss like a thin coat of paint over rust, but the real business still happens in the alleys between Arc Might catwalks and forgotten mech bays.  
Down here, the waste drums and cargo stacks are where routes get rewritten and inconvenient records disappear, if someone remembers to finish the job.  
The one you are after should have been scrubbed weeks ago; instead it sits untouched, half-buried under newer shipments, as if the person meant to tidy this particular mess was called away mid-move.  
So far the trail has run through a discarded dataslate in the backcountry, strange jump vectors pulled from a damaged freighter, and now whispered directions in this settlement from salvagers and route brokers who all describe the same quiet analyst whose predictions keep putting ships in the wrong place at the worst possible time.
zh:
加加林着陆点把它新的公司光泽像一层薄漆涂在锈上，可真正的生意仍发生在"弧威"栈道与废弃机甲库之间的小巷里。  
在这下面，废料桶与货堆正是航线被改写、碍事的记录消失的地方——如果有人记得把活干完的话。  
你要找的那份东西本该在几周前就被擦掉；可它反而原封不动地待着，半埋在新到的货物之下，仿佛本该来收拾这摊烂局的人干到一半被叫走了。  
目前为止，线索穿过乡间一块被丢弃的数据板、从一艘受损货船上拉出的古怪跃迁向量，如今又到了这座定居点里打捞者与航路掮客低语指出的方向——他们描述的都是一名安静的、其预测不断把船只送进最糟糕时间点的最糟糕位置的分析员。

#en: Gagarin Landing is where temporary fixes come to die slowly. Emergency grav-drive patches, provisional cargo routings, "just-for-now" overrides in the tugyard software, all layered until nobody remembers what the original settings were meant to do. Somewhere in that tangle, the engineers have been feeding a sliver of anomalous traffic into routine checks for so long that the anomaly itself is now part of the standard workflow, an invisible companion to every refit and recalibration. If there is a trace of her signature left anywhere, it will be here, buried under institutional laziness and old workarounds. So far the trail runs through an abandoned outpost where a stray dataslate logged the wrong ship twice, a research station whose incomplete logs lined up with no known route, and a deserted relay still echoing traffic its operators swore they shut down years ago.
zh: 加加林着陆点，是临时修补慢慢死去的地方。应急引力引擎补丁、临时货运路由、拖船坞软件里"暂时先用"的覆写，全都层层叠加，直到没人记得原始设置本该做什么。在那团乱麻里的某处，工程师们太久以来一直把一小片异常交通喂进例行检查，以至于这异常本身如今已是标准工作流的一部分，是每一次翻新与重校的隐形同伴。若说她的签名还有任何痕迹留存，它就会在这里，埋在体制性的懒散与旧日的变通之下。目前为止，线索穿过一座废弃前哨——那里一块散落数据板把错误的船记录了两次；一座研究站——它不完整的日志与任何已知航线都对不上；以及一座废弃中继——它仍在回响着操作员发誓多年前就已关闭的交通。

#en: Down here in recycled air and permanent shadow, the lines between freight and contraband blur until only the handlers can tell the difference, and even they pretend not to see. This is where manifests get rewritten, serials shaved off, and whole shipments are quietly reclassified from charity relief to salvage, then to something with no name at all. If a navigator wanted to move parts and data through official space without leaving a trail, these back corridors would be the first waypoint; everyone knows to talk in nods and half-phrases, to let certain names slip away mid-sentence and point instead at crates, routes, and favors owed. So far, the trail begins with an anonymous cache in a forgotten yard beyond the city, and a whisper in a workers' canteen about rerouted colony ships, a missing LIST planner, and star charts that never match the ones on the public boards.
zh: 在这下面的循环空气与永久阴影里，货运与违禁品之间的界线模糊到只有经手人分得清，而连他们也假装没看见。这里正是舱单被重写、序列号被磨掉、整批货运被悄悄从慈善救济重新归类为打捞物、再归为某种完全没有名字的东西的地方。若一名领航员想在官方太空里运送零件与数据而不留痕迹，这些后走廊会是第一个航点；人人都知道要用点头与半句话交谈，让某些名字在句子中间溜走，转而指向货箱、航线与欠下的人情。目前为止，这条线索始于城市之外一处被遗忘场区里的匿名储藏点，以及某间工人食堂里的一句低语——关于被改道的殖民船、一名失踪的独立盟规划者，以及永远与公告板上那些对不上的星图。

#en: The moonside cargo relay module sits where official routes blur into private arrangements, a quiet choke point where credits change hands long before any ledger admits it. Its stacked containers and half-lit corridors hide the only full picture of how certain shipments kept dodging fees, penalties, and the kind of attention that gets routes shut down. Here, buried in a broker's private cache, is the pattern of diverted loads and forgiven balances that traces back to a single guiding hand, the kind of map no bank or pirate will willingly leave intact. Back on that empty farm, the foreclosure that canceled itself looked like a glitch; now, with a dead spacer's half-burned notes in mind, the same signature corrections keep appearing along this smuggling chain, and every whisper about a rogue auditor twisting the tides of credit feels less like rumor and more like design.
zh: 那座卫星侧货运中继舱坐落于官方航线与私人安排模糊交界之处，一处安静的咽喉，信用币在账册承认之前很久就已在此易手。它堆叠的货柜与半亮的走廊藏着唯一一幅完整图景：某些货运如何持续躲过费用、罚款，以及那种会让航线被关停的注意力。在这里、埋在一名掮客的私人储藏里的，是"被截留的货物与被免除的余额"的模式——它追溯回一只单独的引导之手，那种任何银行或海盗都不愿原样留下的地图。回到那座空农场，那笔自我注销的止赎看起来像个小故障；如今，想起一名死掉太空劫匪半烧毁的笔记，同样的标志性修正不断出现在这条走私链上，而每一句关于"一名流氓审计员搅动信用潮汐"的低语，都不再像传闻、而更像设计。

#en: Down here, under the Span where the lightning feeds the city and the runoff of a thousand bad decisions trickles through rusted grates, the noise is loud enough to hide what needs hearing. This is where illicit power is spliced, where anonymous packets ride stolen current, and where a mind like hers would lean on the grid without ever touching an official terminal. The pattern you have been chasing lives in the static and hum, encoded in routes that cross storms, Helium-3 lines, and forgotten farm skies, and only a place that drinks directly from Neon's heartbeat could hold a clean echo of it.  \nSo far the trail has run from a stray lead in the back end of nowhere, through cautious files at a frontier support post and odd diagnostics along a fuel operation; all of it pointing, step by step, toward her habit of hiding inside the places everyone else takes for granted.
zh: 在这下面、在桥架之下——闪电喂养着这座城市，一千个糟糕决定的径流从锈蚀格栅里滴下——噪声大到足以藏住需要被听见的东西。这里正是非法电力被接续的地方，是匿名封包乘着偷来的电流的地方，也是像她那样的头脑会不碰任何官方终端就倚在电网上之处。你一直追的模式活在静电与嗡鸣里，编码在那些穿越风暴、氦-3 航线与被遗忘农场天空的路线中，而只有一个直接从霓虹城心跳里饮水的地方，才可能保存它干净的回声。  \n目前为止，线索从天涯之外一条散落线报，穿过某座边境补给站里戒备的文件与一处燃料设施沿线的古怪诊断；全都一步步指向她那种"藏在别人习以为常之处"的习惯。

#en: Neon's underbelly is where the city forgets itself, where old wiring, rerouted power, and unpaid favors tangle into something no administrator tracks anymore. Down here, a single mislabelled conduit or unreported junction can live for years, feeding back rooms, side hustles, and quiet schemes under the Conduction Grid. Somewhere along the line, a tech skipped a form, a contractor cut a corner, and a whole layer of sublevel links slipped past official schematics, becoming the perfect skeleton for someone who thinks in flows and failures. The first whispers of this came from a shaken broker on Akila and half-burned notes drifting near Gagarin; along with a locker of marked freight claims below Neon's lights, they all suggested the same thing: someone is using forgotten infrastructure as their private balance sheet, and the trail starts in the ducts no one bothered to fix.
zh: 霓虹城的下腹，是这座城市遗忘自己的地方，旧线路、被改道的电力与未偿的人情缠成某种再没有管理者追踪的东西。在这下面，一根标签错误的导管或一处未申报的接点能存活多年，喂养着输电网格下的后室、副业与安静图谋。一路走来，某个技师跳过了一张表格，某个承包商偷了一个工，整层地下链路就此溜过官方图纸，成了某个"以流量与故障思考"之人的完美骨架。关于此事的第一批低语，来自阿基拉城一名受惊的掮客与加加林星附近漂着的半烧毁笔记；连同霓虹城灯光下一柜子标记过的货运索赔，它们都暗示同一件事：有人在把被遗忘的基础设施当作私人资产负债表，而线索始于那些没人费心去修的管道。

#en: If it had to end anywhere, it would be here, under leaking conduits and flickering gridlight, where nobody asks how a ship crossed a lane it should not have survived. Neon's lower decks are where Kade's believers drink beside her casualties, where Vector's name is spoken with equal parts envy and dread, and where a pilot who knows too much about ghost jumps can disappear into a crowd that owes him favors. The Underbelly hums with outlaw tech and bad bets, the perfect place for him to cut one last deal, bury one last data trace, and slip away toward whatever Echo he thinks is waiting. Faces around the bars remember a burned courier staggering into dock, a fight in a gutted test bay on Gagarin, strange blackbox fragments traded through a Neon broker, and that drifting Trade Authority hull, all sketching the same pattern of impossible vectors and ships that never came home.
zh: 若说它必须在某处终结，那就是这里——在渗漏的导管与闪烁的网格灯光下，没人会问一艘船是如何穿过一条它本不该活着穿过的航道。霓虹城的下层甲板，是凯德的信徒与她造成的伤亡者比邻饮酒的地方，是"向量"的名字被以同等的嫉妒与恐惧念出的地方，也是一个对幽灵跃迁知道太多的飞行员能消失进一群欠他人情之人的地方。下腹嗡鸣着法外技术与糟糕赌注，是他做最后一笔交易、埋下最后一处数据痕迹、然后溜向他以为在等待的"回声"的完美地点。酒吧周围的面孔记得一艘烧毁的信使船踉跄进港、加加林星一间被掏空的测试舱里的一场打斗、经由霓虹城掮客交易的古怪黑匣碎片，以及那具漂着的贸易管理局船壳——全都勾勒出同样不可能向量与从未归家船只的模式。

#en: Out on the fringe, this little Ranger post is the only place where all the half-spoken stories actually touch the same wall. Settlers drift through with dust on their boots and static in their hair, arguing over what they saw in the storms and how many ships really vanished, but no one wants their name on an official complaint. Here the liaison pins their conflicting accounts side by side, ink bleeding through cheap paper, while the comms console crackles with weather alerts no central office will ever read. If there is a pattern hiding in the noise, it lives in these cramped corridors and coffee-stained logs. So far, all you know is that frontier families describe the same quiet pilot threading convoys through impossible weather, insurers insist every loss was a simple navigational error, and both sides fall silent the moment you ask for something you can actually file.
zh: 在边境上，这座小小的游骑兵哨所是唯一一个所有半说出口的故事真正撞上同一面墙的地方。定居者带着靴上的尘土与发间的静电来来去去，争论着他们在风暴里看到了什么、究竟有多少船真地消失，可没人愿意把自己的名字写在一份官方投诉上。在这里，联络官把那些相互矛盾的说法并排钉起来，墨迹洇过廉价纸张，而通讯控制台噼啪作响着任何中央办公室都不会去读的天气警报。若说有什么模式藏在噪声里，它就活在这些逼仄的走廊与被咖啡渍染黄的日志里。目前为止，你只知道：边境家庭描述着同一名安静地把车队引过不可能天气的飞行员，保险公司坚称每一次损失都只是简单的导航错误，而当你索要任何真能归档的东西时，双方都沉默了。

#en: Out in far orbit, where traffic thins to silence and only old signals drift, this is the one place the pattern can be seen without interference. The VR-6919 Ghostforge sits on the edge of the well like a knife on a map, hull lights dark, listening and relaying in directions no public chart admits exist. Whatever passes through its arrays ties the nameless gas giant, the drifting graveyards, and the hidden barge into one geometry of jumps that only a navigator obsessed with control would design.  \nSo far the trail runs from that forgotten rock where the first dataslate turned up, through crooked dock records near Neon and a smuggler's ledger in a sweating cavern. Each retelling of how those pieces connect shifts a little in the mouths of spacers, but the same shadow keeps showing up at the edge of every route chart anyone is brave enough to mention in more than a whisper.
zh: 在远轨道上，交通稀薄成寂静、只有旧信号漂荡之处，这是唯一能不受干扰看清那个模式的地方。"VR-6919 幽灵熔炉"像一把插在地图上的刀，停在引力井边缘，船壳灯光熄灭，朝任何公开星图都不承认存在的方向聆听与转发。凡是穿过它阵列的东西，都把无名气态巨行星、漂移的墓地与那艘隐藏驳船系进一套只有痴迷控制的领航员才会设计的跃迁几何。  \n目前为止，线索从第一块数据板出现的那块被遗忘岩石，穿过霓虹城附近歪斜的船坞记录与一座湿漉漉洞窟里走私者的账册。关于这些碎片如何连接的每一次转述，在太空劫匪口中都会略有变化，可同一道阴影总是出现在每一张"有谁鼓起勇气用多于一句低语提起"的航线图边缘。

#en: Down here the air tastes like coolant and cheap Aurora runoff, and the walls sweat with every storm that hits the Span above. If someone wanted to hide the pattern behind ships coming and going, behind which hulls get pushed past safe load and which ones drift out to die, they would bury it in these back corridors, between unmarked freight offices and terminals no one admits to owning. The Underbelly is where dockhands talk off-shift, where Sanctum zealots whisper about endings, where LIST surveyors trade rumors for a drink; paper trails do not survive here, only schedules traded hand to hand. So far, all I have are those fragments: a stray log from a lonely surface outpost, an orbital cache that should not have existed, and a derelict SysDef hull whose records were scrubbed too neatly for chance. Everywhere I go, different people tell the same story with different names.
zh: 在这下面，空气尝起来像冷却液与廉价极光径流，每当风暴打上头顶的桥架，墙壁就渗出水来。若有人想把模式藏在船只来往背后——藏在哪些船壳被推过安全负载、哪些漂出去等死背后——他们会把它埋在这些后走廊里，埋在无标记的货运办公室与没人承认自己拥有的终端之间。下腹是码头工在休班时闲聊的地方，是圣宇教信徒低声讲述末日的地方，是独立盟勘探员用传闻换一杯酒的地方；纸面痕迹在这里活不下来，只有一手交一手传下去的日程。目前为止，我只有那些碎片：一座孤独地面前哨的散落日志、一处本不该存在的轨道储藏点，以及一具记录被擦得过于干净、绝非偶然的星防队弃船。无论我走到哪里，不同的人都在用不同的名字讲同一个故事。

#en: Out here, the old UC listening post still hums faintly, its dishes fixed on dead lanes and forgotten wars, the perfect shell for someone who lives inside signals and silence. Starline chose this place because its arrays were built to hear what others miss; tied into them, she can scrub beacons, bend civilian routes, and finish rewriting the maps that have killed convoys and led hunters into graveyards. Every false corridor, every doctored jump, has been steering traffic toward a pattern only she fully sees, and now she is seconds from locking that pattern in, purging the last raw logs that prove how many lives were spent to draw her lattice across the stars. Backwater contracts, a stray dataslate, wrecked haulers, a gutted scrapyard trail, and a corrupted orbital clue have all converged on one truth: her charts were never accidents, just small choices layered into a design.
zh: 在这里，那座旧联殖听音哨仍在微弱嗡鸣，天线盘锁定在死掉的航道与被遗忘的战争上，是某个"活在信号与沉默里"之人的完美外壳。"星线"选中这里，是因为它的阵列本就是为听见别人错过的东西而建；接进其中，她能擦净信标、掰弯民用航线，并完成对那些"杀死过车队、把猎人引进坟墓"的地图的改写。每一条假走廊、每一次被做手脚的跃迁，都一直在把交通引向一个只有她完全看得见的模式；如今她离把那个模式锁死只差几秒——清除最后那些证明"为把她的网格画遍群星花掉了多少条命"的原始日志。穷乡合同、一块散落数据板、损毁的货船、一条被掏空废料场的线索，以及一处损坏的轨道线索，全都汇聚到一个真相：她的星图从来不是意外，只是被层层叠进一个设计里的小选择。

#en: Skyclipper TA-1174 drifts where the lanes thin out and the patrol grids look the other way, the kind of place a Trade Authority hauler can go missing without anyone filing more than a delayed-shipment note. Its numbered hull and corporate transponders make it look routine, harmless, but that is exactly why records tied to dangerous routes and unregistered jumps would be buried here rather than on any flagged smuggler's ship. The air inside will still taste of processed cargo dust and burnt electronics, a quiet reminder that someone thought this was the safest place to hide the pattern behind impossible transits and ships that never arrived. So far the trail has been fragments and whispers: a discarded dataslate on a backwater rock, scrambled beacon logs from a broken orbit, and stories of a pilot who keeps appearing on the edges of misjumps no one wants to audit too closely.
zh: 天帆船 TA-1174漂在航道变稀薄、巡逻网格转开视线之处，那种一艘贸易管理局货船能失踪、而没人提交超出"货运延误"备注的地方。它带编号的船壳与公司应答器让它显得例行、无害，而这正是为什么与危险航线和未登记跃迁相关的记录会被埋在这里，而不是在任何被标记的走私者船上。里面的空气仍会尝起来像处理过的货物粉尘与烧焦电子件，安静地提醒：有人认为这里是藏起"不可能通行与从未抵达船只"背后模式的最安全之地。目前为止，这条线索是碎片与低语：一穷乡岩石上被丢弃的数据板、一条断裂轨道上被搅乱的信号日志，以及关于一名不断出现在"没人想仔细审计的错跳"边缘的飞行员的故事。

#en: Out here in far orbit, where dead satellites drift like slow shrapnel and old war hulls still stain the scans, the quiet anomalies finally resolve into a single, deliberate line. The device anchored among them is not just another dusty aid to navigation its geometry mirrors the strange adjustments you have seen bleeding through traffic updates, a silent metronome teaching every passing ship to favor one distant, forgotten quadrant. As long as it keeps pulsing, rumor and misdirection win; stories of "unlucky" convoys and bad UC math stay comfortably vague, passed around in backrooms until no one remembers who first changed the numbers. So far the trail has run from a bloodied dataslate in a forgotten stopover to a dead surface relay with altered logs, each step proving that someone inside the system has been bending courses for years while the truth was quietly polished smooth.
zh: 在这里的远轨道上，死掉的卫星像缓慢的弹片漂着，旧战争船壳仍在扫描上留下污渍，那些安静的异常终于解析成一条单一的、刻意的线。锚在它们之间的那台设备不只是又一件蒙尘的导航辅助——它的几何映照着你见过从交通更新里渗出的那些古怪调整，一只无声的节拍器，教每一艘过往船只偏好某个遥远、被遗忘的象限。只要它持续脉动，传闻与误导就占上风；关于"倒霉"车队与糟糕联殖数学的故事就舒适地停留在含糊里，在后室传来传去，直到没人记得是谁先改了那些数字。目前为止，线索从一座被遗忘的中途站一块沾血的数据板，延伸到一座日志被改动的死掉地面中继，每一步都证明体制内有人多年来一直在掰弯航向，而真相则被悄悄打磨光滑。

#en: Out here the Deserted Relay Station is more than scrap and silent dishes it is the knot where every tampered lane and falsified beacon converges. Its antique arrays still see what official eyes pretend to miss, and Vector has folded them into a single choke point, using their reach to rewire traffic across half a dozen systems. She is here to finish what started with those quiet anomalies, to purge the last raw telemetry, lock her algorithms in place, and decide who lives or dies in the corridors between stars. In dockside bars and GalBank offices, people only mention this system in half sentences and lowered voices, as if an open word might flip some unseen switch. So far the trail has run from an anonymous dataslate on a backworld rock to an orbital clue guarded by jumpy Spacers, then into a drifting UC cargo hull whose logs proved the accidents follow a pattern, not chance.
zh: 在这里，那座"被遗弃的中继站"不只是废铁与沉默的天线盘——它是每一条被动手脚的航道与被伪造的信标汇聚的结。它古旧的阵列仍看得见官方眼睛假装错过的东西，而"向量"把它们折成一个单独的咽喉，用它们的触及范围重接半打星系间的交通。她来这里是为了完成从那些安静异常开始的一切：清除最后的原始遥测、把她的算法锁死到位，并决定群星之间走廊里谁生谁死。在码头酒吧与盖尔银行办公室里，人们只用半句话与压低的声音提起这个星系，仿佛一句公开的话就可能扳动某个看不见的开关。目前为止，线索从一穷乡岩石上一块匿名数据板，到一处由紧张兮兮的太空劫匪把守的轨道线索，再到一具漂着的联殖货船壳——它的日志证明那些事故遵循一个模式，而非偶然。

#en: The deserted UC listening post hangs in the dark like a bad habit the Navy never quite managed to quit. Its dishes are dead, but the buried servers still whisper on backup power, quietly cycling through intercepts and salvage telemetry no one officially admits exist. If there is a key to the pattern behind her derelicts, it lives here, in the gap between what was supposed to be temporary surveillance and what quietly became a permanent shadow ledger. Vanguard Direwolf sits on it like a hired conscience, guns and contracts wrapped around something their employers do not want questioned. Back on that lonely rock where a stray dataslate turned up, in the cramped monitoring bunker where censored reports piled too neatly, and in the dead corridors of this same station, small anomalies stacked atop each other until they stopped feeling like coincidence and started reading like a map.
zh: 那座废弃的联殖听音哨像海军始终没能彻底戒掉的一个坏习惯悬在黑暗中。它的天线盘死了，可被埋的服务器仍在备用电力上低语，悄悄循环着官方从不承认存在的拦截数据与打捞遥测。若说她的弃船背后那个模式有把钥匙，它就活在这里，活在"本该是临时监视"与"悄悄变成永久影子账册"之间的缝隙里。"先锋队恐狼"像一份雇来的良心般坐镇其上，枪炮与合同裹住一件他们雇主不愿被质疑的东西。回到那块出现散落数据板的孤独岩石、那座被审查报告堆得过于整齐的逼仄监控掩体，以及这同一座星际站的死走廊，小小的异常一层层堆叠，直到它们不再像巧合、而开始读起来像一张地图。

#en: The Widebeam AX-1562 hangs in a slow, ugly roll, navigation lights dead, hull paint scoured away until only the Trade Authority markings remain like a bad joke. Whoever stripped her did it in a hurry and in anger, leaving torn cabling and half-wiped consoles that tell three different stories depending on which log you believe. Some entries swear she jumped clean from Gagarin, others show a detour through a med station she was never licensed to approach, all of them looping around the same quiet gaps where routing data should be. What is consistent, buried under conflicting time stamps and overwritten manifests, is a pattern of medical shipments threaded toward places no longer on standard charts. So far the trail amounts to a dead hauler full of the wrong cargo and a handful of veterans in backwater bars talking about a combat medic who shows up when official channels look away.
zh: 宽带 AX-1562以一种缓慢而难看的姿态翻滚着，航行灯熄灭，船壳油漆被刮掉，只剩贸易管理局的标记，像一个冷笑话。把它剥光的人做得又急又怒，留下撕裂的线缆与被擦掉一半的控制台——它们会根据你信哪份日志，讲出三个不同版本的故事。有些条目发誓它是从加加林星干净跃迁出来的，另一些则显示它绕经一座它从未获准靠近的医疗站；所有条目都绕着本该有航线路由数据的同样那些安静空缺打转。一致的部分——埋在互相矛盾的时戳与被覆写的舱单之下——是一批朝不再出现在标准星图上的地点穿针引线的医疗货运模式。目前为止，这条线索相当于一艘装满错误货物的死掉货船，以及几名在穷乡酒吧里谈论一名"在官方信道转开视线时出现"的战斗医疗兵的老兵。

#en: It had to be here, coasting in high orbit where traffic thins and only the patient machines remain, a quiet bend in space where someone like her could stack routes and wait for patterns to converge. The processing hub below hums through its cycles, blind to the BR-1331 Riftblade holding station like a knife in the dark, its guns and sensors tied into whatever narrowcast threads she left behind. This is where separate paths knot together  automated schedules, drift corrections, and those strange timing offsets you have seen before, all sliding toward the same solution as if pulled by gravity itself.  \n\nSo far the chase has moved from a dead slate on a lonely rock to strange shipping talk over coffee, then to dirt and debt where a mechanic replayed an old argument, each step confirming that diverted routes, buried logs, and missing ships all curve back toward her predictive hand.
zh: 必须在这里——在高轨道上巡航，那里交通稀薄、只剩耐心的机器；一处安静的太空弯折，像她那样的人可以在那里堆放航线、等待模式汇聚。下方那座处理枢纽按周期嗡鸣，浑然不觉"BR-1331 裂隙之刃"像黑暗中的一把刀般驻守，它的枪炮与传感器接进她留下的无论什么窄播线程。这里正是各条分离路径打结之处——自动化日程、漂移修正，以及你此前见过的那些古怪时间偏移，全都像被引力本身牵引般滑向同一个解。  \n\n目前为止，这场追查从一块孤独岩石上的死数据板，到咖啡桌旁古怪的航运闲谈，再到一名机械师复述旧日争吵的尘土与债务之地，每一步都证实：被改道的航线、被埋葬的日志与失踪的船只，全都弯回她那只能预测的手。

#en: Only out here, suspended above a nameless world where the traffic lanes thin to whispers, can you see how someone has been carving new paths into the dark and erasing the cuts afterward. The fragment you are after drifts in the quiet between shipping routes, just far enough from scrutiny that its readings are dismissed as noise, yet close enough that a patient hand has been nudging jump solutions toward it for years. Whatever is encoded there ties together the detours that killed settlers, the missing survey partner no one files reports on, and the Va'ruun transmissions scrubbed from official archives, details everyone knows but folds away in the same drawer. So far the trail has been a discarded dataslate in the back end of nowhere, hushed complaints from wrecked haulers, salvaged logs from a gutted scrapyard, and now a pattern of altered routes that lines up too neatly to ignore.
zh: 只有在这里，悬在一颗无名世界上方、航道稀薄成低语之处，你才能看出有人一直在黑暗中凿出新路、随后又把切口抹掉。你要找的那块碎片漂在航运路线之间的安静里，离审视刚好足够远、让它的读数被当作噪声打发，却又近到一只耐心的手多年来一直在把跃迁解朝它推去。在那里编码的任何东西，都把"杀死定居者的绕行"、"没人提交报告的失踪勘探搭档"，以及从官方档案里被擦掉的瓦鲁传输系在一起——这些细节人人都知道，却都被折进同一个抽屉里。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡之地一块被丢弃的数据板、损毁货船船员压低的抱怨、一座被掏空废料场里打捞出的日志，如今又是一种"太整齐、无法忽视"的被改动航线模式。

#en: Out here in the dim halo of a forgotten orbit, the wrecked trail of engines and broken hull plating feels less like salvage and more like a discarded thought, pushed just far enough from traffic that no one sane would come looking. This is the kind of graveyard a combat medic would choose to bury data in, far from scanners yet close enough to slipping lanes for a clean escape, and the presence of a gun-heavy escort suggests the secret inside those fragments is still very much alive. Sensor echoes, corrupted transponders, and overlapping combat logs paint different versions of how this ship died, but each insists on the same thing in its own distorted way. We began with a lone dataslate on a backwater world, then chased altered patients, tampered medical couriers, and UC marks through empty orbits and a silent SysDef hull, always circling the same surgically neat pattern in his wake.
zh: 在这里、在被遗忘轨道的昏暗光晕中，那条由引擎与破碎船壳板构成的残骸带，与其说是打捞物，不如说像一个被丢弃的念头，被推到离交通刚好足够远、没有理智的人会来找的地方。这是战斗医疗兵会选择用来埋数据的墓地：远离扫描仪，却又近到溜进航道就能干净脱身；而一支重火力护航队的存在说明，那些碎片里的秘密还活得很好。传感器回声、损坏的应答器与相互重叠的战斗日志，描绘出这艘船如何死去的不同版本，可每一个都以其自身扭曲的方式坚持同一件事。我们从一穷乡世界上一块孤独的数据板开始，然后追着被改动的病人、被动手脚的医疗信使与联殖标记，穿过空荡轨道与一具沉默的星防队船壳，始终绕着他身后那个外科手术般整齐的同一模式打转。
