#en: Out here the old Ecliptic garrison hangs over the rock like a bad memory, its gun decks long cold, its corridors lit by failing strips no one bothered to replace. It is perfect for work no faction wants traced back to them, a blind spot in UC records and a forgotten asset in mercenary ledgers, left for someone like Vector to inherit. He has stripped the place down to its wiring, feeding stolen grav models and beacon code through consoles meant for fire-control, turning a derelict battlestation into the nerve center of his private experiment while the official caretakers looked away and never came back. Every phantom misjump, every encrypted warning from freight captains and LIST dispatchers, every fragment of data exhumed from that buried base and the gutted depot has pointed here, to the abandoned guns, the unclaimed power, and the man quietly rewriting the lanes from their shadow.
zh: 在这里，那座旧黄道佣兵团驻军像一段糟糕回忆般悬在岩石上方，它的炮甲板早已冰冷，走廊里亮着没人费心更换的故障灯带。它完美适合任何派系都不愿被追溯到自己头上的工作：联殖记录里的一个盲点、佣兵账册里一件被遗忘的资产，留给像"向量"这样的人去继承。他把这地方剥到只剩线路，把偷来的引力模型与信标代码喂进本用于火控的控制台，把一座废弃战斗站变成他私人实验的神经中枢，而官方的看管者转开视线、再没回来。每一次幽灵错跳、每一则来自货船船长与独立盟调度员的加密警告、每一块从那座被埋基地与被掏空货运站挖出的数据碎片，都指向这里——指向被遗弃的枪炮、无人认领的电力，以及那个从它们的阴影里悄悄改写航道的男人。

#en: The asteroid field is exactly where you hide something you do not want found, tucked between drifting rock and old collision scars, broadcasting just softly enough that only a curious fool or a determined hunter would ever notice. The signal here is crooked in all the right ways, nudging ships a few degrees off sanctioned lanes, humming on an interval that looks like noise until you stare too long and realize there is a mind behind it. Whatever hand has been rewriting routes would anchor their work somewhere like this, where broken hulls are just more clutter and traffic reports never quite agree. Before this, all you had were half-erased incident logs, redacted names in UC debriefs, and freight-yard stories about drives that remembered shortcuts nobody filed, each rumor quietly insisting that someone has been bending the lanes for years while the official record pretends otherwise.
zh: 小行星带，正是你藏起不想被发现之物的地方：夹在漂移的岩石与旧碰撞伤疤之间，广播得轻到只有好奇的蠢货或坚定的猎人才会注意到。这里的信号以所有"正确的方式"歪斜，把船只推离获批航道几度，以一段看起来像噪声的间隔嗡鸣——直到你盯得太久，意识到它背后有一个头脑。任何一直在改写航线的手，都会把作品锚在这样的地方：在那里，破损船壳只是更多杂物，而交通报告永远对不上。在此之前，你只有半擦除的事件日志、联殖述职里被涂黑的名字，以及货运场里关于"引擎记得没人归档的近路"的故事，每一则传闻都悄悄坚称有人多年来一直在掰弯航道，而官方记录则假装并非如此。

#en: The old relay bunker still hums faintly beneath its dust, a forgotten node in the patrol grid that once watched every breath of air over this sector. Whatever was pulled from its systems cut a clean hole in official history, and only here  in the raw telemetry still buried under corrosion and cobwebbed cables  does the shape of that absence become clear. The deserter chose this place because it sat between duty and silence, because a single set of scans could prove who really crossed restricted sky and when. The truth is likely straightforward, just wrapped in omission and misdirection until it feels unreal.  \n\nSo far the trail runs from a dead slate on a lonely rock to subtle shipping anomalies whispered over coffee, then to a quiet farm's strange traffic patterns  each step tightening the same loop of diverted routes, buried logs, and one navigator's invisible hand on the lanes.
zh: 那座旧中继掩体仍在尘土下微弱嗡鸣，是巡逻网格里一个被遗忘的节点，曾注视这片星域上空每一次呼吸般的空气流动。凡是从它系统里被抽走的东西，都在官方历史里切出一个干净的洞；而只有在这里——在仍埋在腐蚀与蛛网线缆下的原始遥测里——那份缺席的形状才变得清晰。那名逃兵选中这里，是因为它坐落在职责与沉默之间，因为一组扫描就能证明谁真正穿越过受限天空、在何时。真相大概很直白，只是被省略与误导包裹到感觉不再真实。  \n\n目前为止，线索从一块孤独岩石上的死数据板，到咖啡桌旁低声议论的细微航运异常，再到一座安静农场古怪的交通模式，每一步都收紧着同一个循环：被改道的航线、被埋葬的日志，以及一名领航员搭在航道上的无形之手。

#en: Out in this thin band of orbit, the stars feel slightly out of place, like someone has been tugging the sky a few degrees at a time. The sensor hub anchored here drinks in stray radiation no one bothers to catalogue, then quietly nudges jump plots by fractions, enough to send whole convoys skimming a different stretch of dark. Whatever has been watching the lanes from this vantage has been doing it for a long time, long enough that course corrections and "harmless" detours have started to stack into a pattern nobody will admit seeing. From a forgotten slate on a frontier rock, to convoy reports that all blamed the same phantom malfunction, to a derelict node full of stolen Fleet math, every fragment I have touched points toward someone mapping a second set of routes underneath the official ones, as if the Settled Systems have been walking in their sleep along a path they never chose.
zh: 在这条稀薄的轨道带上，群星感觉略有错位，像有人一直在一次几度地拽动天空。锚定于此的传感器中枢啜饮着没人费心编目的游离辐射，然后把跃迁图悄悄推偏几个零头——足以让整支车队贴着另一段黑暗掠过。无论是什么从这个视角监视航道，它都做了很久，久到航向修正与"无害"绕行开始堆叠成一个没人愿意承认自己看见过的模式。从边境岩石上一块被遗忘的数据板，到全都归咎于同一"幽灵故障"的车队报告，再到一座塞满偷来的舰队数学的废弃节点，我碰过的每一块碎片都指向有人在官方航线之下绘制第二套路线，仿佛定居星系一直在睡梦中沿着一条他们从未选择的路径行走。

#en: The UC warship hanging cold in the dark is where the patterns finally start to line up; only a combat ship with classified telemetry and sealed routing orders could carry the kind of navigational truth everyone else has been careful to obscure behind jargon, half-redacted reports, and convenient memory lapses. Its designation still whispers authority, even as the hull scars and powered-down guns say it was written out of the official story, a perfect vault for records nobody wants to acknowledge exist. Here, buried in Navy systems, is where whispers about bad drives, missing recalls, and engineered failures either converge into something solid or dissolve into sanctioned amnesia. So far the trail runs like this: a stray slate in the dust, scattered logs in a lonely outpost, glitching data on a small, drifting hull, and now a warship whose silence says more than any testimony ever has.
zh: 那艘冷寂地悬在黑暗中的联殖军舰，是这些模式终于开始对齐的地方；只有一艘带着机密遥测与密封路由命令的战斗舰，才可能承载那种别人都小心翼翼地用术语、半涂黑报告与"方便的记忆空白"掩盖起来的导航真相。它的编号仍在低语着权威，即便船壳上的伤痕与断电的枪炮说明它已被写出了官方故事——一件存放"没人愿意承认存在之记录"的完美保险库。在这里、埋在海军系统里的某处，关于坏引擎、失踪召回与被人为制造的故障的低语，要么汇聚成某种坚实之物，要么消散成获批的失忆。目前为止，线索是这样的：尘土里一块散落数据板、一座孤独前哨里零散的日志、一具小而漂移的船壳上闪故障的数据，如今又是一艘沉默比任何证词都说得更多的军舰。

#en: Only in the quiet between planets could she afford to be careless, stashing her trail in the shadow of a drifting hull and trusting that no one would look twice at another dead ship in a busy grav lane. Out here, far from city sensors and frontier gossip, familiar routines do the hiding for her: patrols skim past on autopilot, haulers file their standard reports, and yet one vessel hangs slightly off its declared vector, its systems humming just enough to keep a buried grid alive. Crack this shell and the pattern she has been flying suddenly has a spine, a plotted route back to the place she erased from every official record. So far the trail has been fragments and afterthoughts a stray slate in the back country, altered logs from a ruined farm, a nervous broker on Neon, a broken survey cutter full of curses and half a jump plan all pointing toward something she once called Hearthline.
zh: 只有在行星之间的安静里，她才负担得起粗心：把痕迹藏在某具漂移船壳的阴影下，并笃信没人会对一条繁忙引力航道里又一艘死船多看一眼。在这里，远离城市传感器与边境闲话，熟悉的惯例替她藏身：巡逻队在自动驾驶下掠过、货船提交标准报告，而偏偏有一艘船微微偏离它申报的向量，系统嗡鸣得刚好够让一张被埋的电网存活。撬开这具外壳，她一直飞行的模式就突然有了脊柱，一条绘回她从所有官方记录上抹掉之处的路线。目前为止，这条线索是碎片与事后的想法：乡间一块散落数据板、一座毁坏农场上被改动的日志、霓虹城一名紧张的掮客、一艘塞满咒骂与半份跃迁计划的破损勘探切割船，全都指向她一度称作"炉线"的东西。

#en: The science facility hangs in the dark like a sealed wound, its official Reliant Medical transponder the perfect mask for what has been growing inside. Here Stitch has everything he needs in one sterile shell: containment fields for unwilling donors, chem labs for his counter-formulas, servers to house every forbidden triage decision he ever logged. The stolen stimulants, vanished organ tags, and black-box data all converge on this lab, feeding a single, coherent design to break the scarcity he blames on UC and corporate hands. If he secures his archive and stabilizes his latest blends, that design spills uncontrolled across the Settled Systems. Back at the maintenance bay, the first hint was a too-clean table and missing chems; at the blood-slick track, whispers and doctored logs proved he was still practicing, just out of sight of those who swear they saw nothing worth worrying about.
zh: 那座科研设施像一道封住的伤口悬在黑暗中，它官方"信实医疗"的应答器为内部正在滋长的一切提供了完美的面具。在这里，"缝合"在一个无菌外壳里拥有了他需要的一切：为不自愿供体准备的隔离场、为他那些对抗配方准备的化学实验室、以及存放他记录过的每一次禁忌分诊决策的服务器。被盗的兴奋剂、消失的器官标签与黑匣数据全都汇聚到这座实验室，喂养着一个单一而连贯的设计——用来打破他归咎于联殖与公司之手的稀缺。若他保住自己的档案并稳定最新配方，那个设计就会不受控地溢满定居星系。回到那间维修舱，第一条线索是一张干净得过分的桌子与失踪的药剂；在血迹黏滑的赛道上，低语与被做手脚的日志证明他仍在行医，只是离开了那些发誓"没看见任何值得担心之事"之人的视线。

#en: Out here the research module hangs quiet over nothing much at all, exactly the kind of place bureaucrats forget and contractors exploit. This is where analysts once pulled threads on stolen data, cross-checking corridor updates and ship manifests until their questions started drifting too close to someone's off-the-books routes. Whatever record survived will not be loud, just a buried file or half-archived trace that shows which jump patterns were nudged, when, and for whose benefit. A thousand tiny approvals, ignored discrepancies, and "temporary" fixes must have piled up in these systems until entire ships vanished off their own charts. So far the trail is a scrubbed slate on a lonely rock and scattered notes about disrupted theft chains, all pointing toward a navigator who has been working the gaps between what was reported and what really happened for far longer than anyone admitted.
zh: 在这里，那座研究舱安静地悬在几乎一无所有之上，正是官僚会遗忘、承包商会利用的那类地方。这里曾是分析员们追查被盗数据线索的地方，他们交叉核对走廊更新与船只舱单，直到自己的问题开始靠某人的账外航线太近。存活下来的任何记录都不会张扬，只是一份被埋的文件或半归档的痕迹，显示哪些跃迁模式被推动过、在何时、以及为了谁的利益。一千个微小的批准、被忽略的差异与"临时"修补，必然在这些系统里堆叠，直到整艘整艘的船从自己的星图上消失。目前为止，这条线索是一块孤独岩石上被擦净的数据板与关于被打断的盗窃链的零散笔记，全都指向一名领航员——他在"被报告的"与"真正发生的"之间的空档里运作的时间，比任何人承认的都长。

#en: The listening post sits at the edge of forgotten space, a rusting ear pointed toward the lanes long after its operators packed up and left, never bothering to ask what their machines kept hearing. The array buried here has been singing to itself for years, stitching together the subtle shoves and course corrections that turn routine jumps into slow-motion collisions, and the Salvage Crown Syndicate is only guarding it because they know anything this old and this secret has to be worth something. Whatever patterns have been recorded are anchored to this spot; pull them here and the whole map of nudged ships and curated wrecks shifts into focus. So far, all you have are a stray scrap of data from a backwater world and an abandoned relay humming with mismatched pings, both pointing to someone who started re-writing the lanes and then walked away before anyone understood what that would mean.
zh: 那座听音哨坐落在被遗忘太空的边缘，一只生锈的耳朵指向航道，而在它的操作员早已打包离开、从未费心问过他们的机器一直在听什么之后很久。埋在这里的阵列多年来一直在对自己歌唱，把那些把例行跃迁变成慢动作碰撞的细微推搡与航向修正缝在一起；"打捞王冠辛迪加"守着它，只是因为他们知道任何这么古老、这么隐秘的东西必然值点钱。被记录下的任何模式都锚定在这个点上；在这里把它们拉出来，那些被推动的船只与被策展的残骸的整张地图就会清晰起来。目前为止，你只有一穷乡世界上一块散落的数据碎片与一座嗡鸣着对不上脉冲的废弃中继，两者都指向某个开始改写航道、然后在任何人明白那意味着什么之前就走开的人。

#en: The automated harvesting platform drifts half-buried in the asteroid field, its cutters long silent, but its navigation spine still humming with course data no miner ever needed. This is where someone clever would hide a signal that piggybacks on routine telemetry, a quiet tug on any condemned ship routed along certain corridors, bending traffic toward the same patch of forgotten sky. The field itself keeps prying eyes away; only scavvers and the desperate risk threading these rocks, and even they give this hulk a wide berth without saying why. When the topic surfaces in mess halls and dock bars, the ones who work these lanes glance away, change subjects, pretend not to remember which wrecks vanished out here. So far the trail is a dead spacer's logs, a scrubbed patrol grid, and a deserter's stolen scans, all pointing to ships being steered off manifest into the dark by the same unseen hand.
zh: 那座自动化收割平台半埋在岩石场里漂着，它的切割臂早已沉默，可导航脊柱仍在嗡鸣着没有任何矿工需要的航向数据。这里正是某个聪明人会藏一道信号的地方——它搭在例行遥测的顺风车上，对任何沿特定走廊航行的报废船只轻轻一拽，把交通掰向同一片被遗忘的天空。岩石场本身挡住了窥探的眼睛；只有拾荒者与走投无路的人才冒险穿过这些岩石，而连他们都会不言原因地远远绕开这具残骸。当话题在食堂与码头酒吧浮现时，跑这些航道的人会移开目光、换个话题、假装不记得哪些残骸在这里消失。目前为止，这条线索是一块死掉太空劫匪的日志、一张被擦净的巡逻网格，以及一名逃兵偷来的扫描，全都指向船只在同一只无形之手的引导下被推出舱单、驶入黑暗。

#en: The orbit here is crowded with junk traffic and idle sats, a forgotten ring of hardware looping a world nobody bothers to check twice. That is precisely why the cache matters  a tiny misfiled update, some long-abandoned protocol left running on auto, and over time the system learned to route more and more course corrections through this one quiet lane. Now a lone escort, the ST-6273 Starblade, circles the clutter like it is guarding nothing at all, which makes it the most suspicious ship in local space. Somewhere in that tangle sits the key that links her hidden station to the rest of the grid.  \n\nSo far the trail runs from a stray dataslate on a backwater rock, through odd shipment timing flagged in farm logs, then into a dead relay still watching the skies on forgotten orders, each step revealing the same pattern of diverted routes and one navigator quietly bending traffic around herself.
zh: 这里的轨道挤满了废旧交通与闲置卫星，一圈被遗忘的硬件环绕着一颗没人费心复核两次的世界。这正是那处储藏点要紧的原因：一次微小的归档错误的更新、某个被遗弃后仍在自动运行的协议，久而久之，系统学会了把越来越多的航向修正经由这一条安静的航道。如今一艘单独的护航船，"ST-6273 星刃"，绕着那团杂物打转，像在守着一无所有——这让它成了本地区最可疑的飞船。在那团乱麻里某处，坐着那把把她隐藏的星际站与这张网格其余部分连起来的钥匙。  \n\n目前为止，线索从一穷乡岩石上一块散落数据板，穿过农场日志里被标记出来的古怪货运时机，然后钻进一座仍在按被遗忘命令注视着天空的死中继，每一步都揭示出同样的被改道航线模式，以及一名在自己周围悄悄掰弯交通的领航员。

#en: Only in high orbit does the pattern resolve: the beacon hangs in a thin sliver of space where grav readings slip between official survey grids, exactly the kind of blind angle a former stress analyst would trust more than any report. The Bloodwake holds position over it like a hired lock, Crimson Fleet gunners watching a prize they only half understand, guarding echoes of drive failures and lane distortions that have been traded as rumor and bar-talk so long the edges have worn smooth. Tapping this node here, at the point where his stolen models and real-space anomalies intersect, is the only way to separate myth from math and follow the chain back to its source. Up to now, the trail has been redacted incident logs in a quiet lab, frightened technicians hinting at tampered safety systems, and captains passing around distorted tales of a vanished analyst who keeps turning accidents into messages.
zh: 只有在高轨道，这个模式才清晰起来：那座信标悬在一条细狭的太空隙缝里，引力读数从官方勘探网格之间滑过——正是前应力分析员会信任甚于任何报告的盲角。"血尾流"像一把租来的锁般守在其上方，深红舰队的炮手看守着一件他们只懂一半的战利品，守着引擎故障与航道畸变的回声——它们被当作传闻与酒吧闲谈交易得太久，棱角都已磨平。在这里、在他被偷的模型与真实空间异常相交的节点上接入，是分辨神话与数学、并顺着链条追回源头的唯一办法。目前为止，这条线索是某间安静实验室里涂黑的事件日志、暗示安全系统被动手脚的受惊技师，以及船长们传述着关于一名失踪分析员的扭曲故事——他把事故不断变成信息。

#en: The Deimos yard is where old metal comes to be stripped of its identity, and that makes it the perfect place to hide a record no one wants to admit exists. Between rusted hull frames and half-gutted drive cores, the Hellbound Dustwalkers pick at whatever is left, selling stories about "bad jumps" and "cursed ships" to anyone who pays for drama, sanding the sharp edges off what really happened until it sounds like bar gossip instead of evidence. Somewhere under their grease-stained terminals and repurposed cores is the straight version, the one name and series of routes that keep showing up behind every quiet disaster. Up to now it is all been secondhand: a corrupted ping from a lonely outpost, a freighter log that did not match its manifest, a whispered account over cheap liquor in Neon and a half-joking warning from a freestar drifter about a hunter who follows broken drives instead of bounties.
zh: 火卫二场区，是旧金属被剥去身份的地方，这让它成了藏起一份"没人愿意承认存在之记录"的完美地点。在锈蚀的船壳框架与半掏空的引擎核心之间，地狱尘行者拾捡着剩下的东西，向任何愿意为戏剧性付钱的人兜售"坏跃迁"与"被诅咒的船"的故事，把真正发生之事磨平棱角，直到它听起来像酒吧闲话而非证据。在他们油污斑斑的终端与被改作他用的核心之下某处，是那个直白的版本：一个不断出现在每一场安静灾难背后的名字与一连串航线。到目前为止，全都是二手的：一座孤独前哨传来的损坏脉冲、一份与舱单不符的货船日志、霓虹城廉价烈酒间的一句低语，以及一名自由星系联盟流浪者关于"追着坏引擎而非赏金的猎人"的半开玩笑警告。

#en: The orbital-drop shelter is where the stories start overlapping, so if any place holds a trace of what really moved through those corridors, it is here among the scorched bulkheads and half-packed crates. Its battered consoles still hum with old traffic patterns, gaps and timing windows someone carved into the lanes and then tried to scrub away in a hurry. The liaison swore a navigator had threaded their runs through those gaps, but every retelling shifted a little: different rendezvous times, different exit points, always the same unseen hand. From manifests that do not balance at the mid-tier port, to a smuggler convoy that arrived early without extra burn, to whispers of charts marked with symbols no official route uses, every fragment points back to the same thing; someone is editing space itself, and this shelter is where their edits first brushed the people desperate enough to pay for them.
zh: 那座轨道投放掩体，正是故事开始重叠的地方；所以若有哪处保存着"真正穿过那些走廊的是什么"的痕迹，那就是这里——在烧焦的舱壁与半打包的箱子之间。它破损的控制台仍嗡鸣着旧交通模式，那些有人刻进航道、随后又匆忙试图擦掉的空缺与时机窗口。联络官发誓有一名领航员把他们的航次穿过了那些空缺，可每一次转述都稍有偏移：不同的会合时间、不同的出口点，永远是同一只看不见的手。从中间层港市对不上的舱单，到一支没额外点火却提前抵达的走私车队，再到关于"用任何官方航线都不用的符号标记星图"的低语，每一块碎片都指回同一件事：有人在编辑太空本身，而这座掩体正是他们的编辑最先触碰到那些绝望到愿意付钱之人的地方。

#en: The autonomous factory is the first place the numbers stopped adding up and the machines started whispering someone else's intent, which is why the file you are after would be buried here, half-forgotten in a system no one thinks to audit. Its guidance arrays sit at the crossroads of production and transit, where altered routes and stray rescue-frequency echoes can be dismissed as software noise, and where a mercenary outfit can loiter under contract cover without raising corporate alarms. Forward Shadowline holds this ground like they expect someone to come back for what was started in the diagnostics then abruptly abandoned mid-entry, a trail of half-written logs and rerouted shipments left hanging in mid-process. So far, all we have is a dead tech at a remote relay, a pattern of nudged shipping lanes, and scattered stories of a rescue pilot who always arrives just before the reports go missing.
zh: 那座自动化工厂是数字第一次不再对得上、机器开始低语别人意图的地方，这正是你要找的那份文件会被埋在这里的原因——半遗忘在一个没人想着去审计的系统里。它的制导阵列坐落在生产与运输的十字路口：在那里，被改动的航线与游离的救援频率回声都能被当作软件噪声打发；在那里，一支佣兵队伍能借合同掩护徘徊而不触发公司警报。"前锋暗影线"守在这片地面上，像在等着有人回来取那些在诊断中开始、随后又中途突然弃置的东西：一串写到一半的日志与被改道的货运，悬在流程中间。目前为止，我们只有一名死在远程中继的技师、一种被推动航运航道的模式，以及关于一名"总在报告消失之前恰好抵达"的救援飞行员零散的故事。

#en: Down here in Neon's Underbelly, nothing ever really leaves; it just seeps into the corners, into the pipes, into the people no one looks at twice. If someone wanted to bleed off the traces of bad jumps, scrub drive signatures and dump whatever a Grav core should never carry, it would end up in these channels, where runoff and secrets share the same conduits. The grid hums overhead, lights strobing through steam, and every maintenance hatch looks like it has not been opened in years, despite the warmth of recent work on the seals. This place has a habit of holding onto cargo, chems, even bodies longer than anyone planned, and the same goes for data ghosts. So far the trail has been a crooked line: a discarded slate on a forgotten rock, smeared beacon logs in lonely orbit, and a derelict Trade Authority hauler whose corrupted records all whisper the same name and point, again and again, toward Neon.
zh: 在霓虹城的下腹，没有什么东西真正离开过；它只是渗进角落、渗进管道、渗进那些没人会多看一眼的人里。若有人想把坏跃迁的痕迹放掉、擦净引擎签名、倾倒任何引力核心本绝不该携带的东西，它就会流进这些水道——径流与机密共用同一批管道。网格在头顶嗡鸣，灯光穿过蒸汽频闪，每一扇维护舱门看上去都像多年没开过，尽管密封圈上还有近期作业的余温。这地方有个习惯，会把货物、药剂、甚至尸体留得比任何人计划的都久，数据幽灵也一样。目前为止，这条线索是一条歪斜的线：被遗忘岩石上一块被丢弃的数据板、孤独轨道上被拖抹的信标日志，以及一艘损坏的贸易管理局货船——它损坏的记录全都低语着同一个名字，并一次又一次地指向霓虹城。

#en: Neon's rooftops are the only place he can see the whole grid he has been bending, a tangle of star lanes, corporate pads, and anonymous freighters lifting off into the storms beyond the Span. Up here, away from official flight control, Vector can patch directly into illicit nav buoys and shipboard relays, finalizing the jump lattice that will carry his most loyal captains beyond anyone's jurisdiction. If he finishes the work, his shadow routes harden into a permanent artery no faction can shut down without crippling their own traffic. A missed timestamp at a remote cache, a garbled Ryujin memo, and a SysDef analyst reading the wrong transponder log brought the trail here; a stolen dataslate in the hinterlands, quiet questions in a Neon tower, and a drifting tactical hull full of corrupted VectorSet runs all pointed to the same conclusion: someone has been rewriting how ships move through the dark.
zh: 霓虹城的屋顶，是他唯一能看清自己一直在掰弯的整张网格的地方：一团由星际航道、公司停机坪，以及升入桥架之外风暴的无名货船构成的乱麻。在这里，远离官方飞行控制，"向量"能直接接进非法导航浮标与船载中继，最终确定那张将把他最忠诚的船长们带出任何人管辖的跃迁网格。若他完成这项工作，他的影子航线就会硬化成一条任何派系都无法在不残废自身交通的情况下关闭的永久动脉。一处远程储藏点错过的时戳、一份乱码的龙神备忘录，以及一名读错应答器日志的星防队分析员，把线索带到了这里；腹地里一块被偷的数据板、霓虹城某座塔里安静的提问，以及一具塞满损坏 VectorSet 运行的漂移战术船壳，全都指向同一个结论：有人在改写船只如何在黑暗中移动。

#en: Out here, among rusted hulls and half gutted frames, Deadlock is surrounded by the language he understands best; every twisted beam and stripped Grav Drive mount is a tool he has already weighed and repurposed in his head. The abandoned Deimos scrapyard sits just far enough from official lanes for SysDef to look the other way, and close enough to old contracts that he can bleed value from forgotten war steel while he finishes what he started with those stolen schematics. If he is going to lock his story into place forever, burying evidence or rigging one last structural collapse to erase his part in the Vanguard disaster, it will be here, where corporate ledgers already read "written off." They counted on time and paperwork to smother this mess, but yard logs in a quiet corner, a runaway field tech in a buried bunker, and loose tongues in Gagarin Landing kept dragging his name back into circulation.
zh: 在这里，在锈蚀的船壳与被掏空一半的框架之间，"死锁"被他最了解的语言环绕；每一根扭曲的梁与每一个被剥光的引力引擎支架，都是他已在脑中称量并改作他用的工具。那座废弃的火卫二废料场离官方航道刚好足够远、让星防队转开视线，又离旧合同足够近、让他能在完成那些偷来的图纸所开始之事的同时从被遗忘的战争钢铁里榨取价值。若他要把自己的故事永久锁死——埋葬证据或策划最后一次结构坍塌来抹掉他在先锋队灾难中的角色——就会在这里，在公司账册早已写着"已核销"的地方。他们指望时间与文书闷死这摊烂局，可安静角落里的一份场区日志、一座被埋掩体里一名出走的战地技师，以及加加林着陆点里的碎嘴，都不断把他的名字拖回流言中。

#en: Out here, away from ports and patrol routes, the orbital lane is almost empty, which is exactly why this fragment of navigation data matters. No station traffic to muddy it, no civilian relays rewriting it for convenience; only raw vectors showing where the hidden tankers break from registered routes and vanish toward whatever off-grid cistern Catalyst favors. The RD-1964 Scrapviper circling this rock is not here by chance; someone paid Spacers to sit on these numbers and make sure no one compares them to what Cydonia and Neon keep on file. Some haulers swear they have seen ghost convoys peeling off into dark space, others shrug and say it is just spacer exaggeration. So far the trail runs from a dead relay sheltering bad manifests, through whispered complaints in Neon's underlevels, to mismatched cargo records at the mining hub, all pointing to a single hand quietly redrawing where the water flows.
zh: 在这里，远离港口与巡逻航线，那条轨道几乎空无一物，这正是这块导航数据值得在意的原因。没有星际站交通把它搅浑，没有民用中继为方便而改写它；只有赤裸的向量，显示那些隐藏的罐车在何处脱离登记航线、消失向"催化剂"偏爱的某座账外蓄水池。绕着这块岩石的"RD-1964 废料蝰蛇"不是偶然在此；有人付钱给太空劫匪，让他们盯着这些数字、确保没人把它们与赛多尼亚和霓虹城存档的内容比对。有些货船船工发誓见过幽灵车队脱离驶入黑暗太空，另一些人则耸肩说那不过是太空劫匪的夸张。目前为止，线索从一座庇护坏舱单的死中继，穿过霓虹城下城层里压低声音的抱怨，到采矿枢纽处对不上的货运记录，全都指向一只手在悄悄重画水流的方向。

#en: The retreat sits alone against the sky, a place people come to forget things and be forgotten in turn, which makes it the only fitting ground for a record that was never meant to survive. Its cabins and storm-scarred outbuildings shelter more ghosts than guests, and someone has threaded those ghosts into neat columns of names and dates, then cut the pages off where the stories turn ugly. Whatever was written here links the missing settlers, the quiet screenings, and that soft-voiced courier whose trail never quite lines up, but whole segments of memory feel shaved away, like everyone present agreed which parts would never be spoken of. So far the trail is simple on paper and twisted in the telling: a stray slate on a dead rock, altered logs in a backline clinic, a medic who remembered a Belizean accent, and an old missioner who kept careful lists of people who met the same woman and never came home.
zh: 那座隐居地孤零零地倚着天空，一个人们来此遗忘事情、也反过来被遗忘的地方——这让它成了唯一适合存放一份"本不该存活之记录"的地面。它的木屋与布满风暴伤痕的附属建筑庇护的幽灵比客人还多，而有人把那些幽灵穿成了整齐的名字与日期之列，然后在故事变丑的地方把书页剪掉。在这里写下的无论什么，都把失踪的定居者、安静筛查，以及那名行踪总对不上的柔和嗓音信使系在一起，可整段整段的记忆感觉被削掉了，仿佛在场所有人都同意哪些部分将永不被提起。目前为止，这条线索在纸面上简单、在转述中扭曲：死岩石上一块散落数据板、后方诊所里被改动的日志、一名记得伯利兹口音的医疗兵，以及一名仔细列出"见过同一个女人、再没回家的人"的老传教士。

#en: If she has been feeding altered routes into the lanes, the only place to catch the pattern clean is at the heart of sanctioned traffic, where every freighter, courier, and shadow-run must file a story about how it came and went. New Atlantis hums with official versioned truth, but in its freight offices and backroom berths the real paths are whispered, sold, and quietly forgotten as long as the cargo keeps flowing. Buried among routine manifests and hushed arguments over who took which shortcut, there will be one thread that repeats the same off-lane approach too many times to be coincidence, a line no one will admit to plotting but everyone seems to have used. So far the trail is a stray dataslate on a backwater world, wreck reports from vanished settlers, and salvaged records from a stripped-out yard, all hinting that someone has been bending the safe corridors away from where the maps say they go.
zh: 若她一直在把被改动的航线喂进航道，那唯一能干净捕捉到这个模式的地方，就是获批交通的心脏——在那里，每一艘货船、信使船与影子航次都必须提交一份关于它如何来去的说法。新亚特兰蒂斯城嗡鸣着官方的版本化真相，但在它的货运办公室与后室泊位里，真正的路径被低语、被买卖、被悄悄遗忘——只要货物继续流动。埋在例行舱单与关于"谁抄了哪条近路"的低声争吵之间，会有一根线把同一种偏航进近重复太多次、无法当作巧合：一条没人愿意承认自己绘过、却似乎人人都用过的线。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡世界上一块散落数据板、失踪定居者的残骸报告，以及一座被剥光场区里打捞出的记录，全都暗示有人一直在把安全走廊掰离星图所指之处。

#en: This forgotten depot sits at the edge of every shipping lane and nobody's responsibility, a place where manifests go missing and hardware "tested to failure" is stacked out of sight. If someone wanted to slip a piece of code into the flow of cargo, to quietly rewrite how drives behave from the shadows, this is the kind of dead corner they would use as a staging ground. The Deadspace crew here watch their words as closely as their smuggling routes, like people who have seen what happens when you speculate too loudly about why certain ships never make it home. So far the trail has been a scattering of corrupted logs from a remote outpost and murmurs at a derelict yard, all hinting that someone has been tuning accidents into a pattern and that the next link in that chain was born right here, between rusting containers and men who have learned that survival means keeping your opinions carefully measured.
zh: 这座被遗忘的货运站坐落在每条航运航线的边缘与"谁都不管"之间，一个舱单失踪、被"测试到失效"的硬件堆在视线之外的地方。若有人想把一段代码溜进货物流动里，从阴影中悄悄改写引擎的行为，这就是他们会用作集结场的那种死角。这里的死域帮看守自己的言辞就像看守自己的走私航线，像那些见识过"过分大声猜测某些船为何从不归家会发生什么"的人。目前为止，这条线索是一座远程前哨零散的损坏日志与某座废弃场区的低语，全都暗示有人一直在把事故调成一个模式，而那条链上的下一环就诞生在这里——在锈蚀的货柜与那些学会了"活命意味着小心拿捏意见"的人之间。

#en: The old UC garrison sits half-swallowed by dust and neglect, its crest worn down to a pale shadow, yet the mainframe still breathes on emergency power, cycling through long-forgotten patrol grids as if the war never ended. This is where numbers were quietly nudged, where a single line of code could slide a convoy a few degrees off safety, and where no one bothered to check the logs once the banners came down. Now a salvage gang works the bones, Dead Orbit Claim Jumpers stringing lights through dead corridors, swearing they are only here for scrap while they stand watch over a core that has been shaping routes longer than anyone noticed. Back at the moonside relay, contraband manifests showed the same tiny course corrections repeated across years, and the first dataslate in that remote dustbowl flagged matching designations; the trail keeps circling back to one unseen hand rewriting risk into routine.
zh: 那座旧联殖驻军半被尘土与荒废吞没，它的徽记磨损成淡影，可主框架仍在应急电力上呼吸，循环着早已被遗忘的巡逻网格，仿佛战争从未结束。这里正是数字被悄悄推动的地方，一行代码就能让一支车队滑出安全几度；也是旗帜一落下就没人费心去查日志的地方。如今一伙打捞帮派在骨架上作业——"死轨抢矿队"在死走廊里串起灯线，发誓只为废料而来，一边看守着一个塑造航道比任何人注意到的都久的核心。回到卫星侧中继，走私舱单显示同样微小的航向修正年复一年地重复，而偏远尘暴窝里第一块数据板标记了相符的编号；线索不断绕回同一只无形之手，把风险改写成例行公事。

#en: The Well is where her numbers were first written in flesh, where overdue notices and hunger taught her what a balance sheet never could; if she is going to prove that the core can be strangled the way the lower decks were, she has to do it from here, buried under New Atlantis where the city will feel every flicker. She has laced forgotten GalBank conduits into the grid, piggybacking old hydro controls and maintenance lines so one last simulated panic can lock accounts across the capital before anyone can cut power, and the murmur among locals is not outrage but uneasy hope that a little chaos might finally count in their favor. Earlier, ledgers in Neon's shadows and scrubbed audit files aboard a drifting SysDef hulk traced the same careful hand, the same rehearsed disaster, all pointing back to the woman who grew up in these corridors and decided the safest place to break the system was at its heart.
zh: 深井区，是她的数字第一次被写进血肉的地方——在那里，逾期通知与饥饿教会了她资产负债表永远教不了的东西；若她要证明核心也能像下层甲板那样被扼住喉咙，就必须从这里下手：埋在新亚特兰蒂斯城之下，让这座城市感受到每一次闪烁。她把被遗忘的盖尔银行导管接进电网，搭着旧水力控制与维护线的顺风车，好让最后一次模拟恐慌在任何人能切断电力之前锁死首都各地的账户；而当地人的低语不是愤怒，而是一种不安的希望——希望这点混乱最终能对他们有利。早先，霓虹城阴影里的账册与一具漂着的星防队船壳上被擦净的审计文件，追着同一只谨慎的手、同一场排练过的灾难，全都指回那个在这些走廊里长大、并认定"打破系统的最安全之处就是它的心脏"的女人。

#en: The dead moon was never meant to matter; just another UC listening post left to rot once newer arrays came online. Yet this is where the lattice tightens. Every dish, every buried relay, every forgotten buffer Omar ever bent to his own geometry converges here, feeding the phantom corridors that let ships slip off the starmap and never return. He is using the station as both shield and scalpel, realigning ancient hardware to push a belt of derelicts into living lanes and burn the last surviving record of his routes. The place feels half-erased, as if some clerk meant to decommission it and never came back, leaving a perfect blind spot for him to finish his work. Back at the first derelict hangar it was only erased flight plans and gossip; at the relay on that airless moon it became contraband manifests and altered hashes, all pointing to the same invisible road and the same quiet hand on the controls.
zh: 那颗死卫星本不该有任何意义；不过是又一座在新阵列上线后被弃置腐坏的联殖听音哨。然而这里正是网格收紧之处。每一面天线盘、每一座被埋的中继、每一个被奥马尔掰向他自己的几何的遗忘缓冲区，都汇聚于此，喂养着那些让船只从星图上溜走、再不复返的幽灵走廊。他把这座星际站同时当作盾牌与手术刀，重校古旧的硬件，把一条环绕的弃船带推进活航道，并烧掉他航线最后存活的记录。这地方感觉被抹掉了一半，仿佛某个文书本想退役它、却再没回来，从而给他留下一个完成工作的完美盲点。回到第一座弃船机库，那只是被抹除的飞行计划与闲话；在那颗无气卫星上的中继，它变成了走私舱单与被改动的哈希值，全都指向同一条看不见的路与同一只安静搭在操纵装置上的手。

#en: The fields look like any other out on the fringe  tilled soil, tired fences, a farmhouse patched more with hope than credits. That is why this place matters. Out here, a single extra antenna buried under corrugated scrap, a timing anomaly in the crop shipments, a power draw that does not match the tools on site  it all blends into the background until someone stares hard enough. Whatever has been riding the farm's signal out to orbit is small, consistent, and just clever enough to pass for noise. Strip that carrier down and the route it is feeding becomes obvious, even if the reason it was hidden stays stubbornly plain.  \n\nSo far the trail is little more than fragments  a stray dataslate on a lonely rock, whispers about impossible delivery windows, and now a homestead whose transmissions do not match the life it pretends to live, all hinting at one navigator quietly tightening her grip on the lanes.
zh: 这些田地在边境上看起来和别处一样——翻耕过的土壤、疲惫的围栏、一座用希望比用信用币修补得更多的农舍。这就是这地方要紧的原因。在这里，一根埋在波纹废料下的多余天线、作物货运里的一处时机异常、与现场工具对不上的耗电——全都融进背景，直到有人盯得足够用力。一直在把这座农场的信号送进轨道的那个东西很小、很稳定，也刚好聪明到能冒充噪声。把那个载波剥离下来，它正在喂养的航线就一目了然，即便它被藏起来的原因仍顽固地浅白。  \n\n目前为止，这条线索无非是碎片——孤独岩石上一块散落数据板、关于"不可能的配送窗口"的低语，如今又是一座传输与它所假装的生活不符的农庄，全都暗示一名领航员在悄悄收紧她对航道的掌控。

#en: Whoever met this agent chose a place far from any official channel, a patch of ground where uniforms and badges stop meaning anything and the only currency is what you whisper and who you trust not to repeat it. Whatever he managed to pull together out here will not exist in any sanctioned archive; if there is a thread that ties her falsified approvals to missing ships and off grid settlements, it will be in whatever he was too cautious to send over open comms. This is the sort of lead that gets traded in half sentences between old comrades, then buried when the wrong ears get close. So far all I have are those fragments a caseworker muttering about duplicated IDs, a ruined homestead with its logs scrubbed crooked, a broker on Neon fencing partial routes, and a derelict cutter whose last jump pointed into nameless dark all different pieces of the same story no one is willing to tell from start to finish.
zh: 凡是见过这名特工的人，都选了一个远离任何官方信道的地方——一片制服与徽章不再有任何意义的地面，唯一流通的货币是你低语的内容，以及你信任谁不去重复它。他在这里设法拼起来的东西不会存在于任何获批档案里；若说有一根线把她伪造的批准与失踪船只和账外定居点系起来，它就会在那些他谨慎到不敢通过公开通讯发送的东西里。这是那种会在老战友之间用半句话交易的线索，然后在错误的耳朵靠近时被埋葬。目前为止，我只有那些碎片：一名案件员嘟囔着重复的 ID、一座日志被歪斜擦净的毁坏农庄、霓虹城一名兜售部分航线的掮客，以及一艘最后一次跃迁指向无名黑暗的弃置切割船——同一个故事的不同碎片，而没人愿意把它从头讲到尾。

#en: Out here, the orbital lane looks empty, but the transponder chatter tells another story: rerouted freighters, misfiled cargo tags, course corrections that never got signed off by anyone with a name. If someone wanted to hide a pattern of impossible jumps, they would bury it in the paperwork of space itself, in manifests and drift reports that never quite matched what the beacons saw. This patch of sky is where those errors converge, where a crate that should have burned up in reentry is still tumbling cold, carrying the record of which ships slipped sideways through the dark and who was flying them. So far the trail has been a chain of small mistakes and quiet edits: a lost slate on a forgotten rock, smeared jump logs around a lonely planet, and a Trade Authority hull with waste cycles that did not match its registered route, all circling back toward the same pilot and the routes he refuses to let go of.
zh: 在这里，轨道航道看似空荡，可应答器的闲谈讲的是另一个故事：被改道的货船、归档错误的货物标签、从未被任何有名字的人签批过的航向修正。若有人想藏起一个不可能跃迁的模式，他们会把它埋进太空本身的文书里——埋进那些从不完全与信标所见相符的舱单与漂移报告里。这片天空正是那些错误汇聚之处：一个本该在再入时烧毁的货箱仍在冰冷翻滚，携带着"哪些船侧身滑过黑暗、又是谁在驾驶它们"的记录。目前为止，这条线索是一串小错误与安静的编辑：一块被遗忘岩石上丢失的数据板、一颗孤独行星周围被拖抹的跃迁日志，以及一具废料循环与登记航线不符的贸易管理局船壳，全都绕回同一名飞行员和他拒绝放手的航线。

#en: The trail runs through this forgotten depot because that is where freight stops being cargo and starts becoming leverage. Old containers sit stacked in the dust, manifests half-burned or rewritten, watched over by ex-military who know how to hold a perimeter and how to keep their mouths shut. Whatever crate the defectors chose to guard out here is not about its contents but about the routes and signatures attached to it, the quiet redirection of value from one set of hands to another. Among the Breakaway crew, stories about why they left and who gave the order never quite match, but no one presses; out here, arguing about the past is a good way to get shot in the present. So far the chase has moved from an anonymous slate in deep space to nervous dockside whispers and skewed port schedules, each step pointing toward a deliberate reshaping of traffic that always seems to benefit the same invisible banker.
zh: 线索穿过这座被遗忘的货运站，因为那里正是货运不再只是货物、而开始变成筹码的地方。旧货柜堆在尘土里，舱单半烧毁或被重写，由懂得如何守住周界、如何闭紧嘴巴的老兵看守。那些叛逃者选择在这里看守的无论什么货箱，重点都不在内容，而在附着其上的航线与签名：价值从一组手中被悄悄转往另一组手中。在分裂打击群里，关于他们为何离开、谁下的命令，说法从来对不上，可没人追问；在这里，争论过去是在当下挨枪子的好办法。目前为止，这场追查从深空中一块匿名数据板，移动到码头边紧张的低语与歪斜的港务日程，每一步都指向一次刻意的交通重塑——它似乎总是有利于同一个看不见的银行家。

#en: Every broken hull that drifts through this pit leaves a little truth behind, buried under rust and spacer lies. Out here, where cutters work by lantern-glow and ownership papers are a joke, nobody audits where a datapack came from or why its casing was half-melted when it arrived. That makes this salvage trench the only place a saboteur could afford to throw away a fragment of their own flight path, trusting the noise of scavenger gossip to drown it. Word is the pack came off a ship that "just spun itself apart" near old war corridors; some say a ghosted drive, some swear a quiet hand pulled the failsafes. So far the trail has run from a nameless outpost slate to a dead freight yard and then into Neon's service guts, each step humming with the same pattern of bad jumps, missing annexes, and that angled mark in the logs that keeps showing up wherever engines die for reasons no one wants to put in writing.
zh: 每一个漂过这个坑的破损船壳都会留下一点真相，埋在锈迹与太空劫匪的谎言之下。在这里，切割工靠提灯的光作业、所有权文件是个笑话，没人审计一个数据包从何而来、或它运到时外壳为何半融。这让这条打捞壕沟成了唯一一个破坏者负担得起"扔掉自己飞行路径碎片"的地方，笃信拾荒者闲话的噪声能把它淹没。据说那个包来自一艘在旧战争走廊附近"就那么自己转散了架"的船；有人说是幽灵引擎，有人发誓是一只安静的手拉下了保险。目前为止，线索从一块无名前哨的数据板，到一片死掉的货运场，然后钻进霓虹城的服务内脏，每一步都嗡鸣着同样的模式：坏跃迁、缺失的附属文件，以及日志里那个每当引擎因无人愿意写下来的原因死亡时就会出现的偏角标记。

#en: The hangar is where her mathematics become metal. Here, on the edge of a forgotten strip, she can park stolen hulls under a failing atmosphere shield, spool her tugs in silence, and patch new vectors into the ghost-yards without orbital patrols noticing a blip. The walls remember hard burns and emergency landings; in that noise she can hide one last course correction, one last transfer of black-boxes and deadman triggers before the archive disperses beyond anyone's reach. Those closest to these flights stare at their boots when asked, unwilling to name the pilot who steers ships off their charts.  \n\nWe followed a stray dataslate from the back end of nowhere, then half-erased sensor logs in an old UC relay, then a Trade Authority freighter's falsified manifests. Every scrap of telemetry pointed to the same invisible hand, nudging wrecks just out of sight and rewriting the record one stolen vector at a time.
zh: 那座机库，正是她的数学变成金属的地方。在这里、在一条被遗忘跑道的边缘，她能把偷来的船壳停在失效的大气护盾下，让拖船在寂静中待命，并把新向量接进幽灵船坞，而轨道巡逻队察觉不到一丝异动。墙壁记得硬着陆与紧急降落；在那片噪声里，她能藏起最后一次航向修正、最后一次黑匣与死人开关的转移——赶在档案散开到任何人触及范围之外以前。与这些航次最亲近的人被问起时盯着自己的靴子，不愿说出那名把船只驶出星图的飞行员的名字。  \n\n我们追着一块天涯之外散落的数据板，然后是一座旧联殖中继里半擦除的传感器日志，再然后是一艘贸易管理局货船被伪造的舱单。每一点遥测碎片都指向同一只无形的手，把残骸推离视线，并一次一个偷来的向量地改写记录。

#en: Down here, stories about her move through the pipes faster than the water; every time someone repeats them in the food line or outside the LIST door, a detail shifts, a date slips, a destination changes by a system or two. That is exactly why whatever she left buried in these cramped offices and backroom kiosks matters it is the only version of events that is not filtered through fear, gratitude, or spite. In the tangle of requisition logs, shipment timings, and quietly amended approvals, there will be a pattern that does not care who is listening, only where the cargo went next. So far all I have are fragments a wiped trail in a forgotten lab, a broken data chain pointing into deep space, a smug broker moving partial routes, and a derelict cutter with half a jump; different mouths tell it differently, but every version ends the same way, with people vanishing into a grid that no official chart admits exists.
zh: 在这下面，关于她的故事在管道里跑得比水还快；每当有人在取餐队伍里或独立盟门外重复它们，某个细节就会偏移、某个日期就会滑走、某个目的地就会差上一两个星系。这正是"她埋在这些逼仄办公室与后室小摊里的东西"要紧的原因：它是唯一一个没有被恐惧、感激或怨恨过滤过的事件版本。在领用日志、货运时机与被悄悄修改的批准构成的乱麻里，会有一个不在乎谁在听、只在乎货物下一步去了哪里的模式。目前为止，我只有碎片：被遗忘实验室里一条被擦净的痕迹、一条指向深空的断裂数据链、一名兜售部分航线的得意掮客，以及一艘只跳了一半的弃置切割船；不同的嘴讲得不同，可每个版本都以同样的方式结束——人消失进一张没有任何官方星图承认存在的网格。

#en: The Red Mile is the only place loud enough to drown out the screams that still follow a man like this; its crater is a kill box carved into a betting floor, a perfect blind where a navigator who lives on probabilities can hide his last throw of the dice behind Mauler roars and cheering drunks. Here, under the storm-lit sky and the neon promises of easy money, he can test one final route in real time, slipping a broadcast through the chaos or erasing the last logs that tie his corridors to so many drifting hulls. If he finishes the Run, every faction watching will rewrite their charts around whatever he does next. All we really know is this much; back in Gagarin I heard captains whisper the same three-pointed pattern, and in that drifting GalBank transport I found routes massaged to fail in all the right places, but the order of those sins and who paid him when is lost in redacted logs and dead men's memories.
zh: 红里是唯一吵闹到足以盖过那种仍跟着这类人的尖叫的地方；它的火山口是一座刻进赌场地面的杀伤盒，一个完美的盲点——靠概率为生的领航员可以在那里把最后一次掷骰藏在劫掠兽的咆哮与欢呼的酒鬼背后。在这里，风暴照亮的天空下与"轻松赚钱"的霓虹许诺中，他能实时测试最后一条航线：让一道广播溜过混乱，或擦掉那些把他的走廊与如此多漂移船壳系起来的最后日志。若他完成那场"跑"，每一个观望的派系都将围绕他接下来的行动重画自己的星图。我们真正知道的只有这些：在加加林星我听到船长们低语着同样的三岔模式，在那具漂着的盖尔银行运输船上我发现被揉捏得"恰好在所有正确的地方失败"的航线，可那些罪行的次序、以及谁在何时付钱给他，已丢失在涂黑的日志与死人的记忆里。

#en: Neon's starport is where all the wrong cargo brushes shoulders with the right paperwork, where a mislabeled canister or a mistimed docking code can slip past a tired controller and vanish into the flow. If there is anywhere fragments of dust and hull scrap from forgotten battlefields could ride in unnoticed, it is here, clinging to freighters that swear they fly clean lanes. Buried in those traces is the shape of where they have really been jumping, the quiet detours one particular navigator keeps carving into the sky.  \nSo far, I have a forgotten rock with a stray dataslate, a hazy report from a frontier stop that never quite matches its own logs, and whispers in portside bars about routes that always arrive late yet never trigger fines. None of it lines up cleanly, but every discrepancy points back to the same kind of mistake: numbers nudged just enough that everyone shrugs, signs, and lets the slot clear.
zh: 霓虹城太空港，是错误货物与正确文书擦肩而过的地方，一个标签错误的罐体或一个时机不对的停靠代码就能溜过一个疲惫的调度员、消失进那股人流。若说有什么地方能让被遗忘战场的尘土与船壳碎屑不被注意地搭车进来，那就是这里——攀附在发誓自己飞干净航道的货船上。埋在这些痕迹里的，是它们真正一直在何处跃迁的形状，是某一名特定领航员不断刻进天空的安静绕行。  \n目前为止，我有一块带着散落数据板的被遗忘岩石、一份来自边境站、永远与自身日志对不太上的模糊报告，以及码头边酒吧里关于"总是迟到却从不触发罚款的航线"的低语。没有一样能干净地对齐，可每一处差异都指回同一种错误：数字被推得刚好让所有人耸耸肩、签个字、让位置清出来。

#en: The deserted relay station hangs alone in the dark, a broken tooth at the edge of a forgotten orbit, yet its arrays still sweep the void with mechanical patience. This is where she has tied together every stolen chart and corrupted timetable, bending an obsolete node into the fixed point her shifting routes could never otherwise have. The coils are overdriven, telemetry warped, the air thick with the hum of grav calculations seconds away from locking new corridors into place that no faction can see, let alone intercept. If she finishes here, the lanes change for everyone, and not even the UC SysDef interdiction teams will know why. Looking back, the smuggler's shelter with its altered manifests and the gutted warship with its sabotaged nav core felt like noise; only when the same notation surfaced in both did the coincidences pile up into a pattern that pointed straight to this station and the hand shaping it.
zh: 那座废弃中继站孤悬于黑暗中，一颗被遗忘轨道边缘的断牙，可它的阵列仍以机械般的耐心扫过虚空。她在这里把每一张偷来的星图与每一份损坏的时间表绑在一起，把一个过时的节点掰成她那些变动航线本不可能拥有的定点。线圈被超频驱动，遥测扭曲，空气里充满引力计算的嗡鸣——离把新走廊锁进位置只差几秒，而那些走廊任何派系都看不见，更别说拦截。若她在这里完工，航道将因所有人而改变，连联殖星防队的阻截队都不会知道原因。回头看，那座舱单被改动的走私者掩体与那艘导航核心被破坏的被掏空军舰感觉都像噪声；只有当同样的记号在两者中浮现时，那些巧合才堆叠成一个模式，直指这座星际站与塑造它的那只手。

#en: The hangar matters because it sits just outside anyone's official concern, a forgotten shell where flight plans can be rewritten and then left to rust. It is the kind of place a salvage crew claims as their own, stacking cut hull, splicing power from dead lines, and locking down any stray data core that looks more valuable than scrap. The gang squatting here are not guarding junk; they are sitting on the last clean imprint of a route correction made too quickly, a ghost in the circuitry that someone meant to wipe and never finished. Stray burns on the deck, half-cut cables, and a console frozen mid-overwrite say whoever touched it left in a hurry, and no one noticed what survived in the buffers. So far the trail has been fragments and rumor: a wiped nav rig in a derelict bay, nervous talk in spacer bars about freighters arriving early or not at all, and the same quiet signature buried in altered approach math.
zh: 那座机库之所以要紧，是因为它恰好坐落在任何人的官方关切之外，一个被遗忘的外壳，飞行计划可以在那里被改写、然后任其锈蚀。这是打捞队会据为己有的那类地方：堆起切割下的船壳、从死线上接线取电，并锁住任何看起来比废料更值钱的游离数据核心。蹲在这里的帮派守的不是垃圾；他们坐在一次做得太快的航向修正的最后一道干净印记上，电路里一个有人本想抹掉却从未完工的幽灵。甲板上零星的灼痕、被切到一半的线缆，以及冻结在覆写中途的控制台，都说明碰过它的人走得匆忙，而没人注意到缓冲区里存活了什么。目前为止，这条线索是碎片与传闻：一座弃置泊位里被擦净的导航设备、太空劫匪酒吧里关于"货船提前抵达或根本没到"的紧张闲谈，以及埋在被动过的进近数学里同一道安静签名。

#en: Neon's lower decks were built to forget things, and that is exactly why she came here. In the tangle beneath the Conduction Grid, where Aurora haze and leaking conduits blur sightlines, it is easy to make people vanish and signals die in the noise. Gravlock has turned these alleys into her last relay, meeting brokers who wash her salvage records and arranging for key logs and payout trails to disappear into Trade Authority coffers. Tonight she is closing the loop, silencing anyone who can tie her altered distress queues to the lost settlers remembered on a lonely farm in Cheyenne. The dataslate in the dust of that first backwater outpost, the doctored manifests buried in a forgotten freight yard, and the encrypted tag behind a candlelit memorial have all said the same thing in different ways: the same hand moves the beacons, the same ship reaches the wrecks first, and the lies all lead down into Neon's underbelly.
zh: 霓虹城的下层甲板本就是为遗忘事情而建，这正是她来这里的原因。在输电网格之下的乱麻里，极光的雾气与渗漏的导管模糊了视线，让人很容易消失、让信号死在噪声里。"重力锁"已把那些小巷变成她最后一处中继：会见替她洗白打捞记录的掮客，安排关键日志与付款痕迹消失进贸易管理局的金库。今晚她正在合上这个循环，让任何能把"她改过的遇险队列"与"夏延星一座孤独农场上被纪念的失踪定居者"系起来的人闭嘴。那块落在最初穷乡前哨尘土里的数据板、埋在废弃货运场里的被做手脚舱单，以及烛光纪念碑背后的加密标签，都以不同方式说着同一件事：同一只手在移动信标，同一艘船最先抵达残骸，而所有谎言都通向霓虹城的下腹。

#en: Neon's Underbelly is the last place anyone checks for ghosts of UC programs, which is exactly why he chose it. Down here the air is thick with Aurora vapor and coolant leaks, the perfect cover for a medic who needs dim corridors, easy access to desperate bodies, and no questions about scars behind the ear. The noise of the city dies to a wet, electric hum that could hide any kind of white-noise loop still whispering in conditioned minds. If forgotten subroutines in his head ever woke up, they would have steered him somewhere like this, where Ryujin influence, GalBank shadows, and loose chem traffic keep official eyes away while old code quietly finishes its work. We started with a stray dataslate on a dead rock, followed the trail of altered patients and UC signatures through orbital debris and SysDef wreckage, and learned that wherever the stitched scars showed up, the same buried protocols were already there first.
zh: 霓虹城的下腹，是任何人最后才会去查找"联殖计划幽灵"的地方——这正是他选中它的原因。在这下面，空气因极光蒸汽与冷却液泄漏而厚重，对一个需要昏暗走廊、易于接触走投无路之人、且不问耳后伤疤的医疗兵来说，这是完美的掩护。城市的噪声死去，只剩一种潮湿的电气嗡鸣——它能藏住任何仍在被训导过头脑里低语的白噪声回路。若他脑中那些被遗忘的子程序曾苏醒，它们会把他引向这样的地方：龙神的影响力、盖尔银行的阴影与松散的药剂交易让官方的眼睛避开，而旧代码悄悄完成它的工作。我们从死寂岩石上一块散落数据板开始，追着被改动的病人与联殖签名穿过轨道碎片与星防队残骸，并得知：凡是有缝合伤疤出现的地方，同样的被埋协议早已先在那里。

#en: Gagarin Landing is where industrial metal and bad paper were meant to be quietly reconciled, a place where refitted hulls and new loans pass under the same harsh lights until no one remembers who owned what first. If the pattern you have been chasing exists anywhere in full, it is in the grimy terminals and forgotten offices overlooking Arc Might's refurbished bays, where a diligent hand was supposed to tidy the numbers and then simply never finished the job. In half-closed kiosks and dusty archives, transactions trail off mid-correction, complaint tickets stop just short of escalation, and the outline of a hidden fleet begins to show through the gaps. So far the trail runs from a frightened broker's manifests on that lonely cargo hub to discrepancy logs and angry captains pointing at a vanished GalBank auditor with a Caracas accent, all telling the same story of ships that disappeared on screen first, then in space.
zh: 加加林着陆点，是工业金属与糟糕文书本应被悄悄调和的地方；在那里，翻新的船壳与新的贷款在同一排刺眼灯光下经过，直到没人记得谁先拥有过什么。若说你一直在追的那个模式有哪里完整存在，它就在俯瞰"弧威"翻新货舱的那些邋遢终端与被遗忘办公室里——本该有一双勤勉的手来整理那些数字，然后干脆没把活干完。在半关的小摊与积灰的档案里，交易在修正中途断掉，投诉单停在升级之前一步，而一支隐藏舰队的轮廓开始从缝隙里透出来。目前为止，线索从那名受惊掮客在那座孤独货运枢纽上的舱单，延伸到不符日志与愤怒的船长们——他们指向一名带着加拉加斯口音、消失的盖尔银行审计员，全都在讲同一个故事：船只先在屏幕上消失，然后在太空中消失。

#en: The PX-15 drifts in silent formation with ghosts of old patrol routes, its hull still bearing UC SysDef markings that once guaranteed order along the frontier skyways. For a navigator bent on rewriting how worlds connect, there is no better vault than a derelict combat ship wired into forgotten threat maps, jump interdiction data, and classified overlays of the Silent Span. Inside, amid dead consoles and flickering bulkheads, the patterns she has been etching into stolen corridor charts can finally be cross-stitched against military-grade surveys, turning rumor of a hidden refuge into a precise, inverted path no registry can trace. It is no accident the trail led here; a discarded slate on a backwater rock, odd route variants buried in an office beneath New Atlantis, then the hint of tampered projections in SysDef records, each small disturbance nudging the hunt toward this dead warship at the edge of sanctioned space.
zh: PX-15与旧巡逻航线的幽灵编队静默漂行，它的船壳仍带着联殖星防队的标记——那些标记曾在边境天路上保证秩序。对一个执意改写世界如何相连的领航员来说，没有比一艘接进被遗忘威胁图、跃迁阻截数据与"静默地带"机密叠图的弃置战斗舰更好的保险库了。在它内部、在死掉的控制台与闪烁的舱壁之间，她刻进偷来走廊星图的模式终于能与军用级测绘交叉缝合，把"隐秘避难所"的传闻变成一条任何登记册都追不到的精确反向路径。线索引到这里绝非偶然：一穷乡岩石上被丢弃的数据板、埋在新亚特兰蒂斯城下方某办公室里的古怪航线变体，然后是星防队记录里被动手脚的投影暗示，每一处小小的扰动都把追猎推向这艘位于获批太空边缘的死掉军舰。

#en: Helium-3 flows through the plant in shimmering streams, every valve and pressure gauge tied to contracts, futures, and insurance tables written lightyears away; this is where numbers become propellant, where a single fluctuation can upend markets and erase settlements. Rafael chose it because the place already runs on risk, because one calculated overload here can turn abstract projections into a shockwave that justifies every quiet policy he once audited. He has wired his models directly into the refinery controls, feeding in raids, accidents, and your own approach, letting a lifetime of small compromises converge into one catastrophic proof. Earlier, a frightened broker in the moonside relay passed along contraband manifests that did not add up, and the abandoned garrison's logs showed patrols redirected moments before ambushes; together, they traced a pattern of minor adjustments leading, step by step, to this edge.
zh: 氦-3 在工厂里以闪烁的溪流穿行，每一个阀门与压力表都连着光年之外写下的合同、期货与保险表；这里是数字变成推进剂的地方，一处波动就能颠覆市场、抹掉定居点。拉斐尔选中它，是因为这地方本就靠风险运转，因为这里一次算计好的过载就能把抽象预测变成一道冲击波，为他曾审计过的每一项安静政策提供理由。他把自己的模型直接接进炼油控制，喂进袭击、事故与你自己的逼近，让一生的微小妥协汇聚成一个灾难性的证明。早先，卫星侧中继里一名受惊的掮客转交了对不上的走私舱单，而废弃驻军的日志显示巡逻队在伏击发生前一刻被调走；合在一起，它们追出一种由细微调整构成的模式，一步步通向这道边缘。

#en: Out past the pressure domes, where Cydonia's glow thins into rust and rock, the old survey bunkers still sit wired into approach beacons no one bothered to decommission. It is here that quiet adjustments to traffic patterns can become collisions, here that one navigator with the right codes can turn every arriving ship into a loaded gun pointed at the city. Vector has nested himself in that blind spot, feeding on the same negligence that let his first disaster be buried, preparing to fold military and pirate traffic into one catastrophic crossing. This ends where his lines intersect. So far the trail runs clean: a forgotten dataslate on a dead rock, desperate warnings and half-solved equations; then whispers in the station bars, where route-sellers spoke of a ghost who fixed broken jumps; finally the gutted SysDef hulk, its nav core still echoing his signature, every vector bending back toward this dust-choked horizon.
zh: 在压力穹顶之外，赛多尼亚的辉光变稀薄成锈与岩石处，那些旧勘探掩体仍接在没人费心退役的进近信标上。正是在这里，对交通模式的安静调整能变成碰撞；正是在这里，一名持有正确代码的领航员能把每一艘抵达的船变成指向这座城市的上了膛的枪。"向量"把自己嵌进那个盲点，以让他的第一场灾难得以被埋葬的同样疏忽为食，准备把军用与海盗交通折成一次灾难性的交叉。这一切终结于他的线相交之处。目前为止，线索干净利落：死寂岩石上一块被遗忘的数据板、绝望的警告与半解出的方程；然后是星际站酒吧里的低语——航路贩子谈起一个修好坏跃迁的幽灵；最后是那具被掏空的星防队残骸，它的导航核心仍在回响他的签名，每一个向量都弯回这道积灰的地平线。

#en: The rusted ribs of the Abandoned Deimos Scrapyard are the only place Rivet would trust for his last move. Here, he knows every beam, every stress fracture, every forgotten crane cable he can turn into a noose. Deimos built the ships he spent a life cutting apart, and its castoff graveyard gives him all the raw metal and blind corners he needs to brace his final defenses and erase the last surviving records of that courier job before anyone can tie them back to the right names in New Atlantis. People say this is where his story ends, or began, or loops back on itself; every retelling shifts, as if the scrapyard itself is editing the truth to keep him half legend, half warning. We started with a stray dataslate on a nowhere rock, chased whispers from a lonely homestead to a derelict UC warship, and every step in between has narrowed the pattern to one stubborn shipbreaker and a single bad contract no one wants on the books.
zh: 废弃火卫二废料场锈蚀的肋骨，是"铆钉"唯一信任的最后一着之地。在这里，他熟悉每一根梁、每一道应力裂纹、每一根能被他变成绞索的遗忘吊缆。火卫二造了他花一辈子拆解的船，而它的弃置墓地给了他撑起最后防御、并在任何人能把这些与"新亚特兰蒂斯城里正确的名字"系起来之前抹掉那趟信使差事最后幸存记录所需的一切生金属与盲角。人们说他的故事在这里结束、或开始、或绕回自身；每一次重述都偏移，仿佛废料场本身在编辑真相，好让他一半是传说、一半是警告。我们从一穷乡岩石上一块散落数据板开始，追着从孤独农庄到一艘废弃联殖军舰的低语，而中间每一步都把这个模式收窄到一名固执的拆船工与一份没人愿意记入账册的坏合同。

#en: GalBank does not leave a ship like GL-1355 Capitalwing adrift and unclaimed; an escort this valuable is either recovered quickly or written off very carefully, which makes its slow tumble in dead space the loudest kind of silence. Whatever was tested in its navigation core was important enough for someone to risk destroying a corporate asset and then scrub the ledgers clean, leaving only half-melted consoles and a flicker of altered routes behind. If you want to know who has been trimming risk ratings and pushing small ships toward the dark between charts, you have to start where the math first stopped adding up, inside the bones of this abandoned guardian. So far, all you have are rumors of a vanished settler transport, whispers that certain green-rated corridors were never properly signed off, and a pattern of erased beacons that feels less like bad luck and more like a decision made in a quiet office far from any viewport.
zh: 盖尔银行不会把"GL-1355 资本之翼"这样的船扔在那里无人认领；这样一件宝贵的护航物要么被迅速回收，要么被非常小心地核销——这让它在死寂太空中的缓慢翻滚成了最响亮的那种沉默。无论它导航核心里测试了什么，都重要到有人甘冒摧毁一件公司资产的风险、再把账册擦干净，只留下半融的控制台与一丝被改动航线的闪烁。若你想知道谁一直在削薄风险评级、把小船推向星图之间的黑暗，你就得从数学第一次不再对得上的地方开始——在这具被遗弃护卫者残骸的骨骼里。目前为止，你只有关于一艘失踪定居者运输船的传闻、关于某些绿色评级走廊从未被妥善批准的耳语，以及一种被擦除信标的模式——它感觉不再像霉运，更像某个远离任何舷窗的安静办公室里做出的决定。

#en: The deserted relay station sits like a dead nerve at the edge of the system, yet its consoles still pulse with faint, unsupervised traffic. This is where her shadow navnet converges, where all those tiny corrections and erased warnings are injected into the lanes, turning distant ships into wreck statistics. Every misaligned beacon and corrupted buoy you have chased leads back to this forgotten node; here she is routing one last cascade, tying off loose ends, purging proof that the disasters were designed, not random. The longer she works, the closer the Settled Systems drift toward a future where no route can be trusted. It started with a scorched dataslate in an out-of-the-way station and a nameless relay spewing ghost vectors, then a quiet Ryujin contact confirming corporate tampering and archived UC sims bearing her mathematical fingerprints; each step left just enough trace to reveal the same unseen hand shaping the sky.
zh: 那座废弃中继站像一根死掉的神经坐落在星系边缘，可它的控制台仍在以微弱的、无人监督的交通脉动。这里是她影子导航网汇聚之处，所有那些微小的修正与被抹除的警告都在此被注入航道，把远方的船只变成残骸统计数字。你追过的每一座错位信标与损坏浮标都指回这个被遗忘的节点；在这里，她正在安排最后一场连锁、系紧所有松散的线头、清除"那些灾难是被设计的、而非随机的"之证据。她工作得越久，定居星系就越接近一个"任何航线都不可信"的未来。它始于一穷乡星际站上一块烧焦的数据板与一座喷吐幽灵向量的无名中继，然后是龙神一名安静的线人证实了公司的动手脚，以及一批带着她数学指纹的联殖模拟存档；每一步都留下刚好足够的痕迹，揭示出同一只塑造天空的无形之手。

#en: In the quiet corners of the Cydonia residential decks, people trade favors and secrets more often than credits, and no one asks why a mid-level functionary needs extra storage tucked behind a false bulkhead. This is where incident reports are rewritten over dinner and grav-solution models are carried home on personal slates, where a careful ghost could slip fragments of a routing archive into private caches and trust that the noise of everyday life would hide them. Lately, though, too many civilian near-misses, too many scrubbed black box summaries, and too many "lucky" detours have traced back to the same timing, the same geometry, the same unseen hand. I started with half-drunken stories in a Neon lounge and a discarded slate on a rock no one visits, then found Kryx-era telemetry buried in a dead SysDef hull; taken alone they were coincidences, but lined up they spell a pattern that always bends the lanes the way she wants.
zh: 在赛多尼亚居住甲板安静的角落里，人们交换人情与秘密比交换信用币更频繁，没人会问一个中层职员为何需要在假舱壁后多藏一处存储。这里正是事故报告在晚餐时被改写、引力解模型被装进私人数据板带回家的地方，一名谨慎的幽灵可以把航线档案的碎片溜进私人储藏，并笃信日常生活的噪声能藏住它们。然而近来，太多民用惊险擦碰、太多被擦净的黑匣摘要、太多"幸运"绕行，都追溯回同样的时机、同样的几何、同一只无形的手。我从霓虹城一家酒廊里的半醉故事与一块落在无人造访岩石上的被丢弃数据板开始，然后在一具死掉星防队船壳里发现克里克斯时代的遥测；单看它们都是巧合，但排在一起，它们拼出一个总按她想要的方式掰弯航道的模式。

#en: All the quiet damage starts here, in a relay no one has monitored in years, where update cycles kept humming after the last technician walked away and nobody bothered to notice when the timing slipped. Bit by bit, its dishes turned off their assigned beacons and began listening instead, feeding Vector everything she needed to bend convoys, mask ghost tugs, and carve her own corridor through UC and Freestar traffic like a scar only she could read. Now the station is a live nerve in her network, pulsing stolen telemetry and falsified routes toward whatever she is building on the edge of mapped space, and every minute it stays online is another ship nudged toward becoming wreckage. Up to this point the trail has led from a bloodied dataslate in a forgotten stopover to a dead relay full of altered logs, then to a sabotaged buoy in orbit, each step proving that the same precise hand has been rewriting the lanes for a very long time.
zh: 所有那些安静的破坏都始于此——在一座多年无人监控的中继里，更新周期在最后一名技师离开后仍在嗡鸣，而没人费心注意到时机何时滑脱。一点一点地，它的天线盘关掉被指派的信标、转而开始聆听，把"向量"掰弯车队、掩护幽灵拖船、并像一道只有她能读懂的伤疤般在联殖与自由星系联盟交通中凿出自己走廊所需的一切都喂给她。如今这座星际站是她网络里一根活的神经，把偷来的遥测与伪造的航线脉动向她在已测绘太空边缘正在建造的无论什么；它每多在线一分钟，就又多一艘船被推向成为残骸。到目前为止，线索从一座被遗忘中途站一块沾血的数据板，到一座塞满被改动日志的死中继，再到轨道上一枚被动过手脚的浮标，每一步都证明同一只精确的手很久以来一直在改写航道。

#en: The Underbelly is where Neon breathes out what it does not want the towers to smell, and the grid techs down here are the ones who hear every irregular heartbeat in the conduits. Coil access, maintenance windows, "unscheduled" shutdowns; if Vector or anyone tuning drives for him is piggybacking on the city's power, the timing will be written into these work logs long before anyone admits it topside. Down here, people learn fast that asking why the same sectors keep going dark on nights when certain ships slip out is a good way to lose contracts, or teeth, so they talk in half-sentences and shrugs. So far the path has been a trail of careful omissions: a discarded slate with missing entries on a backwater rock, smeared jump data around a quiet orbit, and a Trade Authority record that skipped over an entire burn, each pointing with what they do not say toward Grav work being done in the shadows and a pilot who lives in those gaps.
zh: 下腹，是霓虹城呼出它不愿让高楼闻到的东西之处，而这里的电网技师就是那些听得见导管里每一次不规则心跳的人。线圈访问、维护窗口、"未排期"停机；若"向量"或任何替他调校引擎的人搭着这座城市的电力顺风车，那个时机早在任何人承认之前就会写进这些工作日志里。在这下面，人们很快学会：追问为何同样的区段在某些船只溜出的夜晚不断断电，是失去合同或牙齿的好办法，所以他们用半句话与耸肩交谈。目前为止，这条路是一串小心省略的痕迹：一穷乡岩石上一块带着缺失条目的被丢弃数据板、一处安静轨道周围被拖抹的跃迁数据，以及一份跳过整段燃烧的贸易管理局记录，每一处都用它们没说出口的东西，指向阴影中正在进行的引力作业与一名活在这些空隙里的飞行员。

#en:
The sky here never quite settles, thin and off-color, the kind of air people learn to live with until they stop asking what is riding on every breath.  
That is why he chose this forgotten installation, where a poor atmosphere is normal and a new instability feels like just another bad day.  
Every hijacker chip, every stolen microcell, every quiet retrofit of a tower or rig has been building toward this moment, a final test far from regulators and Rangers, where one last adjustment could push a marginal world past recovery before anyone understands what changed.  
You have trailed him from a dead survey site, through a courier gone cold in the Trade Authority's ledgers, across a grease-stained garage floor, and finally to a silent beacon in orbit; each step has confirmed the same pattern of tampered systems, missing hardware, and a man who learned that the easiest place to hide his work is where failure was already expected.
zh:
这里的天空从不真正安定，稀薄而色泽不正，人们学会与之共处，直到不再追问每一次呼吸里都承载着什么。  
这正是他选中这座被遗忘设施的原因：糟糕的大气是常态，新的不稳定感就像又一个坏日子。  
每一个被劫持的芯片、每一个偷来的微电池、每一次对塔台或设备的安静改装，都一直在为这一刻积累——一场远离监管者与游骑兵的最终测试，在那里，最后一次调整就能把一个边缘世界推过不可恢复的临界点，而没人明白改变了什么。  
你已追着他从一座死掉的勘探场，穿过一艘在贸易管理局账册里冷掉的信使船，越过一片油污斑斑的车库地面，最后到轨道上一座沉默的信标；每一步都证实了同样的模式：被动手脚的系统、失踪的硬件，以及一个懂得"藏起自己作品的最容易之处，就是失败早已被预期的地方"的人。

#en: This forgotten Deimos scrapyard is where their ghosts are stacked in plain sight, hulls warped by bad math and quiet compromises, yet written off as obsolete hardware and left to rot under a thin veneer of corporate amnesia. If anywhere still holds a clean thread back to the hands that signed off those frames, it is here among the serial plates no one has bothered to scrub and the brace geometry someone has been carving fresh into rust. Executioner Warbrand have been hired to stand over the secrets and call it just another guard job, which only confirms there is something simple at the core of all this, made slippery by money and time. So far the trail has been fragments and half truths: a Ranger's off ledger notes about patterned failures, a dead drop dataslate full of angry schematics, whispers of a masked engineer saving some ships and gutting others, and every scrap of it pointing back toward one quiet name under Deimos steel.
zh: 这座被遗忘的火卫二废料场，是他们的幽灵被明晃晃堆起来的地方：船壳被坏数学与安静的妥协弄歪，却被核销为过时硬件、留在公司失忆的薄薄漆面下腐烂。若有哪处还留着一根通往"签批那些框架的手"的干净线头，那就是这里——在没人费心擦净的序列号牌与有人一直在锈上刻出新纹的支撑几何之间。"处刑者战痕"受雇守着这些秘密，把它叫作又一份看守差事，这恰恰证实这一切核心有一个简单的东西，只因金钱与时间而变得滑不留手。目前为止，这条线索是碎片与半真半假：一名游骑兵关于"成模式故障"的账外笔记、一块塞满愤怒图纸的死信数据板、关于一名蒙面工程师救下一些船、又拆空另一些船的低语，而每一块碎片都指回火卫二钢铁之下的一个安静名字。

#en: The edge of Akila City's fields is the only place that makes sense for an ending like this; the climate towers hum over crops that should not have survived this season, their patched routines bearing the same eccentric signatures you have chased from one system to the next. Here, where hungry settlers depend on a sky she has quietly rewritten, Isobar is finishing what she started, tuning one last set of parameters to prove that her way works and to bury any trace of who really broke the first colony grid. Every minor override, every "temporary" fix, every favor for a desperate farmer has added up to this moment, a balance point where one more adjustment could ripple across Freestar breadbaskets. Looking back, it began with a stray slate in the dust, a dead hunter's half-burned log, a lonely prefab in the wilderness, then orbital telemetry that all whispered the same thing: someone has been steering the weather for a very long time.
zh: 阿基拉城田地的边缘，是这种结局唯一说得通的地方；气候塔在那些本不该熬过这个季节的作物上方嗡鸣，它们打过补丁的例程带着你从一个星系追到另一个星系的同样古怪签名。在这里、在饥饿的定居者依赖一片她悄悄改写的天空之处，"等压线"正在完成她开始的一切，调校最后一组参数以证明她的方式可行，并埋葬"究竟是谁弄坏了第一张殖民地电网"的任何痕迹。每一次小小的覆写、每一次"临时"修补、每一次为绝望农夫的人情，都累积到这一刻——一个平衡点，再多一次调整就可能让涟漪扩散到自由星系联盟的粮仓。回头看，它始于尘土中一块散落数据板、一名死掉猎人半烧毁的日志、荒野里一座孤独预制房，然后是轨道遥测——它们都低语着同一件事：有人很久以来一直在操纵天气。

#en: On most worlds, chemical variance reports are dull compliance work; here, in a tower that has seen more black-budget projects than honest peer review, anomalies are how you tell where the bodies are buried. Whatever was tested on these levels needed controlled conditions and a lot of institutional blind spots, and the stories drifting through barracks and spacer bars say a rogue unit has been selling their experience to whoever wants deniable muscle around such experiments. If those records are not pinned down at the source, every later trace will look like natural noise. So far the trail is a farmer's reversed foreclosure in Freestar space, an orbital relay whose traffic did not match its own logs, a dead SysDef hull with cargo manifests arguing with themselves, and a quiet cache on a forgotten rock full of half-shredded drafts, all whispering the same thing: someone good with numbers has been practicing on both ledgers and lives.
zh: 在多数世界上，化学差异报告是枯燥的合规工作；在这里、在一座见过的黑预算项目比诚实同行评审还多的塔楼里，异常就是你判断尸体埋在哪里的方式。在这些楼层上被测试的东西需要受控条件与大量体制盲点，而在军营与太空劫匪酒吧里流传的故事说，一支失控单位一直在把他们在这些实验周围的见不得光的武力卖给任何想要的人。若那些记录不在源头被钉住，之后每一道痕迹都会看起来像自然噪声。目前为止，这条线索是自由星系联盟星域里一名农夫被撤销的止赎、一座交通与自身日志不符的轨道中继、一具货运舱单自相矛盾的死掉星防队残骸，以及一处塞满半撕毁草稿的被遗忘岩石上的安静储藏点，全都在低语同一件事：有个精于数字的人一直在拿账册与人生练手。

#en: The Deserted UC Listening Post hangs over silent rock like a question no one wants answered, its old sensor dishes still wired into grav-space in ways only a navigator would truly understand. Here, the network is thinnest and the data remains uncorrected, perfect for someone to splice in a new corridor without drawing immediate fire from MAST or Freestar eyes. Every console he touches folds official charts around his own overlays, turning this forgotten node into the keystone of a route that could tug unsuspecting ships off safe lanes before anyone knows why. Shut down anywhere else and the pattern persists; cut it here, at the source, and the experiment dies before it becomes doctrine. All anyone knows for certain is that earlier logs from this station did not match what the bunker tech carried when he ran, and that both pointed back to the same missing pilot and a trail of altered readings no two witnesses recount quite the same way.
zh: 那座"被遗弃的联殖听音哨"像一道没人想被回答的问题悬在沉默岩石之上，它老旧的传感器天线盘仍以只有领航员才真正理解的方式接进引力空间。在这里，网络最稀薄、数据未被修正，完美适合有人接进一条新走廊而不立刻引来三头同盟或自由星系联盟的眼线火力。他触碰的每一台控制台都把官方星图围绕他自己的叠图折起来，把这处被遗忘的节点变成一条航线的拱心石——那条航线能在任何人明白原因之前，把毫无戒心的船只拽离安全航道。在别处关停，模式仍在；在这里、在源头切断它，实验就会在变成信条之前死去。所有人能确定的只是：这座星际站早先的日志，与那名掩体技师逃跑时携带的东西对不上，而两者都指回同一名失踪的飞行员与一连串被改动的读数——没有两个证人的复述方式完全相同。

#en: Down in Neon's underbelly, where the grid hum drowns out official channels and every bulkhead has three owners, this is the only place Rivet's kind of secret could survive. The mechanics here speak in half-finished sentences and hand signals, deals scribbled on scrap and never properly logged. A route, a brace point, a quiet tweak to a transponder signature can pass from tongue to tongue and come out the other side as something entirely different, until no one is sure who asked for what or why. That is why the trail bends through these leaking corridors; misheard job orders, misfiled part numbers, a yard clerk on a distant rock reading the wrong note have all conspired to funnel your search here. So far you have followed a stray slate off a forgotten world, then sifted through yard gossip and a grieving family's recording, each step tightening the pattern around one burned contract cutter and the courier that should have died with him.
zh: 在霓虹城的下腹，电网嗡鸣盖过官方信道、每面舱壁都有三个主人的地方，这是唯一能让"铆钉"那种秘密存活的地方。这里的机械师用半截话与手势交谈，交易潦草写在废料上、从不妥善记录。一条航线、一个支撑点、对应答器签名的一次安静微调，能从一张嘴传到另一张嘴，出来时已变成完全不同的东西，直到没人确定谁要求了什么、为什么。正因如此，线索才拐过这些渗漏的走廊：听错的工作指令、归档错误的零件编号、远方岩石上一名船坞文书读错了备注，全都在合力把你的搜索引到这里。目前为止，你追着一块来自被遗忘世界的散落数据板，然后筛过船坞闲话与一名悲痛亲属的录音，每一步都收紧着围绕一艘烧毁的合同切割船与那艘本该随他一同死去的信使船的模式。

#en: Everything narrows here, above the glare and noise, where air tastes of metal and ozone and the city's pulse falls away into the distant hum of the Span. Up on the rooftops Vector has no crowds to foul her lines; only clean sight angles, antenna spires, and the tight geometry of escape routes mapped years in advance. This height lets her ride Neon's relay lattice directly, splicing the last fragments of her archive into compromised beacons and outbound flight plans, one final correction that could bend entire shipping lanes if left to propagate. Down below, those who brokered her routes keep their eyes on their drinks, conversations dying whenever her callsign drifts too close. The trail to this edge started with a stray dataslate on an empty rock, then a quiet pattern in anonymous hauler logs near the starport, and finally an orbital clue that proved someone had been rewriting paths through graveyards since the war never really ended.
zh: 在这里、在炫光与噪声之上，一切收窄——空气尝起来有金属与臭氧味，城市的脉搏褪成桥架远处的嗡鸣。在屋顶上，"向量"没有人群妨碍她的视线；只有干净的视角、天线尖塔，以及多年前预先测绘好的逃生路线那紧凑的几何。这个高度让她能直接骑着霓虹城的中继网格，把她档案的最后碎片接进被攻陷的信标与出港飞行计划——最后一次修正，若任其传播，就能掰弯整条整条航运航线。在下面，替她经手航线的人盯着自己的酒杯，每当她的呼号飘得太近，谈话就死去。通往这道边缘的线索始于一空岩石上一块散落数据板，然后是星际站附近匿名货船日志里一个安静的模式，最后是一处轨道线索——它证明有人在战后从未真正结束的墓地里改写路径已有多时。

#en: Whatever was tested here, it needed machinery that could mimic orbital stresses without attracting attention, and a robotics lab left to gather dust is the perfect place to do that in a hurry. Half-disassembled frames and scorched test bays still smell faintly of burned insulation, the kind of damage you get when someone pushes a system past its limits then walks away before the alarms finish logging. If he has been nudging gravity and weather in tandem, the first rough calculations would have run in rooms like this, not in any polished corporate array. Out on that nameless rock, the storms shifted a little too neatly; at the forgotten station, warning tapes ended mid-sentence; now the pattern of unauthorized experiments, scrambled telemetry, and hastily abandoned equipment all points to someone trialing new alignments, then leaving the mess behind for crews like Dead Orbit Breakers to pick over without realizing what they are guarding.
zh: 无论这里测试的是什么，它都需要能模拟轨道应力而不引人注意的机械，而一座任其积灰的机器人实验室正是匆忙做这件事的完美地点。半拆解的框架与烧焦的测试舱仍带着一丝烧灼绝缘层的味道——那种你把系统推过极限、然后在警报记录完毕之前就走开时留下的损伤。若他一直在同时推动引力与天气，最初的粗略计算就会在这样的房间里跑，而不在任何光鲜的公司阵列里。在那颗无名岩石上，风暴的偏移整齐得有点过分；在那座被遗忘的星际站，警告磁带在句子中间断掉；如今，未经授权的实验、错乱的遥测与匆忙遗弃的设备这一模式，全都指向有人在试验新的对齐方式，然后把烂摊子留给像"死轨破门队"这样的队伍去翻拣——而他们并不知道自己在守着什么。

#en: Hidden in the lee of a rock no one charts twice, the pirate relay shack is where signals go to disappear and get sold back as secrets. The broker here has been skimming more than traffic, hoarding pieces of conversations that cut across corporate lanes, Vanguard patrols, and the strange, knife-edge jumps only one pilot seems to fly with confidence. If any place holds a clean splice between her voice and the routes she favors, it is this hole where criminals trade in half-truths and misrouted pings. Pulling the right fragment now means choosing which pattern to believe and which to burn, before the story mutates again in someone else's hands. So far all we have are corrupted logs from a quiet lab and the nervous testimony of analysts who see the same signature curling through black box after black box, each insisting they heard of her from someone who swore they heard it from someone closer, but no one ever claims to have the whole thing.
zh: 藏在一块没人测绘两次的岩石背风处，那座走私者中继小屋是信号前去消失、再被当作秘密卖回来的地方。这里的掮客揩取的不只是交通，还囤着那些横穿公司航道、先锋队巡逻，以及只有一名飞行员似乎有信心飞的古怪刀锋跃迁的对话碎片。若有哪处保存着她声音与她偏爱航线之间的干净拼接，那就是这个罪犯们用半真半假与错投脉冲交易的地洞。现在拉出正确的碎片，意味着选择相信哪个模式、烧掉哪个——赶在这故事在别人手里再次变异之前。目前为止，我们只有一间安静实验室里损坏的日志，以及分析员们紧张的证词：他们在一个个黑匣里看到同一签名蜷曲，每人都坚称自己是从某个"发誓从更近的人那里听说"的人那里听来她的，可没人声称掌握全部。

#en: The science facility looks ordinary from orbit, another block of steel and glass sunk into a quiet rock, but its drive bay has seen more grav stress than half the test ranges in UC space. Whatever Vector did started in places like this, where numbers matter more than people and maintenance logs are treated as gospel. Someone here captured the way a jump sounds when it is about to go wrong, and the Executioner Ash Syndicate moved in fast enough to tell me that data is worth killing for. Their presence turns every corridor conversation into a murmur; anyone who ever saw something odd in the readings learned to measure their words, if they are still breathing at all. So far I have a doctored incident report from a sealed lab, a discarded slate of frantic equations, and orbital telemetry that quietly matches "isolated" drive failures across two systems, all pointing back to a single analyst who stopped trusting the math everyone else swore by.
zh: 那座科研设施从轨道上看很寻常，又一块沉进安静岩石里的钢与玻璃，可它的引擎舱见过的引力应力比联殖太空里半数试验场都多。"向量"做过的事就始于这样的地方——在那里，数字比人重要，维护日志被当作福音。这里有人捕捉到一段跃迁在即将出错时的声音，而"处刑者灰烬辛迪加"搬进来得快到足以告诉我：那份数据值得为之杀人。他们的存在把每一场走廊谈话都变成低语；任何在读数里见过古怪东西的人，都学会了掂量自己的话——如果他们还在呼吸的话。目前为止，我有一份来自密封实验室的被做手脚事故报告、一块写满狂乱方程的废弃数据板，以及在两个星系间悄悄吻合"孤立"引擎故障的轨道遥测，全都指回一名不再相信别人都信誓旦旦的那套数学的分析员。

#en: Out here, where war relics rot beneath dust and static, a forgotten base is the only place left where a man like this can work undisturbed. Old targeting arrays and comm towers give him the reach he needs to bend corridors, while its abandoned command bunkers offer enough hardened storage to hide every log that proves what he has done. He is not just running; he is recalculating, using the skeleton of a dead campaign to overwrite routes, purge manifests, and carve one last path toward that final coordinate he thinks will save him from judgment. Someone tried to bury all this under decommission orders, redacted briefings, and sealed hangars, but the numbers bled out anyway in stolen telemetry, drunken pilot stories, and files that refused to stay erased. We followed those whispers from that first stray dataslate, through a shuttered relay in the dust, and finally across a derelict Navy scout that carried his signature in every skewed jump log.
zh: 在这里，战争遗物在尘土与静电下腐烂，一座被遗忘的基地是像他这样的人唯一还能不受干扰地工作的地方。旧瞄准阵列与通讯塔给了他掰弯走廊所需的触及范围，而它废弃的指挥掩体提供了足够的加固存储，藏下证明他所做之事的每一份日志。他不只是在逃；他在重算，用一场死掉战役的骨骼覆写航线、清除舱单，并凿出通往他认为能让他免于审判的最终坐标的最后一条路。有人试图把这一切埋在退役令、涂黑简报与密封机库之下，可数字还是从偷来的遥测、醉醺醺的飞行员故事，以及拒绝被擦除的文件里渗了出来。我们追着那些低语，从最初那块散落数据板，穿过尘土中一座关闭的中继，最后越过一艘弃置海军侦察船——它在每一份歪斜的跃迁日志里都带着他的签名。

#en: Someone killed the lights on this relay in a hurry, left panels hanging open and fuse racks half-pulled, then walked away before checking what the systems had already soaked up from the lanes; whatever stain the last signals left behind is still embedded in the hardware here, quietly warping anything that tries to talk past it. The Coldlight Sparks squatting in the corridors clearly only care about the scrap value, not the way comms hiss and stutter whenever a ship drifts through this sector, as if echoes from old distress calls are still being misrouted by a hand no one sees. If I can isolate what this place is leaking into traffic, I can trace where all those "unavoidable" misjumps began. Right now, all I know is a nameless rock held a fragment of altered navigation data, and somewhere between that and this dead station, a pattern of rushed shutdowns and overlooked interference has been nudging ships toward the same unmarked stretch of space.
zh: 有人匆忙掐灭了这座中继的灯，留下敞开的板子与半拉出的保险丝架，然后在检查系统已从航道吸收了什么之前就走开了；最后那些信号留下的无论什么污渍，仍嵌在这里的硬件里，悄悄扭曲任何试图越过它通话的东西。蹲在走廊里的"冷光火花"显然只在乎废料价值，而不在乎每当有船漂过这片星域时通讯为何嘶哑断续——仿佛旧遇险呼叫的回声仍被一只无人看见的手错误转发。若我能隔离这地方正在漏进交通的东西，我就能追出所有那些"不可避免"的错跳从何处开始。眼下，我只知道一块无名岩石上保存着一片被改动的导航数据，而在那与这座死掉星际站之间的某处，一种由匆忙关停与被忽视干扰构成的模式，一直在把船只推向同一段未标注的太空。

#en: This orbit was chosen because no one really looks at it anymore; tankers and bulk haulers have been skimming past this patch of sky for years, trusting old charts and tired habits. Whatever she tested out here relied on that comfort, a way to bend gravity just enough that ships could slide between patrol sweeps and traffic scans without anyone noticing they had gone slightly, dangerously wrong. Catching the device in the same quiet lane where it was first slipped into use is the only way to see how she is hiding her corridors, instead of just following the wreckage they leave behind. So far I have a half-buried report from a forgotten outpost, a misbehaving transmitter that everyone blamed on solar noise, and a drifting vault ship full of logs that almost line up; taken together they all say the same thing in different words, that someone has been using the most familiar routes in the Settled Systems as cover for something nobody wanted to see.
zh: 这条轨道被选中，是因为再没人真正看它了；罐车与散货船多年来贴着这片天空掠过，信任旧星图与疲惫的习惯。她在这外面测试的无论什么，都依赖那份安逸：一种把引力掰弯到刚好让船只滑过巡逻圈与交通扫描、而没人注意到它们已稍稍、危险地走偏的方式。在它最初被接进使用的那条安静航道上抓住这台设备，是看清她如何藏起自己走廊的唯一办法，而不是只追着它们留下的残骸跑。目前为止，我有一份来自被遗忘前哨的半埋报告、一台被所有人归咎于太阳噪声的异常发射机，以及一艘塞满"几乎对齐"日志的漂移金库船；合在一起，它们用不同的话说着同一件事：有人一直在把定居星系最熟悉的航线当作"没人想看之物"的掩护。

#en: The abandoned Deimos scrapyard hangs in dead orbit like the inside of Gravline's head laid bare, a ring of gutted hulls and stripped avionics wired into one last, desperate experiment in control. Every grav sensor, every cut-down frame here has been turned into a single vast instrument panel, letting him reach into emergency channels and nudge ships toward disaster with the same precision he once used to pull them clear. This place is the sum of a thousand small compromises: a firmware tweak for "safety," a falsified beacon to shave response time, a single convoy allowed to drift a little too long. Left intact, the scrapyard will keep feeding his ledger, pushing the next accident just over the line from misfortune to massacre. I traced him here from the first dead relay on that lonely rock, through the quiet anomalies hidden in factory diagnostics, then the contraband cargo lists that danced every time his callsign flickered across a distress band.
zh: 那座废弃的火卫二废料场像"重力线"头脑内部被摊开般悬在死寂轨道上，一圈被掏空的船壳与被剥光的航电，接进最后一次绝望的控制实验。这里的每一个引力传感器、每一个被削减的框架，都被变成一块巨大的仪表盘，让他能把手伸进紧急频道，并以他曾用来把船只拽出险境的那种精确，把船推向灾难。这地方是一千次微小妥协的总和：为"安全"做的固件微调、为缩短响应时间而伪造的信标、被允许漂得太久的一支车队。任其完好，废料场就会继续喂养他的账本，把下一场事故从不幸推过界、变成屠杀。我从那块孤独岩石上第一座死中继起追他到这里，穿过藏在工厂诊断里的安静异常，再穿过每当他的呼号在遇险频段闪烁时就会起舞的违禁货物清单。

#en: The Abandoned Bionics Lab is the only place that fits the pattern: forgotten corporate hardware, intact neural bays, and enough dead registry space for someone to hide a spine of code meant to stitch scattered minds into a single, untouchable mesh. Old Ryujin markings still ghost the walls, a language Splice speaks better than anyone alive, and the Cerberus Slick Syndicate have moved in like they are guarding scripture they do not understand, swearing they have seen lights in the sealed wings while others scoff and call it all nerves. Whatever anchor she left behind will be wired into this rusting skeleton of implants and interface rigs, humming just low enough to dodge every official scan. Up to now the trail runs like this: a discarded dataslate in the wild, then a quiet corporate contact whispering about missing firmware, and finally a half-erased reference to a buried node out in this derelict lab where her work first began to bend off the books.
zh: 那座废弃仿生学实验室是唯一契合这个模式的地方：被遗忘的公司硬件、完好的神经舱，以及足够多的死登记空间，供人藏起一根意在把散乱心智缝成单一不可触碰网格的代码脊柱。墙上仍幽灵着旧龙神的标记，一种"拼接"说得比任何活人都好的语言；而"地狱犬滑头辛迪加"搬了进来，像在守护他们并不理解的经文，发誓他们在密封翼楼里见过灯光，而另一些人则嗤之以鼻、说那全是神经紧张。她留下的无论什么锚点，都会被接进这具由植入体与接口设备构成的锈蚀骨架，嗡鸣得刚好够躲过每一次官方扫描。到目前为止，线索是这样的：荒野里一块被丢弃的数据板，然后是一名安静的公司联系人低语着失踪固件，最后是一处对这座废弃实验室深处某被埋节点的半擦除引用——她的作品正是在那里开始偏离账册。

#en: Out here, the old UC listening post hangs like a bad secret someone tried to forget, its dead dishes still aimed at the same debris fields where too many ships have gone silent. The place was built to hear everything the war left behind, and Rivet has turned that purpose inward, feeding its archives with doctored logs while its processors chew through the last untouched records of his work. Every purged file wipes one more wreck from history and makes it easier for higher-ups to claim nothing was ever wrong with those drives, those routes, those bodies. By the time the first patrol notices the station has gone quiet, his pattern of "acceptable losses" will be buried for good, and the accidents can start again without anyone seeing the shape. We traced the arc from a nameless buoy full of retired tags to a forgotten Deimos yard, found falsified inspections, vanished hull IDs, and one stubborn engineer's signature threaded through every quiet disaster.
zh: 在这里，那座旧联殖听音哨像一个有人试图遗忘的糟糕秘密悬着，它死掉的天线盘仍瞄准着同样那些太多船只陷入沉默的碎片场。这地方本是为听见战争留下的一切而建，而"铆钉"把那个用途转向内部，用被做手脚的日志喂养它的档案，同时它的处理器咀嚼着他作品最后未被触碰的记录。每一次被清除的文件都从历史上抹掉一处残骸，也让上级更容易声称那些引擎、那些航线、那些尸体从来没有任何问题。等到第一支巡逻队注意到这座星际站已陷入沉默时，他那套"可接受的损失"模式将已被永久埋葬，而事故可以在没人看清形状的情况下重新开始。我们追着那条弧线，从一枚塞满退役标签的无名浮标到一片被遗忘的火卫二场区，发现了伪造检查、消失的船体 ID，以及一名固执工程师的签名——它穿在每一场安静的灾难里。

#en: These rocks are where the lanes fray, where stray cargo and broken hulls drift just far enough off the charts that no one argues over who lost them; if anyone wanted to keep quiet records on how ships really end up in graveyards, they would tuck them here, between shadows and sensor blind spots. The crate you are after has clearly changed hands more than once, scribbled over with conflicting claim codes and half-baked transponder tags, a victim of rushed handoffs and sloppy manifests that accidentally preserved what more careful edits might have erased. Hidden among this debris, the true pattern of diverted traffic and engineered "accidents" can be reconstructed before someone finally tidies it away.
