Up to this point, all you have is a lonely scrap of data from a forgotten world and a dead relay humming with mismatched pings, both hinting that a trail of minor oversights and quiet edits has been steering ships toward the same unmarked stretch of space.
zh: 这些岩石，是航道磨损之处：散落的货物与破损的船壳漂得刚好偏离星图，没人会为"谁弄丢了它们"争论；若有人想给"船只究竟如何最终进入墓地"留下安静的记录，他们会把它藏在这里，藏在阴影与传感器盲点之间。你要找的那个货箱明显几度易手，涂满相互矛盾的索赔代码与半吊子的应答器标签，是匆忙交接与潦草舱单的受害者——而那些潦草反而意外保存了更仔细的编辑本可能抹掉的东西。埋在这片残骸里的，是被改道交通与人为"事故"的真实模式，能在有人终于把它收拾掉之前重建。到目前为止，你只有一穷乡世界上一块孤独的数据碎片与一座嗡鸣着对不上脉冲的死中继，两者都暗示一串小小的疏忽与安静的编辑一直在把船只引向同一段未标注的太空。

#en: Down here under Neon, the air tastes of ozone and old fry oil, and the Conduction Grid groans overhead like some caged storm; if anyone was going to sketch forbidden jump paths, it would be in a place where nobody asks what ships are being stripped or why certain hulls never reappear topside. The Underbelly is where captains whisper about off-chart test volumes and dead buoys, where mechanics trade drive logs like contraband, and where the people who know too much about misaligned vectors drink until they remember to keep quiet. Somewhere in this rusted maze lies the pattern that ties wrecked freighters, missing recall codes, and a bounty hunter's changing allegiances into one line of travel, thinned and redacted by omission. So far the trail runs from a stray slate in the dust, to fractured telemetry in a lonely monitoring shack, to a gutted ship whose drive history did not match the manifest, each step marked by what was almost said and then swallowed.
zh: 在霓虹城之下，空气尝起来像臭氧与旧炸油，输电网格在头顶像某种被关起来的雷暴般呻吟；若有人要画下被禁止的跃迁路径，那就会在一个没人问"哪些船正在被拆、为何某些船壳再没回到地面"的地方。下腹是船长们低语着账外测试量与死浮标的地方，是机械师像交易违禁品一样交易引擎日志的地方，也是太了解错位向量的人喝到记得该闭嘴为止的地方。在这座锈蚀迷宫的某处，藏着那个把受损货船、失踪的召回代码与一名赏金猎人不断变化的立场系成一条行迹的模式——它被省略磨薄、涂黑。目前为止，线索从尘土里一块散落数据板，到一座孤独监控棚里断裂的遥测，再到一艘引擎履历与舱单不符的被掏空船只，每一步都以"几乎说出口、随后又被咽下"的东西为标记。

#en: Waggoner Farm is where all of Mira's careful abstractions finally touch real soil; here, her designs are no longer numbers in a lab archive or freight codes buried in GalBank manifests, but towering stalks and choking pollen wrapped around a family's livelihood. She has turned this quiet homestead into a proof of concept and a dead man's switch at once, calibrating a strain that can either rescue half the frontier from famine or show HelioGen and their UC handlers exactly what their denial crops can do when unleashed. As you arrive, rival hunters close in and containment thresholds edge toward failure, seconds from tipping a local test into a sector-wide incident. Back at the factories and docks, you scraped scorch marks and altered manifests out of Gagarin, then pried financial ghosts from a drifting GalBank hulk, and the pattern they drew was simple enough to sketch yet strangely slippery, always circling the same name without ever quite landing on why.
zh: 瓦戈纳农场，是米拉所有那些细致抽象最终触碰真实土壤的地方；在这里，她的设计不再是实验室档案里的数字或埋在盖尔银行舱单里的货运代码，而是缠绕着一个家庭生计的高耸茎秆与令人窒息的粉雾。她把这处安静的农庄同时变成了概念验证与死人开关：正在校准一种既能从饥荒中拯救半个边境、又能向"赫利奥根"及联殖经手人展示"他们的拒绝作物一旦放出能干什么"的菌株。当你抵达时，对手猎人正在逼近，围控阈值正向失效滑动，离把一次本地测试倾覆成一场星区级事件只差几秒。回到工厂与码头，你从加加林星刮出了灼痕与被改动的舱单，又从一具漂着的盖尔银行残骸里撬出了财务幽灵，而它们画出的模式简单得可以速写、却又奇怪地滑不留手——总是绕着同一个名字，却从未真正落到"为什么"上。

#en: The abandoned industrial compound is where every angle she has been plotting finally converges. Buried beneath rusted gantries and dead cranes sits the only place left in the system where she can run a grav core hot enough, quiet enough, to stitch her private corridors together and slip beyond anyone's reach. The old test chamber gives her the shielding, the isolation, and the dirty power feeds to burn all remaining logs or broadcast them in one last, devastating pulse that could rewrite blame across half the Settled Systems. Waiting any longer means watching UC, Crimson captains, and Trade Authority fixers inherit a weaponized map of space itself, all wrapped in the softer lies told in mess halls and backroom deals. So far the trail has led through a Freestar trailer packed with redacted Ranger notes, then to a scarred orbit where a drifting sensor buoy showed her signature threaded through the convoy's death, each clue more warped by rumor than the last.
zh: 那座废弃工业区，是她一直在策划的所有角度终于汇聚之处。埋在锈蚀龙门架与死吊车之下的，是这个星系里仅剩的一处她能足够热、足够安静地运转引力核心、把自己的私人走廊缝在一起并溜出任何人触及范围的地方。那座旧测试舱给了她屏蔽、隔离与肮脏的电力馈线，去烧掉所有剩余日志，或以最后一次毁灭性脉冲把它们广播出去——那能改写半个定居星系的罪责归属。再等下去，就意味着看着联殖、深红舰队长官与贸易管理局掮客继承一张把太空本身武器化的地图，而这一切还裹在食堂与密室交易里说的那些更温和的谎言中。目前为止，线索穿过一辆塞满涂黑游骑兵笔记的自由星系联盟拖车，然后到一条伤痕累累的轨道——一枚漂移传感器浮标显示她的签名穿在车队的死亡里，每一条线索都比上一条被传闻扭曲得更厉害。

#en: The UC Vanguard hulk drifts in a slow, wounded roll, its transponders long silent but its systems still whispering to anyone who knows how to listen. Whatever Rahimi pulled from here, she chose this ship for a reason the Vanguard ran the same kind of high-stress combat lanes she once flew, its black boxes soaked in the exact drive responses and anomaly signatures she needs to refine her corridors beyond military oversight. Buried in its dead circuits is the only clean record of how her stolen math behaves in actual combat metal, a bridge between the corporate telemetry you pried out of that quiet research post and the rumors of wrecked haulers and missing couriers scattered along off-chart routes. So far the trail is a chain of corrupted nav logs, a nervous analyst tracing impossible vectors through restricted space, and scattered testimonies of ships that took a shortcut and never came back, all pointing to a single pilot tuning the grid to her own design.
zh: 那具联殖先锋队残骸以缓慢而受伤的姿态翻滚，应答器早已沉默，可它的系统仍在对任何懂得如何聆听的人低语。无论拉希米从这里拽出了什么，她选中这艘船都有原因：先锋队曾跑着她一度亲历的那类高应力战斗航道，它的黑匣浸透了她把走廊精炼到军用监督之外的所需的确切引擎响应与异常签名。埋在它死掉电路里的，是她偷来的数学在真实战斗金属里如何表现的唯一干净记录，是"你从安静研究据点撬出的公司遥测"与"散落在偏图航线上的损毁货船和失踪信使传闻"之间的桥梁。目前为止，这条线索是一串损坏的导航日志、一名在受限太空中追踪不可能向量的紧张分析员，以及零散证词——关于"抄了近路就再没回来"的船只，全都指向一名把网格调成自己设计的飞行员。

#en: Out here on the dark side of a nameless moon, this relay is the only place her trail could be both hidden and useful at the same time; every crate that passed through, every falsified manifest, bled a little of her pattern into the cargo logs, and this broker has been skimming those echoes for profit. The module sits just far enough off the main lanes that no official auditor ever checks its numbers, but close enough that smugglers and desperate settlers rely on it, letting the past settle into ledgers and routing tables that quietly nudge shipments toward an off grid canyon she wants kept fed. The crate tags from the abandoned farmstead, the altered figures behind the ruined homestead, the traffic flagged under the Trade Authority contact on Neon, and the queue anomalies traced in New Atlantis all point to the same conclusion someone has been bending the flow of supplies, inch by inch, toward a hidden settlement that does not exist on any sanctioned chart.
zh: 在这里、在一颗无名卫星的暗面上，那座中继是她痕迹唯一能同时既隐藏又有用的地方；每一个经过的货箱、每一份被伪造的舱单，都把她的模式渗了一点进货运日志，而这里的掮客一直在为利益揩取那些回声。那座舱室离主航道刚好足够远、任何官方审计员都从不核对它的数字，却又近到走私者与走投无路的定居者都依赖它，让过去沉淀成账册与航线表——它们悄悄把货运推向一条她想保持供应的账外峡谷。废弃农庄的货箱标签、被毁农庄背后被改动的数字、霓虹城贸易管理局联系人名下被标记的交通，以及新亚特兰蒂斯城里被追溯到的队列异常，全都指向同一个结论：有人一直在把补给流一寸一寸地掰向一个不存在于任何获批星图上的隐藏定居点。

#en: Out here, the Deserted UC Listening Post hangs between routes like a bad memory, still wired into ancient corridor telemetry the Navy never fully shut off. Its antennae drink in grav-drive noise from every passing ship, feeding Vector the raw data she needs to refine her illegal paths, scrub her own trail, and decide whose convoy lives or dies. Now she is using the post as both shield and knife, collating Echo Trench casualty records with fresh jumps, ready to erase the last evidence that those losses were ever more than numbers on a screen. If she finishes, the pattern behind years of vanished haulers and impossible ambushes dissolves into static and rumor again, another ghost story traded in dockside bars. All I have before stepping through that airlock are the half-truths bought over drinks on Neon and the corrupted Trade Authority logs drifting in that derelict support ship, each retelling of her routes bending a little differently under the weight of fear.
zh: 在这里，"被遗弃的联殖听音哨"像一段糟糕记忆悬在航线之间，仍接在海军从未完全关闭的古老走廊遥测上。它的天线啜饮着每一艘过往船只的引力引擎噪声，把"向量"精炼她非法路径、擦净自己痕迹、决定谁的车队生谁的车队死所需的原始数据喂给她。如今她把这座哨所同时当作盾牌与刀，正在核对"回声海沟"伤亡记录与新鲜跃迁，准备抹掉"那些损失曾不只是屏幕上数字"的最后证据。若她完工，多年失踪货船与不可能伏击背后的模式就会再次溶解成静电与传闻，成为码头酒吧里交易的又一则鬼故事。在踏进那道气闸之前，我只有霓虹城酒桌上买来的半真半假，以及那艘漂着的贸易管理局支援船里损坏的日志；每一次对她航线的转述，都在恐惧的重压下弯得略有不同。

#en: In this thin stretch of orbit, the debris fields all seem to lean the same way, as if every broken hull and dead satellite has been quietly sliding along an unseen current toward this exact point. Whatever is wired into the machinery out here is not just broadcasting; it is holding a pattern in place, keeping old triage routes and evacuation vectors from ever fully decaying, like muscle memory in a wounded limb that refuses to relax. Following that geometry means stepping into the same slow pull that has been guiding diverted transports, mislogged patrols, and one tireless medic from system to system without anyone quite noticing.  \nSo far I have chased an anonymous cache on a nameless rock, a derelict SysDef frame still obeying half-erased orders, and a curated war exhibit that accidentally admitted one medic walked away when the records say otherwise; every piece has curved me closer to this orbit, as if the whole investigation was always going to end up here.
zh: 在这条稀薄的轨道带上，那些碎片场似乎都朝同一方向倾斜，仿佛每一个破损船壳与死卫星都在沿一道看不见的水流悄悄滑向这个确切的点。接在这外面机械里的东西不只是在广播；它是在把一个模式固定在原处，让旧的分诊路线与撤离向量从不完全衰败，就像一条受伤肢体里拒绝放松的肌肉记忆。追着那个几何走，意味着踏进同样那股缓慢的牵引——它一直把被改道的运输船、记录错误的巡逻队，以及一名不知疲倦的医疗兵从一个星系引到另一个星系，而没人真正察觉。  \n目前为止，我追过无名岩石上一处匿名储藏点、一具仍服从半擦除命令的弃置星防队船架，以及一处意外承认"有一名医疗兵在记录声称并非如此时走了出去"的策展战争展览；每一块都把我更弯向这条轨道，仿佛整场调查注定要在这里结束。

#en: Only a derelict like CM-1304 could hold what everyone else missed the first time through; its hull is still flagged as a routine loss, its orbit too quiet for anyone but insurance clerks and grave-robbers to care. The UC Navy walked away after the reports were signed, systems sealed, and flight data shunted into cold storage, never asking why a supposedly safe corridor tore this ship open on a perfect approach. Down its dark spine, the old navigation core still whispers in stored vectors and rejected routes, the place where her calculations brushed against official doctrine and were quietly buried. The crew and their overseers are long gone, promoted, transferred, or dead, having moved on before they understood what they had helped set in motion. So far the trail is a half-burned dataslate from a forgotten outpost, then an orbital beacon guarded by jumpy Spacers, all pointing to manipulated lanes and a controller who knew exactly which ships could be written off.
zh: 只有像"CM-1304"这样的弃船才能装下别人第一次经过时全都错过的东西；它的船壳仍被标为一次例行损失，它的轨道安静到只有保险文书与盗墓者才在意。联殖海军在报告签完、系统封存、飞行数据被塞进冷库之后就走开了，从没问过为何一条据称安全的走廊会在一次完美的进近中把这艘船撕开。在它黑暗的脊骨里，旧导航核心仍在储存的向量与被否决的航线里低语——那是她的计算擦过官方学说、随后被悄悄埋葬的地方。船员与他们的监工早已不在，升迁、调职或死亡，在他们明白自己帮助启动了什么都之前就已离开。目前为止，这条线索是一块来自被遗忘前哨的半烧毁数据板，然后是一座由紧张兮兮的太空劫匪把守的轨道信标，全都指向被操弄的航道与一名确切知道哪些船可以被核销的调度员。

#en: The Seamender hangs in the dark like it died mid-sentence, drives cold, running lights gone, only the faint echo of emergency power bleeding through its hull. Whatever was being moved for Trade Authority on this run was worth routing through a corridor no one admits exists, and worth silencing every transponder that might have remembered why. If there is any place left where the pattern of adjusted delays and missing ships has not been rewritten to fit the official story, it is inside this courier's forgotten logs, tucked behind the kind of encryption merchants reserve for debts and blackmail. So far, all anyone has are pieces: a stray dataslate pulled off a drifting rock, a Navy scout that vanished between pings, delay codes a nervous scheduler swears they never issued, and hushed talk in dockside bars about a controller who can bend routes like wire; no one holds the whole story, just fragments traded in low voices when they are sure they are not being recorded.
zh: 缝海者像在句子中途死去般悬在黑暗中，引擎冰冷，航行灯熄灭，只有一丝应急电力从船壳渗出。这趟贸易管理局的运货值得经由一条没人承认存在的走廊转运，也值得让每一个可能记得原因的应答器都闭嘴。若说还有哪里保存着"被调整的延误与失踪船只"这一模式、尚未被改写成符合官方说法，它就在这艘信使船被遗忘的日志里，藏在商人专为债务与勒索保留的那种加密之后。目前为止，所有人只有碎片：一穷乡岩石上拽下的一块散落数据板、一艘在两次脉冲之间消失的海军侦察船、一名紧张调度员发誓自己从未签发的延迟代码，以及码头酒吧里关于"能把航线像铁丝一样掰弯的调度员"的低语；没人掌握整个故事，只有在确信没在录音时低声交易的碎片。

#en: The broken command post is the first place her story frays in more voices than one, where the shouting stopped mid-order and only blast scars and buried data are left to finish the sentences. Here the raiders thought they understood her pattern well enough to spring a trap, charting her passes between outlying farms, forgotten labs, and lightning-choked ports, but whatever they learned died with them and their bodies do not talk. What remains in these splintered walls is the only unfiltered record of that study, written by hands that had no reason to protect reputations, where certain names are scratched out and pointed references turn into vague gestures and half-legible arrows on a map.  \nSo far the trail began with an anonymous lead in the back end of nowhere, firmed up by worried chatter at a frontier support post and anomalous readings near a Helium-3 line, and ended in this ruin where an overconfident crew tried to anticipate her route and vanished instead.
zh: 那座破损指挥所，是她的故事第一次在不止一张嘴里走样的地方：喊叫声在某道命令中途停止，只剩爆痕与被埋的数据来把句子补完。在这里，掠夺者以为足够了解她的模式、足以布下一个陷阱，把她在外围农场、被遗忘实验室与闪电缠绕港市之间的穿行绘成图；可他们学到的任何东西都随他们一同死去，而尸体不会说话。留在这四壁裂痕里的，是那项研究唯一未经筛选的记录，由没有理由维护名声的手写下——其中某些名字被划掉，明确的指认变成含糊的手势与地图上半可辨认的箭头。  \n目前为止，这条线索始于天涯之外的一条匿名线报，被某座边境补给站里忧心忡忡的闲谈与氦-3 航线附近的异常读数坐实，最终终结在这片废墟——一支过于自信的队伍试图预料她的路线，却反而消失了。

#en: The FX-1555 drifts dark and silent, yet this is where the lines finally cross, where an old UC Navy hull still carries enough authority in its dead circuits to make or break every closed claim you have been chasing. Someone with registry expertise has been feeding war-era convoy logs into civilian loss reports, stitching a hidden lattice of routes and disappearances through its surviving cores; left untouched, that lattice becomes either a shield for the people who profited from those losses or a weapon in their hands. The ship is a junction, not a relic, and the traffic that once moved under its guns is the same traffic that kept vanishing just off its patrol paths, too often to pass as bad luck. Earlier, you found a discarded arbitration slate in the dust and a crippled relay spliced to throttle beacons, both pointing to the same pattern of ships written off and signals quietly strangled until coincidence stopped feeling like chance and started looking like design.
zh: FX-1555黑暗而沉默地漂着，可这里正是线条最终相交之处：一具旧联殖海军船壳，在它死掉的电路里仍携带足够的权威，足以成就或击碎你一直在追的每一笔已结清索赔。某个拥有登记专业技能的人，一直在把战时护航日志喂进民用损失报告，通过它幸存的核心里缝出一张由航线与失踪构成的隐藏网格；任其不理，那张网格就会成为"从那些损失中获利之人"的盾牌，或他们手中的武器。这艘船是一个枢纽，不是遗物，而曾在其枪炮下移动的交通，正是那批不断在它巡逻路径外侧消失、频繁到无法当作霉运的交通。早先，你在尘土里发现一块被丢弃的仲裁数据板，以及一座被接上扼流信标的残废中继，两者都指向同一个模式：船只被核销，信号被悄悄扼杀，直到巧合不再像偶然、而开始像设计。

#en: The deserted relay station sits at the edge of mapped space, an old UC bone left to bleach in vacuum, which makes it perfect cover for whoever has been whispering into the lanes. Its dishes look frozen and dead, but down in the control well the boards still flicker with low-power diagnostics, just enough to catch a faint, recurring spike in the traffic a tiny shift in timing, the same crooked signature that keeps turning routine jumps into wrecks. The Silk Collective are dug in here, smugglers using the blind spot for their own routes, unaware or uncaring that someone else has been riding their shadow to test corrections on passing haulers. The more you sift through old log fragments and burned-out cores, the clearer it is that none of this started today a missing convoy written off years ago, a relay quietly reactivated off the books, a pattern first glimpsed in a scorched dataslate and confirmed by a frightened analyst watching anomaly folders vanish in New Atlantis.
zh: 那座废弃中继站坐落在已测绘太空的边缘，一根被留在真空中漂白的联殖旧骨，这让它成了任何"朝航道低语之人"的完美掩护。它的天线盘看起来冻结而死，可在控制井深处，那些板子仍在低功率诊断下闪烁，刚好足以捕捉交通里一个微弱而反复出现的尖峰：一次微小的时机偏移，同一道把例行跃迁变成残骸的歪斜签名。"丝绸联合体"在这里扎了根，走私者用自己的航线利用这个盲点，浑然不觉或毫不在乎另有谁一直在骑他们的阴影、拿过往货船测试修正。你越是翻检旧日志碎片与烧毁的核心，就越清楚这一切并非始于今日：多年前被核销的一支失踪车队、一座被悄悄账外重启的中继、一个最初在烧焦数据板上瞥见、并由一名在新亚特兰蒂斯城看着异常文件夹消失的受惊分析员证实的模式。

#en: Out past the standard lanes, the Deserted UC Listening Post hangs in the dark like a rusting ear, still wired into the same deep-space channels that once carried classified test telemetry. It is the one place Rahimi can splice ancient sensor grids and fresh anomaly data without tripping modern oversight, turning a forgotten war relic into the keystone of her campaign against controlled skies. Here she has dragged every stolen fragment together the erased reports hinted at in that quiet research module, the corrupted vector chains recovered from the drifting Vanguard hulk and is using the station's long-range arrays to align a final corridor that will either expose the system's lies or tear open space around half the settled routes. From the scraps we trust, the trail began with a discarded slate of warped nav logs, sharpened through corporate telemetry, then confirmed by wreck-field data on a dead UC combat ship all pointing to one pilot reshaping the grid from the shadows.
zh: 在标准航道之外，那座"被遗弃的联殖听音哨"像一只生锈的耳朵悬在黑暗中，仍接在那些曾承载机密测试遥测的深空频道上。这是拉希米唯一能在不触发现代监督的情况下，把古老传感器网格与新鲜异常数据拼接起来的地方，把一件被遗忘的战争遗物变成她对抗"受控天空"战役的拱心石。在这里，她把每一块偷来的碎片拽到一起——那座安静研究舱里暗示的被抹除报告、从那具漂移先锋队残骸里找出的损坏向量链——并用这座星际站的长程阵列对齐最后一条走廊：它要么揭穿系统的谎言，要么在半个定居航线周围撕开太空。从我们信任的碎片看，这条线索始于一块写满扭曲导航日志的被丢弃数据板，经由公司遥测变得清晰，再由一艘死掉联殖战斗舰上的残骸场数据证实，全都指向一名从阴影里重塑网格的飞行员。

#en: This abandoned Ecliptic garrison sits on the intersection of too many lanes to be coincidence, a forgotten node where patrol charts, mercenary manifests, and traffic control feeds once crossed in quiet patterns. Its guns are cold now, but the buried relays still listen to every jump signature in a dozen systems, a perfect blind spot for someone who lives inside routes and probabilities. Here, Vector can finalize whatever she and Kraye have been building, tying together stolen nav-suites and altered patrol grids into a single, self-sustaining web before slipping away along a corridor only she can see. Too many captains vanished along those lines, too many "accidents" written off without question. We traced the first anomaly to a chance dataslate in the black, followed the trail through a freighter with impossible course changes and a silent beacon in orbit; each step pointed to one truth, that someone has been editing the map for years while everyone else looked the other way.
zh: 这座废弃的黄道佣兵团驻军坐落在太多航线的交点上，不可能只是巧合；一个被遗忘的节点，在那里，巡逻星图、佣兵舱单与交管数据流曾以安静的规律相交。它的枪炮如今冰冷，可被埋的中继仍在聆听十来个星系里的每一个跃迁签名，对某个活在航线与概率里的人而言，这是个完美的盲点。在这里，"向量"能最终完成她与克雷一直在建造的东西，把偷来的导航套件与被改动的巡逻网格系成一张单一、自持的网，然后沿一条只有她看得见的走廊溜走。太多船长沿着那些线消失，太多"事故"被毫无疑问地核销。我们把第一处异常追到漆黑中一块偶然的数据板，顺着线索穿过一艘航向变化不可能的货船与轨道上一座沉默的信标；每一步都指向同一个真相：有人多年来一直在编辑地图，而其他人都转开了视线。

#en: A GalBank protection ship does not simply vanish from the lanes, yet the CB-6735 Trustsphere hangs here in dead orbit, its hull scoured and its escorts conspicuously absent, as if every calculation that should have kept it safe had been nudged a fraction off course. This was the bank's armored promise that certain convoys could never be touched, which makes its ruin the perfect ledger of who has been quietly rewriting the odds; only inside this derelict will the protected manifests, jump chains, and loss files still speak in the language Vector understands best. The ship's silence feels less like an accident and more like a sum finally reaching its inevitable result, every misaligned route and insured disaster converging on this one piece of proof. Before this, all you had was a half-buried dataslate on a forgotten rock and muttered accusations in a worn-down quarter of Akila, talk of discount vectors and a ghost navigator who walked away when the numbers stopped favoring her.
zh: 一艘盖尔银行护航船不会就这么从航道上消失，可"CB-6735 信球"却死寂地悬在这条轨道上，船壳被刮蚀，护航队显著缺席，仿佛每一个本该保证它安全的计算都被推偏了一点。这本是那家银行"某些车队永不能被碰"的装甲承诺，这让它的残骸成了"谁一直在悄悄改写概率"的完美账册；只有在这具弃船内部，那些受保护的舱单、跃迁链与损失文件，才会仍以"向量"最精通的语言说话。这艘船的沉默感觉不太像意外，更像一个总和终于抵达它不可避免的结果：每一条错位航线与每一场被保险的灾难，都汇聚到这一件证据上。在此之前，你只有一块被遗忘岩石上被半埋的数据板，以及阿基拉城某个破败街区里压低声音的指控——关于打折向量与一名"在数字不再偏向她时走开"的幽灵领航员。

#en: New Atlantis wears its routine like armor: commuter trams humming, TerraBrew cups in every bin, corporate shipments cycling through waste bays so regular nobody really looks at the manifests anymore. That is why the trace has to be pulled here, in the one city where Vector knew every maintenance schedule, every inspection blind spot, and could slip dangerous math into the stream under the cover of habit. UC oversight, Calyx contractors, and shipwrights all passed their eyes over the same numbers for years, trusting familiar signatures while the anomalies tucked themselves deeper into background noise. Now, choosing this line of inquiry means committing to the idea that the rot started in plain sight, not at some distant frontier rock. So far the trail holds a falsified accident report from a quiet lab, a discarded dataslate of frantic equations, and orbital telemetry that matches buried drive failures, all hinting that someone inside the core worlds let this go on far too long.
zh: 新亚特兰蒂斯城把它的例行公事像盔甲一样穿着：通勤电车嗡鸣、每个垃圾桶里都有地球酿酒的杯子、公司货运以规律到再没人细看舱单的节奏循环穿过废料湾。正因如此，这条痕迹必须在这座城市里被拽出来——在这唯一一座"向量"熟悉每一份维护日程、每一处检查盲点、并能以习惯为掩护把危险数学溜进数据流的城市。联殖监督、花萼承包商与造船师们的目光多年来都扫过同样的数字，信任着熟悉的签名，而异常则把自己藏进更深的背景噪声里。如今，选择这条调查路线，意味着认定腐烂始于众目睽睽之下，而非某颗遥远的边境岩石。目前为止，这条线索包含一份来自安静实验室的被伪造事故报告、一块写满狂乱方程的废弃数据板，以及与埋藏引擎故障相符的轨道遥测，全都暗示核心世界内部有人让这一切持续得太久。

#en: The deserted robotics lab matters because this is where code and chassis first learned to move together without oversight, a forgotten testbed for exactly the kind of hybrid work the fugitive has been refining in the shadows. Bravo Razorpoint holding the floor means someone with deep pockets wants this place sanitized, not examined, and the way their patrol routes circle the data banks says the real prize is not the scrap on the lines but the map burned into their drives. The air hums with half-drained power and half-finished lies, and there is a low murmur under it all that feels like unease, as if everyone involved knows the truth sits somewhere between fear and convenience. So far the trail runs from a freestar investigator's half-redacted notes to implant failures in the frontier and suppressed logs out of Neon, each file pointing back to the same rogue technician and a pattern of erased clinics, missing firmware, and clients who vanish once their augments start to whisper.
zh: 那座废弃机器人实验室之所以要紧，是因为这里正是代码与底盘第一次学会在无人监督下共同运作的地方，一处被遗忘的试验台，恰是那名逃犯一直在阴影里精炼的那类混合工作所需。"布拉沃剃刀尖"守在这片地面上，说明有人出重金想把这地方消毒、而非检查；而他们巡逻路线绕着数据库转的方式说明，真正的战利品不是流水线上的废料，而是烧进他们硬盘里的地图。空气因半耗尽的电力与半途而废的谎言而嗡鸣，底下还有一声低低的杂音，听起来像不安，仿佛每一个相关的人都明白真相就坐在恐惧与便利之间的某处。目前为止，线索从一名自由星系联盟调查员半涂黑的笔记，延伸到边境上的植入体故障与霓虹城流出的被压制日志，每份文件都指回同一名流氓技师与一种"诊所被抹除、固件失踪、客户在增强体开始低语后消失"的模式。

#en: In deep transit lanes where laws thin out and insurance clauses grow teeth, nothing hides better than a vault ship gone quiet. This one once ferried the secrets of clients and corporations, each deposit sealed behind armored bulkheads and GalBank legal muscle. Now its transponder stutters, its orbit decays, and its datastacks sit beyond any official audit, which makes it the one place a careful saboteur could stash a record that would embarrass both the UC and Deimos. Every corridor here hums with suppressed arguments about Cheyenne that never made it into reports, and the log you are chasing is the first time those voices were pinned to numbers instead of rumor. So far the trail has run through a dead outpost where a nameless dataslate surfaced, then a cargo yard where Vector's mark was etched into ghost code, each step confirming that the old stories about vented crews, missing annexes, and buried retrofits were not accidents but a pattern everyone saw and chose not to fight.
zh: 在法律变稀薄、保险条款长牙的深空运输航道里，没有什么比一艘安静下来的金库船藏得更好。这一艘曾运送客户与公司的秘密，每一笔存款都封在装甲舱壁与盖尔银行的法律肌肉之后。如今它的应答器结巴、轨道衰减，数据库坐在任何官方审计之外，这让它成了某个谨慎破坏者唯一能藏起"同时羞辱联殖与火卫二之记录"的地方。这里的每条走廊都嗡鸣着从未进入报告的、关于夏延星的被压制争吵，而你要追的那份日志，正是那些声音第一次被钉在数字上、而非传闻上的时刻。目前为止，线索穿过一座浮现无名数据板的死掉前哨，然后是一片被刻进幽灵代码里的"向量"标记的货运场区，每一步都证实：关于"被排空大气的船员、失踪的附属文件与被埋的改装"的旧故事不是意外，而是一个人人都看见、却选择不与之为敌的模式。

#en: Gagarin Landing is where his ghosts and his grudges overlap, the one place that still remembers both the mechs he once guarded and the people he walked away from. The elevated catwalks and dead assembly lines give him sightlines, choke points, and power runs he helped design in another life, and now he is using them to erase the last proof of what he has done and who paid for it. You can feel the half-finished clean up in the darkened bays: data cores half-pulled, scorch marks scrubbed but not repainted, security shutters jammed halfway as if someone started tidying the scene and never came back. If he locks this place down, the story ends on his terms instead of the Settled Systems. So far the trail says only this much for certain: a dataslate in a forgotten outpost named a dead breacher, New Homestead whispered that his family history does not match the UC files, and a gutted SysDef scout in deep space confirmed someone has been hunting and hiding him off the books for years.
zh: 加加林着陆点，是他的幽灵与他的怨恨重叠之处——唯一仍同时记得他曾看守过的机甲、以及他转身离开的人们的地方。高架栈道与死掉的装配线给了他视线、咽喉点，以及他在另一段人生里参与设计的电力线路；如今他用它们抹掉"他做了什么、谁为此付了钱"的最后证据。在昏暗的货舱里，你能感觉到那场半途而废的清理：数据核心被拽出一半、灼痕被擦掉却没重新上漆、安保卷帘卡在中途，仿佛有人开始收拾现场、却再没回来。若他把这地方锁死，故事就会按他的条件结束，而不是按定居星系的条件。目前为止，这条线索只确定这些：一座被遗忘前哨里的数据板点出了一名死掉破门手，新家园低语说他的家族史与联殖档案对不上，而深空中一具被掏空的星防队侦察船证实：有人多年来一直在账外追猎并藏匿他。

#en: Out here in the quiet above the planet is where the stories say her work really happened, not in crowded offices or backroom bars, but in the numbers no one bothers to read twice. The listening posts, the survey nodes, all those old arrays left ticking along on forgotten firmware that smugglers and settlers swear she could talk to better than most people. If there is any place she would hide the map behind her maps, it is in a station like this, where course corrections and survey pings can be nudged a fraction of a degree without anyone on the ground ever knowing. So far everything I have is secondhand a caseworker muttering about duplicate IDs, a dead contact who complained of "vanishing" approvals, a broker in Neon fencing half finished routes, and a gutted cutter whose last jump pointed toward an unnamed patch of sky; every retelling twists the details, but the outline stays the same someone has been bending the grid itself to feed a settlement that officially does not exist.
zh: 在这里、在行星上方的安静中，就是故事说她工作真正发生的地方——不在拥挤的办公室或密室酒吧，而在那些没人费心读两遍的数字里。那些听音哨、勘探节点、所有那些靠被遗忘固件滴答运行的旧阵列，走私者与定居者发誓她跟它们交流得比跟多数人还好。若说有什么地方她会把"地图背后的地图"藏起来，那就是这样一座星际站：在那里，航向修正与勘探脉冲能被推偏零点几度，而地面上没人会知道。目前为止，我的一切都是二手的：一名案件员嘟囔着重复的 ID、一名抱怨批准"凭空消失"的死掉线人、霓虹城一名兜售半成品航线的掮客，以及一艘最后一次跃迁指向某片无名天空的被掏空切割船；每一次转述都扭曲细节，但轮廓始终如一：有人一直在掰弯网格本身，去供养一个官方上并不存在的定居点。

#en: This is where the official story was scrubbed clean, where a garrison full of hurried decisions and panicked signatures got boiled down into a single neat version of the past; if the record stays intact, every ship nudged into a graveyard remains just another "unavoidable loss" on a report no one can challenge. Iron Unit dug in here tells you how important that fiction is, veterans guarding a stack of pages like it is the last shield between them and what really happened in these halls when orders came too fast and people died in the wrong places. Erasing this account is the only way to force the truth back into the lanes, to make the patterns of redirected traffic and rearranged wrecks stand out against the silence. So far the trail is a stray data fragment from a forgotten rock, a relay that went dark with mismatched timestamps, and this abandoned post where beacon logs and casualty notes were clearly altered in haste, their consequences drifting unseen through space ever since.
zh: 这里正是官方故事被擦干净的地方：一座满是仓促决定与惊慌签名的驻军被浓缩成一份整洁的过去版本；若这份记录保持完好，每一艘被推进墓地的船就仍只是报告上一桩"不可避免的损失"，没人能质疑。钢铁单位扎在这里，说明那份虚构有多重要：一群老兵守着一摞纸页，像守着他们与"当命令来得太快、人死在错误的地方时这些走廊里真正发生了什么"之间的最后一道盾牌。抹掉这份记录，是迫使真相回到航道、让"被改道的交通与被重新排列的残骸"这些模式在沉默中凸显出来的唯一办法。目前为止，这条线索是一块来自被遗忘岩石的散落数据碎片、一座带着对不上时戳陷入黑暗的中继，以及这座明显被仓促改动的信标日志与伤亡笔记的废弃哨所——它们的后果从此在太空中无人看见地漂荡。

#en: The Tradewind LT-8645 drifts on the edge of sanctioned space like an account no one wants to close, powered just enough to keep its lights dim and its transponders polite. Trade Authority paint still clings to the hull, but the silence around it feels negotiated, as if too many people agreed not to ask why a fully capable support ship was left to rust between lanes. Inside those maintenance decks and cargo bays sit the untouched mirrors of transactions, ownership chains, and the subtle scars of someone who knew exactly where to cut. If there is a map to the hidden system that has been rewriting lives, it will be chained to this ship's records, not any public terminal. The unease in the air is the same you felt when that first stray dataslate surfaced out in the black, when the quiet anomalies in the city branch did not match the stories upstairs, when a tired lawyer in the underlevels spoke of a second voice on old calls that kept "simplifying" things until people vanished on paper.
zh: 贸易风 LT-8645像一笔没人想结清的账户，漂在获批太空边缘，电力刚好够让灯光昏暗、应答器保持礼貌。贸易管理局的油漆仍黏在船壳上，可它周围的沉默感觉经过协商，仿佛太多人同意不问"一艘完全可用的支援船为何被留在航道之间锈蚀"。在那些维护甲板与货舱里，坐着交易、所有权链，以及某个确切知道该在哪里下刀之人所留微妙伤疤的未被动过的镜像。若说有一张通往那个一直在改写人生的隐藏星系的地图，它会被锁在这艘船的记录上，而不是任何公共终端。空气里的那种不安，与你在漆黑中第一块散落数据板浮现时感到的一样，与城市支行的安静异常与楼上传言对不上时一样，与下城层一名疲惫律师说起"旧呼叫里第二个声音不断'简化'事务、直到人在纸面上消失"时一样。

#en: Neon's rooftops are where routes become rumors given shape. Up here, above the glare of the Core and the stink of Ebbside, Zuri can see every ship threading Volii's sky, every corridor she has bent around tolls, patrols, and pirate nets. The antennas bristling from these towers are her last improvised array, bleeding stolen GalBank vault data into a final recalculation that could overwrite the lanes of half a dozen systems or wipe the only clean record of what Trident and its partners did in Dead Lane. She is seconds from locking in a new map, one that trades a thousand unseen lives for her vision of "safe passage," and once those corrections propagate there will be no pulling them back from the void. Earlier, scraps from a forgotten survey cabin, jittery logs in orbit, and that compromised vault ship all whispered the same thing in different voices, each source swearing it came from someone else first: Vector is still drawing, and the Settled Systems are already flying on her lines.
zh: 霓虹城的屋顶，是航线变成有了形状的传闻之处。在这上面、在核心区的炫光与埃布赛德的臭气之上，祖里能看见每一艘穿行沃利星天空的船，每一条她绕着过路费、巡逻与海盗网掰弯的走廊。这些塔楼上竖起的密集天线，是她最后一套临时阵列，把偷来的盖尔银行金库数据渗进最后一次重算——那能覆写半打星系的航道，或抹掉"海神叉及其伙伴在死航线做了什么"的唯一干净记录。她离锁定一张新地图只差几秒：用一千条看不见的命，换她那份"安全通行"的愿景；而那些修正一旦传播，就再无法从虚空中拉回。早先，一座被遗忘勘探小屋的碎片、轨道上抖动的日志，以及那艘被攻陷的金库船，都用不同的声音低语同一件事——每一处来源都发誓自己是从别人那里先听来的："向量"仍在绘图，而定居星系已经在她的线上飞行。

#en: Out here, where the planet is just a dim curve and the only weather is the static on your hull, the pattern she has been drawing across the Settled Systems finally resolves into something you can touch. The orbital net at this altitude is wired into the same forgotten monitoring lattice she once used for honest work; if she wanted a place to hide a master forecast, somewhere that could whisper to every frontier sky without anyone on the ground noticing, it would be in a grid like this, watched over by a gunship whose registry appears in no official shipping lanes. The briefings that sent you here skipped certain names, glided past who first flagged this orbit, as if everyone agreed not to say them out loud. So far you have followed a trail of corrupted logs from a lonely prefab, a dead hunter's derelict with half a bounty report burned away, and a string of remote outposts where the weather never quite matched the records, all pointing back toward the same careful hand on the controls.
zh: 在这里，行星只是暗淡的一弧、唯一的天气是船壳上的静电，她一直在定居星系上画的模式终于解析成某种你能触碰的东西。这个高度的轨道网，接在她曾用于正当工作的同一张被遗忘监测网格上；若她想找个地方藏一份总预报——一个能朝每一片边境天空低语、而地面上无人察觉的地方——那就会是在这样一张网格里，由一艘登记号从不出现在任何官方航运航道上的炮舰看守。把你派来这里的简报跳过了某些名字，滑过了"是谁最先标记这条轨道"，仿佛所有人都同意不把它们说出口。目前为止，你追着一串线索：一座孤独预制房传来的损坏日志、一名死掉猎人的弃船（半份赏金报告被烧掉），以及一连串远程前哨——那里的天气从未与记录相符，全都指回同一只谨慎搭在操纵装置上的手。

#en: The deserted biotics lab is where every coincidence finally lines up and stops looking like chance. Its isolated power grid, independent sensor net, and abandoned life-support systems give Deadbolt a space he can lock down without interference from Harmonization protocols or Navy patrols, turning a forgotten research shell into a perfect, sealed test chamber for his timing games. Here he can reroute air, doors, security drones, even experimental equipment with the same cold precision he once used on grav lanes, while finalizing whatever algorithm, anomaly map, or blackmail package he has been building from stolen logs and ruined ships. Too many ambushes triggered at the same offset, too many "missing" freighters sharing identical delay orders, too many pirate strikes aligning with falsified corridor tags found on a dataslate in the dust, in altered couriers, in Navy scout records, and in a silent marker drifting over a nameless world; stacked together, the pattern shouted a single name.
zh: 那座废弃的生物实验室，是每一个巧合终于排成一列、不再像偶然的地方。它孤立的电网、独立的传感器网络与被弃置的生命维持系统，给了"死栓"一个能不受"协调协议"或海军巡逻干扰、直接封锁的空间，把一座被遗忘的研究外壳变成他那些时机游戏的完美密封测试舱。在这里，他能以曾在引力航道上用过的那种冷静精确重接空气、门、安保无人机乃至实验设备，同时完成他从偷来的日志与报废船只里搭建的无论什么算法、异常图或勒索包。太多伏击在同一偏移量触发，太多"失踪"货船共享同样的延迟命令，太多海盗袭击与"尘土中数据板上、被改动的信使船里、海军侦察船记录中，以及一座漂在无名世界上方的沉默标记里"发现的被伪造走廊标签相吻合；堆在一起，这个模式喊出了一个名字。

#en: The Well is where routes are born and buried, where overworked clerks and forgotten terminals quietly decide which lives get a clean corridor and which ships vanish into a line item, so it is the only place she could twist the knife. Here, beneath the shining tiers of New Atlantis, Luna has spliced her private lattice into the transit grid, feeding on the same power and data that once made her indispensable to LIST. From this tangle of metal walkways and maintenance cubbies she is preparing to loose years of doctored charts and erased pings into every office that ever signed off on a convenient grav-drive failure, ready to redraw the politics of safe lanes in a single broadcast. Coincidences piled up to bring you to this junction: a gutted GalBank escort with route logs that did not match its manifest, an ambush in an asteroid field triggered the moment you touched a beacon carrying her signature checksum, patterns in traffic that stopped looking like noise and started to look like intent.
zh: 深井区，是航线诞生与埋葬之处；在那里，超负荷的文书与被遗忘的终端悄悄决定哪些人能得到干净的走廊、哪些船变成一行条目，所以这是她唯一能下刀的地方。在这里、在新亚特兰蒂斯城闪亮层级之下，露娜已把她的私人网格接进运输网，以那套曾让她对独立盟不可或缺的同样电力与数据为食。在这片由金属步道与维护隔间构成的乱麻里，她正准备把多年被做手脚的星图与被抹除的脉冲倾泻进每一个曾签批过"方便的引力引擎故障"的办公室，准备以一次广播重画安全航道的政治。巧合层层堆叠，把你带到这个枢纽：一具被掏空的盖尔银行护航船，航线日志与舱单不符；一场在你刚碰到一枚带着她签名校验和信标的瞬间触发的小行星带伏击；以及那些不再像噪声、而开始像意图的交通模式。

#en: If her work ever had a heartbeat, it was down here, where the queues knot around the LIST office and every name on a waiting slate is another pressure point she learned to twist. Buried in this tangle of ducts and drip stained bulkheads lie the silent tallies of who was moved forward, who was stalled, and who vanished into off grid promises; only here do the numbers line up with the faces that paid for them. The samples taken from these depths carry the faint, cumulative imprint of every quiet exception she pushed through, every application diverted to nowhere, the kind of subtle trace that can be followed back along the path she thought erased. So far the trail runs from a dead end contact in the back country to a sealed lab on a nameless world, to a nervous broker in Neon and a derelict survey ship with half a jump plan, and each step has confirmed the same pattern a hidden network of settlements threaded through the gaps in official records, all drawn to a point she once called Hearthline.
zh: 若说她的工作曾有过心跳，那就是在这下面——独立盟办公室周围人群打结、候补名册上每个名字都是她学会扭动的一个压力点。埋在这片导管与滴水舱壁的乱麻里的，是"谁被提前、谁被拖延、谁消失在账外承诺里"的无声清点；只有在这里，数字才与为之付钱的面孔对得上。从这些深处取出的样本，携带她推过的每一次安静例外的微弱累积印记，每一份被改道到虚空的申请——那种能沿着她以为已抹掉的路径回溯的微妙痕迹。目前为止，线索从乡间一名死掉联系人，到一颗无名世界上密封的实验室，再到霓虹城一名紧张的掮客与一艘只带着半份跃迁计划的弃置勘探船，每一步都证实同样的模式：一张藏在官方记录缝隙里的隐藏定居点网络，全都绘向一个她一度称作"炉线"的点。

#en: The old barracks sit half-swallowed by dust and silence, a place built to train soldiers how to kill and then abandoned when the war moved on without them; if any records survived the sanitizing, they would cling to a place like this, layered under drill routines and casualty tallies no one officially kept. Wayward Taskforce holding this ground tells you enough about what is hidden here, ex-operatives guarding a past they have all agreed never to have seen, stepping around scorch marks and nameplates as if they were just flaws in the concrete. Somewhere in these dead halls the trajectories that keep guiding ships into graveyards will be written down, if only in corrupted logs or forgotten briefing slates. So far the trail has been a lonely data scrap on a backwater world, a silent relay full of mismatched timestamps, and a gutted garrison with beacon code that did not match the wrecks outside, all pointing toward someone who knows exactly which details everyone else has chosen not to remember.
zh: 那座旧营房半被尘土与沉默吞没，一座为训练士兵如何杀戮而建、随后在战争把他们抛下继续前行时被弃置的设施；若有任何记录在清理中存活，它会黏在这样的地方，层层压在进行演练与没人正式保留的伤亡统计之下。任性特遣队据守这片地面，已足够说明这里藏着什么：一群前特工守着一段他们都同意"从未见过"的过去，绕着灼痕与铭牌走，仿佛它们只是混凝土上的瑕疵。在这些死掉的大厅里某处，那些不断把船只引向墓地的轨迹会被写下来——哪怕只在损坏的日志或被遗忘的简报数据板里。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡世界上一块孤独的数据碎片、一座塞满对不上时戳的沉默中继，以及一座信标代码与外面残骸不符的被掏空驻军，全都指向某个确切知道"其他所有人选择不记得哪些细节"的人。

#en: This forgotten freight yard is a dead space in every registry, a place where cargo goes to be lost and paperwork goes to die. That makes it perfect for work no one wants to admit exists; perfect for a final adjustment to a grav system no inspector will ever audit, and for a saboteur who needs shielding from eyes in New Atlantis and Akila alike. Here the containers are stacked like tombstones, humming with old power, ready to amplify whatever she has wired into the conduits. If Vector completes what she is calibrating in this rusted maze, the next "accident" will not be local to some unlucky hauler, it will echo along whole trade lanes before anyone can respond. The UC and Deimos hoped the incidents would blur into background noise, that the Cheyenne files and the first vented testbed would dissolve into rumor, but scattered engineers, a LIST foreman, and a few nervous GalBank clerks kept the pattern alive long enough for the trail of shards, ghost code, and vanished consultants to point straight here.
zh: 这座被遗忘的货运场在每个登记册里都是死空间，货物来此失踪、文书来此死去。这让它成了"没人愿意承认存在的工作"的完美地点：一次任何检查员都不会审计的引力系统最终调整，以及一名需要躲开新亚特兰蒂斯城与阿基拉城眼线的破坏者。在这里，那些货柜像墓碑一样堆着，带着旧电力嗡鸣，随时放大她接进导管的任何东西。若"向量"完成她在这座锈蚀迷宫里校准的东西，下一场"意外"就不会只局限于某艘倒霉货船，它会在任何人能响应之前沿整条整条贸易航道回响。联殖与火卫二本希望那些事件模糊成背景噪声，希望夏延星文件与第一座被排空的试验台溶解成传闻，可零散的工程师、一名独立盟工头，以及几名紧张的盖尔银行文书，让这个模式活到足够久——久到由碎片、幽灵代码与消失顾问构成的线索直指这里。

#en: Gagarin Landing has always been a waystation, never a destination, which is why people talk too freely here and think nothing lingers longer than the dust from old mech yards. That makes its loading rings and backline clinics the perfect catch-basin for stories no one bothered to write down, the place where her name is never spoken but her habits are. Dockhands remember a certain soft accent, customs techs recall tiny gaps in sensor sweeps, and someone always knows a ship that was logged two minutes before or after it really arrived. All those slips and shrugs left small bends in the paperwork, faint grooves in memory, guiding certain crates and certain people along the same quiet channels until they ended up far from where the manifests said they should be. So far the trail is this: a discarded slate on an empty rock, a clinic's scrubbed patient list, and now a port where gossip, altered timestamps, and half-forgotten favors all point toward the same invisible courier shaping routes from the shadows.
zh: 加加林着陆点一向是中转站、从不是目的地，所以这里的人说话太随意，以为没有任何东西比旧机甲场的尘土留得更久。这让它的装货环与后方诊所成了"没人费心写下来之故事"的完美接水盆：她名字从不被提起、她的习性却在此地的地方。码头工记得某种柔和的口音，海关技师回忆起传感器扫描里的微小空隙，而总有人知道某艘船的被记录时间是早于还是晚于它真正抵达两分钟。所有那些口误与耸肩，都在文书里留下小小的弯折、在记忆里留下浅浅的沟槽，把某些货箱与某些人沿同样的安静渠道引去，直到他们最终落在舱单所说位置很远的地方。目前为止，这条线索是这样的：一空岩石上一块被丢弃的数据板、一份诊所被擦净的病人名单，如今又是一座闲话、被改动的时戳与半被遗忘的人情全都指向同一名从阴影里塑造航线的隐形信使的港市。

#en: The UC warship WK-9192 drifts in the dark like a monument to routine gone wrong, its hull marked by skirmishes everyone thought were already accounted for in the logs. This is where patrol routes, emergency deployments, and interdiction patterns were written and rewritten until the crew stopped questioning the math and simply trusted the console glow. Somewhere in that quiet confidence, her hand slipped in, bending familiar scripts into unseen corridors while officers signed off without a second glance. To understand how she has been hiding fleets in plain sight, the ship that trusted her calculations is the only place the pattern can be read clean. So far the trail runs from a nervous smuggler contact who swore their runs arrived early without burning extra fuel, to route discrepancies buried in customs reports, all of it pointing to one truth: someone with system-level access has been nudging traffic just far enough off expected vectors that no one noticed until ships started vanishing between lanes.
zh: 那艘联殖军舰"WK-9192"像一座"例行公事出了岔"的纪念碑般漂在黑暗中，船壳上留着所有人都以为早已计入日志的冲突痕迹。这里正是巡逻航线、应急部署与阻截模式被写下又被改写到船员不再质疑那套数学、只信任控制台辉光的地方。在那份安静的笃定里某处，她的手溜了进来，把熟悉的脚本掰成看不见的走廊，而军官们不假思索地签了字。要弄懂她一直在如何把舰队藏在明面上，这艘信任她计算的船，是唯一能干净读出那个模式的地方。目前为止，线索从一名发誓自己的航次没多烧燃料却提前抵达的紧张走私者线人，延伸到海关报告里被埋的航线差异，全都指向一个真相：某个拥有系统级权限的人一直在把交通推得刚够偏离预期向量，以至于没人注意到——直到船只开始在航道之间消失。

#en: The dead arrays of the deserted UC listening post still sweep the stars in slow, meaningless arcs, a relic that once heard every whisper along this stretch of space and then, somehow, missed the one that mattered most. Here, buried in half-scrubbed logs and obsolete grav telemetry, Starline could work unobserved, splicing his ghost corridors straight through the gaps in official attention. UC abandoned the place; he turned its quiet into a launchpad, feeding routes to captains while he watched which ships came back and which fell silent. You arrive as the last cycle completes, just as he moves to erase the final proof that his patterns ever ran through UC ears at all.  \n\nWe started with a stray dataslate in the back end of nowhere, then a buried analyst pod that hinted at doctored navigation reports, and finally a rigged beacon in high orbit broadcasting impossible jump solutions. Every step pointed to the same hand, the same spiral in the numbers, hiding in the blind spots everyone else chose not to see.
zh: 那座废弃联殖听音哨死掉的阵列仍以缓慢而无意义的弧线扫过群星，一件遗物——它曾听见这片太空沿线的每一句低语，然后不知怎地错过了最重要的那一句。在这里、埋在半擦除的日志与过时的引力遥测中，"星线"能不受观察地工作，把他的幽灵走廊直接接进官方注意力的空隙。联殖放弃了这地方；他把它的安静变成发射台，向船长们喂航线，同时观察哪些船回来、哪些陷入沉默。你在最后一个周期完成时抵达，正好在他动手抹掉"他的模式曾穿过联殖耳朵"的最后证据之时。  \n\n我们从天涯之外一块散落数据板开始，然后是一座暗示导航报告被动过手脚的被埋分析舱，最后是轨道上一座广播着不可能跃迁解的被动过手脚信标。每一步都指向同一只手、数字里同一个螺旋，藏在别人选择不去看的盲点里。

#en:
This empty relay sits on the rim of real traffic, where civilian ships fall off the charts and only maintenance drones were ever meant to listen.  
Its dishes still drink in background noise from the lanes, and that noise is the one thing Vector cannot fully scrub; every falsified route, every doctored misjump leaves a faint echo in its buffers.  
He has come here to collapse the pattern, purge the last record tying his algorithms to the wrecks scattered through Kessler's Veil and the test yards near Protectorate Systems.  
If he succeeds, the accidents become ghost stories, forever blamed on bad luck and faulty hardware no one can disprove.  
The trail to this place was stitched from half-heard bar talk in the hinterlands, a corrupted slate found where the first hint surfaced, garbled transponder logs pulled off a drifting hull, then contraband manifests pried from a frightened broker on that moonside module; no one ever had the full story, just fragments traded between people who learned to talk quietly.
zh:
这座空中继坐落在真实交通的边缘，民用船只在此脱离星图，只有维护无人机本该在此聆听。  
它的天线盘仍在啜饮航道传来的背景噪声，而那种噪声是"向量"唯一无法完全擦除的东西；每一条被伪造的航线、每一次被做手脚的错跳，都会在它的缓冲区里留下一道淡淡回声。  
他来这里是为了坍缩这个模式，清除"他的算法与散落在凯斯勒之幕及保护国系统附近试验场里的残骸有关"的最后记录。  
若他成功，那些事故就会变成鬼故事，永远被归咎于坏运气与无人能推翻的故障硬件。  
通往此地的线索，是由边境半听来的酒吧闲谈、一块在第一处线索浮现之地找到的损坏数据板、从一具漂移船壳上拉出的乱码应答器日志，以及从那座卫星侧舱室一名受惊掮客那里撬出的违禁舱单缝成的；没人拥有完整故事，只有在学会低声说话的人之间交易的碎片。

#en: Down here, beneath the neon sheen and corporate gloss, the conduits run like exposed nerves, every junction tagged, rerouted, and quietly stolen from. This is where maintenance logs are falsified, power siphons are normalized, and a single mislabeled junction can divert half a city's traffic without anyone topside noticing. That same complacency makes this spine the only place a former inspector could sketch safe corridors through the chaos, turning forgotten service tunnels and unregistered airlocks into a private transit map no security sweep will ever catch. A minor oversight in access control became a habit, then a custom, and now an invisible highway that only one saboteur truly understands. The trail so far began with a stray slate at a dead outpost and a cargo yard humming with unexplained drive faults; together they painted the outline of someone who knows every shortcut, prefers to work in the blind spots, and has been using abandoned infrastructure as waypoints between ruined ships and redacted reports.
zh: 在这下面、在霓虹光泽与公司亮面之下，那些导管像裸露的神经一样延伸，每个接点都被标记、被改道、被悄悄偷接。这里正是维护日志被伪造、电力虹吸被正常化，以及一个标签错误的接点就能改道半座城市交通而楼上无人察觉的地方。同样的自满让这道脊骨成了唯一能让一名前检查员在混乱中勾出安全走廊的地方，把被遗忘的服务隧道与未登记气闸变成一张任何安保扫描都抓不到的私人运输图。门禁控制里的一处小小疏忽变成了习惯，然后是惯例，如今成了一条只有一名破坏者真正理解的隐形高速公路。到目前为止，这条线索始于一死掉前哨上一块散落数据板与一片嗡鸣着无法解释的引擎故障的货运场区；合在一起，它们画出了某个"熟悉每一条近路、偏爱在盲点里工作、并一直把废弃基础设施当作废墟船只与涂黑报告之间航点"之人的轮廓。

#en: Only up on the rooftops can you hear Neon without the walls lying for it. The hum of grav pads and private shuttles passing just low enough to skim the Span is where contracts change hands, off the record, passed between executives who do not want their own systems seeing the numbers. Whatever was logged about Vector and his routes was never meant to sit in a clean office downstairs; it lives up here, tucked into side-channel traffic and rooftop relays that only the desperate and the crooked bother to touch. Word is, a smuggler bragged in a corner booth that their miracle escape corridor came from someone who talks in coordinates instead of names, and a nervous clerk mentioned forged permits that always pointed one jump beyond the usual lanes. Out in the hinterlands, a LIST camp swore a clipped voice walked them past a storm, and a drifting cutter near UC space carried logs stamped with a familiar sigil. Taken alone, each story is just bar talk. Lined up against the skyline, they all start whispering the same direction.
zh: 只有在屋顶上，你才能听见没有墙壁替它说谎的霓虹城。引力停机坪与私人穿梭机的嗡鸣低得刚好掠过桥架，那里正是合同在账外转手的地方，在那些不愿让自己的系统看见数字的高管之间传递。凡是关于"向量"及其航线的记录，从来就注定不会待在楼下一间干净的办公室里；它活在这里，藏在侧信道交通与屋顶中继里——只有走投无路者和歪门邪道者才会费心去碰。据说，一名走私者在角落卡座里吹嘘他们那条奇迹逃生走廊来自某个"用坐标而非名字说话"的人；一名紧张的文书提到总是指向"常规航道之外一次跃迁"的伪造许可。在边境，一支独立盟营地发誓有个简短的声音带他们走过了风暴；而在联殖太空附近一艘漂着的切割船，带着盖着熟悉印记的日志。单看，每个故事都只是酒吧闲谈。与天际线排在一起，它们都开始低语同一方向。

#en: The abandoned garrison sits at the edge of nowhere, its sirens long silenced, its walls thick with old militia dust and newer scorch marks that do not match any logged engagement. Whatever was dragged into its bunkers was meant to be buried under Freestar jurisdiction and forgotten, far from UC eyes and the ships Rivet likes to cut open. The Stray Rust Syndicate were hired to stand watch on something they only half understood, then bled away as the pay dried up and the rumors sharpened, leaving hardened sentries guarding a secret none of them could name. If this place is left intact, the pattern Rivet has been tracing between wrecks, stolen drives, and vanished convoys will find another outpost to infect. So far, the trail runs like this: a stray slate in deep space whispering about a shipbreaker with too many aliases, soil-stained scrap on a quiet farm stamped with Deimos marks, and now a deserted Freestar site where Syndicate guns loiter over tech that hums in the same wrong frequency as the anomaly pinned in UC archives.
zh: 那座废弃驻军坐落在天涯之外，警报早已沉默，墙壁厚积着旧民兵的尘土与更新、且与任何记录过的交火都不符的灼痕。凡是被拖进它掩体的东西，本都打算埋在自由星系联盟管辖下被遗忘，远离联殖的眼睛与"铆钉"喜欢切开的船。"游荡锈迹辛迪加"受雇看守一件他们只懂一半的东西，随后在薪酬枯竭、传闻变尖锐时渐次流失，只留下硬派哨兵守着一个没人说得出名字的秘密。若这地方被任其完好，"铆钉"一直在残骸、被偷引擎与失踪车队之间追查的模式就会找到下一个前哨去感染。目前为止，线索是这样：深空中一块散落数据板低语着一个绰号太多的拆船工、一座安静农场上带着火卫二标记的沾土废料，如今又是一处废弃自由星系联盟场址——辛迪加的枪口在那些以同样错误频率嗡鸣的技术上方闲晃，与联殖档案里钉住的异常一样。

#en: The Helium-3 plant is the last place she can work unseen, its automated rigs and sealed conduits perfect camouflage for someone who lives between manifest lines and maintenance schedules. Every pipe is a route, every pressure chamber another room where a mind can be tuned and a witness made to forget why they came here. Quietline needs these reactors to power and mask the neuroamps she has folded into the plant's control lattice, one final attempt to cut herself free of every record and every debt before UC, Freestar, or worse can close in. If she finishes rewriting the staff and the logs, she walks away as a ghost and the station becomes another blind spot in the Settled Systems, its crew loyal to a woman they cannot name. All we know for certain is this: a stray dataslate in the dark, half-scrubbed signatures around a backline clinic, and the altered testimony of a raider and a farmstead led from a quiet rock, through Gagarin's alleys and a hard-bitten refuge, to a courier whose trail never quite lines up with the reports.
zh: 氦-3 工厂是她唯一能不被看见地工作的地方，它的自动化设备与密封导管对某个活在舱单行间与维护日程之间的人来说是完美的伪装。每根管道都是一条航线，每个压力舱都是又一个房间，心智可以在那里被调校，证人可以在那里被弄得忘记自己为何而来。"静默线"需要这些反应堆来驱动并掩盖她折进工厂控制网格的神经增幅器，这是她在联殖、自由星系联盟或更糟的东西合围之前，切断自己与每一份记录、每一笔债务联系的最后一搏。若她完成对员工与日志的改写，她就会像幽灵一样走开，而这座星际站成为定居星系里又一个盲点，它的船员效忠于一个说不出名字的女人。我们唯一确定的是这些：漆黑中一块散落数据板、后方诊所周围半擦除的签名，以及一名掠夺者与一座农庄被改动的证词——它们从一块安静岩石，穿过加加林星的小巷与一处饱经风霜的避难所，引到一艘痕迹总与报告对不太上的信使船。

#en: Down here, where the grid hums overhead and leaking pipes keep their own slow time, this is the only place her routes would be written down honestly. Customs offices and starport kiosks deal in official lanes; the real paths run underfoot, traded between haulers, chem runners, and anyone desperate enough to risk a shortcut that does not exist on any map. Somewhere among these rusted bulkheads is the pattern of ships she has bent to her purposes, the off-hour departures and unscheduled dockings that only a courier from this city would trust. Every dockhand has a different version of how she moves and who she serves, the tale shifting a little with each retelling, like fear and superstition sand down the details no one wants to own. So far the trail runs like this: a discarded slate on a dead rock, scrambled logs in a back-room clinic near Gagarin, a rattled runner who remembers a soft accent and the wrong sigil on the right crate, all pointing toward the same invisible corridors she has been carving through the Settled Systems.
zh: 在这下面、在网格头顶嗡鸣、渗漏管道以自己缓慢节奏计时之处，这是唯一会如实写下她航线的地方。海关办公室与太空港小摊做的是官方航道；真正的路径在脚下流动，在货船船员、药剂跑腿，以及任何绝望到愿意冒一条任何星图上都不存在的近路风险的人之间交易。在这些锈蚀舱壁之间某处，是她掰向自己目的的船只的模式，是只有来自这座城市的信使才会信任的错峰离港与未排期停靠。每个码头工对"她如何行动、效忠于谁"都有不同版本，故事随着每次重述稍作偏移，仿佛恐惧与迷信把没人愿意认领的细节一点点磨掉。目前为止，线索是这样的：死岩石上一块被丢弃的数据板、加加林星附近某间后室诊所里被搅乱的日志、一名记得柔和口音与"正确货箱上错误印记"的心有余悸的跑腿，全都指向她一直在定居星系里凿出的同一些看不见的走廊。

#en: Out on the edge of the lane, the wreckage hangs in a slow tumble, its hull etched with scorch marks that do not quite match any honest misjump or weapons test. This is where stories diverge: freighter crews mutter about a ship that appeared sideways to its own trajectory, then sheared away like glass under a bad grav surge, while more sober traffic controllers dismiss it as panicked testimony and faulty sensors. The metal does not lie, though; the scoring and twisted struts sketch the kind of impossible turn only a pilot obsessed with shaving reality thin would attempt, and whoever was flying left just enough of their signature burned into the plating to trace the direction they were trying to escape in. So far, everything I have seen fits the same crooked outline: a forgotten rock with a half-wiped slate, beacons reporting ships where no flight plan put them, Neon's lower levels hiding power cuts nobody wants to log, and now this broken shell, floating exactly where all those rumors about ghost jumps insist something went wrong.
zh: 在航道边缘，那具残骸以缓慢翻滚悬着，船壳上刻着与任何诚实的错跳或武器测试都不太吻合的灼痕。这里正是故事分岔之处：货船船员嘟囔着一艘"相对自身轨迹侧着出现、随后在糟糕引力浪涌下像玻璃一样崩开"的船，而更冷静的交管员则把它当作惊慌的证词与故障传感器打发。可金属不会说谎；那些刮痕与扭曲的支柱，勾画出一种只有痴迷于把现实削薄的飞行员才会尝试的不可能转向，而驾驶者留在钢板上、足以追溯他们试图逃离方向的签名。目前为止，我见过的一切都契合同一道歪斜轮廓：一块带着半擦除数据板的被遗忘岩石、报告着"飞行计划中并不存在的船只"的信标、霓虹城下层隐藏着没人愿意记录的断电，以及如今这具破碎外壳——它就漂在所有那些关于幽灵跃迁的传闻坚称"出了问题时"的确切位置。

#en: Gagarin Landing looks the same on approach, all rusted gantries and tired floodlights, but the real work here has always been hidden in rote paperwork and unremarkable cargo runs. This is where freighters drift in from every direction, where manifests get adjusted, fees waived, and traffic patterns nudged a few degrees at a time without anyone raising their voice. If someone wanted to bend the lanes around a single pilot, to make their comings and goings disappear into a new normal, it would start in the ledgers and schedules no one reads twice. Only by pulling those quiet changes apart here can you see which ships began arriving early, which routes inexplicably rerouted around the same patch of sky, and how a forgotten station suddenly became a waypoint in everything from grain hauls to scrap deliveries. So far the trail runs from a ghost signal at an old listening post to buried scans in a relay bunker, each step showing the same unmarked ship cutting through restricted air while the official charts insist nothing unusual ever happened.
zh: 加加林着陆点从进近方向看依旧是老样子，满是锈蚀龙门架与疲惫泛光灯，可这里真正的活计一向藏在刻板的文书与不起眼的货运里。这是货船从各个方向漂来的地方，是舱单被调整、费用被免除、交通模式被一次几度地推动而没人抬高嗓门的地方。若有人想围绕一名飞行员掰弯航道、让他们的来去消失进一种新的常态，它就会始于那些没人读两遍的账册与日程。只有在这里把这些安静的改动拆开，你才能看出哪些船开始提前抵达、哪些航线莫名其妙地绕开同一片天空，以及一座被遗忘的星际站如何突然变成从谷物运输到废料交付的一切航次中的中转点。目前为止，线索从旧听音哨的一道幽灵信号，延伸到中继掩体里被埋的扫描，每一步都显示同一艘未标记的船切过受限天空，而官方星图坚称从未发生任何异常。

#en: It had to end at the edge of a city that lives on exhausted rock and old war ghosts, where ship lanes pinch low over the dust and every vector in and out passes through the same narrow sky. Out here, there is no crowd to vanish into, no storm corridor to ride; the only cover is the heat shimmer off Cydonia's scarred outskirts and the static whisper of overworked traffic beacons that Vector has tuned one too many times. He chose this place because its patterns are familiar, because a dozen minor route edits and quiet favors have slowly braided into a single escape line he thinks only he can see. Breaking that line here stops his last attempt to fold the map around himself before corporate cleaners or desperate smugglers turn his tricks into something far worse. So far the trail has run from a forgotten dataslate on a backworld, through a drifting Trade Authority courier and a silent orbital clue, each step tightening the graph of falsified routes, buried logs, and one navigator whose small compromises finally drew a hunter into his shadow.
zh: 它必须终结在一座靠枯竭岩石与旧战争幽灵为生的城市的边缘——在那里，航道在尘土上方低低收窄，每一个进出向量都穿过同一片狭窄天空。在这里，没有人群可以混入，没有风暴走廊可以骑行；唯一的掩护是赛多尼亚伤痕累累郊外腾起的热浪，以及"向量"调过太多次的过载交通信标的静电低语。他选中这地方，是因为它的模式熟悉，是因为十几处小小的航线编辑与安静人情已慢慢编成一条他以为只有自己能看见的逃生线。在这里打断那条线，就能阻止他在公司清理人或绝望走私者把他的把戏变成远更糟的东西之前，把地图折向自己的最后尝试。目前为止，线索从一穷乡星上一块被遗忘的数据板，穿过一艘漂移的贸易管理局信使船与一处沉默的轨道线索，每一步都收紧着那张由伪造航线、被埋日志，以及一名"其小小妥协最终把猎人引向自己阴影"的领航员构成的图。

#en: This forgotten cryo lab hangs between star systems like a discarded hypothesis, its power failing in fits and starts, emergency lights stuttering over frost-fogged corridors and half-dead monitors. It matters because Torque chose it, not for cover, but for control: a place where he can scrub signatures, reroute life support, and bury what he has become in rusted hardware no corporation will ever bother to audit. Here he has been unspooling Iyla Korr's trail and everyone else's, cross-checking crash logs from freighters and luxury liners alike, deciding which truths to exhume and which to freeze forever, and now he is close to erasing the last proof that any of this was engineered. If he finishes, the pattern of bad drives, missing recall orders, and dead witnesses will become just another rumor, like the oldest version of this story, already smudged by bar talk about a dataslate in the dust, a lonely hut full of glitching telemetry, a silent ship on the edge of nowhere, and a UC warship whose black-box reports were never meant to see daylight.
zh: 这座被遗忘的冷冻实验室像一份被丢弃的假设悬在星系之间，电力断断续续地衰竭，应急灯在多霜迷雾的走廊与半死的显示器上闪烁。它要紧，是因为"扭矩"选中了它——不是为了掩护，而是为了控制：一个他能擦净签名、重接生命维持，并把自己变成的样子埋进公司永远不会费心审计的锈蚀硬件里的地方。在这里，他一直在展开艾拉·科尔的痕迹与所有其他人的痕迹，交叉核对货船与豪华邮轮的坠毁日志，决定哪些真相该被挖出、哪些该被永久冻结；如今他离抹掉"这一切都是人为设计"的最后证据只差一步。若他完工，坏引擎、失踪召回令与死掉证人的模式就会变成又一则传闻——就像这个故事最古老的版本一样，早已被酒吧闲谈抹淡：尘土里一块数据板、一座满是故障遥测的孤独小屋、一艘天涯边缘的沉默船只，以及一艘"黑匣报告本不该见天日"的联殖军舰。

#en: No one logs a relay out here by mistake; an asteroid field this thin, this far from any declared corridor, exists to lose signals, not anchor them, which is exactly why someone like Luna would lace her work through its static. The rocks and dust give cover to whatever she tested first, the bad corridors and half-finished vanish routes that never made it onto official charts, and to anyone now hired to erase those traces before a hunter can read them. Out in this drift, there is no jurisdiction, no flight control, only the raw noise of grav drives and broken stone, and somewhere inside that noise is the pattern she has been refining since her first ship went missing. Stories about a ghost in the traffic have passed from LIST clerks to GalBank pilots and bar-front fixers, picking up new details every retelling, but the only solid things so far were a protection escort whose route logs did not match its manifest and whispers that certain beacons in dead space repeat the same warped checksum, like an echo waiting for someone stubborn enough to chase it.
zh: 没人在这种地方误建中继；一片这么稀薄、离任何申报走廊这么远的小行星带，生来就是为了让信号失灵、而非锚定它们——这正是像露娜那样的人会把作品编织进它静电里的原因。岩石与尘土为"她最先测试的东西"提供掩护：那些从未进入官方星图的坏走廊与半途而废的消失航线，以及任何如今受雇、要在猎人读懂它们之前擦掉那些痕迹的人。在这片漂流带里，没有管辖，没有飞行控制，只有引力引擎与碎石的原始噪声；而那片噪声里的某处，是她自第一艘船失踪以来一直在精炼的模式。关于交通中一个幽灵的故事，已从独立盟文书传到盖尔银行飞行员与酒吧门前的掮客，每次重述都添了新细节；可目前为止唯一确凿的东西，是一艘航线日志与舱单不符的护航船，以及"死寂太空中某些信标重复着同一段扭曲校验和"的低语——像一道等着某个足够固执的人去追的回声。

#en: The empty barracks still hum with recycled air and old orders, a forgotten outpost built to outlast the Colony War and then quietly abandoned when the treaties came. Rivet chose this place because no one counts the dead here anymore, and because the walls are already wired for controlled demolitions and silent drills; it is the perfect frame to cut apart and vanish inside. His grav logs, stolen drives, and the star map that ties every gutted wreck together will be staged to jump from here, slipping past Freestar patrol routes and UC scrutiny alike. If he succeeds, the pattern he has been tracing in secret will move beyond anyone's reach, along with the last unedited record of what really happened in those forgotten battles. From the frozen carcass in deep space where a stranded cutter dropped Rivet's name, to the quiet farm where Waggoner soil hid Deimos-marked scrap, to the garrison stripped along precise load-bearing seams, every step has pointed to one hand testing structures, erasing witnesses, and following that same impossible signal through the wreckage.
zh: 那座空营房仍带着循环空气与旧命令的嗡鸣，一座为熬过殖民地大战而建、随后在条约到来时被悄悄弃置的被遗忘前哨。"铆钉"选中这里，是因为这里再没人清点死者，也因为墙壁本就为受控爆破与静默演练布好了线；它是拆解与消失的完美框架。他的引力日志、偷来的引擎，以及那张把每一具被掏空残骸连起来的星图，都将从这里跃迁出去，滑过自由星系联盟巡逻航线与联殖审查。若他成功，他一直在暗中追查的模式就会移出任何人的触及范围，连同那些被遗忘的战斗中真正发生了什么的最后未删改记录。从深空中一名搁浅切割船船员念出"铆钉"名字的冷冻残骸，到瓦戈纳的土壤藏着火卫二标记废料的安静农场，再到沿精确承重接缝被剥光的驻军，每一步都指向同一只手：测试结构、抹掉证人，并循着同一道不可能的信号穿过残骸。

#en: Places like The Clinic are supposed to scrub the blood off history, pin it behind glass with a comforting plaque, and call that healing. That is why the trail bends here: if anyone tried to turn a battlefield horror into a neat case study, it would be the station that survived a war by changing hands instead of course. Somewhere in its curated corridors there will be a sanitized version of what happened at that garrison, and tucked behind that, the parts the UC was glad to misplace and Freestar has no incentive to dig up. Staff whisper different stories when they think no one is listening; some fear what an unedited record might stir up, others like the safety that comes from not asking questions.  \nUp to now, the path has been fragments and contradictions: a stray slate on a forgotten rock, a derelict patrol ship still following half-erased orders, conflicting mentions of the same medic in logs that should never overlap. Everything points back to one incident no one wants to own, and a man who walked out of it still answering to commands nobody remembers signing.
zh: 像"星际诊所号"这样的地方，本应把血从历史里擦净，用一块让人安心的铭牌把它钉在玻璃后面，然后称之为疗愈。这就是线索拐向这里的原因：若有人曾试图把一场战地恐怖变成一个整齐的案例研究，那一定会是那座靠"易主而非改航"在战争中幸存下来的星际站。在它策展过的走廊里某处，会有关于那座驻军所发生之事的净化版本；而在那之后，则藏着联殖乐于弄丢、自由星系联盟没有动力去挖出的部分。员工们在以为没人听时会讲不同的故事；有些人害怕一份未删改记录会搅起什么，另一些人则喜欢"不问问题"带来的安全。  \n到目前为止，这条路是碎片与矛盾：被遗忘岩石上一块散落数据板、一具仍服从半擦除命令的弃置巡逻舰，以及在那些本绝不该重叠的日志里对同一名医疗兵的矛盾提及。一切都被指回一起没人愿意认领的事件，以及一个从中走出、仍在回应没人记得签署过的命令的人。

#en: The Deserted Relay Station hangs at the edge of the system like a dead nerve in the grav lattice, perfectly placed where old UC traffic once converged and where Vector can now listen to every tremor in the lanes. Its dishes have been twisted into a spider's web of jury-rigged antennas, feeding his stolen diagnostics and anomaly models into a humming core that treats the whole sector as a laboratory. Here, at the intersection of abandoned infrastructure and unstable readings, he can attempt the final proof he has been chasing since the testbed freighter died, a localized grav twitch big enough to force the truth into the open or tear this orbit apart. A misrouted UC maintenance order, an unsigned transfer request in New Atlantis, and a delayed pirate intercept have all nudged this confrontation here, now. Earlier, the quiet failures at the research site, the corrupted logs in high orbit, and the redacted disputes buried in Calyx files all traced the same pattern of staged "accidents" and missing data, pointing to the same exhausted analyst running out of places to hide.
zh: 那座"被遗弃的中继站"像引力网格里一根死掉的神经悬在星系边缘，恰好位于旧联殖交通曾汇聚之处，也是"向量"如今能听见航道每一次颤抖之处。它的天线盘被扭成一张由临时拼凑天线构成的蛛网，把他的偷来诊断与异常模型喂进一个把整个星区当作实验室的嗡鸣核心。在这里、在废弃基础设施与不稳定读数的交汇处，他能尝试自那艘试验台货船死亡以来他一直追逐的最终证明：一次足以迫使真相暴露、或把这条轨道撕开局部的引力抽搐。一份被错投的联殖维护令、新亚特兰蒂斯城里一份未签名的转运请求，以及一次被延误的海盗拦截，都把这面对撞推到了此地、此刻。早先，研究场址的安静故障、高轨道里损坏的日志，以及埋在花萼文件里的涂黑争执，全都追溯出同样的"人造事故与失踪数据"模式，指向同一名"快没地方可藏"的疲惫分析员。

#en: The farm is the first wound on the map, a place the banks wrote off and the locals forgot, which makes it perfect for hiding the kind of record no one wants audited. Its fields lie fallow under a thin sky, but the power feed to the main house still hums, and there are fresh boot tracks in the dust that do not belong to settlers. Uniform Blackguard watch the place with the stiff patience of contractors told to guard something they are not allowed to open, their black-and-white marks stark against sun-bleached siding; whatever is on that farm terminal, it scared someone enough to pay for silence. In town, stories about the foreclosure and the family who vanished never quite match, and every time the argument starts over who was at fault, it ends in a shrug and a change of subject, like everybody agreed not to dig any deeper. So far the trail is thin but steady: a dead spacer clutching stolen audit clips, a homestead that settled its debts after it was already empty, and scattered whispers that the same unseen hand keeps touching accounts from Akila to forgotten LIST rocks.
zh: 那座农场是地图上的第一道伤口，一个银行核销、当地人遗忘的地方，这让它成了藏起一份"没人想被审计之记录"的完美地点。它的田地在稀薄天空下休耕，可主屋的电力馈线仍在嗡鸣，尘土里有不属于定居者的新鲜靴印。"黑卫制服"以那种"被告知看守某样不许打开之物"的承包商的僵硬耐心看着这地方，他们黑白分明的标记在被晒白的墙板上格外醒目；无论那座农场终端上有什么，它都吓到了某人，吓到有人出钱买沉默。在镇上，关于那笔止赎与那户消失人家的说法从来对不上，而每次争起"谁该负责"，都以耸肩与换话题告终，仿佛所有人都同意不再深挖。目前为止，这条线索稀薄却稳定：一名死掉太空劫匪紧抓着偷来的审计片段、一座在早已空掉之后才清偿债务的农庄，以及零散低语说同一只无形之手不断从阿基拉城伸向被遗忘的独立盟岩石、触碰账户。

#en: No court, no committee, would ever authorize a strike here, which is why he chose it; this forgotten Deimos scrapyard is where the company buried its mistakes under rust, slag, and sealed manifests, then agreed to never speak of them again. The ground is a lattice of failed grav mounts and warped frames, each plate stamped with dates and serials no one in New Atlantis admits exist, and Rivet has threaded himself through that history like a live wire. He has been stripping these carcasses for parts, building one last test frame and rigging the yard with "lessons" to collapse around anyone who gets close, all while consolidating the telemetry and design logs that prove who really cut corners. If he completes his work here, the evidence disappears in a plume of twisted metal and decompressed air, and the pattern of quiet disasters he followed from a Ranger's field notes to this very graveyard becomes just another rumor spacers pretend not to remember: anonymous schematics on a dataslate in the dust, erased audits on Deimos, and a trail of ships saved or shattered by the same invisible hand.
zh: 没有法庭、没有委员会会批准在这里发动打击，这正是他选中它的原因；这座被遗忘的火卫二废料场，是公司把错误埋进锈、渣与密封舱单之下、然后同意永不再提的地方。地面是一张由失效引力支架与扭曲框架构成的网格，每块板材都盖着新亚特兰蒂斯城里没人承认存在的日期与序列号，而"铆钉"像一根带电的线一样穿过了那段历史。他一直在从这些残骸上拆零件，搭建最后一具试验框架，并在场区里布置"教训"，好让任何靠近的人被压垮，同时整合那些证明"究竟是谁偷了工"的遥测与设计日志。若他在这里完工，证据会在一股扭曲金属与泄压空气的烟柱中消失，而他从未自一名游骑兵的战地笔记追到这片墓地的"安静灾难"模式，就会变成太空劫匪假装不记得的又一则传闻：尘土中数据板上的匿名图纸、火卫二上被抹除的审计，以及一条由同一只无形之手拯救或击碎的船只的线索。

#en: The PX-3446 hangs dead in the dark, a UC SysDef hull that should have been quietly towed and buried but instead left drifting just outside the busy lanes, where only someone following the wrong kind of math would think to look. Inside, the blast-sheared corridors and frozen fire doors say "training accident" to any official report, yet every sealed compartment hums with the sense of work interrupted just before it named a culprit. This is where field data and private suspicions were burned into the ship's memory banks, far from the committee rooms where admirals now swear they saw only random failures. The wreck is less a tomb than a locked filing cabinet, holding the one record of how Diego's patterns bled into military jumps, and why those who noticed chose to keep that knowledge in vacuum, not daylight. Up to now the trail has been whispers and half-truths: a dying captain's complaints on a forgotten rock, nervous route-sellers speaking off the record in a station bar, and scattered flight plans marked "mishap" that all shared the same quiet signature curling back to the same hand on the console.
zh: PX-3446死寂地悬在黑暗中，一具本该被悄悄拖走埋葬、却被留在繁忙航道外侧漂着联殖星防队船壳——只有追寻"错误类型数学"的人才会想到去看那里。在它内部，被爆炸剪开的走廊与冻结的防火门对任何官方报告来说都是"训练事故"，可每一个密封舱室都嗡鸣着"工作在被指认罪魁之前恰好中断"的感觉。这里正是实地数据与私人怀疑被烧进舰船记忆库的地方，远离那些海军上将如今发誓"只看到随机故障"的委员会会议室。这具残骸与其说是坟墓，不如说是一个锁着的档案柜，藏着"迭戈的模式如何渗进军事跃迁"的唯一记录，以及那些注意到的人为何选择把这份知识留在真空、而非日光下。到目前为止，这条线索是低语与半真半假：一块被遗忘岩石上一名垂死船长的抱怨、某家星际站酒吧里小声说话的紧张航路贩子，以及零散标着"事故"的飞行计划——它们都共享同一道安静签名，蜷曲回同一只搭在控制台上的手。

#en: Out here, the rock itself hums with the residue of what he has been doing. The mining complex was never built to host Grav Drive arrays, yet the shafts run straight into dense veins that bend readings, masking field tests from distant UC sensors and Freestar patrols alike. In these tunnels he can hide unstable prototypes between loaders and ore hoppers, burn stolen fuel, and dump irradiated slag into the walls while the workers call it a bad day in the drills. This is where his pattern converges where every anomalous route, every missing crate, every grav spike along the hauler lanes finally points. By the time the alarms trip, he will be one trigger pull from erasing the last proof of his part in the tender misjump and stepping fully into the shadows he helped Rhys open. The earliest version of how this began has already been traded away in bar stories and half wiped logs, but the trail is clear enough now remote datapads with scrambled signatures, a silent recorder drifting in orbit, hushed talk in a farming settlement, and a bruised asteroid field full of broken echoes all narrowing toward this buried heart.
zh: 在这里，岩石本身都因他一直在做的事而嗡鸣。那座采矿综合体从不是为承载引力引擎阵列而建，可那些竖井直通能扭曲读数的致密矿脉，把实地测试同时向远方联殖传感器与自由星系联盟巡逻掩藏。在这些隧道里，他能在装载机与矿石漏斗之间藏起不稳定的原型、烧掉偷来的燃料，并把受辐照的矿渣倒进岩壁，而工人们只当那是钻探倒霉的一天。这里正是他的模式汇聚之处——货船航线上每一道异常航线、每一个失踪货箱、每一个引力尖峰，最终都指向这里。等到警报触发时，他离"抹掉自己在温柔错跳中所扮演角色的最后证据、并彻底走进他帮里斯打开的那些阴影"只差一次扳机。这一切如何开始的最早版本早已在酒吧故事与半擦除日志里被交易掉了，但如今这条线索足够清晰：远程数据板上被搅乱的签名、轨道上一台漂着的沉默记录仪、一座农业定居点里的低声谈话，以及一片满是破碎回声的瘀伤小行星带，全都收窄向这颗被埋藏的心脏。

#en: The skymaps all say this mining pit should be quiet rock and thin air, yet the clouds above it twist like something half-tamed and half-feral, caught between vacuum and storm. Stormglass chose this scar in the crust for a reason: the drills already pierce deep seams, the Helium-3 lines and old grav infrastructure hum beneath the surface, and the thin atmosphere responds faster than any regulated world. Here she can fold every lesson and every mistake into one last experiment, trying to rewrite the hyperstorm that ruined her life by bleeding reactor exhaust and microclimate tweaks into the open sky. A single miscalculated correction from her early models turned one settlement into a grave; left alone, what she is forcing through the rock and air here could echo across systems.  \nWe traced her from a stray dataslate in the back end of nowhere to Ranger logs and worried technicians at a supply post, then through a strained Helium-3 facility running odd atmospheric diagnostics and a raider command site choked in storm-scoured rubble; every step pointed to the same pattern of tampered skies and abandoned safeguards.
zh: 所有的星图都说这个矿坑该是安静的岩石与稀薄空气，可它上方的云却像某种半驯服、半野性的东西般扭曲，卡在真空与风暴之间。"风暴玻璃"选中地壳上这道伤疤是有原因的：钻头本就穿透深层矿脉，氦-3 管线与旧引力基础设施在地表之下嗡鸣，而稀薄大气比任何受监管世界响应得更快。在这里，她能把每一课与每一个错误折进最后一次实验，试图通过把反应堆废气与微气候微调渗进露天天空，来改写那场毁掉她人生的超级风暴。她早期模型里一次算错的修正就把一座定居点变成了坟墓；任其自行，她此刻正从岩层与空气里强推出去的东西，可能在多个星系间回响。  \n我们从天涯之外一块散落数据板追到她，到游骑兵日志与某座补给站忧心的技师，然后穿过一座做着古怪大气诊断的紧张氦-3 设施与一处被风暴刮蚀的碎石塞满的掠夺者指挥场址；每一步都指向同样的模式：被动手脚的天空与被弃置的保障措施。

#en: The Well is where forgotten things are supposed to sink and stay down, drowned beneath tourist gloss and MAST rhetoric. Down here, records get lost, debts get rolled into shadows, and faces blur into the press of the crowd. For a man who lives by erasing people on paper, this undercity is the perfect last staging ground, close enough to GalBank's veins to tap them, low enough that no one in the towers wants to look too hard. He has been threading everything toward this point, consolidating false identities, liquidating hijacked claims, and preparing to cut loose from the Settled Systems with a ledger wiped clean. The quietly reassigned freighters in the drift, the altered case files beneath the plazas, the corrupted manifests hidden in Trade Authority holds were all pieces of the same exit strategy. Someone in the core tried to smother what they found, but the story kept leaking through bar talk and ruined captains. From that first stray dataslate in the black, to the nervous clerk in the city above, to the corrupted support ship parked off the main lanes, every whisper has led back to this pressure sink under New Atlantis.
zh: 深井区，是遗忘之物本应沉下去、留在下面的地方，淹在旅游亮面与三头同盟话术之下。在这下面，记录会丢失、债务会滚进阴影、面孔会在人群的涌动中模糊。对一个靠"在纸面上抹掉人"为生的人来说，这座下城是完美的最后一个集结点：离盖尔银行的血脉足够近、能把管子伸进去，又足够低、让高楼里没人愿意细看。他一直在把一切穿向这一点：整合假身份、变现被劫持的索赔，并准备带着一本擦干净的账册切断与定居星系的联系。漂流带里被悄悄改派的货船、广场下方被改动的案卷、藏在贸易管理局货舱里的损坏舱单，都是同一套撤离策略的碎片。核心区有人试图把他们的发现闷死，可这故事不断从酒吧闲谈与完蛋船长的口中漏出来。从漆黑中第一块散落数据板，到楼上城市里那名紧张的文书，再到停在主航道外的损坏支援船，每一句低语都被引回新亚特兰蒂斯城下方这个压力沉淀区。

#en: The Abandoned Bionics Lab sits at the end of every line you have pulled, a dead facility with live power and just enough automated systems left for someone like her to bend into a private theater. Here the tools are already in the walls: surgical bays, dormant prosthetic rigs, and half-coded interface suites she can wake with a keystroke, all buried far from regulators and still wired to old Ryujin standards she helped design. Out here she can finish stitching together the network hinted at in stolen firmware archives and smuggling ledgers, using the last intact equipment to tune a free mesh that would slip past any corporate leash, then ghost away behind her augmented clients. The scorched access door and a half-completed breach charge suggest another crew tried to end this and never made it past the first line of defenses. So far the trail reads like this: a forgotten dataslate in the back of beyond, ghost references to missing neuroamp designs in a quiet research outpost, then this same lab half-lit and full of erased logs, pointing to Splice circling back to weaponize the only place that still remembers how to build her.
zh: 那座废弃仿生学实验室位于你拉出的每一条线的尽头，一座带着电力的死设施，剩下的自动化系统刚好够像她那样的人把它掰成私人剧场。这里的工具已在墙里：手术舱、休眠的义体设备，以及她一个按键就能唤醒的半编码接口套件，全都埋在远离监管者之处，仍接在她参与设计的旧龙神标准上。在这外面，她能完成把被盗固件档案与走私账册里暗示的网络缝在一起，用最后完好的设备调校一张能溜过任何公司牵引的自由网格，然后藏到她的增强客户背后消失。被烧焦的入口门与一枚半完成的破门炸药说明，另有一支队伍曾试图终结这一切，却从没闯过第一道防线。目前为止，这条线索读起来是这样：天涯之外一块被遗忘的数据板、某座安静研究前哨里对失踪神经增幅器设计的幽灵引用，然后就是这同一座半亮、塞满被擦除日志的实验室，指向"拼接"绕回、要把唯一仍记得如何建造她的地方武器化。

#en: This part of Akila is where ships come to die slow, and the people who worked them are not far behind, which is exactly why any talk worth hearing sinks into the rust instead of floating up to the Core. Between leaning shacks and crooked repair stalls, actuators and grav rings pile in heaps, tagged with half-legible IDs from haulers that vanished on routes no insurance adjuster wants to audit too closely. The junction buried under all this clutter is not just scrap; it is a scar from a job that went wrong in a very specific way, a place where someone tested how far they could bend a flight path before it snapped. To pick through it here, at the edge of polite notice, is to step into a conversation every spacer in this quarter pretends they are not having, their words clipped short and eyes sliding away whenever timing, discounts, or a certain unseen navigator come up. So far, all you have are a half-burned dataslate from a forgotten camp and low-voiced rumors from worn-out haulers, enough to suggest that some jumps are being nudged off true and that the same quiet signature keeps surfacing wherever wreckage and bad luck pile together.
zh: 阿基拉城的这个区，是船只前来慢慢死去的地方，而开它们的人也紧跟其后，这正是为什么任何值得一听的谈话都会沉进锈里、而不会浮上核心区。在倾斜陋屋与歪斜修理摊之间，执行器与引力环堆成一堆，贴着半可辨认的 ID——它们来自那些在无人愿意细审的航线上消失的货船。埋在这堆杂物下的那个枢纽不只是废料；它是一桩以非常特定方式出错的工作留下的伤疤，一处有人测试"能在飞行路径断裂前把它掰弯多远"的地方。在这里、在体面注意的边缘翻检它，就是踏进一场这个区每个太空劫匪都假装自己没在进行的对话——他们的字句被削短，每当时机、折扣或某位看不见的领航员被提起，目光就滑开。目前为止，你只有一块来自被遗忘营地的半烧毁数据板与疲惫货船船员的低声传闻，足以暗示某些跃迁正被推离真实，而同样的安静签名不断在残骸与霉运堆积之处浮现。

#en: This outpost was never meant to matter; just another research shell on a quiet rock, built for routine data pulls and then half forgotten as priorities drifted elsewhere. That is what makes it perfect for what she did to it. When departments shifted, staff rotated, and oversight thinned to the occasional automated ping, the traffic through here kept flowing on old schedules, half monitored and half ignored. Somewhere in that slow slide from purpose to neglect, someone rewired a single exchange a handshake that once just synced survey results now brushes past LIST archives, Trade Authority ledgers, and settlement queues before vanishing into blank space. If I can pry open what is left of that link, I can see which chains she broke on purpose and which ones she quietly grafted together. Up to now all I have are scattered signs a dead end contact who asked the wrong question, a sealed lab with its logs scrubbed too clean, a nervous broker on Neon fencing partial routes, a derelict survey cutter with half a jump plan and every fragment points to her carefully bending systems over time, until nobody remembers what they were built to do in the first place.
zh: 这座前哨本不该有任何意义；不过是安静岩石上又一个研究外壳，为常规数据拉取而建，随后在优先级漂移时被半遗忘。这正是她把它变成现在这样的完美条件。当部门轮换、人员调动、监督稀薄成偶尔的自动脉冲时，经过这里的交通仍按旧日程流动，一半被监控、一半被忽视。在那场从"用途"滑向"忽视"的缓慢过程里，有人在某处重接了一次交换——一次曾只同步勘探结果握手，如今擦过独立盟档案、贸易管理局账册与定居点队列，然后消失在空白区域。若我能撬开那条连接剩下的东西，我就能看出她故意扯断了哪些链、又悄悄嫁接了哪些。到目前为止，我只有零散的迹象：一名问了错误问题的死掉联系人、一座日志被擦得太干净的密封实验室、霓虹城一名兜售部分航线的紧张掮客、一艘带着半份跃迁计划的弃置勘探切割船；每一块碎片都指向她小心地随时间弯折系统，直到没人记得它们最初被造来做什么。

#en: The Abandoned Deimos Scrapyard is where her whole crusade was always heading, a place built on the lie that wrecks are just metal and not the people written out of the manifests. Here, among gutted hulls and stripped grav drives, she is threading the last of her stolen data through hidden cores, preparing to erase or broadcast everything the salvage ring buried under "administrative resolutions." UC and Freestar patrols turned blind eyes to this yard for years, calling it obsolete while she turned it into a fortress and an archive in one. The rusted cranes, mined walkways, and jury-rigged turrets are not simply defenses but levers; if she finishes locking her ledgers here, the ghost-insured ships become more than rumor and the factions complicit in their loss may burn or double down. This is the last gap before the graveyards belong entirely to her or are swallowed again by the same silence that let her work go unnoticed for so long. So far, the trail has run from a discarded report in the dust to a sabotaged relay that throttled distress calls, then into a derelict UC combat ship whose untouched logs showed military routes overlapping "accidental" civilian disappearances.
zh: 那座"废弃火卫二废料场"，是她整场圣战一直朝着去的地方，一座建立在"残骸只是金属、而非被写出舱单的人"这个谎言之上的地方。在这里、在被掏空的船壳与被剥光的引力引擎之间，她把最后一批偷来的数据穿进隐藏核心，准备抹掉或广播那伙打捞集团埋在"行政决议"之下的一切。联殖与自由星系联盟巡逻队多年来对这片场区视而不见，在它变成堡垒兼档案馆时称它过时。那些锈蚀吊车、布雷步道与临时拼凑炮塔不只是防御，更是杠杆；若她完成把自己账册锁在这里，那些被"幽灵保险"的船就会不再只是传闻，而共谋其损失的派系或将焚毁、或将加注。这是最后一道缝隙——在那之后，墓地要么完全属于她，要么再次被那种"让她的工作长期不被注意"的同样沉默吞掉。目前为止，线索从尘土里一份被丢弃报告，到一座扼杀遇险呼叫的被动过手脚中继，然后钻进一艘弃置联殖战斗舰——它未被动过的日志显示军用航线与"意外"民用失踪重叠。

#en: A station like this was supposed to host short-term trials and emergency protocols, not keep them humming in the background for generations. But habits harden, staff change, and what began as provisional containment has settled into routine: anonymous specimens tagged, stored, and fed through machines that no one bothers to question anymore. If any trace of what he is trying to map was ever captured in flesh or residue, it will be catalogued here as just another anomaly in a system that forgot it was temporary. So far the trail runs from a corrupted slate on a nameless rock, to falsified records on a wandering freighter, to a forgotten military archive each step pointing to someone quietly turning improvised workarounds into standing practice, and bending those practices into a way to move unseen between the lanes.
zh: 像这样的星际站本只该承载短期试验与应急协议，而不是让它们一代代地在后台嗡鸣。可习惯会硬化、人员会更换，起初只是临时围控的东西逐渐沉淀成了例行：匿名样本被标记、储存，喂进再没人费心质疑的机器里。若说他试图绘制的任何东西曾在血肉或残留物中被捕捉到，那它也会被当作这套"忘了自己只是临时"的系统里又一处异常编入目录。目前为止，线索从一块无名岩石上损坏的数据板，到一艘漂游货船上被伪造的记录，再到一座被遗忘的军事档案库，每一步都指向有人在悄悄把临时的变通变成常设做法，并把这些做法掰成一条在航道之间隐形移动的路。

#en: The abandoned depot is where forgotten cargo comes to rest and paperwork comes to die, which is exactly why this place still matters. Its racks are full of containers that never matched their manifests, tagged with routing codes no one admits to issuing, overseen by contractors who swear they only guard "generic assets." Grid Warbrand holds the ground with the bored focus of people paid to ignore the fine print, but the routing clusters here still hum with patterns that do not belong to any sanctioned lane. So far the trail has been built from things everyone pretends not to remember: a stray signature from that lonely rock, incomplete schedules from the quiet lab, a shuttered relay that logged traffic after shutdown, and dockside gossip in Gagarin Landing about a tug that always left light and was never challenged.
zh: 那座废弃货运站，是被遗忘货物停下、文书死去的地方——这正是这地方至今仍要紧的原因。它的货架塞满了从未与舱单对上的货柜，标签上是不承认自己签发过的航线路由代码，由那些发誓只守卫"普通资产"的承包商看着。网格战痕帮以"被雇来无视细则的人"那种无聊的专注守在这里，可这里的路由簇仍在嗡鸣着不属于任何获批航道的模式。目前为止，这条线索是由所有人都假装不记得的东西搭成的：那块孤独岩石上的一道散落签名、那座安静实验室里不完整的日程、一座关机后仍在记录交通的关闭中继，以及加加林着陆点码头边关于一艘总在轻载离港、从未被拦查的拖船的闲话。

#en: A GalBank contract hauler should never drift this far off its lane, yet BX-1113 Creditforge hangs in the dark like a cancelled debt, its running lights dead, its registry still quietly billing hours no one has checked in months.
