This is where the numbers and the routes intersect, where a logistics workhorse doubled as a vault for the wrong kind of ledger, humming along the same corridors Vector once calibrated. In its cargo logs and nav cores, you are not just chasing one man, but the silent tolerance that let his corrections ride unchallenged across the network. So far the trail has been a forgotten dataslate on a fringe rock and buried notes from a nervous corporate contact, all pointing toward altered corridors, missing ships, and a cartographer whose fingerprints keep surfacing in the margins of official records.
zh: 一艘盖尔银行的合同货船本绝不该漂离航道这么远，可"BX-1113 信贷熔炉"像一笔被注销的债务悬在黑暗中：航行灯熄灭，登记册却仍在悄悄计费，而那些工时已好几个月没人查过。这里正是数字与航线相交之处，是某台物流主力兼作那种"错误账册"的金库之处，沿着"向量"曾经校准过的同样走廊嗡鸣。在它的货运日志与导航核心里，你追的不只是一个人，而是那种让他的修正得以在网络中不受质疑地穿行的沉默容忍。目前为止，这条线索是一块边缘岩石上被遗忘的数据板，以及某个紧张的内部联系人埋下的笔记，全都指向被改动的走廊、失踪的船只，以及一名指纹不断在官方记录页边浮现的制图师。

#en: The farm sits exactly where her math needs it to be, a quiet notch between patrol sweeps and commercial lanes, a place early LIST planners marked as convenient refuel and every smuggler since learned to forget. Here the airfields and broken silos hide a ship that can spin up without drawing distant eyes, and the soil still holds cables from when this was a refit stop for haulers testing risky shortcuts. Now Vector folds her grief and stolen telemetry into one last set of calculations, close enough to the line she has been sketching across half the map. No one out here knows the full story, only fragments traded in low voices: a burnt courier's slate on a dead rock, a shaken Fleet liaison in a rusting drop shelter, murmurs in Neon's shadows that her routes draw an invisible curve back to a convoy that never came home.
zh: 这座农场恰好坐落在她的数学需要它在的位置：巡逻圈与商业航道之间一道安静的凹口，一处早期独立盟规划者标记为便利补给点、而此后每个走私者都学会忘掉的地方。在这里，简易机场与破损筒仓藏着一艘能不引来远方目光就点火的船，土壤里仍埋着线缆——那时这里还是货运船测试冒险近路的中转站。如今"向量"把她的悲伤与偷来的遥测折进最后一组计算，离她半张地图上一直在勾勒的那条线足够近。这外面没人知道完整的故事，只有低声交换的碎片：死寂岩石上一块烧毁信使的数据板、某座锈蚀投放掩体里一名心有余悸的舰队联络官，以及霓虹城阴影里的低语——说她的航线画出一条无形的弧线，绕回一支从未回家的车队。

#en: Ebbside is where the city forgets what time it is, where shifts blur together and nobody notices when one more crate starts moving under the wrong name. If someone wanted to buy adjustments to their weather and tuck the payments into everyday freight, this is where the paperwork would vanish into the background noise of liquor runs, chem drops, and replacement filters. Hidden in those routine manifests is the list of who has been paying for storms, and from that, a pattern of worlds she keeps circling back to.  \nUp to now the trail has only given me fragments: an anonymous tip from the fringe, cautious files at a support post, refinery readings that did not match their own reports; all hinting that what began as "special deliveries" became standard practice long before anyone thought to ask who signed for the skies.
zh: 埃布赛德是这座城市忘记时间的地方，班次彼此模糊，没人注意又多了一个货箱以错误的名义开始移动。若有人想给自己买天气调整、并把款项塞进日常货运里，这里就是那些文书会化进酒类运输、化学空投与更换滤芯的背景噪声之处。藏在那些例行舱单里的，是"谁一直在为风暴付钱"的清单，而由它可以推出一串她不断绕回的世界。  \n目前为止，这条线索只给了我碎片：来自边境的一条匿名线报、某座补给站里谨慎的文件、与其他报告不符的炼油读数；全都暗示着，起初的"特别配送"早在任何人想起问"是谁替天空签收"之前就已成了标准做法。

#en: Out here in high orbit, this sliver of hardware is the only thing that still remembers how the lanes really run. The array was never meant to be interesting a maintenance waypoint, a passive relay, the kind of thing captains ignore while they worry about fuel and docking slots. Then its update schedule slipped, its handshake pattern shifted by a few milliseconds, and someone rerouted a patrol to sit on top of it without changing the public charts. A Spacer hull like BR-8628 Shatterjaw does not park over dead metal for nothing; whatever is buried in that signal trail is worth guarding in gun range. So far the trail is nothing but altered timetables and traffic rumors quiet changes in approach windows, new vectors filed under old codes, routines that bent a little each week until nobody could remember when they started.
zh: 在这里的高轨道上，这一小片硬件是唯一仍记得航道真正如何运行的东西。那座阵列本不该有任何意思——一个维护航点、一座被动中继，船长们在操心燃料与泊位时会忽略的那种东西。然后它的更新日程滑了、握手模式偏移了几毫秒，而有人不经改动公开星图就把一支巡逻队调到它上方压着。像"BR-8628 碎颚"这样的太空劫匪船壳不会无缘无故停在死金属上方；埋在那些信号轨迹里的任何东西，都值得用枪炮射程守着。目前为止，这条线索无非是被改动的时间表与交通传闻：进近窗口的安静变化、以旧代码归档的新向量，以及每周都弯一点、直到没人记得它们何时开始的惯例。

#en: The Voyager AX-1329 hangs cold and lightless, a Trade Authority hulk that should have been towed long ago, if its last manifests had matched what the docks expected to see. Instead, it slipped between schedules and signatures, stranded in a patch of quiet space where no one would question a little missing cargo or a few extra welds. Its idle cranes and frozen conveyors mark it as the only place where freight, identity, and trajectory could have been rewritten cleanly enough to hide a moving yard in plain sight. The trail up to here is a chain of near-misses and overlooked warnings: a forgotten slate in a remote shed, monitoring logs at an abandoned relay that flagged unregistered work barges, then half-scrubbed entries in an old listening post that hinted someone was bending the lanes without ever quite breaking them.
zh: 旅行者 AX-1329冷寂无光地悬着，一艘本该早就被拖走的贸易管理局残骸——如果它最后几份舱单与码头预期的相符的话。可它偏偏从日程与签名之间滑了出去，搁浅在一片没人会质疑"少了一点货物、多了几道焊缝"的安静太空中。它闲置的吊臂与冻结的传送带，标志着它是唯一能让"货物、身份与轨迹"被干净改写、从而把一个移动船坞藏在明面上的地方。通往这里的线索是一连串惊险擦碰与被忽略的警告：偏远棚屋里一块被遗忘的数据板、某座废弃中继处标记了未登记作业驳船的监控日志，然后是一座旧听音哨里半擦除的条目，暗示有人一直在掰弯航道、却从未真正把它们掰断。

#en: Where the debris thins and the stars feel too close, the last working machinery in this graveyard is still quietly doing its job, shunting phantom triage routes and evac paths along a line nobody remembers authorizing. As long as that logic loop keeps running, wounded ships and desperate crews will keep drifting the same way, and he will always have a reason to be waiting at the end of it. Breaking the chain here means cutting into the nervous system of some forgotten war protocol before it can drag anyone else into his hands.  \nSo far all I have are fragments of a pattern: an anonymous cache on a dead rock, a derelict patrol frame still obeying half-erased orders, and a cleaned-up account of a massacre that leaves one medic unaccounted for, all hinting that something old and automatic has been steering him for years.
zh: 在残骸变稀薄、群星显得太近之处，这片墓地里最后一台仍在运转的机械仍在悄悄干活，沿一条没人记得谁批准过的线调度着幽灵般的分诊路线与撤离路径。只要那个逻辑回路继续运行，受伤的船与走投无路的船员就会继续朝同一方向漂去，而他总能有个理由守在它的尽头。在这里打断这条链，意味着切进某套被遗忘战争协议的中枢系统——赶在它把更多人拖进他手里之前。  \n目前为止，我只有一些模式碎片：死寂岩石上一处匿名储藏点、一具仍服从半擦除命令的弃置巡逻船架，以及一份把一名医疗兵留作"下落不明"的清白屠杀记录——全都暗示某种古老而自动的东西多年来一直在引导他。

#en: The Helium-3 plant hums like a caged storm, its vats and stacks bleeding heat into the thin air, the kind of place someone obsessed with the sky would hijack without ever setting foot planetside. Whatever she seeded into this line is feeding off the reactors and telemetry here, bending data and weather both, and as long as it lives in the machinery, every refinery ping and atmospheric readout is suspect. Cut it out here and the path she has been hiding behind those signals finally stands alone.  \nSo far the trail runs from a nameless fringe tip to guarded files at a frontier post, then to odd refinery diagnostics; in every room where this work is whispered, certain names vanish mid-sentence, replaced by shrugs and careful pronouns that all seem to circle back toward the same missing scientist and her unfinished storm.
zh: 那座氦-3 工厂像一头被关进笼子的风暴嗡鸣，它的罐体与烟囱把热量渗进稀薄的空气，是那种痴迷天空的人从不着陆就能劫持的地方。她播进这条链路的东西正以这里的反应堆与遥测为食，同时掰弯数据与天气；只要它活在机械里，每一次炼油脉冲与大气读数都不可信。在这里把它切掉，她一直藏在那些信号后面的路径终于会独自站住。  \n目前为止，线索从一条无名边境线报，到某座边境哨所里戒备的文件，再到古怪的炼油诊断；在每一间有人低声谈论这项工作的房间里，某些名字都会在句子中间消失，被耸肩与谨慎的代词取代——而它们似乎都绕回同一名失踪的科学家与她未完成的风暴。

#en: Out here, where the relay hangs in a thinning orbit no one admits still exists, she can work without oversight or witnesses, cutting and splicing grav lanes through a node that was quietly erased from every official chart. The old UC hardware still trusts her credentials, feeding her live routes and transponder chatter as she shapes a final correction that will send multiple ships into the same blind corridor, then burn the last proof of how she has been steering deaths and rescues for years. If she finishes, the pattern vanishes with the station, and everyone gets to pretend they never saw it coming. All I have are a discarded dataslate from a dead-end rock, half-sober rumors traded over Aurora in Neon, and blackened SysDef logs pulled from a drifting tactical hull, each one sketching the same unseen hand in the lanes.
zh: 在这里，在那座悬于一条没人承认仍存在的衰减轨道上的中继处，她能不受监督、没有证人在场地工作，通过一个被从所有官方星图上悄悄抹掉的节点剪切、拼接引力航道。旧联殖硬件仍信任她的凭证，把实时航线与应答器闲谈喂给她，任她塑成最后一次修正——那会把多艘船送进同一条盲走廊，然后烧掉"她多年来如何操纵死亡与救援"的最后证据。若她完工，这个模式就随星际站一同消失，所有人都能假装自己从没看出苗头。我只有一块来自死胡同岩石的废弃数据板、在霓虹城就着极光交易的半醉传闻，以及从一具漂移战术船壳里拉出的焦黑星防队日志，每一份都勾勒出航道中同一只无形的手。

#en: The old relay was never meant to live this long a stopgap node left running on borrowed power, its protocols flagged for decommissioning in some forgotten UC docket. Somewhere along the way, the patches and workarounds hardened into habit, and the station slipped from oversight into shadow, perfect cover for someone clever enough to feed new routes through old code. Now Vermin Gravepack squat in its hollowed corridors like rats in the wiring, guarding a single cache of traffic records and smuggler notes that does not match any official chart, a document that will show where the lanes have really been bending. So far the trail is faint a bloodied dataslate in a remote outpost, rumors of manufactured accidents in spacer bars, a damaged tug captain swearing a calm voice rewrote his course and paid him to forget the details.
zh: 那座旧中继本不该活这么久——一个靠借来的电力运行的临时节点，其协议在某个被遗忘的联殖案卷里早已被标记待退役。一路走来，那些补丁与变通硬化成了习惯，星际站从监督滑入阴影，成了某个聪明到能把新航线喂进旧代码之人的完美掩护。如今"害虫坟场帮"像线路里的老鼠一样蹲在它被掏空的走廊里，守着唯一一处交通记录与走私者笔记的储藏——它不与任何官方星图相符，是一份能显示航道真正在何处弯折的文件。目前为止，这条线索很淡：某座偏远前哨一块沾血的数据板、太空劫匪酒吧里关于"人造意外"的传闻，以及一名受损拖船船长发誓有个平静的声音改写了他的航向、并付钱让他忘掉细节。

#en: Out here, this prefab box of metal and dust is where bad luck gets written down and quietly misfiled, which is exactly why the trail has to be lifted from here and not from some polished office on Akila. The deputy's notes are messy, half for a local dispute and half for a string of implant failures no one ever officially linked, all cross-referenced on a personal tablet because the main system was "too busy" that day. One minor oversight, one unsubmitted report, and the pattern sat here, growing in the dark while more colonists signed the same contracts and woke up with the same whispers in their heads. So far I have a frontier investigator who saw just enough to be scared, a scattered list of failed upgrades from outlying clinics, and a name that keeps surfacing in complaints that never make it into the official queue.
zh: 在这里，这个金属与尘土的预制盒，是霉运被记录下来、并被悄悄错误归档的地方——这正是为什么线索必须从这里、而不是从阿基拉城某间光鲜的办公室里提取。那位副警长的笔记很乱：一半是本地纠纷，一半是一串从未被正式联系起来的植入体故障，全都交叉引用在一台私人平板上，因为主系统那天"太忙"。一次小小的疏忽、一份未提交的报告，模式就坐在这里，在黑暗中生长，而更多殖民者签下同样的合同、醒来时脑中响着同样的低语。目前为止，我有一名"看到的东西刚好够让他害怕"的边境调查员、一份来自外围诊所的失败升级零散清单，以及一个不断出现在从未进入官方队列之投诉里的名字。

#en: Out in the dim sliver of orbit where traffic control forgets to look, a lone Crimson Fleet hauler holds position just off the standard lanes, repeating the same lazy drift-and-burn pattern like a metronome. It has been doing that for weeks, maybe months, subtle shifts in timing that never quite rise to a violation, never quite trip an alarm. Rerouted freighters skim its shadow, patrol paths bend a few degrees wider, and each small adjustment disappears into routine until someone bothers to stack the plots side by side. I started with offhand complaints in a Neon lounge and half-scrubbed logs from a dead SysDef hull; now the private archive buried in Cydonia's back corridors and this ghost-patterned ship in orbit both point to the same conclusion, that her hand has been on these levers longer than anyone wanted to notice.
zh: 在交管系统忘记去看的那道昏暗轨道缝隙里，一艘孤零零的深红舰队货船停在标准航道外侧，像节拍器一样重复着同样懒散的"漂移—点火"模式。它已经这么做了一周、也许好几个月：时机上的细微偏移从未真正构成违规，也从未真正触发警报。被改道的货船贴着它的阴影掠过，巡逻路径弯宽了几度，每一处小小的调整都化进例行公事，直到有人费心把那些轨迹并排叠起来看。我最开始是从霓虹城一家酒廊里的随口抱怨，以及一具死掉星防队船壳里半擦除的日志入手的；如今，埋在赛多尼亚后走廊里的私人档案与轨道上这艘幽灵模式的船，都指向同一个结论：她的手搭在这些操纵杆上的时间，比任何人愿意注意到的都久。

#en: The remote research module is where the trail first bent out of sight, a half-forgotten node still tethered to corporate networks yet far enough from Neon's politics to be overlooked. Its servers once mirrored countless routine transfers, but someone with intimate access reached in and broke a single link in a data-theft chain, nudging stolen code and shipment logs just off their expected paths. In the process, they left the kind of hairline distortions only seen when you stack years of records together: routing quirks, repeating gaps, and an anomaly in the way certain neural design files simply never arrive where they should. Earlier sweeps of frontier clinics, smugglers' manifests, and a whisper from a nervous archivist all point back here, to the quiet machine that watched it happen and still remembers every deviation.
zh: 那座偏远研究舱，是线索第一次拐出视线的地方：一个半被遗忘的节点，仍系在公司的网络上，却离霓虹城的政治足够远、以至于被忽视。它的服务器曾镜像过无数例行传输，可有某个拥有内部权限的人伸手进来，打断了一条数据盗窃链上的单一环节，把被盗代码与货运日志轻推出它们预期的路径。在这个过程中，他们留下了那种只有把多年记录叠起来才能看见的细如发丝的畸变：路由怪癖、重复出现的空缺，以及某些神经设计文件"干脆从不抵达该去之处"的异常。早先对边境诊所、走私者舱单的排查，以及某名紧张档案员的一句低语，全都指回这里——那台安静看着它发生、并仍记得每一处偏差的机器。

#en: On this station that once ignited a war simply by existing in the wrong orbit, every corridor hums with the quiet certainty that medicine here is neutral, apolitical, clean. Yet the research decks and intake archives are precisely where small compromises become doctrine a misfiled case, an unchecked dosage pattern, a forgotten trial note, each a minor oversight that lets someone like Catalyst slip official protocols into the veins of people the system pretends not to see. Buried among years of emergency triage records and transfer authorizations is the thread she could not fully erase, a record of who she still treats and where they vanish afterward. So far, the trail has led from a dead courier freighted with diverted chems to whispers of a ghost medic aiding veterans and settlers, always just off the official manifests.
zh: 在这座仅因身处错误轨道就点燃一场战争的星际站上，每条走廊都嗡鸣着一种安静的笃定：这里的医学是中立的、不问政治的、干净的。然而研究甲板与收治档案正是小妥协变成信条的地方：一份归档错误的病例、一个无人核查的给药模式、一条被遗忘的试验备注，每一处都是小小的疏忽，让像"催化剂"这样的人把官方协议溜进那些系统假装看不见之人的血管里。埋在多年急救分诊记录与转运授权之间的，是她无法彻底抹掉的那根线——一份记录，写着她还治疗谁、以及他们之后消失去了哪里。目前为止，这条线索从一艘载着被截留药剂的死掉信使船，延伸到关于一名帮助老兵与定居者的幽灵医疗兵的低语——她总是恰好不在官方舱单上。

#en: Out here, this quiet research module is where corporate paranoia and outlaw ingenuity first brushed against each other, and the scuff marks never quite faded. This is where competing routes were modeled, where data streams split and recombined, where someone with Vector's instincts could decide which paths lived and which were quietly erased. The local systems still hum with half-sanitized access logs and aborted transfers, the kind of digital crossfire that only matters to people who know how to weaponize information and jump corridors in the same breath. What started as a stray dataslate on a forgotten rock, then smeared beacon echoes in high orbit, then a Trade Authority hull with impossible waste cycles, has now become a stack of "lucky" overlaps and recycled names that stopped feeling like chance about two clues ago.
zh: 在这里、在这座安静的研究舱，公司的偏执与法外之徒的巧思第一次相互擦碰，而那些擦痕从未真正褪去。这里正是竞争航线被建模、数据流被拆分又重组、某个有"向量"那种直觉的人能决定哪些路径存活、哪些被悄悄抹掉的地方。本地系统仍嗡鸣着半清理的访问日志与中断的传输，那种只有懂得"把信息武器化与跃迁走廊操弄在同一口气里完成"的人才在意的数字交火。起初只是被遗忘岩石上一块散落数据板，然后是高轨道上被拖抹的信标回声，再然后是一具带着不可能废料循环的贸易管理局船壳——如今它已成了一大堆"幸运"的重叠与被重复利用的名字，而大约两条线索之前，它们就不再像是巧合了。

#en: Neon's Astral Lounge is where routes are bought with whispers and lost with a single bad drink, so if she sold anyone a path the galaxy was not meant to see, the echo of that deal lives here. In the haze of Aurora and cheap soundproofing, smugglers and haulers trade more than stories; they pass on fragments of access, codes and ciphers scrawled on coasters then half-erased, like someone meant to come back and tidy the trail and simply never returned. Whatever was left behind in this corner of the lounge is not just another trinket; it is the one remaining thread tying her name to the shadow corridors everyone swears do not exist. Up to now all you have is a half-remembered rumor from barflies and the knowledge that certain haulers vanished after dealing with a Kyrgyz-born navigator whose work no one will admit to funding.
zh: 霓虹城的"星光酒廊"，是航线靠低语买入、因一杯喝坏而失去的地方；所以若她卖给过谁一条星系本不该看见的路径，那笔交易的余音就活在这里。在极光与廉价隔音的雾气中，走私者与货船船员交换的不只是故事；他们传递的是权限碎片——写在杯垫上、又被擦掉一半的代码与暗语，像有人打算回来收拾痕迹、却再没回来。留在酒廊这个角落里的东西不只是又一件小玩意；它是唯一一根仍把她的名字与所有人都发誓不存在的阴影走廊系起来的线。目前为止，你只有酒客们记忆模糊的一则传闻，以及一个认知：某些货船船员在与一名吉尔吉斯出生的领航员打交道后消失了，而没人愿意承认资助过她的工作。

#en: Out here, the old UC listening post hangs over the landscape like a forgotten accusation, its antennae still straining toward traffic patterns the Navy no longer admits exist. This is where Vector can work without interference, quietly rewriting the sky, tuning Grav Drives against the ghosts of archived signals pulsing through abandoned relays. Every encrypted ping he sends from here lets him stitch his ghost corridor closer to reality and scrub the last traces of his earlier tampering from official registries. If he finishes, the map itself changes and no tribunal will ever prove who moved the lanes. So far the trail has been a dataslate on a backworld, hushed corporate whispers in a quiet research module, and a derelict GalBank contract hauler stuffed with corrupted charts and one name threaded through every altered route.
zh: 在这里，那座旧联殖听音哨像一桩被遗忘的指控悬在大地之上，它的天线仍在朝着海军不再承认存在的交通模式伸探。"向量"能在这里不受干扰地工作，悄悄重写天空，把引力引擎调谐到那些通过废弃中继脉动的归档信号幽灵。他从这里发出的每一次加密脉冲，都让他把自己的幽灵走廊缝得更接近现实，并从官方登记册上擦掉他早先动手脚的最后一痕。若他完工，星图本身就会改变，而任何法庭都永远无法证明是谁移动了航道。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡星上一块数据板、某座安静研究舱里压低的公司低语，以及一艘塞满损坏星图的盖尔银行合同弃置货船——每一个被改动的航线上都穿着一根同一个名字。

#en: If anyone is still keeping score on the missing ships, the numbers live here, in the rusted bones Deimos left to rot. The scrapyard squats on the edge of nowhere, a tangle of collapsed gantries and half-gutted frames, exactly the sort of place where routes get rewritten and manifests quietly disappear under new paint and old dust. Uniform Blacksteel holds the perimeter with the bored vigilance of people paid to look the other way, not to ask why so many condemned drives all died on the same corridors. The boardrooms and officers who ordered that pattern buried trusted time to smother the rumors, but the whispers never quite went away; a dead spacer's logs in orbit, then inconsistencies in yard reports, all hinting that someone has been steering wrecks into the dark and signing off on their erasure with the same careful hand.
zh: 若说还有人在给失踪船只记账，那些数字就活在这里，活在火卫二留下腐烂的锈蚀骨骼里。那片废料场蹲在天涯之外，一片坍塌的龙门架与被掏空一半的框架的乱麻，正是那种航线被改写、舱单在新油漆与旧尘土下悄悄消失的地方。"黑钢制服"以一种"被雇来转开视线、而非追问为何这么多报废引擎都死在同样几条走廊上"的无聊警惕守着周边。下令掩埋那个模式的董事们与军官们指望时间闷死传闻，可低语从未真正消失：轨道上一名死掉太空劫匪的日志，然后是船坞报告里的不一致，全都暗示有人一直在把残骸引向黑暗，并用同样一只谨慎的手签下它们的抹除。

#en: The old industrial shell still hums faintly with forgotten power, its rusted conduits and half-dead consoles the last place anyone would look for something worth killing over, which makes it exactly where a careful thief would tuck away the tool that rewrites how ships move through space. Whatever she lifted from her former associates will not just be schematics or raw numbers; it will be the working memory of jumps already taken, the kind of data that shows not only where she has been steering traffic, but where she intends the next bend in the lanes to fall. So far the trail is a discarded slate on a backwater world, convoy reports that blame "malfunction" instead of admitting a pattern, and whispering Fleet deserters who all agree on one thing: something vital went missing right before their routes started turning strange.
zh: 那座旧工业空壳仍带着一丝被遗忘电力的嗡鸣，它锈蚀的导管与半死的控制台，是任何人最不会去寻找"值得为之杀人"之物的地方——这让它恰好成了一名谨慎的窃贼藏匿"改写船只如何在太空中移动之工具"的地方。她从旧同伙那里拿走的，不会只是图纸或原始数字；那会是已经进行过的跃迁的工作记忆，那种不只显示她一直在把交通引向何处、还显示她打算让航道的下一个弯落在哪里数据。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡世界上一块被丢弃的数据板、把"故障"当作借口而不肯承认模式的护航报告，以及低声说话的舰队逃兵——他们在一件事上达成一致：就在他们的航线开始变得古怪之前，某样至关重要的东西失踪了。

#en: Gagarin Landing is where the numbers finally stop being abstract and turn into rust, oil, and faces that remember who rewrote their skies. The industrial warrens sit at the junction of UC contracts, Trade Authority salvage, and the same tug crews Vector once flew beside, a perfect blind spot where corporate auditors look away while broken haulers sell their last components for another chance at a profitable run. Here, amid shipbreaker gantries and refit stalls, she can finish purging stolen black boxes and GalBank claim logs, sealing off the evidence that her vectors were never accidents but calculated leverage against the same boardrooms that cashed in on her dead crew; if she erases it now, the pattern of staged disasters collapses back into rumor and bad luck, and the next "optimized route" will just be another unremarked loss. From the first dataslate in a remote camp to bitter whispers in the outskirts of Akila and the wrecked protection ship drifting in deep space, every scrap of timing data, every altered manifest, and every frightened testimony has pointed to the same conclusion: someone has been quietly moving the lanes themselves, and the signature on those distortions all traces back to Vector.
zh: 加加林着陆点，就是那些数字终于不再抽象、而变成锈、油与记得是谁改写他们天空的面孔的地方。工业迷宫坐落在联殖合同、贸易管理局打捞物与"向量"曾并肩飞行过的同一批拖船船员的交汇处，一个完美的盲点：公司审计员转开视线，而破损货船变卖最后的部件以博取又一次获利航次的机会。在这里、在拆船龙门架与翻修摊位之间，她能完成清除偷来的黑匣与盖尔银行索赔日志，封死"她的向量从不是意外、而是针对那些在死掉船员身上捞钱的同一批董事会的算计好的杠杆"的证据；若她现在擦掉它，那些被安排灾难的模式就会坍缩回传闻与霉运，而下一条"优化航线"也只会成为又一次无人注目的损失。从一座偏远营地里的第一块数据板，到阿基拉城郊的苦涩低语与深空中那艘损毁的护航船，每一点时机数据、每一份被改动的舱单、每一句受惊的证词，都指向同一个结论：有人一直在悄悄移动航道本身，而那些扭曲上的签名全都追溯回"向量"。

#en: No one built this pod to be found; it sits deep under regolith and rock, humming quietly against the planet's pulse, its consoles still listening to channels the UC pretends it shut down years ago. If any place would log a ghost crossing into restricted space, it is here, in the blind spot between sanctioned feeds and forgotten operations. The analyst who ran from this post knew enough to be afraid, but not enough to see how routine crossings and familiar callsigns had dulled their edge while someone slipped an unauthorized asset through the cracks. So far the trail is a frightened preacher's stories from a remote retreat, half corrupted schematics scraped from a lonely cache, and now a classified file that finally admits our fugitive once moved under official cover, right where no one was supposed to be watching too closely.
zh: 没人把这个监控舱造成会被发现的；它深埋在风化层与岩石之下，贴着行星的脉搏轻轻嗡鸣，控制台仍在聆听联殖假装多年前就关闭的频道。若说有什么地方会记录下一次"幽灵穿越受限太空"，那就是这里，在获批数据流与被遗忘行动之间的盲点里。从这个岗位逃走的那名分析员知道的东西够多到足以害怕，却不够多到看清：当有人把一件未授权资产从缝隙里溜过去时，那些例行穿越与熟悉的呼号是如何让他们失去了警觉。目前为止，这条线索是某名受惊传教士在偏远隐居地讲的故事、从一处孤独储藏点刮来的半损坏图纸，如今又是一份机密文件——它终于承认我们的逃犯曾以官方身份移动，恰恰在没人该盯得太近的地方。

#en: Down in Neon's lowest decks, under flickering grid-light and dripping coolant, records go to be forgotten rather than erased. This is where overworked techs and off-book captains stash the things that look too small to matter: misfiled service orders, unsigned firmware notes, a recall draft that never quite became official. If there is a place where the story was written plainly, then quietly buried under bad lighting and Aurora haze, it is here, between scavenged panels and repurposed junction boxes. Every step so far has been like that: a half-corroborated ping from a lonely shack, a freighter whose drive history did not match its manifest, a dead ship carrying a manifest that bent routes by a few innocent degrees, each hint straightforward on paper yet strangely slippery when you try to hold the whole pattern in your hands.
zh: 在霓虹城最底层的甲板，在闪烁的网格灯光与滴落的冷却液之下，记录是去被遗忘、而非被抹除的。这里正是超负荷工作的技师与账外船长藏起那些"看起来太小、不值一提"的东西的地方：归档错误的服务单、未签名的固件备注、一份从未正式成形的召回草稿。若说有一个故事曾被平白写下、然后悄悄埋在糟糕灯光与极光雾气之下的地方，那就是这里，在拾来的面板与被改作他用的接线盒之间。目前为止的每一步都是这样：一座孤独棚屋传来半被证实的脉冲、一艘引擎履历与舱单不符的货船、一艘载着把航线掰偏了几度——"几度无辜"——的舱单的死船，每一处线索在纸面上都直白，可当你试图把整个模式握在手里时，却奇怪地滑不留手。

#en: Out here, anchored beside a lonely beacon in high orbit, the sky itself is the archive. This is where he would tune his quiet corrections, nudging satellites and survey nets until entire worlds saw false trajectories as truth. The calibration data that slips through this node never touches official channels; it rides on test pings and maintenance checks, the kind of traffic no one audits until something falls out of the sky. Back on that forgotten rock, farmers only whispered about storms that learned new paths; at the abandoned relay, warning signals died mid-sentence; in the dead lab, grav experiments were left half-scrubbed. Every fragment has come secondhand, traded between people who insist they do not know the whole story, yet all their half-told versions curve the same way, toward an unseen hand repositioning the stars.
zh: 在这里，锚定在高轨道上一座孤独信标旁，天空本身就是档案。这里是他会调校自己那些安静修正的地方，把卫星与勘探网一路推到整个世界都把虚假轨迹当作真相。从这个节点溜过的校准数据从不接触官方信道；它乘着测试脉冲与维护检查，那种直到有东西从天上掉下来才有人审计的交通。回到那块被遗忘的岩石，农场主只低声议论学会了新路径的风暴；在那座废弃中继，警告信号在句子中间死去；在那座死掉的实验室，引力实验被半途抹除。每一块碎片都是二手的，在坚称自己不知道全貌的人之间转手，可他们那些半截版本全都朝同一方向弯曲——指向一只重新摆放星辰的无形之手。

#en: HM-7378 drifts like a sealed question in UC livery, its running lights cold but its transponder still dutifully pinging into a void no one answers anymore. If there is anywhere a buried set of routing orders might still be ticking over on autopilot, it is inside a forgotten SysDef hull whose crew never lived long enough to shut anything down properly. The silence feels procedural rather than abandoned, like a ward left prepped for patients who never arrived, systems still waiting on triggers written by officers who are now dust.  \nSo far I have chased fragments: an anonymous slate on a distant rock, a ghost signal in high orbit, hints of diverted evac flights and scrubbed medical logs, all suggesting that whatever directive turned a good medic into a roaming clinic is still active in the background, following its own schedule.
zh: HM-7378像一枚封着的问号漂着，涂着联殖涂装，航行灯冰冷，应答器却仍尽职地朝一个再无人应答的虚空发出脉冲。若说有一套被埋的航线路由命令可能仍在自动驾驶下滴答运行，那就是在某具被遗忘的星防队船壳里——它的船员活得不够久，没能把任何东西妥善关掉。那份寂静感觉像程序性的，而非被遗弃的，像一间已为从未抵达的病人备好的病房，系统仍在等着那些如今已成尘土的军官写下的触发条件。  \n目前为止，我一直在追碎片：遥远岩石上一块匿名数据板、高轨道上一道幽灵信号、关于被改道撤离飞行与被擦净医疗日志的暗示，全都指向：那道把一名好医疗兵变成流浪诊所的指令，仍在后台按它自己的日程运行。

#en: Out here in quiet orbit, the thing humming against the black is less a beacon than a scar in the traffic lanes, a slow, deliberate kink in how ships choose their jumps. It was never meant to exist this close to settled space; layer by layer someone bent the routes around it, until captains began to follow a curve they could not see. Left alone, it keeps teaching drives to lean toward the same blind corner of the map, tightening the pattern Starline has been sketching in other people's engines.  \n\nSo far, the trail runs through a forgotten datapad in backcountry rock, a buried analyst station full of censored telemetry, and whispers of a missing settler convoy whose last jumps echo the same wrong angles. Taken together, the numbers all tilt toward a second, unseen mass casting its shadow across every chart he has ever touched.
zh: 在这里的安静轨道上，贴着黑暗嗡鸣的那东西与其说是信标，不如说是交通航道上一道伤疤，一种船只如何选择跃迁时缓慢而刻意的扭结。它本不该存在于离定居太空这么近的地方；有人一层层地把航线绕着它掰弯，直到船长们开始跟随一条他们看不见的曲线。任其自生自灭，它会继续教引擎朝星图上同一个盲角倾斜，收紧"星线"在别人的引擎里一直在勾勒的模式。  \n\n目前为止，线索穿过乡间岩石上一块被遗忘的数据板、一座塞满被审查遥测的被埋分析站，以及关于一支失踪定居者车队的低语——它的最后几次跃迁回响着同样错误的夹角。合在一起看，这些数字全都倾向第二个看不见的质量体，它的阴影投在他碰过的每一张星图上。

#en: Gagarin is where the numbers first slipped their leash, even if nobody logged it that way. In the rusted shadows of the agro annex and the noise of loaders on the strip, someone threaded a new path into existing routes, a quiet edit that turned routine grain into a message only a careful reader could catch. Whatever was installed here touches every cargo link she has used since; without that pattern, everything you have heard about failed inspections and miracle harvests stays as bar talk and burned terminals. From what little survives, you can piece together that anonymous survey logs on a forgotten rock mentioned recall orders that never came, inspectors here muttered about shipments moving too fast for comfort, and somewhere between those two points, a single routing fragment keeps repeating like a nervous tick in the system.
zh: 加加林星，就是那些数字第一次挣脱缰绳的地方，尽管没人那样记录过。在农业附属区锈蚀的阴影与装卸带的噪声中，有人把一条新路径穿进现有航线，一次安静的编辑，把例行的谷物变成只有细心读者才能捕捉到的信息。安装在这里的东西触及她此后用过的每一条货运链路；没有那个模式，你听到的关于失败检查与奇迹收成的所有说法，就都只是酒吧闲谈与烧坏的终端。从残存下来的极少东西里，你能拼出：某块被遗忘岩石上的匿名勘探日志提到从未到来的召回令，这里的检查员嘟囔着货运快得令人不安，而在这两点之间的某处，一段单一的航线路由碎片像系统里一根紧张的抽搐一样反复出现。

#en: Ryujin's tower in Neon is where numbers stop being theory and start buying silence; whatever was carved out of their internal ledgers will show which clients paid for routes that just happened to skirt disaster, and which accidents were never accidents at all. The trail of altered vectors disappears into their accounting stacks, where navigation experiments are buried as research write-offs and side-channel contracts, and if anything links corporate money to those ghost corrections, it will be here, half-redacted and mislabeled. So far, all anyone agrees on is this much: a burned slate on a forgotten relay showed the first pattern, freight captains in frontier bars swore the same unseen hand nudged their jumps, and a jittery analyst in New Atlantis confirmed that whole folders of anomaly data vanished the moment her name came up.
zh: 霓虹城的龙神大楼，是数字不再是理论、而开始买得起沉默的地方；从他们内部账册里挖出的任何东西，都会显示哪些客户为"恰好擦过灾难"的航线付了钱、哪些事故根本不是事故。被改动向量的线索消失进他们的会计堆里——导航实验被当作研究注销与侧信道合同埋起来；而若说有任何东西把公司的钱与那些幽灵修正系在一起，它就会在这里，半涂黑、标签错乱。目前为止，所有人唯一一致认同的只有这些：一块被遗忘中继上烧毁的数据板显示了第一个模式，边境酒吧里的货船船长发誓同一只无形之手推动了他们的跃迁，而新亚特兰蒂斯城一名神经紧张的分析员确认，整批整批的异常数据在她名字被提起的那一刻就消失了。

#en: The old relay station hangs over the dead plain like a rusted crown, its dishes still clawing at the sky long after the UC crossed it off their maps. Out here the noise floor is low, clean enough for one mind to bend every beacon and emergency channel in a half-dozen systems. This is where years of quiet rerouting, falsified distress calls, and engineered "ghost rescues" converge into a single live grid, its cores running hot with civilian traffic that does not know who is holding the switch. If the work is cut anywhere else, it heals; sever it here, and the pattern breaks. From the first scorched dataslate on that nameless rock to the gutted drone lab and the bunker tech clutching stolen sensor traces, every lead has pointed to one architect, one hidden hand inside the emergency network, drawing everything toward this silent node.
zh: 那座旧中继站像一顶锈蚀的王冠悬在死寂平原之上，它的天线在联殖把它从星图上划掉很久之后仍在抓挠天空。在这外面，本底噪声很低，干净到足以让一个头脑弯折半打星系里的每一座信标与紧急频道。这里正是多年安静改道、伪造遇险呼叫与精心设计的"幽灵救援"汇聚成一张活网格的地方，它的核心为那些不知道谁握着开关的民用交通而发烫。若在别处切断这项工作，它会自愈；在这里切断它，模式就断了。从那块无名岩石上第一块烧焦的数据板，到被掏空的无人机实验室与紧抱偷来传感器痕迹的掩体技师，每一条线索都指向同一位设计者、同一只藏在应急网络里的手，把一切引向这座沉默的节点。

#en: The hut squats alone against the wind-scoured ridge, its sensor masts half-frozen, lenses crusted with dust and ice. Out here, nobody bothers to clean up after a storm, or after a fugitive; they just let the monitors keep quietly recording heat and motion until the buffers fill and overwrite. This is the one place where the ground itself will have told the truth about who crossed it, how fast they moved, what they were running from or toward, long after the locals started shrugging and claiming they "did not see much that night." So far the trail is built on those kinds of omissions: a remote station that logged a spike and filed it under "atmospherics," a patrol pilot who swore his scopes glitched, a frontier sheriff who remembered a stranger's ship but not the direction it left, each testimony neat where it should have been messy.
zh: 那座小屋孤零零地蹲在风蚀山脊旁，它的传感器桅杆半冻着，镜头结满尘土与冰。在这外面，没人在风暴过后清理现场，也没人在逃犯过后清理；他们只是让监测器继续悄悄记录热量与动静，直到缓冲区满、自行覆写。这是唯一一处地面本身会说出真相的地方——谁曾穿越它、移动得多快、在躲开什么或奔向什么，而这一切都远在当地人开始耸肩声称"那晚没看见什么"之后。目前为止，这条线索正是建立在那样一些省略上：一座记录了尖峰却把它归进"大气现象"的远程星际站、一名发誓自己示波器出故障的巡逻飞行员、一名记得陌生人的船却记不得它离开方向的边境治安官——每一份证词都在本该凌乱的地方显得过分整洁。

#en: The Freestar field command trailer is the only place where someone outside UC bothered to map the same warped routes you have been chasing, scribbled between patrol schedules and casualty tallies. Out here, away from polished briefing rooms, a deputy had time to notice which convoys kept vanishing after buying discount guidance, and which coordinates no one wanted to write into official reports. The air inside hums with generator noise and unasked questions; the few Rangers still working the board go quiet when traffic anomalies are mentioned, suddenly busy with anything that does not involve meeting your eyes. So far, the trail runs from a drifting buoy packed with falsified vectors to dockside manifests showing identical edits, all pointing toward a single hand quietly selling bad directions to anyone desperate enough to trust them.
zh: 自由星系联盟战地指挥拖车，是唯一一个联殖之外的人费心绘制过你一直在追的同样扭曲航线的地方，涂写在巡逻日程与伤亡统计之间。在这外面，远离光鲜的简报室，一名副警长有时间注意到：哪些车队在买了打折导航后接连消失、哪些坐标没人愿意写进官方报告。里面的空气因发电机噪声与未问出口的问题而嗡鸣；仍在板前工作的少数游骑兵一提到交通异常就沉默下来，突然忙于任何不必与你对视的事。目前为止，线索从一枚塞满伪造向量的漂移浮标，延伸到显示相同编辑的码头舱单，全都指向一只悄悄把错误方向卖给任何绝望到愿意相信之人的手。

#en: If she ever left a fingerprint anywhere, it would be here, buried beneath Aurora haze and music that makes your bones vibrate. The lounge sits at the crossroads of half the Settled Systems; captains, smugglers, and data-fixers drift through with pockets full of half-scrubbed logs and stories they only tell when they think no one important is listening. Routing anomalies become bar talk, emergency advisories become drinking jokes, and the same odd timing in the lanes gets mentioned just enough to prove it is not coincidence anymore. So far I have a discarded slate from a forgotten rock, jittery rumors traded over Neon cocktails, and echoes in SysDef telemetry; taken together they show how an old shuttle disaster and a string of "lucky" saves bent people and traffic just enough to land me at this bar, listening for a ghost in the noise.
zh: 若说她曾在任何地方留下过指纹，那就会在这里，埋在极光的雾气与让你骨头共振的音乐之下。这家酒廊坐落在半个定居星系的十字路口；船长、走私者与数据掮客来来去去，口袋里塞满半擦除的日志与他们只在以为没有要紧人在听时才讲的故事。路由异常变成酒吧闲谈，紧急通告变成下酒笑话，而航道上同样古怪的时机被提起的次数刚好足以证明它不再是巧合。目前为止，我有一块来自被遗忘岩石的被丢弃数据板、在霓虹城鸡尾酒中交易的紧张传闻，以及星防队遥测里的回声；合在一起，它们显示出一起旧穿梭机空难与一连串"幸运"救援如何把人与交通掰得刚好足以把我带到这家酒吧，在噪声里听一个幽灵。

#en: Neon's underbelly holds on to things time should have shaken loose; debts, bodies, and secrets all settle in the dripping steel and humming conduits beneath the lights. Vector chose this place precisely because nothing leaves here quickly, not cargo, not rumors, not witnesses. Down in the wet market shadows she can buy fuel, scrub transponders, and disappear experimental samples into a biotech gray zone that answers to no law but profit. Every false trail she and Rourke laid, every redirected shipment and vanished homestead, has been angling them toward this bolt-hole beneath the city that never forgets what it swallows. Earlier we found the first crooked data at that lonely outpost, then strange telemetry in high orbit, and finally a courier's gutted hold; together they sketched one truth, that their route always bent back toward Neon.
zh: 霓虹城的下腹会留住时间本应摇松的东西；债务、尸体与秘密都在灯光下滴水的钢铁与嗡鸣的导管里沉降下来。"向量"选中这地方，恰恰是因为这里没有东西会很快离开——货物不会、传闻不会、证人也不会。在湿货市场的阴影里，她可以买燃料、擦净应答器，并把实验样本消失进一个只认利润、不认任何法律的生物技术灰色地带。她和鲁尔克布下的每一条假痕迹、每一次被改道的货运与每一个消失的农庄，都一直把他们引向这座城市下方那个从不忘掉自己吞下过什么的藏身洞。早先我们在那座孤独前哨发现了第一批歪斜数据，然后是高轨道上的古怪遥测，最后是一艘信使船被掏空的货舱；合在一起，它们勾勒出一个真相：他们的航线总是弯回霓虹城。

#en: The combat hulk hanging dead in space is more than wreckage; it is where financial models and weapons doctrine were spliced together, then abandoned when the operators realized the currents they were testing ran deeper than any patrol route. Only here, in the frozen CIC of this UC SysDef vessel, do the cross-linked transfer logs and engagement priorities still lie side by side, untouched by GalBank censors or naval tribunals, a record of how Ledger's work was folded into war games by officers who walked away before understanding what they had set in motion. Back in Neon's shadows, ledgers and whispered rumors first tied her numbers to criminal traffic; now the trail has climbed from undercity lockers to a lost warship, and the pattern looks less like a heist and more like someone teaching the Settled Systems how to weaponize a bank run.
zh: 那具死寂地悬在太空中的战斗船壳不只是残骸；它是"金融模型与武器学说被拼接在一起、随后在操作者意识到他们测试的暗流比任何巡逻航线都更深时被弃置"的地方。只有在这里、在这艘联殖星防队舰船的冻结指挥中心里，交叉关联的转账日志与交战优先级才仍并排躺着，未被盖尔银行审查员或海军法庭碰过——一份记录，记录着军官们如何把"账本"的工作折进战争演习，而他们还没来得及理解自己启动了什么都已转身离开。在霓虹城的阴影里，账册与低语传闻最初把她的数字与犯罪交通系在一起；如今线索从下城储物柜爬上一艘失落的军舰，而这个模式看起来不再像一次盗窃，更像有人在教定居星系如何把"挤兑银行"武器化。

#en: Survey buoys do not usually sit this far off the standard lanes, and they do not usually whisper coordinates that disagree with every official chart by the same precise margin. Whatever has been nudging jump data sideways chose this empty orbit on purpose; adjust trajectories here and whole trade routes, patrol paths, and escape vectors drift without anyone noticing until it is too late. Letting that anchor point remain hidden means every later trace of the target's movements will be built on warped space. Up to now the trail has been small, crooked signatures on forgotten worlds, a scratched dataslate in the dust, a beacon whose heartbeat never matched its traffic, and a dead SysDef hull whose own logs argued with themselves, all hinting that someone has been editing both paths and fates from the shadows for longer than anyone realized.
zh: 勘探浮标通常不会离标准航道这么远，也通常不会低语着与每一张官方星图都以同样精确幅度不符的坐标。一直在把跃迁数据往侧面推的东西，是刻意选中这条空荡轨道；在这里调整轨迹，整条贸易航线、巡逻路径与逃生向量都会漂移，而没人察觉到，直到为时已晚。让那个锚点继续隐藏，意味着之后对目标行踪的每一条追踪都会建在扭曲的太空上。目前为止，这条线索是那些被遗忘世界上的小小歪斜签名、尘土里一块被划花的数据板、一座心跳从未与自身交通相符的信标，以及一具与自己日志争吵的死掉星防队船壳，全都暗示有人从阴影里同时编辑路径与命运，时间比任何人意识到的都久。

#en: The abandoned listening post still remembers every whisper the UC tried to bury; its dishes sit crooked under a dead sky, but the racks below hum just enough to prove someone repurposed its ears. Hotel Hardstrike did not set up here for nostalgia they are guarding whatever beacon data survived deletion, the off-angle pings that show where lanes were bent, not broken. Whoever sold them this watch claims the contract came from a friend of a friend, no names attached, every story passed down secondhand until truth and cover blend. So far the trail runs like this a ghost relay spilling corrupted timings, freight captains in frontier dives swearing the same unseen hand nudged their jumps, a nervous analyst in New Atlantis watching anomaly folders vanish, then corporate ledgers in Neon quietly acknowledging routes no one will admit authorizing.
zh: 那座废弃听音哨仍记得联殖试图埋葬的每一句低语；它的天线盘在死寂天空下歪斜着，可下面的机架嗡鸣得刚好足以证明有人改用了它的耳朵。"硬击旅社"扎在这里不是为了怀旧——他们守着删除后残存的信标数据，那些显示航道被掰弯、而非被折断的偏角脉冲。把这份看守卖给他们的人声称合同来自"朋友的朋友"，不具名，每个说法都二手传递，直到真相与掩护混成一体。目前为止，线索是这样的：一座喷吐损坏时序的幽灵中继、边境廉价酒馆里的货船船长发誓同一只无形之手推动了他们的跃迁、新亚特兰蒂斯城一名神经紧张的分析员看着异常文件夹消失，然后是霓虹城的公司账册悄悄承认了没人愿意承认自己批准过的航线。

#en: The relay was never meant to matter; just another aging node left to hum along on stale firmware at the edge of anyone's responsibility. That is exactly why someone chose it. One forgotten maintenance window, one unsupervised access change, and the traffic through this place started to warp: distress calls stretched, ship IDs misfiled, routes quietly bent away from prying eyes. The Starbreak Salvors squatting in its corridors think they are guarding a lucky glitch in the network, a tap on unclaimed signals, but whatever was nudged here has been snowballing for years. All anyone really knows so far is that a discarded dataslate in a remote landing site hinted at closed claims on missing ships, and word from station bars says those same registry numbers keep reappearing in the kind of off-ledger salvage auctions that should not exist at all.
zh: 那座中继本不该有任何意义；不过是又一个陈旧节点，靠过期固件在"谁都管不着"的边缘嗡鸣。这正是有人选中它的原因。一次被遗忘的维护窗口、一次无人监督的权限变更，经过此地的交通就开始扭曲：遇险呼叫被拉长、船只 ID 被错档、航线被悄悄掰离窥探的眼睛。蹲在它走廊里的"破星打捞队"以为自己在守着网络里一处幸运的小故障、一个搭上无主信号的便宜，可这里被推过的东西已经滚雪球般积累多年。所有人目前真正知道的只有：某处偏远着陆点一块被丢弃的数据板暗示了失踪船只上被结清的赔偿，而星际站酒吧里的消息说，那些同样的登记号不断出现在本不该存在的账外打捞拍卖里。

#en: This tower is where theory quietly becomes hardware, where someone's off-the-record experiment slipped past review and kept being funded because shutting it down would mean admitting it ever existed. Whatever Rourke is shaping out on the fringes started with samples and figures like these, and Vector will keep finding safe landing pads as long as the data backing their work remains buried in institutions that refuse to own their mistakes. Fractured Phalanx holding the doors suggests a small security favor grew into a permanent shadow contract, another oversight no one wanted to untangle. So far the trail runs from that isolated homestead, to the crooked beacon in high orbit, to the gutted courier and its doctored routes, then down into Neon's lower decks, each step pointing toward the same pattern of quiet approvals and redirected research.
zh: 这座塔，是理论悄悄变成硬件的地方，是某人的不记录在案实验溜过审查、而继续获得经费——因为关停它就意味着承认它存在过——的地方。鲁尔克在边境上正在塑形的东西，就是从这样的样本与数字开始的；而只要支撑他们工作的数据仍埋在拒绝认领自己错误的机构里，"向量"就会不断找到安全的落脚点。把守大门的破碎方阵说明，一次小小的安保人情长成了一份永久的影子合同，又一处没人愿意理清的疏忽。目前为止，线索从那座与世隔绝的农庄，到高轨道上歪斜的信标，到被掏空的信使船及其被做手脚的航线，再向下钻进霓虹城的下层甲板，每一步都指向同一种安静批准与改道研究的模式。

#en: This forgotten Colony War barracks is where her story always bends back a place built for breaking bodies and patching them just enough to send them out again. The rusted cots and dead med scanners are more than ruins to her; they are familiar instruments, now wired into a final lab where she can refine the same stimulants and counter-chems that slipped from field improvisations into black contracts and frontier dependence. Here, away from oversight, she can stabilize a last generation of formulas and sever any trail that points back to the veterans and settlers relying on her work. The courier stripped in deep space, the doctored manifests, the discreet interventions traced through orbital medicine all left faint patterns in routing codes and dosage signatures that narrow, step by step, to this one bunker where Catalyst has chosen to stand.
zh: 这座被遗忘的殖民地大战军营，是她的故事总是拐回的地方——一座为折断躯体、再把他们修补到刚好够用、又送出去而建的设施。那些锈蚀的床铺与死掉的医疗扫描仪对她而言不只是废墟；它们是熟悉的器械，如今接进了最后一座实验室——她可以在那里精炼那些从战地临时应变溜进黑合同与边境依赖的同款兴奋剂与对抗药剂。在这里，远离监督，她能稳定最后一代配方，并切断任何指回那些依赖她工作的老兵与定居者的痕迹。深空中被剥光的信使船、被做手脚的舱单、经由轨道医疗追溯到的谨慎干预，都在航线路由代码与剂量签名里留下了淡淡的模式，一步步收窄到这座掩体——"催化剂"选择站定的地方。

#en: The deserted UC listening post sits at the exact hinge of the traffic web Vector has been bending, an old ear left humming on the edge of nowhere while newer arrays took the spotlight. Its consoles still remember what passed through them, even after the crews rotated out and the inspections stopped paying attention; familiarity bred complacency, and in that blind spot he buried the patterns that point straight to him. Now a local gang has sprawled through the corridors, more interested in cover and contraband than in the half-wiped logs under their boots, giving his secrets a layer of noisy, human camouflage. All I know walking in is this: an orbital relay burned with falsified routes, dockside records showed matching edits in freight manifests, and the same signature rode both, hiding in the static while everyone called it a harmless glitch.
zh: 那座废弃的联殖听音哨，恰好坐落在"向量"一直在掰弯的交通网铰链上，一只被留在天涯之外嗡鸣的旧耳朵，而更新的阵列抢走了聚光灯。它的控制台仍记得穿过它们的东西，即便船员轮岗离开、检查也不再留意；熟悉养出了自满，而在那个盲点里，他埋下了直接指向自己的模式。如今一伙当地帮派在走廊里蔓延开来，比起他们靴子底下那些半擦除的日志，他们更在意掩护与违禁品——这给他的秘密盖上了一层喧闹的人形伪装。我入场时只确定这些：一座轨道中继被烧上了伪造航线，码头记录显示货运舱单里有相同的编辑，而同一道签名骑着两者，藏在静电里，而所有人都说它不过是无害的小故障。

#en:
You're going to find this eventually, so I'll be direct.

That facility doesn't belong to Caius Maren. It never did. The people you just killed built it. Worked it. Lived in it. Maren took it from them eighteen months ago with a fraudulent land registry filing and a well-placed bribe. They had no legal recourse. They were non-citizens.

So they took it back. And they killed the bastards that worked for him.

I don't expect you to care. The Vanguard serves citizens, and Maren is a citizen, and that's the end of the moral arithmetic as far as MAST is concerned. File your report. Collect your pay.

But you should know what you did today. And know there will be consequences.

Owen Carver
zh:
你迟早会看到这东西，所以我就直说了。

那座设施不属于凯乌斯·马伦。从来都不属于。你刚杀掉的那些人，是它的建造者，是它的工人，也曾住在里面。十八个月前，马伦靠一份造假的土地登记文件和一笔送到位的贿赂，把它从他们手里夺走了。他们没有任何法律途径申诉，因为他们不是公民。

所以他们把它夺了回来。还杀掉了替马伦卖命的那些混蛋。

我不指望你在意。先锋队只为公民服务，而马伦是公民——在三头同盟看来，道德上的算术到此为止。交你的报告，领你的报酬。

但你该知道自己今天做了什么。也该知道，这件事不会没有后果。

欧文·卡弗

#en: Whoever's running point on the Vanguard's Mars and Paradiso files has been filing accurate reports. Accurate reports get read. Accurate reports get cross-referenced. I have spent two years and a great deal of money ensuring certain things don't get cross-referenced. I don't know what this operative has seen, but I know they've been honest about what they've seen, and that is, at this point, a more dangerous quality in a person than competence. Sonder is not UC space. No one will ask questions about pirate casualties. Make sure there are some.\r\n\r\nC.M.
zh: 负责先锋队火星与天堂乐园档案的那个人，一直在提交准确无误的报告。准确的报告会被人读，会被交叉比对。我花了两年时间和一大笔钱，就是为了确保某些事情不会被交叉比对。我不知道这名特工看到了什么，但我知道他对自己所见的一切都如实相告——而到了这一步，这种品质比能力更危险。桑德不属于联殖空域。没人会追问海盗的伤亡。确保确实留下一些伤亡。\r\n\r\nC.M.

#en:
The Vanguard pilot they've been sending after my people has been manipulating the reports Tuala sees. I don't know if they're on Maren's payroll or just covering their own back, but the effect is the same. He stays protected. We stay manageable. Nothing ever reaches the question it should.

I wanted to believe someone in that uniform might actually be paying attention. That's on me.

Take them out. You'll get the usual fee.

O.C.
zh:
他们派来追查我手下人的那个先锋队飞行员，一直在操纵图阿拉看到的报告。我不知道他是拿了马伦的钱，还是只为保住自己，但结果是一样的。他始终受到庇护。我们始终处于可控范围。什么事都到不了它本该抵达的那个问题上。

我本愿意相信，穿那身制服的人里也许真有人在留心。这算我看走了眼。

干掉他。报酬照旧。

O.C.

#en:
Renna

Convoy's manifest confirms the target is aboard, with a rich family who'll pay rather than wait on a Vanguard rescue. Take them to the rendezvous, not Hangar Seven; Seven's been compromised since the Dustwell job. Demand goes out once you're secure, not before. You know what this money is for. The UC has spent decades deciding the Well doesn't count. We're just sending them the invoice. Look after your people. 

Owen
zh:
蕾娜

运输船的舱单确认目标就在船上，随行的还有一户有钱人家——他们宁愿掏钱，也不会等着先锋队来救人。把他们带去会合点，别去七号机库；自打尘井那票之后，七号机库就已经暴露了。等你站稳脚跟再发出赎金要求，不要提前。你知道这笔钱是用来干什么的。联殖花了几十年时间，认定深井区不算数。我们不过是把账单寄给他们而已。照顾好你的人。 

欧文

#en:
Vanguard

If you're reading this, you bested me. You've been honest. I don't know why. Maybe it costs you nothing. Maybe it costs you everything and you do it anyway. Doesn't matter. The Vanguard sent you here because Maren told them to. You've been doing his work this whole time, cleaning up what he made, making it look manageable, keeping the reports clean so MAST never has to ask the hard question. I built the Unwanted on people the UC decided didn't count. I am not a good man. I know what I ordered at Dustwell. I know what the Well raids became. I know what I am. But Maren is in orbit in the system right now, above the place where he had me kill people so he could file the paperwork cleanly afterward. He will land when you're done. He will survey his property. He will go home. If you have any of that honesty left, use it for something. He has an Ecliptic escort. Do whatever you want with that.

Owen Carver
zh:
先锋队

如果你读到了这东西，说明你赢了我。你一直很诚实。我不知道为什么。也许这对你毫无代价。也许这对你代价极大，可你还是这么做了。都不重要。先锋队派你来这里，是因为马伦让他们这么做。你从头到尾都在替他干活：收拾他造出来的烂摊子，让它看起来还在可控范围内，让报告干干净净，好让三头同盟永远不必问出那个难堪的问题。我用那些被联殖判定为不算数的人，建起了弃民。我不是好人。我知道自己在尘井下令做了什么。我知道深井区的突袭最后变成了什么。我知道自己是什么货色。但马伦此刻就在这个星系的轨道上，正悬在他让我杀人、好让他事后把文件写得漂漂亮亮的那片地方上空。等你办完事，他就会降落。他会巡视自己的产业。他会回家。如果你还剩一点那份诚实，就拿去做点有用的事。他有一支黄道佣兵团护卫。随你怎么处置。

欧文·卡弗

#en:
Vanguard

You've been filing thin reports. Keeping things vague. I don't know who you're protecting, Maren, yourself, the idea of a clean conscience, but you've been doing his work and calling it discretion. The Vanguard thinks you've been running down spacers. Maren thinks you're manageable. Maybe you are. I built something here. I know what it became. I'm not asking you to mourn it. But Maren is in orbit in the system right now, above the place where he had me kill people so he could file the paperwork cleanly afterward. He will land when you're done. He will survey his property. He will go home. If you have any of that honesty left, use it for something. He has an Ecliptic escort. Do whatever you want with that.

Owen Carver
zh:
先锋队

你的报告一直写得单薄，什么都含糊其辞。我不知道你在保护谁——马伦、你自己，还是“良心清白”这么个念头——但你一直在替他干活，还把这叫做谨慎。先锋队以为你一直在追剿太空劫匪。马伦觉得你很听话。也许你确实听话。我在这里建起过一些东西。我知道它变成了什么。我不是要你为它哀悼。但马伦此刻就在这个星系的轨道上，正悬在他让我杀人、好让他事后把文件写得漂漂亮亮的那片地方上空。等你办完事，他就会降落。他会巡视自己的产业。他会回家。如果你还剩一点那份诚实，就拿去做点有用的事。他有一支黄道佣兵团护卫。随你怎么处置。

欧文·卡弗

#en:
Dez

The package is secured, still alive. Sit on it until the demand goes out. If you move early and spook the buyers, I'll hear about it before you do. We're holding position near Lantana IV, far enough off the lane that the Vanguard won't stumble onto us by accident, close enough that I'm not losing a week getting back to the Well once this is done. 

Once the family has paid, route the credits through the same channels as Dustwell, split as agreed, your cut off the top, the rest comes to me. If anyone asks why a fence in Paradiso suddenly has a missing UC citizen to whisper about at a card table, you don't know anything. You're good at that part. Stay good at it. 

Renna
zh:
德兹

货已经到手，人还活着。在赎金要求发出去之前，先按兵不动。要是你动手太早、吓跑了买家，我会比你先听到风声。我们正停在马缨丹IV附近：离航线足够远，先锋队不会误打误撞撞上我们；也足够近，等这事办完，我不会在路上耗掉一星期才回到深井区。 

那家人付钱之后，走和尘井一样的渠道把款项转过来，按约定分账：你先扣下自己那一份，剩下的归我。要是有人问起，天堂乐园的一个销赃贩子怎么突然有了个失踪联殖公民的谈资、可以在牌桌上悄悄说——你什么都不知道。这方面你很在行。继续保持。 

蕾娜

#en: We held onto the Vanguard pilot instead of killing him. That was always the smarter play. A live Vanguard is worth more than a dead one, and whoever commands him will want him back in one piece. We're pulling off-world before the UC sends anyone else. He's aboard the ships in orbit of Rhea for now, alive and cooperative enough that we haven't had to remind him why that's the better option. Settle up with the miners on Luna, then get back here.\r\n\r\nBrak
zh: 我们没杀那个先锋队飞行员，把他留下了。这一直是更聪明的做法。活着的先锋队员比死掉的更值钱，而且他的上司肯定想让他完完整整地回去。我们会在联殖再派人来之前撤离这颗行星。目前他在土卫五轨道上的飞船里，活着，而且配合得不错，我们还没必要提醒他为什么这才是更好的选择。跟月球上的矿工把账结了，然后回到这里来。\r\n\r\n布拉克

#en: UC Navy Disciplinary Record, restricted, classification authority C. Maren: Subject O. Carver was ordered to engage civilian settlement designated "Halvorsen's Reach" under direct authorization, citing intelligence of spacer collaboration later confirmed fabricated by this office. Subject completed the engagement as ordered. Subject's subsequent testimony alleging this office issued an unlawful order is, on its face, accurate. Recommend discharge proceedings cite conduct unbecoming rather than the engagement itself. The engagement was authorized. The order was mine.
zh: 联殖海军纪律记录，机密，密级核准人 C. 马伦：受试者 O. 卡弗接到命令，在直接授权下攻击代号“哈尔沃森聚居地”的民用聚居点，所依据的情报称当地居民与太空劫匪勾结，该情报后经本办公室确认系伪造。受试者按命令完成了攻击。受试者随后作证称本办公室下达了非法命令——从表面上看，该证词属实。建议在除役程序中援引“行为不端”，而非攻击行动本身。该行动是经授权的。命令是我下的。

#en: Vanguard Contract\r\nAegis believe that a ship in the <Alias=TargetSystemLocation> system contains a slate they are interested in. Locate the <Alias=PrimaryRef>, retrieve the Slate, and return it to New Atlantis.
zh: 先锋队合同\r\n宙斯盾认为<Alias=TargetSystemLocation>星系中的一艘飞船载有他们感兴趣的数据板。找到<Alias=PrimaryRef>，取回数据板，并将其送回新亚特兰蒂斯城。

#en: Vanguard Contract\r\nA criminal responsible for attacking United Colony ships has been reported in the <Alias=TargetSystemLocation> system. Locate the <Alias=PrimaryRef> and kill them.
zh: 先锋队合同\r\n有报告称，一名袭击联合殖民地飞船的罪犯出现在<Alias=TargetSystemLocation>星系。找到<Alias=PrimaryRef>并将其击杀。

#en: Vanguard Contract\r\nAn Outpost belonging to a United Colony citizen has been overrun by a Terrormorph in the <Alias=TargetSystemLocation> system. Locate the <Alias=Boss> and kill it.
zh: 先锋队合同\r\n<Alias=TargetSystemLocation>星系中，一座属于联合殖民地公民的哨站被骇变兽侵占。找到<Alias=Boss>并将其击杀。

#en: Vanguard Contract\r\nAn cave near an interest belonging to a United Colony citizen has been overrun by a Terrormorph in the <Alias=TargetSystemLocation> system. Locate the <Alias=Boss> and kill it.
zh: 先锋队合同\r\n<Alias=TargetSystemLocation>星系中，一处属于联合殖民地公民的产业附近的洞穴被骇变兽侵占。找到<Alias=Boss>并将其击杀。

#en: Vanguard Contract\r\nAn Outpost belonging to a United Colony citizen is being threatened by a <Alias=Boss> in the <Alias=TargetSystemLocation> system. Locate the <Alias=Boss> and eliminate the threat.
zh: 先锋队合同\r\n<Alias=TargetSystemLocation>星系中，一座属于联合殖民地公民的哨站正受到<Alias=Boss>的威胁。找到<Alias=Boss>并消除威胁。

#en:
The Vanguard exists to protect the people of the United Colonies. That means more than just shooting pirates and filing incident reports; it means showing up for the communities we serve.
I'm authorizing a new initiative. I want Vanguard personnel spending time on the ground in our settlements, New Atlantis, Cydonia, Gagarin, and New Homestead. Talk to people. Find out what they need. Help them with it.
This isn't glamorous work. You might be fixing someone's water recycler or tracking down a missing shipment. That's fine. That's the point. Every citizen who sees a Vanguard pilot go out of their way for them is a citizen who trusts us more than they did yesterday. And right now, trust is a resource we can't afford to waste.
Don't rush it. Don't do it just to check a box. Do it like you mean it.
Commander Tuala
zh:
先锋队的职责就是保护联合殖民地的民众。这不只是击退海盗、填填事故报告，而是要在我们服务的社区里真实地出现。
我要批准一项新计划。我希望先锋队人员能抽出时间，踏上我们各个定居点的土地：新亚特兰蒂斯城、赛多尼亚、加加林星，还有新家园。去和人们交谈。弄清楚他们需要什么。帮他们解决。
这活不体面。你可能是在修某人的水循环器，也可能是在追查一批失踪的货物。没关系。这才是重点。每一个亲眼看到先锋队飞行员专程为他跑一趟的公民，都会比昨天更信任我们一点。而现在，信任是我们浪费不起的资源。
别赶时间。别只为了打勾交差。拿出真心去做。
图阿拉指挥官

#en: A gang of spacers calling themselves the Unwanted have seized a mining facility on Mars, called Dustwell Station. It is registered to a UC citizen, Caius Maren. Maren has filed a formal complaint with MAST and is expecting a swift resolution. Clear the facility, secure any assets on-site, and file your report through the board when done.\r\nMaren is a first-class citizen with administrative connections. Keep it clean and professional. This is a routine recovery operation.\r\nCommander Tuala
zh: 一伙自称“弃民”的太空劫匪占领了火星上一座名为尘井站的采矿设施。该设施登记在联殖公民凯乌斯·马伦名下。马伦已向三头同盟提出正式申诉，要求尽快解决。清空设施，扣押现场所有资产，事毕后通过任务板提交你的报告。\r\n马伦是一等公民，在行政系统里有关系。做事干净、专业。这是一次例行回收行动。\r\n图阿拉指挥官

#en: A UC convoy bound for New Atlantis was attacked three days ago in fringe space. The escort and crew were killed. A citizen was taken hostage, presumably for ransom. The Unwanted have a pattern of this now, and it's escalating. No demand has come through yet, which worries me more than if it had. \r\nAegis flagged a contact in Paradiso, a fence named Dez Okafor, who's reportedly been bragging about "knowing people" involved in the attack. Paradiso isn't UC territory, so we have no arrest authority there. Use your judgment. I just want that citizen back alive. \r\nCommander Tuala
zh: 三天前，一支前往新亚特兰蒂斯城的联殖运输船队在边境星域遭到袭击。护卫和船员全部遇害，一名公民被掳为人质，多半是为了索取赎金。弃民现在已是惯犯，而且正在升级。目前还没有人提出赎金要求——这比有人提出来更让我担心。 \r\n宙斯盾标记出天堂乐园的一个联系人：一个名叫德兹·奥卡福的销赃贩子，据说他一直在吹嘘自己“认识”参与这次袭击的人。天堂乐园不属于联殖领土，我们在那里没有逮捕权。你自己判断。我只要那名公民活着回来。 \r\n图阿拉指挥官

#en: A UC-registered freighter, the Tellurian Drift, was taken by Varuun Zealot raiders four days ago en route from Cydonia. The owner of record is Caius Maren, who has filed directly with MAST rather than waiting on standard salvage channels. He's specifically requesting the return of the cargo slates, which he describes as classified administrative records. I don't love that phrasing, but a citizen's property is a citizen's property. Locate the freighter, recover the cargo, and bring those slates back intact. \r\nCommander Tuala
zh: 四天前，一艘登记在联殖名下的货船“大地漂流号”在从赛多尼亚出发的途中被瓦鲁狂徒劫走。登记船主是凯乌斯·马伦，他没有走标准打捞渠道，而是直接向三头同盟提交了申请。他特别要求返还船上的货物数据板，并称那是机密的行政记录。我不太喜欢这个说法，但公民的财产就是公民的财产。找到那艘货船，取回货物，把那几块数据板完整地带回来。 \r\n图阿拉指挥官

#en: Aegis flagged a data broker on The Almagest moving a slate they are after. The Almagest isn't UC territory and it isn't friendly, it's a spacer waystation, full stop. Go in, get the slate, get out. This slate is dangerous in the wrong hands, so make sure you get it back quickly.\r\nCommander Tuala
zh: 宙斯盾盯上了至高上的一名数据掮客，他正在转移一块他们想要的数据板。至高不是联殖领土，也谈不上友好——那是一处太空劫匪中转站，就这么简单。进去，拿到数据板，出来。这块数据板落在不该拿的人手里会很危险，所以务必尽快取回。\r\n图阿拉指挥官

#en: A Vanguard pilot assigned to a protective detail at a mining settlement on Luna has missed two consecutive check-ins. Captain Jones. Good record, three years in, not the type to go quiet without reason. The settlement reported a Spacer presence moving in their direction four days ago. Jones was dispatched the same day. I haven't been able to raise him or the settlement since. Go and find out what's happening out there. If Jones is alive, bring him home. If he isn't, I want to know that too. \r\nCommander Tuala
zh: 一名被派往月球某采矿定居点执行护卫任务的先锋队飞行员连续两次没有按时报到。琼斯上尉。履历良好，服役三年，不是那种无缘无故失联的人。四天前，该定居点报告有太空劫匪朝他们方向移动。琼斯当天就被派了过去。自那之后，我既联系不上他，也联系不上那个定居点。去查清楚那边出了什么事。如果琼斯还活着，把他带回家。如果没有，我也要知道。 \r\n图阿拉指挥官

#en: Intelligence received through MAST confirms a significant Unwanted presence at an abandoned settlement called <Alias=TargetLocation>. This is the largest concentration of Unwanted leadership we've identified since this operation began. Maren flagged the location himself; he was apparently visiting the site. They spotted the encampment and pulled out before they were noticed. As much as I don't want to attack that settlement for Maren again, this situation needs to end. I want the Unwanted cleared. This ends here.\r\nCommander Tuala
zh: 通过三头同盟收到的情报证实，一处名为<Alias=TargetLocation>的废弃定居点内有大量弃民活动。这是我们开展这次行动以来发现的弃民高层最集中的一次集结。地点是马伦自己标记的；他显然去过那里。他们发现了营地，在被察觉之前撤了出来。尽管我极不愿意再为马伦去攻打那座定居点，但这件事必须了结。我要把弃民清干净。就到此为止。\r\n图阿拉指挥官

#en: Vanguard Contract\r\nA known pirate ship has been reported in the <Alias=TargetSystemLocation> system. Locate the <Alias=PrimaryRef> and destroy it.
zh: 先锋队合同\r\n有报告称，一艘已知的海盗飞船出现在<Alias=TargetSystemLocation>星系。找到<Alias=PrimaryRef>并将其摧毁。

#en: As you write the report on what happened at the Mining Colony, do you report what the slate told you?
zh: 在撰写关于采矿殖民地事件的报告时，你会交代数据板上写的内容吗？

#en: Only UC Vanguard Captains can access this Mission Board.
zh: 只有联殖先锋队队长才能访问此任务板。

#en: As you write the report on what happened on the Long Reckoning, do you report the motives of Renna?
zh: 在撰写关于长清算号事件的报告时，你会交代蕾娜的动机吗？

#en: As you write the report on what happened to the Tellurian Drift, do you mention what was in the report?
zh: 在撰写关于大地漂流号事件的报告时，你会提到那份报告的内容吗？
舰长日志：卡斯托·克拉兹

#en:
Despite persistent operational success, all recovered Mantis gear has been verified as 40+ years out of date. Armor plating, power cores, and weapon modules appear untouched by modern advancement. No known upgrades. No modularity. Possibly allergic to innovation.

Conclusion: The entity operating under the 'Mantis' designation is either obsessively committed to vintage hardware or intentionally sustaining technological inferiority as a tactical flex. We are being outmaneuvered by someone running pre-colony war firmware.

Recommendation: Do not underestimate obsolete systems deployed with absolute precision. Also, begin internal audit for unnecessary gear upgrades. Apparently, those aren't as essential as previously believed.
zh:
尽管其作战行动屡屡得手，所有回收到的祈祷者装备都已被证实落后了四十多年。装甲板、动力核心和武器模块都看不出受过现代技术进步的任何影响。没有已知的升级，没有模块化设计。简直像对创新过敏。

结论：以“祈祷者”之名活动的那个实体，要么对老古董硬件执念深重，要么就是刻意把技术上的落后当成一种战术姿态。我们现在是被一个还在跑殖民地大战前固件的家伙玩弄于股掌之间。

建议：绝不要低估以绝对精度部署的过时系统。另外，着手内部审查不必要的装备升级——显然，这些升级并没有我们过去以为的那么必要。

#en:
<header leftText=Scraphead 'PING' rightText='ZetaReticool'>
+174 Boosts | 51 Echos

Look, I don't know what to think anymore.

The Mantis - people say it's a man, a vengeful ghost, some kinda myth. But what if it's not? What if it's not human at all?

Think about it: no one's ever seen the Mantis kill. It never leaves a body. It doesn't take prisoners. It just... takes. Like we're specimens in some twisted collection.

Maybe it's not a guy in a stealth rig. Maybe it's something else - a ship, a crew, or maybe even alien.

I'm not saying I have proof, but the longer this goes on, the less it feels like a manhunt and more like a harvest.

What do you all think? Anyone else feel like the Mantis isn't what we're being told?

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='SnitchySnitcherson'>
-23 Boosts | 12 Echos

Zeta, you're skirting the edge of truth, brother.

I've been chasing shadows and picking up cosmic breadcrumbs - signals coded in a frequency only dead space and crazed spacers understand. This ain't human tech, it's some alien spookshow with probes that'd make a neural-net blush.

I'm cooked, wired, and ready to roll. Let's gang up, swap ghost stories, and maybe blow this collector's cache wide open.

If you want to survive, you better come hungry... or at least come with snacks.
zh:
<header leftText=Scraphead 'PING' rightText='ZetaReticool'>
+174 点赞 | 51 回响

听着，我已经不知道该信什么了。

祈祷者——有人说那是个男人，是个复仇的幽灵，是某种传说。可万一不是呢？万一它根本不是人类呢？

你想想：从来没人见过祈祷者下手。它从不留下尸体，也不留活口。它只是……拿走。就好像我们是某个变态收藏里的标本。

也许那不是一个穿着隐形装备的家伙。也许是别的东西——一艘船、一支船员，甚至可能是外星生物。

我不是说我有证据，但这事拖得越久，就越不像一场追捕，越像一次收割。

你们怎么看？还有谁觉得祈祷者根本不是我们被告知的那个样子？

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='SnitchySnitcherson'>
-23 点赞 | 12 回响

Zeta，你都快摸到真相的边了，兄弟。

我一直在追影子、捡宇宙里的面包屑——那些信号用的频段，只有死寂的空间和疯掉的太空劫匪才听得懂。这绝不是人类的技术，是某种外星鬼把戏，那探头能让神经网络都脸红。

我烧坏了、接上线、随时能出发。咱们结伙吧，交换点鬼故事，说不定还能把这收藏家的藏货一锅端了。

想活命，你最好带着饥饿来……或者至少带点零食。

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='Mant1sTruth'>
-2198 Boosts | 456 Echos

You can downboost me all you want, but I know what I saw!

That wasn't pirates. That wasn't the Fleet. 

It didn't announce, didn't ping, didn't flash so much as a light. Just dropped outta the black and cut through our skiff like it was Chunks - the Pie kind!

And you're all still sittin' here laughin' like I made it up?

I'm tellin' you: he's out there.

The Mantis is real. You don't believe me now, fine. Just hope when you see him, you don't get time to regret it.

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='Krazinator490'>
+1876 Boosts | 212 Echos

Seriously, Mant1sTruth, take that spooky campfire ping back to cs/MantisHuggers or wherever the rest of you tinfoil-heads are swapping ghost stories.

This channel's for scrappers, not chem-fried fanboys chasing void phantoms.

The Mantis ain't real. You just saw your reflection in a cracked viewport.
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='Mant1sTruth'>
-2198 点赞 | 456 回响

你们尽管踩我，但我清楚自己看到了什么！

那不是海盗。也不是深红舰队。

它没有通报，没有探询信号，连灯都没闪一下。就那么从黑暗里冒出来，把我们的穿梭艇切开，跟切块餐——派味那种——一样轻松！

你们还坐在这儿笑，当是我编的？

我告诉你们：它就在外面。

祈祷者是真的。你们现在不信，行。只希望等你们见到它的时候，还有时间后悔。

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='Krazinator490'>
+1876 点赞 | 212 回响

说真的，Mant1sTruth，把你那套营火鬼故事拿回 cs/MantisHuggers 去，随便你们这帮锡箔帽们在哪儿互相换鬼故事。

这个频道是给拾荒者的，不是给嗑药嗑傻了、追着虚空幽灵跑的脑残粉的。

祈祷者根本不存在。你只是从破裂的舷窗里看到了自己的倒影。

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='ThrusterSniffer'>
+8 Boosts | 1 Echo

She moved through the fire like it was part of her.
Flames curled off her armor and didn't dare land. 
Not a single spark touched her.

That wasn't a pirate.
Wasn't a bounty hunter. 
Wasn't human in any way I know.

I saw her in the flicker-smooth, silent, shaped like shadow given form.
Then she looked at me. Just for a second.
Eyes like the void between stars.

I couldn't speak. Couldn't run.
It felt like time bent around her. 
Like death was pausing to admire itself.

And I swear on every breath I've got left,
She was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen.

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='RealStarborn'>
+2 Boosts | 0 Echos

Sounds like you caught a glimpse of my wife.
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='ThrusterSniffer'>
+8 点赞 | 1 回响

她穿过火焰，仿佛那火焰本就是她身上的一部分。
火舌从她的装甲上卷开，不敢落下来。
没有一粒火星碰到过她。

那不是海盗。
不是赏金猎人。
以我所知，根本不算人。

我在那片摇曳的光里看见了她——平稳、无声，像是阴影被赋予了形体。
然后她看了我一眼。就一秒钟。
那双眼睛，像星星之间的虚空。

我说不出话。跑不动。
感觉时间都绕着她弯了。
像死亡正停下来欣赏自己。

我拿我剩余的每一次呼吸起誓，
她是我见过最美的东西。

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='RealStarborn'>
+2 点赞 | 0 回响

听起来你是瞄见我老婆了。

#en: Some Fleet dogs think the UC's behind the Mantis, cleaning up loose ends. I don't trust no one, but that theory's got teeth. Could be why no patrols ever cross paths with it.\r\n
zh: 舰队里有些狗东西觉得，祈祷者背后是联殖，在替他们收拾尾巴。我谁也不信，但这说法有点嚼头。也许这就是为什么从来没有巡逻队和它撞上过。\r\n

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='MOTHER$HIP69'>
+88 Boosts | 14 Echos

Alright, don't fry me for this-

But how the hell is Mantis gear that old and still running like it's fresh outta a Ryujin vault? I'm talkin' century-old stealth tech that still ghosts ships without leavin' a blip.

How is that even possible? 
Someone smarter than me explain how ancient tech still runs circles around every sensor in the Settled Systems.

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='RyujinReject07'>
-147 Boosts | 82 Echos

Y'all ever think the Mantis isn't using old tech... but that WE'RE using deliberately nerfed systems so the corps can track us easier?
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='MOTHER$HIP69'>
+88 点赞 | 14 回响

行吧，说这个别喷我——

可祈祷者的装备那么老旧，怎么还能跑得跟刚从龙神集团的保险库里拿出来一样？我说的是一百年前的隐形技术，到现在还能像鬼一样溜过飞船、一点信号都不留。

这怎么可能？
来个比我聪明的人解释一下，古代技术怎么还能把定居星系群里的每一台传感器耍得团团转。

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='RyujinReject07'>
-147 点赞 | 82 回响

你们有没有想过，不是祈祷者在用老技术……而是我们用的系统被人为削过，好让那些大公司更容易追踪我们？

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='ZetaReticool'>
+7 Boosts | 0 Echos

I felt his energy signature vanish. You understand?

Snitchy's gone. My best friend. My co-pilot. My truth anchor.

One second he's behind me, mid-rant about freeze-dried noodles, next second - airlock's open, and no Snitchy.

The Mantis? Please. That's just what they want you to think.

This was a hostile retrieval event. Classic xeno op. Smooth, surgical. Like he was plucked from reality.

They've been watching us. Harvesting our thoughts.

You all sit here boosting ghost stories while I'm out here losing my only tether to this dimension.

I filed a Nexus Tier-2 Abduction Notice. You should all be sleeping under copper mesh and thinking in scatter patterns.

They're real. They're here. And they took Snitchy.
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='ZetaReticool'>
+7 点赞 | 0 回响

我感觉到他的能量信号消失了。你们明白吗？

告密精不见了。我最好的朋友。我的副驾驶。我锚定真相的支点。

上一秒他还在我身后，抱怨着冻干面条，下一秒——气闸开着，告密精没了。

祈祷者？得了吧。那只是他们想让你信的。

这是一次敌对回收行动。典型的外星人作业。干净、精准。就像他被从现实中拔了出去。

他们一直在看着我们。收割我们的思想。

你们坐在这儿给鬼故事点赞，而我在外面丢掉了与这个维度的唯一系绳。

我提交了一份枢纽二级绑架通报。你们都该睡在铜网底下，用散射的思维模式思考。

他们是真的。他们就在这里。而且他们带走了告密精。

#en:
Last cycle, we lost Bosh and his crew. No wreckage. No SOS. They were just gone. 

Fleet whispers say the Mantis takes its prizes, but no one knows why. What happens to those crews? Some say they're sold off, others that the Mantis harvests data or worse. 

Whatever the truth, it's enough to keep us all looking over our shoulders.
zh:
上个周期，我们失去了博什和他的船员。没有残骸。没有求救信号。他们就这么没了。 

舰队里私下都在传，祈祷者会带走它的战利品，但没人知道为什么。那些船员后来怎么样了？有人说被卖掉了，有人说祈祷者在收割数据，或者更糟。 

不管真相是什么，光是这样就够让我们所有人时不时回头看了。

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='OverclockedGranny'>
+89 Boosts | 0 Echos

Same armor. Same ship. Same sad story every time.

I was runnin' scrap long before the Colony War lit half the Settled Systems on fire. Trust me - ain't nobody out here stayin' alive that long. Not without help from something unnatural.

Whatever that thing is, it ain't flesh. Never was.

You think it's some lone vigilante with a grudge? No, sugar. It's a rigged-up machine.

Stealth drive, untraceable heat sig, movement too smooth for anything born. That's old tech - maybe even pre-Exodus tech, buried deep and still runnin' its mission.

It ain't killin' for justice. It ain't even angry.

It's just followin' orders.

Problem is, whoever gave 'em is long gone. And the job still ain't finished.
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='OverclockedGranny'>
+89 点赞 | 0 回响

一样的装甲。一样的飞船。每次都是同样凄惨的故事。

早在殖民地大战把半个定居星系群点着之前，我就在跑废料了。信我——在这外面没人能活那么久。除非背后有某种不自然的东西撑着。

不管那东西是什么，它都不是血肉。从来都不是。

你以为那是某个心怀怨恨的独行义警？不，宝贝。那是一台拼装出来的机器。

隐形引擎、无法追踪的热信号、动作顺滑到不像任何有生命的东西。那是老技术——甚至可能是大撤离之前的技术，深埋在地下，至今还在执行它的任务。

它杀人不是为了正义。它连愤怒都没有。

它只是在服从命令。

问题在于，下达命令的人早就没了。而那份差事还没做完。

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='NullVibe404'>
+2893 Boosts | 231 Echos

You ever notice how the Mantis only shows up when it's real damn convenient? Whole crew gone, cargo vanished, no witnesses, no pings - just a spooky bedtime story floating in the wreckage.

And it's always Spacers! Never a UC science ship. Never a Vanguard patrol. Ain't that funny?

I'm telling you, the Mantis ain't real - it's a cover op. A spook story cooked up by UC black ops to clean house without raising alarms.

You see something you weren't supposed to? Boom - cue the ghost story, and the end of your life.

This ain't vengeance. It's narrative control. The UC's own urban legend - just believable enough to scare you, just absurd enough to laugh off if you ask questions.

Open your eyes! Monsters wear badges, too.
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='NullVibe404'>
+2893 点赞 | 231 回响

你们注意到没有，祈祷者只在特别方便的时候才出现？整船人没了，货物不见了，没有目击者，没有信号——只剩一堆漂在残骸里的恐怖睡前故事。

而且每次都是太空劫匪！从来不是联殖的科研船。从来不是先锋队的巡逻队。这不奇怪吗？

我告诉你们，祈祷者根本不存在——那是一次掩护行动。是联殖黑色行动编出来的一出鬼戏，好不惊动任何人就把场子清干净。

你看到了不该看的东西？嘭——鬼故事该上场了，你的命也到头了。

这不是复仇。这是叙事控制。联殖自己的都市传说——可信到能吓住你，荒谬到你要真去追问就会被当成笑话。

睁开眼吧！怪物也是会戴徽章的。

#en: Mantis ain't just a hunter - it's a ghost story told to keep us scared. Makes crews crack. Some say just hearing its name gets you killed quicker.\r\n
zh: 祈祷者不只是个猎人——它是一个讲出来吓唬我们的鬼故事。它能让船员崩溃。有人说，光是听到它的名字，你就会死得更快。\r\n

#en:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='ZetaReticool'>
+79 Boosts | 14 Echos

How many more, huh?

Snitchy, gone. Blorp, gone. Chunkle? Evaporated mid-laugh. Fizzbucket left nothing but his boots and a weird buzzing noise.

You know how many bunkmates I've had in the last cycle? Seven.
You know how many are still here? Just me.

Either I'm cursed, or I'm wearin' some kinda galactic abduction cologne. Eau de "Harvest Me Daddy."

I swear they're savin' me for last. Takin' the weirdest ones first, like they're curating a collection.

So come on, Mantis Alien freaks, you've got the set.

Take me already.

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='ChunksHunk54'>
+8 Boosts | 1 Echo

Alright, Zeta, gotta say - losing Snitchy, Blorp, Chunkle, and Fizzbucket like some kinda space soap?

Honestly, that's the funniest thing I've seen all cycle.

Don't know if I should feel bad for you or just get popcorn and watch what happens next.
zh:
<header leftText='Scraphead PING' rightText='ZetaReticool'>
+79 点赞 | 14 回响

还要少几个，嗯？

告密精，没了。布洛普，没了。查克尔？笑到一半就蒸发了。菲兹桶只留下一双靴子和一阵奇怪的嗡鸣。

你们知道上个周期我换过几个室友吗？七个。
知道还剩几个吗？就我一个。

要么是我中了诅咒，要么是我喷了某种银河绑匪专用香水。“快来收割我吧，爹地”那款。

我发誓他们把我留到最后。先抓最怪的那些，像是在精心挑选藏品。

所以来吧，祈祷者那些外星怪物，你们凑齐一套了。

把我带走吧。

<header leftText='Scraphead ECHO' rightText='ChunksHunk54'>
+8 点赞 | 1 回响

行吧，Zeta，我得说——先后没了告密精、布洛普、查克尔和菲兹桶，这事儿不就跟太空肥皂剧一样吗？

老实说，这是我整个周期里看到最好笑的事。

我都不知道该为你难过，还是直接拿点爆米花看看接下来发生什么。

#en: Enough with the damn rumors. The Mantis is not some ghost or legend - it's a threat, and treating it like a bedtime story gets crews killed. We don't have time for superstition when every job counts. If you hear whispers, shut them down fast. Fear is a weapon, and we're not handing it over for free.\r\n
zh: 这些该死的谣言到此为止。祈祷者不是什么幽灵或传说——它是威胁；把它当睡前故事讲，是会害死船员的。每一票活都算数的时候，我们没时间搞迷信。听到有人私下议论，立刻压下去。恐惧是武器，我们不会白白交出去。\r\n

#en: Fleet's split. Some swear it's a single man, others say a whole crew or AI. Me? Doesn't matter. Whatever it is, it's a hell of a lot smarter than any of us.\r\n
zh: 舰队里分成两派。有人一口咬定那是单独一个人，也有人说那是一整支船员，或者人工智能。我？无所谓。不管它是什么，它都比我们任何一个都聪明得多。\r\n

#en: Mantis hits fast and silent. No warning chatter, no red flags. One second we're hauling crates, next our hull's venting. They don't chase and they don't negotiate. Just vanish into the void before anyone can call backup.\r\n
zh: 祈祷者出手又快又无声。没有预警通讯，没有任何征兆。上一秒我们还在搬箱子，下一秒船体就在漏气。他们不追，也不谈条件。只等有人来得及呼叫支援之前，就已经消失在虚空里。\r\n

#en: Operatives refusing to speak the name. Calling it 'the shadow' now. Recommend full psychological review. Morale drop logged. Tactical cohesion at risk.\r\n
zh: 特工们拒绝说出那个名字。现在改叫它“影子”。建议进行全面心理评估。已记录士气下降。战术协同性存在风险。\r\n

#en:
Behavioral patterns attributed to the entity known as 'Mantis' span over a century. This exceeds the service lifespan of most operatives, most starships, and most office coffee dispensers. Consistency in method, gear, and tactical signature suggests deliberate preservation of style rather than innovation.

Hypothesis: 'Mantis' is not an individual, but a designation - a role passed down. Whether this involves formal succession, ritual, or just extremely convincing cosplay remains inconclusive.

Visual descriptions are unreliable. Survivors report conflicting profiles: male, female, human, non-human. One report described the Mantis as 'glowing', which was later attributed to hypoxia.

Biometric modeling returned 17 mismatched profiles and one blank silhouette marked 'ERROR: SUBJECT NOT FOUND.'

Conclusion: Further investigation into inheritance or replication protocols is warranted.
zh:
归于“祈祷者”这一实体的行为模式已跨越一个多世纪。这超出了大多数特工、大多数星舰，以及大多数办公室咖啡机的服役寿命。其手法、装备和战术特征始终如一，说明它是在刻意维持风格，而不是追求创新。

假设：“祈祷者”并非某个个体，而是一个代号——一个传承下来的角色。至于这背后是正式的继承、某种仪式，还是仅仅一场极具说服力的角色扮演，目前尚无定论。

外貌描述不可靠。幸存者给出的画像互相矛盾：男性、女性、人类、非人类。有一份报告称祈祷者“在发光”，后来被归因于缺氧。

生物特征建模返回了 17 份不匹配的档案，以及一个空白剪影，标记为“错误：未找到目标”。

结论：有必要对继承或复制机制展开进一步调查。

#en: Visual contact lost at 0242. Target engaged briefly - one operative down. No energy signatures recorded. Exit vector unknown. Recommend stealth sweep. Assessment: Probable Mantis encounter.\r\n
zh: 0242 时失去目视接触。目标短暂交火——一名特工阵亡。未记录到任何能量信号。撤离矢量未知。建议进行隐形搜索。评估：很可能是遭遇了祈祷者。\r\n

#en: Picked up the Calling All Spacers slate
zh: 已拾取“召集所有太空劫匪”数据板

#en: I found a Spacer transmission, it appears to be some kind of Call to Arms. I should listen to it.
zh: 我找到了一段太空劫匪的广播，似乎是某种召集令。我应该听一听。

#en: Listened to the Calling All Spacers slate
zh: 已收听“召集所有太空劫匪”数据板

#en: According to the "Calling All Spacers" transmission, the Spacers have found the lair of the Mantis. The transmission had the cordinates to the lair on a planet called Denebola I-B. It sounds like a raid is going down.
zh: 根据那段“召集所有太空劫匪”的广播，太空劫匪已经找到了祈祷者的巢穴。广播里有巢穴的坐标，在五帝座一I-B这颗星球上。听起来那边要开始一场突袭了。

#en: I landed on Denebola I-b and a Spacer warned me to leave the "Lair of the Mantis" before he attacked me. Mantis? Lair? There's a mystery here.
zh: 我在五帝座一I-b上着陆了。有一个太空劫匪警告我，让我立即离开“祈祷者的巢穴”，然后他对我发起了进攻。祈祷者？巢穴？这里藏着不可告人的秘密。
初始太空劫匪进入敌对
已收听多里安的第一条留言
已收听多里安的第二条留言
已听到利维的那番说辞

#en: I arrived at the heart of the Lair of the Mantis. No more traps. This was meant to be for the Mantis's son, Leon. Instead it's all mine.
zh: 我抵达了祈祷者巢穴的中心地带，这里没有陷阱。这里本是属于祈祷者后代利昂的土地，但现在这里是我的了。

#en: Grabbed Everything - Go to the Mantis's ship
zh: 已取得全部物品 - 前往祈祷者的飞船

#en: I've explored the Lair of the Mantis and found the Mantis's suit and ship. I pressed a button and raised the ship to the surface, so I should go check that out.
zh: 我去祈祷者的巢穴探查了一番，并发现了祈祷者的太空服和飞船。我按了一个按钮，把飞船升到地表上，所以我该去看看。

#en: (QC) Player arrived at the Mantis's ship
zh: （质检）玩家已抵达祈祷者的飞船

#en: I explored the Lair of the Mantis and have access to the Mantis's suit and ship. If I wanted I could be the next Mantis.
zh: 我去祈祷者的巢穴探查了一番，并且拿到了祈祷者的太空服和飞船。如果我愿意的话，我也可以成为下一个祈祷者。

#en: Listen to the Calling All Spacers slate
zh: 收听“召集所有太空劫匪”数据板

#en: Go to the Lair of the Mantis on Denebola I-b
zh: 前往五帝座一I-b的祈祷者巢穴

#en: Explore the Lair of the Mantis
(Optional) Learn more about the Lair of the Mantis
zh: （可选）了解更多有关祈祷者巢穴的信息

#en: The orbital vectors sketched across the stolen map match every storm-twisted farm, every anomalous reading along the Helium-3 line, then converge on one lonely band of rock and thin air.
zh: 失窃星图上勾勒的轨道向量，与每一座被风暴扭曲的农场、氦-3 航线沿线每一处异常读数一一吻合，最终汇聚到一条孤零零的岩石与稀薄大气带。

#en: When the hub ruptured, its last buffered frames unfroze into a single, clean spike on your console a narrow jump profile repeating the same heading you first saw whispered in that forgotten farm sky.
zh: 中枢爆裂时，它最后缓冲的几帧在你控制台上解冻成一道干净利落的尖峰——一段狭窄的跃迁剖面，重复着你最初在那片被遗忘农场天空下听到的同一航向。

#en: Cracked from the hangar's core, the buffer replays a single altered vector, looping toward a forgotten relay on the moon's dark side, hinting that the vanished freighters shared more than just bad luck.
zh: 从机库核心破解出的缓冲数据重放着一段被篡改的向量，循环指向月球暗面一座被遗忘的中继站，暗示那些消失的货船共有的不只是坏运气。

#en: A corrupt courier's notes, Neon backroom whispers, and a farmer's "stray shuttle" all spiral around the same call sign and jump corridor, finally sketching a path toward the next shadow he vanished into.
zh: 一名堕落信使的笔记、霓虹城密室里的低语，以及一个农场主口中的"迷航穿梭机"，全都围绕着同一个呼号与跃迁走廊盘旋，最终勾勒出一条通往他下一个消失阴影的路径。

#en: Hidden among nutrient flow schematics is a second pattern orbit tracks overlaid like crop rows, pointing away from the farmworld toward the same thin stretch of sky every other anomaly has quietly circled.
zh: 藏在营养液流示意图中的，是第二组轨道轨迹，像田垄一样层层叠压，背离农场世界，指向其他每一处异常都曾静静环绕的同一片狭长天空。

#en: The buried model shows a corridor sketched only in tiny corrections, a phantom lane implied rather than drawn, each adjustment attributed to a different analyst who swears they only copied someone else's work.
zh: 被掩埋的模型显示出一条只以细微修正勾勒的走廊——一条被暗示而非画出的幽灵航线，每一处调整都归到不同的分析员名下，而他们全都发誓自己只是照抄了别人的成果。

#en: Lines of altered jump data etched into the table match the drift patterns you saw in orbit and the near-miss reports whispered in Gagarin's bars.  \nTogether, they redraw the lanes toward a single, hidden node.
zh: 刻入表盘的篡改跃迁数据，与你在轨道上见到的漂移模式、加加林星酒吧里低语的惊险接近报告完全吻合。\n二者合力，重新勾勒出通往一个隐秘节点的航线。

#en: Decoded from the cargo ship's records, the faint signal in the rocks lines up with missing-lane reports and redacted crash files, pointing the hunt toward an unsanctioned corridor someone has been quietly shaping.
zh: 从货船记录中解码后，岩层里那道微弱信号与失踪航线报告、被涂黑的坠毁档案一一对应，把追查引向一条有人正在暗中塑造的未授权走廊。

#en: Hidden in the split archive, overlapping routes from Neon's whispers and SysDef's erased patrols resolve into one repeating void where traffic bends and records go blind, nudging the hunt toward that missing piece.
zh: 藏在被拆分的档案中，来自霓虹城低语与星防队被抹除巡逻的重叠路线，解析为一个反复出现的空洞——那里交通弯折、记录失明，推动追查走向那块缺失的拼图。

#en: Recovered traffic bursts show the pirate hauler adjusting its drift to match an erased beacon's rhythm, proving someone is feeding Crimson Fleet the same bent lanes whispered about in Neon and buried in SysDef logs.
zh: 恢复的通讯脉冲显示，那艘海盗运货船正调整漂移以契合一座被抹除信标的节奏，证明有人正把霓虹城低语、星防队日志里埋藏的同一条扭曲航线喂给深红舰队。

#en: Decoded coordinates bloom across the display, the same fractured signature stitched through clinic logs and stolen robotics code, now pointing to one forgotten system.  \nThe pattern is no longer rumor; it is a route.
zh: 解码坐标在显示屏上绽开，那同样的破碎特征贯穿诊所日志与被盗机器人代码，如今指向一个被遗忘的星系。\n这图案不再只是传言；它是一条路线。

#en: Decoded pulse timings from the marker sketch a forbidden curve through UC space, ending not at a port but at a forgotten Navy hull.  \nWhoever laid those vectors wanted the next questions asked in that derelict silence.
zh: 从标记中解码的脉冲时序，勾勒出一条穿越联殖空域的禁行曲线，终点不是港口，而是一具被遗忘的海军船体。\n布下这些向量的人，是想让接下来的问题在那片废弃的寂静中被提出。

#en: Cross-checking the ledger's ghost entries against the dead station's routing tables, one name repeats where every ship vanishes.  \nThe pattern points past corporate space, toward the forgotten moon where her relay went dark.
zh: 把账册中的幽灵条目与那座死寂空间站的航路表交叉比对，有一个名字反复出现在每艘船消失之处。\n这图案越过企业空域，指向她中继站失联的那颗被遗忘卫星。

#en: The forged entries split honest haulers from a single unlogged ship, all quietly diverted along the same off-chart corridor.  \nFollow that divergence, and the hunt veers toward the next hidden waypoint in his personal network.
zh: 伪造的条目把诚实的运货船与一艘从未登记的单船分离开来，它们全都悄然改道，驶入同一条图外走廊。\n顺着这处分歧追下去，追查便拐向他私人网络中下一个隐秘航点。

#en: In the Vanguard wreck's dim lab, a fragmentary log links those unstable samples to a quiet data handoff planetside.  \nThe name attached to the transfer points you back toward Neon, and someone willing to pay for impossible drift.
zh: 在先锋队残骸昏暗的实验室里，一份残缺日志把那些不稳定样本与地表一次无声的数据交接联系起来。\n交接记录上的名字把你引回霓虹城，以及一个愿意为不可能的重力漂移掏钱的人。

#en: Decoded in the relay's dim light, the Quiet Current Log traces forgiven debts and reversed charges along a single crooked trade lane, pointing past farms and fringe rocks toward one stubborn, hidden node still drinking from the grid.
zh: 在中继站昏暗的灯光下解码后，《静流日志》沿一条弯曲的贸易航线描出被免除的债务与反向的收费，越过农场与边缘岩带，指向一个仍在从电网取电的顽固隐秘节点。
