zh: 我一向信赖盖尔银行的航道。你飞着那个蓝色标志，就默认某个衬衫干净、薪水更高的人已经把算式核对过三遍。也许他们就是靠这个得手的。我们跑那条走廊跑得太勤，闭着眼都能画出浮标排布，连重力井让你牙齿发麻的那个小小顿挫都记得一清二楚。护航队没能按时报到时，没人惊慌；控制台只是耸耸肩，称之为中继站故障，又盖了一枚绿章。直到三支运输队失踪、一艘货船驱动外壳扭曲着跛行归来，才有人肯去调原始日志。就是在那里，我们看见例行更新之间夹着额外的投影，指向一条从未出现在任何官方星图上的细长岩冰带。

#en:
I keep replaying the approach in my head, but every time it runs a little different.  
The telemetry said clear lane, clean gravity, no debris worth naming, and still the hauler ahead of us drifted off-course like something was tugging at its teeth.  
We scooped three escape pods; the black took the rest.  
LIST stamped it down as pilot error, Argos called the basin a bad investment, and the official records all agree it was nobody's fault in particular.  
Only the stories in station bars refuse to line up, little fragments about the same burned pads, the same families, the same quiet pilot who swore the numbers were solid.  
Some days I think I imagined that extra ping on the scope; other days I am sure it was a hand on the wheel that never makes it into the logs.
zh:
我在脑子里一遍遍重放那次进近，可每次跑起来都略有不同。
遥测显示航道通畅、重力干净、没有值得命名的碎片，可我们前方那艘货船还是偏了航，像有什么在拽它的牙齿。
我们捞起三个逃生舱；其余的都被黑暗收走了。
独立盟把它归为驾驶员失误，阿戈斯称那片盆地是笔糟糕的投资，官方记录也一致认定这不特别怪谁。
只有空间站酒吧里的故事死活对不上：一些碎片般的说法，讲着同样的焦黑停机坪、同样的家庭、同样那个赌咒数据可靠、沉默寡言的飞行员。
有些日子我觉得雷达上那道多余的信号是我自己想象出来的；另一些日子我又确信，那是某只握在操纵杆上的手——而它永远不会出现在日志里。

#en: I log beacon checks at the start and end of every shift. Always have. Flip through the same diagnostics, tap the same acknowledgements, watch the same green lights blink in the same order. Somewhere in the last year, that order changed and I did not see it. A handoff here took a heartbeat longer, a timestamp there drifted by a fraction. The system compensated, captains cursed their nav suites, and traffic flowed on. Only now, looking back over old traces, do I see how the routes bent, almost politely, around the same handful of worlds. The frozen outpost that did not get its evac, the survey run nobody could re-plot, the approvals a LIST clerk swears they sent. The pattern was there the whole time, threaded through my consoles like a quiet apology I never bothered to read.
zh: 我在每个轮班的开始和结束都会记录信标检查。一向如此。翻过同样的诊断项，点下同样的确认，看着同样的绿灯以同样的顺序闪烁。可就在过去这一年里的某个时候，那个顺序变了，而我没看出来。这里一次交接多花了半拍心跳，那里一个时间戳漂移了一丝。系统自行补偿了，船长们咒骂着他们的导航套件，交通照常流动。直到现在，回头翻看旧的轨迹，我才看清那些航线是如何几乎彬彬有礼地绕开同样那几颗星球。那座没等到撤离的冰封哨站、那次谁都重绘不出的勘测航行、那份独立盟文员赌咒说已经发出的批文。图案一直都在，像一句安静的道白穿过我的控制台——而我从未费心去读。

#en: I am recording this from a rented bunk bolted to bulkhead C, because if I say it out loud in the bar again it will turn into another story and I need it to stay a fact.\n\nThe TA broker here swears the manifests he showed me are just misfiled freight, nothing to see, just frontier bookkeeping. But his hands shook when he scrolled past the third ship with the same registry, three different captains, three different lien codes. Same audit signature on each. He told me, real soft, that if I wanted the rest of that pattern I should go where the metal and the money meet: the yards in Gagarin, where freighters are reborn with new names and old debts. Everyone else talks about a ghost auditor like a campfire tale, changing details each time, but her accent and those codes never change.
zh: 我从一张用螺栓固定在 C 隔舱上的租用铺位上录下这段话，因为要是我再在酒吧里大声讲出来，它就会变成又一个故事，而我需要它保持为一个事实。\n\n这里的贸易管理局经纪商赌咒说他给我看的那些清单只是归错了档的货物，没什么可看的，不过是边地记账罢了。可当他滑过第三艘登记号相同的飞船时，他的手在抖——三个不同的船长，三个不同的扣押代码。每一份上都是同样的审计签名。他压低声音告诉我，要是我想看到那图案的其余部分，就该去金属与金钱交汇的地方：加加林的船坞，那里的货船会以新名字和旧债务重生。别的人都把那位幽灵审计员当成篝火边的故事来讲，每次细节都不同，可她的口音和那些代码从来不变。

#en: I have been sleeping next to the bunker wall, just to feel the hum through the metal. It is thin, a background tremor in the old UC wiring, but it matches the cadence I saw in the patrol logs I stole. Same gaps. Same timing. She is still riding the grid.\n\nNo one back at New Atlantis wanted to see it. They skimmed my report once, then started staring past my shoulder, like I was a static burst they could tune out. Out here, the bunker still listens to a sky the registry pretends is quiet, and tonight I caught something new: a tight-beam exchange, bouncing through an unlisted node, then vanishing toward that cluster of grav scars the Crimson crews call the blind corridor. Whatever she is doing next, she is staging it off a dead relay, just far enough outside the charts that no one has to admit it exists.
zh: 我近来一直睡在碉堡墙边，就为了透过金属感受那阵嗡鸣。它很细微，是联殖老线路里的一段背景震颤，可它与我偷来的巡逻日志里看到的节律吻合。同样的间隔。同样的时间。她还在骑着那张电网。\n\n新亚特兰蒂斯那边没人愿意承认它。他们只把我的报告扫了一眼，然后就盯着我肩膀后面的空气，仿佛我只是段能被调静音的静电爆音。而在这外面，碉堡仍在倾听着星图声称寂静的天空，今晚我逮到了新东西：一次窄束通讯，经一座未列名的节点弹跳，随后朝着深红舰队那帮人称作"盲廊"的那簇重力伤痕消失。无论她下一步要做什么，她都在借一座死中继站来布场——远在星图之外，远到没人非得承认它存在。

#en: I keep telling myself I am just here to clean up a mess in the logs, but the deeper I dig, the less it looks like random corruption. The theft chain they handed me was supposed to be simple follow the unauthorized copies, close the holes, file the report. Instead I am staring at the same warped jump curves cropping up in places that should never share traffic, tagged with user IDs that do not exist in any personnel registry I can see. One of the senior analysts flagged this pattern weeks ago, left a half-finished trace on their console, then took urgent leave and never came back to finish what they started. Tonight I pushed their old trace one step further and found a match buried in offsite telemetry from a navy hull that should be nowhere near these experiments, let alone echoing the same impossible vectors.
zh: 我不断告诉自己，我来这里只是清理日志里的一团乱麻，可我挖得越深，它就越不像随机的损坏。他们交给我的这条盗窃链本该很简单：顺着未授权的副本追下去，堵住漏洞，提交报告。可我却盯着同样扭曲的跃迁曲线在意想不到的地方冒出来——那些地方本不该共享任何交通——还带着我看遍所有人员登记册都查不到的用户 ID。有位资深分析师几周前就标记过这个图案，在控制台上留下一段没做完的追踪，随后请了紧急事假，再没回来把自己开头的活儿做完。今晚我把他那段旧追踪又往前推了一步，在来自一具海军船体的站外遥测里找到了一处匹配——那艘船本不该靠近这些实验，更别说回响出同样不可能的矢量。

#en: Been picking through this dead node so long I can taste oxidized metal in my teeth. Most of the consoles here are ghosts, but one of the cores still had heat left in it, tucked behind a wall panel someone thought was welded shut. Jump data, tightened and cleaned in a way no company mechanic around here could dream of, all bent around the same kink in the lanes we have been chasing. Whoever pulled that Fleet package knew exactly what they were stealing; half these coordinates match the accidents everybody swears were just bad luck. The funny part is, the route strings keep referencing a salvage yard on Deimos, like the path always folds back through there before it disappears. I have heard that place mentioned in bar talk for months, always as a joke, always with eyes dropping to the floor the second anyone asks for details.
zh: 我在这座死节点里翻拣得太久，牙缝里都尝得到氧化金属的味道。这里的控制台大多是鬼影，可其中一个核心还留着余温，藏在某块被人以为焊死了的墙板后面。跃迁数据被收紧、清洗过，手法是这一带任何公司技工都想象不出来的，全都绕着我们一直在追的那处航道扭结弯折。把那份舰队数据包拽出来的人，清楚自己在偷什么；这些坐标有一半对得上人人都赌咒说只是运气不好的那些事故。好笑的是，航路串一再提到火卫二上的一座打捞场，仿佛那条路径在消失前总要从那儿折返一次。这地方我在酒吧闲谈里听人提过好几个月了，每次都是当笑话讲，每次一有人问细节，所有人的眼睛就齐刷刷落到地上。

#en: They started changing the duty roster about a year back, but it did not feel like anything at the time. Different pilots pairing with different convoys, a few routes shuffled off the public boards, the usual corporate "optimization" spin. I remember one morning at the TerraBrew stall near Dock 17, seeing a Vanguard jacket at a table that never hosted uniforms before, talking low with a Ryujin type who smelled like fresh plastic and old secrets. Nobody cared. Ships came and went, GalBank still paid out, LIST settlers still limped through bad systems with just enough fuel and just enough luck. Only later, when the same name started whispering through Neon bars and insurance disputes, did it hit me that all those small adjustments were drawing lines around one pilot, setting her apart from the rest of us without ever saying why.
zh: 大约一年前，他们开始改动值班表，但那会儿谁也没觉得有什么。不同的飞行员配不同的运输队，几条航线从公示板上撤下，照例是那套企业式的"优化"说辞。我记得有天早上，在 17 号泊位附近的地球酿酒摊位上，看见一件先锋队夹克坐在从不接待制服客的桌旁，压低声音跟一个闻起来像新塑料与旧秘密的龙神家伙说话。没人在意。飞船来了又走，盖尔银行照常付款，独立盟的定居者仍靠着刚好够的燃料和刚好够的运气，一瘸一拐地穿过糟糕的星系。直到后来，同一个名字开始在霓虹城的酒吧和保险纠纷里低语，我才猛然意识到：所有那些小小的调整，都在围着一名飞行员画线，把她从我们其余人里单独圈出来，却从不说为什么。

#en: I keep telling myself I am only here because the pay is good, that I do not care why some Aegis ghost bled out on this rock with their datapad hugged to their chest. But I walked the perimeter twice before I even cracked the casing. No sign of a fight, no distress beacon in the logs, just a gap in the record where a human being should have left noise. That bothers me more than any scorch mark would have.  \n\nThe file fragments mention a safety inspector who stopped filing reports, a freighter that never finished its jump, and a research contract whose number does not exist in the public registries. Nothing links on paper. Names change, timestamps drift, routes get reclassified. Every time I think I see the chain of events, it smears sideways, like the universe is refusing to hold still long enough for anyone to write it down.
zh: 我不断告诉自己，我来这儿只是因为报酬不错，我根本不在乎某个神盾的鬼为什么胸口紧抱着数据板，流干了血死在这块岩石上。可在我撬开外壳之前，我先绕着外围走了两圈。没有任何打斗的痕迹，日志里也没有求救信标，只有记录中一段空白——一个活人本该在那里留下声响。这比任何焦痕都更让我不安。\n\n文件碎片里提到一名不再提交报告的安全检查员、一艘从未完成跃迁的货船，以及一份编号在公开登记册里查不到的研究合同。纸面上什么都串不起来。名字会变，时间戳会漂，航线会被重新归类。每次我以为自己看清了事件的链条，它就朝侧面糊开一片，仿佛宇宙不肯为任何人的记录静止得足够久。

#en: They say some places in space hold on to things longer than they should. The microgravity platform I swung past today is one of them. It should be scrap and silence, just another drilling rig left to spin itself apart, but the patrol grid still flinches every time its old transponder breathes. I parked just outside the lane and listened; there is a thin, dirty signal riding the standard telemetry, nudging any tagged-for-disposal hull a few degrees off its proper course. Every dock rat back on the station "knows" to give this sector a wide berth, then suddenly forgets why when you press them. Between the dead spacer's slate and that corrupted buoy I burned, both pointing at misrouted wrecks and retired codes that refuse to die, it feels like this whole patch of sky is hanging onto someone else's mistakes until they can be quietly erased.
zh: 都说太空里有些地方比它们该有的样子更念旧。我今天绕过去的那座微重力平台就是其中之一。它本该只剩废铁与寂静，不过又一座任其自行转散的钻井平台，可它的老应答器每喘一口气，巡逻网格就会缩一下。我停在航道外侧听着；有一道又细又脏的信号骑着标准遥测，把任何被打上"待处置"标签的船壳推开几度，偏离它们正确的航向。空间站上每个码头老鼠都"知道"该绕开这片区域，可你一追问，他们又突然忘了为什么。从那个死去太空人的数据板，到我烧掉的那只损坏浮标，两者都指向被错引的残骸和拒绝死去的退役代码——感觉这一整片天空都攥着别人的错误不放，直到它们能被悄悄抹去。

#en: I am parked off this ore platform, watching it turn like it has for decades, still humming through a pattern nobody bothered to erase. Somewhere along the way, some clerk signed the wrong form or looked the other way, and that tiny shrug of bureaucracy carved out a blind lane in the sky. Now the platform's guidance is stitched into bar gossip and half-lost sensor logs, echoes of the same freighter silhouette skimming grids where no one should be. I keep thinking about that first dead homestead, the dirty telemetry from its orbit, the way local fauna started acting like they got new orders. None of it screamed conspiracy at the time. Just glitches. Just bad luck. But all those small, quiet mistakes and compromises nudged things toward this forgotten dot on the map, until everything strange seems to lean, just a little, in this direction.
zh: 我停在这座矿石平台外侧，看着它像几十年来那样旋转，仍在嗡嗡作响地走着一套没人费心去抹除的图案。一路上，某个文员签错了表格，或是别过头去，而官僚系统那一下微不足道的耸肩，就在天上凿出了一条盲航道。如今这平台的导航已缝进了酒吧闲谈和半遗失的传感器日志里，回响着同一个货船轮廓掠过本不该有人的网格。我总想起第一座死去的农庄、它轨道上传来的肮脏遥测，还有当地动物开始像接到新命令一样行事。当时这些都没什么阴谋的味道。只是故障。只是运气不好。可所有那些小小的、安静的失误与妥协，把一切都往地图上这个被遗忘的点推去，直到所有古怪的事似乎都稍稍朝这个方向倾斜。

#en: Hard to tell where the real story starts, so I will pin it to that rusted relay I was paid to wake up last month. The work order called it routine: clear a backlog, reset a few buffers, bill some faceless office in New Atlantis. When I got there, half the panels were already scorched, and the logs did not read like simple neglect. Distress calls came in clean, went out smeared, registry tags folded over themselves. Some entries had been sliced and pasted so many times the timestamps looped. A tug crew swears they saw a hijacked signal bouncing through there weeks before; a dockhand insists those same ship IDs showed up later on a private auction list. None of their stories match perfectly, but every broken piece points at the same thing: someone very patient, nudging ghosts through forgotten circuits until the records forgot they were ever alive.
zh: 很难说真正的故事从哪里开始，那就把它钉在上个月有人付钱让我去唤醒的那座锈蚀中继站上吧。工单上说是例行公事：清理积压、重置几个缓冲区、向新亚特兰蒂斯某个不露面的办公室开账单。等我到那里时，一半的面板已经烧焦，日志读起来也不像单纯的疏于维护。求救呼叫进来时清晰，出去时却糊成一片，登记标签自我折叠。有些条目被剪切粘贴了太多次，时间戳都成了死循环。一支拖船船员赌咒说，几周前他们见过被劫持的信号在那里弹来弹去；一名码头工则坚称，同样的船号后来出现在一份私人拍卖清单上。他们的说法没有一条完全吻合，可每一块碎片都指向同一件事：某个极有耐心的人，把幽灵们从被遗忘的电路里拨弄过去，直到记录忘了它们曾经活过。

#en:
Been running cargo runs since before the Armistice, and I have never seen a ship fly itself like the Boneclaw did last week.

We were three days out, grav drive on cooldown, when the nav console lit up with a route I did not punch in.

Looked official, too, buried under old UC formatting nobody bothers with anymore.

Captain swore it was a relic subroutine, some legacy safety corridor from back when the war made everyone jumpy.

Crew laughed it off, let the autopilot ride it, because who argues with a path that clean.

Thing is, the more I dug into the logs after shift, the more I found those same corrections, repeating like a heartbeat, on runs years apart.

Different captains, different cargo, same quiet nudge.

Somewhere out there, something we forgot to shut down is still talking to our ships, and I do not think it is doing us any favors.
zh:
停战之前我就在跑货了，可我从没见过哪艘船像上周的骨爪那样自己飞。

我们已经出航三天，重力驱动在冷却，这时导航控制台亮起一条我没输入过的航线。

看起来还挺正式，埋在如今谁都不屑一用的联殖旧格式下面。

船长赌咒说那是个遗留子程序，战时人人都神经紧绷的年代留下的某种安全走廊。

船员们一笑而过，让自动驾驶顺着它跑，谁会跟一条那么干净的路径较劲呢。

问题是，交班后我越翻日志，就越发现那些相同的修正，像心跳一样重复着，出现在相隔数年的航次里。

不同的船长，不同的货物，同样安静的轻推。

在外面的某处，某个我们忘了关掉的东西仍在跟我们的飞船说话，而我不觉得它是在帮我们的忙。

#en: I was supposed to be on a six-month temp contract up here, the kind of nowhere posting you take when you want to disappear without quitting. The module hums and breathes like any other relic on the corporate leash, but the logs feel wrong under my hands. Years of clean mirrored transfers, then suddenly one chain fractures: inbound packets split, some land where they are supposed to, others slip sideways into dead space. The anomalies are tiny, like someone with surgeon hands nudged the code, trusting the redundancy to hide the cut. I flagged it in the maintenance queue, marked for a senior tech to review, and then nothing happened. No follow-up, no purge, just my ticket quietly closed without comment. The gaps stayed in the archive, hanging there like half-erased handwriting, as if whoever was meant to come back and tidy the mess simply never made it this far.
zh: 我本来到这里只是签一份六个月的临时合同，就是那种你在想不辞职就消失时会接的、鸟不拉屎的差事。这个模块像企业牵引绳上任何一件遗物那样嗡鸣、呼吸，可日志在我手底下感觉不对劲。多年的干净镜像传输，然后某一天，一条链突然断裂：入站数据包被劈开，有些落在该落的地方，另一些则侧滑进死寂空间。那些异常极其细微，像有人用外科医生的手拨了拨代码，赌定冗余机制会把切痕藏住。我在维护队列里标记了它，注明要交给资深技师复核，然后什么都没有发生。没有跟进，没有清除，我的工单只是悄无声息地无评语结案。那些缺口留在档案里，像写了一半又被擦掉的字迹悬在那儿，仿佛那个本该回来收拾残局的人，根本没走到这一步。

#en: I was a kid when the first version of the story did the rounds, so I only have thirds and fourths by now. The ones who were there do not agree on much anymore. Some swear the sky over the fields tore open, others say it was just a freighter that came in too hot and shook itself apart. The only constant is that the official report never lined up with what people remember, and every retelling drops another hard detail and picks up another maybe. By the time I was old enough to fly, it was just a warning: do not trust the lanes just because they are lit.\n\nNow there is a new name attached to the old unease, a navigator who walked out on the big flags, a whisper about trials buried in some staryard server. Funny thing is, no one here can tell you exactly when he appeared in the tale; it is like he was always part of it, waiting in the gaps where the truth got rubbed smooth.
zh: 这故事最早流传的时候我还是个孩子，所以如今到我这儿，剩下的已经只是第三手、第四手了。当年在场的人如今也没多少说法能对得上。有人赌咒说田野上方的天空裂开了，另一些人说那不过是一艘进得太急、把自己震散的货船。唯一不变的是：官方报告从来和人们记得的对不上，而每一次转述都会丢掉一个硬邦邦的细节，又添上一个"也许"。等我大到能飞的时候，它已经只剩一句警告：不要因为航道亮着就相信它们。\n\n如今，那份旧日的不安又挂上了一个新名字——一名撇下那些大旗出走的领航员，一句关于埋在某个造船厂服务器里的试验的低语。好笑的是，这里没人说得清他究竟是什么时候进了这个故事；就像他一直在其中，守在真相被磨平的那些缺口里。

#en:
I keep thinking someone is coming back.

The garage is loud enough that no one hears the hum from the old core, not really. Fans rattling, music leaking from a busted speaker, arguments over parts prices. But every time I walk past that one bay, the air feels thinner. Bench wiped spotless in a sea of grime, wrappers folded into a neat little pile, like somebody packed up in a hurry and promised themselves they would finish the job later.

The kid they pulled off the floor swears he blacked out, woke up with his arm set better than UC ever did it. Others say he tripped, patched himself, end of story. Except the med stock sheet does not match, and the Static Hackers keep glancing at that core like it is rigged to bite. If there is a ghost in those logs, it is waiting on the same thing I am: the one who cut here, cleaned here, and walked away before the erase cycle finished.
zh:
我总觉得有人会回来。

车库太吵，没人听得见那台旧核心的嗡鸣，其实根本听不见。风扇嘎吱作响，破喇叭里漏出音乐，还有人为零件价格争吵。可我每次走过那个隔间，空气都显得更稀薄。工作台在一片油污中被擦得一尘不染，包装纸被叠成整整齐齐的一小摞，像是有人匆匆收拾了行装，并向自己保证改天再来收尾。

他们从地上抬走的那个小子赌咒说自己昏了过去，醒来时胳膊被接得比联殖哪次都接得好。别的人说他是自己摔了，自己包扎了，故事到此为止。只是药品库存表对不上，而那帮静电黑客老是瞟着那台核心，像它随时会咬人。如果那些日志里真有个鬼，那它等的和我等的是同一样东西：那个在这里切割、在这里清理、并在擦除周期跑完之前就走掉的人。

#en: Found the packet in the last place anyone checks the old relay's maintenance queue. No alarms, no lockouts, just a half finished transfer flagged "deferred" three years running, sitting in a forgotten subdirectory like somebody fully intended to come back and scrub it clean, then got reassigned or spaced. Atmospheric sweeps layered over patrol routes, with one ship path threaded right through the gaps every time. Same vector, same speed, same little pauses in burn where a careful pilot checks their own work. I pulled the trace forward one more hop and the endpoints start clustering around a junk field that is not on any public navchart, but shows up in system grav noise like a bad memory. First it was that stray record out on the rock, then the cut patterns in the Deimos yard, now this: all of it saying the same thing he has a favorite graveyard, and he keeps going back to it.
zh: 我是在大家最不会去查的地方找到那个数据包的——老中继站的维护队列里。没有警报，没有锁定，只有一次三年来一直被标为"延迟"的半成品传输，躺在一个被遗忘的子目录里，像是某人完全打算回来把它清干净，结果却被调走了，或者被丢进了太空。大气扫描图层叠在巡逻航线上，每次都有一条飞船路径从缝隙中笔直穿过。同样的矢量，同样的速度，同样在点火中那些小小的停顿——那是一个谨慎的飞行员在核对自己的活儿。我把追踪又往前推进了一跳，端点开始聚拢在一片垃圾场上，那地方不在任何公开导航图上，却像一段糟糕的记忆一样出现在星系重力噪声里。先是岩石上那条游离的记录，然后是火卫二船坞里的切割图案，现在又加上这个：全都在说同一件事——他有一处偏爱的墓地，而且他总在回去。

#en: I am logging this from the old drop can, sitting under a flickering strip that should have burned out a decade ago. The place hums with half-dead fans and forgotten protocols; I swear I heard a decon cycle spin up on its own two hours after I powered the generator, like some buried routine still thinks infantry are due in from orbit. That is what got me looking deeper. Under the rust and bootleg wiring, the shelter's systems were still filing traffic, still mirroring route updates to a secondary endpoint nobody bothered to wipe from the registry. Buried in a nav cache I pulled off the liaison's terminal was a repeating destination tag hardwired into his latest corridor updates, same code cross-referenced three times in the old system handshakes. All point toward a relay node tucked in the undergrid of Neon, exactly where no honest captain wants their beacon to light up: Ebbside.
zh: 我在从旧空投舱里记录这段话，头顶是一条十年前就该烧断的闪烁灯带。这地方在半死的风扇和被遗忘的协议间嗡鸣；我发誓在我给发电机供电两小时后，听到了一个净化循环自己转了起来，像某个被埋起来的程序还以为步兵要从轨道上降落。就是那东西让我往深处查了下去。在锈迹与私接线路之下，这座掩体的系统仍在归档交通，仍把航线更新镜像到某个没人费心从登记表里抹去的次级端点。在我从联络员终端上提取的导航缓存里，埋着一个反复出现的目的地标签，硬写进了他最新那批走廊更新中，同一个代码在旧系统握手记录里被交叉引用了三次。全都指向嵌入霓虹城下层电网的一座中继节点——正是任何正派船长都不愿让自己信标亮起的地方：埃布赛德。

#en: First time I docked here, I thought it was just another junkyard orbiting the edge of nowhere. Now I cannot shake the feeling that this depot is where the story started, even if nobody remembers the first telling. Every Deadspace loader I talk to starts their version with, "I heard from a guy who heard it from a crew that is gone now," and the details never match, just the punchline: ships that jump out fat and healthy, never ping another beacon, and leave behind drive logs that look like they were written by the same careful hand. The corrupted files I pulled at that remote rock and the whispers from the broken yard point back here, but whatever really happened the first time someone "tested to failure" in this place has already been chewed into rumor. All that is left is the pattern, and the quiet way these people lower their voices when they think the depot itself might be listening.
zh: 我第一次在这里停靠时，以为它不过是又一座绕着天涯边缘转的废品站。如今我却甩不掉一个念头：这个补给站就是故事开始的地方，哪怕没人记得最早的讲述。我聊过的每一个死寂空间装卸工，开场白都是"我听一个哥们说的，那哥们又是听一支如今没了的船队说的"，细节从来对不上，只有那句包袱一样：飞船满载健康地跃出去，从此再没打过一次信标，留下的驱动日志像是同一只谨慎的手写出来的。我在那块偏远岩石上提取的损坏文件、还有那座破船坞里传出的低语，都指回这里；可当年第一次有人在这地方"测到失效"时究竟发生了什么，早已被嚼成了传闻。剩下的只有那图案，以及这些人一觉得补给站本身可能在听时，就压低声音的安静模样。

#en: I am not saying I know where she is, just that the pattern is wrong. I have been stuck on this rusting module for three tours watching traffic for Ryujin, and data does not just decide to jump manifests on its own. The archive pulls show a neat little chain of thefts, then one transfer hits this node and comes out sliced, like someone reached in with a scalpel and rerouted only the parts they cared about. One of the techs swears he saw an old bionics prefix in the checksum, the kind tied to that shuttered lab they swore was scrubbed years ago. Another tech says that prefix is a ghost tag, leftover junk, that we are all seeing shadows because of the stories about a red-haired doc and melted implants. All I know is: every time code goes missing around her name, it leaves the same faint trace, and this time the trace points straight at that dead bionics facility everyone pretends not to remember.
zh: 我不是说我知道她在哪儿，我只是说这个图案不对劲。我为龙神盯着交通数据，被困在这个锈迹斑斑的模块上已经三个任期了，而数据不会自己决定在清单间跳来跳去。档案调取记录显示一串整整齐齐的小盗窃，随后有一次传输打在这个节点上，出来时却被切开了，像有人拿着手术刀伸进来，只改道了他们关心的那部分。有个技工赌咒说，他在校验和里看到过一个旧的仿生学前缀，正是他们赌咒说几年前就已经清洗掉的那座关闭实验室用的那种。另一个技工说那前缀是个幽灵标签、是遗留垃圾，说我们全是因为那些关于红发医生与熔化植入物的故事在看见影子。我只知道：每当代码在跟她名字有关的地方失踪，留下的都是同样微弱的痕迹——而这一次，痕迹直指那座人人都假装不记得的废弃仿生学设施。

#en: I have been sitting in this cramped berth on The Den long enough to know why nobody volunteers for this posting. Everything is beige and half-asleep, the kind of place where reports get filed, stamped, and then quietly forgotten. Which is exactly why whoever hid those numbers chose it. If you want something buried, you do not drop it in a warzone; you tuck it under a bored clerk in a dead system and let routine smother it.\n\nThe stories I picked up on the way here all sound like they have been passed around too many tables. A hauler that was there, then was not. A rigger who saves people in one version and strands them in another. Every time someone tells it, the edges get rounded off, the guilt spread thinner. But underneath the smoke and barroom bravado, the same outline keeps showing through. Missing crews, altered manifests, and a line of drift that curves back toward the same invisible hand.
zh: 我在巢穴站的这间逼仄铺位上坐得太久，久到我知道为什么没人自愿接这个岗位。一切都是米黄色的、半睡不醒的，那种报告被归档、盖章、然后悄悄遗忘的地方。而这正是藏起那些数字的人选中它的原因。你要是想把什么埋掉，就别把它丢进战区；把它塞给一个死气沉沉星系里百无聊赖的文员，让例行公事把它闷死。\n\n我一路听来的那些故事，听起来都像被太多张桌子传来传去过。一艘本来在那里的货船，然后不在了。一名装配工，在一个版本里救人，在另一个版本里把人扔下不管。每被讲一次，棱角就被磨圆一点，罪责就摊得更薄。可在那层烟幕和酒馆式的逞强底下，同一个轮廓始终透出来。失踪的船员、被改动的清单，以及一条总朝同一只看不见的手弯回去的漂移线。

#en: I was supposed to be gone before the storm rolled in. Just a simple refill, a few signatures, then back to hauling grain where the worst thing that happens is a clogged pump. Instead I am sitting in the office watching the wind shove dust against the viewport while the consoles spit out half-finished reports and error flags that no one ever cleared. Someone rushed through this place in a hurry, cut corners in the logs, pushed a few ships through on backdoor clearances, then ran before the numbers could catch up. The ledgers are messy in a very precise way, like a hand that knows exactly which fields matter and which can be left wrong for years without anyone noticing. I am no investigator, but even I can see the pattern of diverted routes and vanished transponders threaded through this depot, and it has me checking over my shoulder every time the comms crackle with another "routine" traffic update.
zh: 我本该在风暴卷来之前就走的。不过是简单补个燃料、签几个名，然后回去运粮食——那份活儿里最糟的情况也就是泵堵了。可现在我却坐在办公室里，看着风把沙尘推上观察窗，控制台吐出一份份没写完的报告和从未有人清除过的错误标记。有人匆匆忙忙地从这地方过了一遍，在日志里抄了近路，用后门许可放行了几艘船，然后在数字追上来之前就跑了。那些账簿乱得很精准，像一只清楚知道哪些字段要紧、哪些可以错着好几年而无人察觉的手。我不是什么调查员，可连我都看得出这片补给站里穿插着被改道航线和消失应答器的图案，每次通讯里噼啪传来又一则"例行"交通更新，我都会忍不住回头看一眼。

#en: I am still shaking dust out of my hair from this bunker, and the consoles are older than half the patrol grid, but they still know how to keep a secret. The deserter was sloppy with his deletions; he scrubbed the export paths, not the cached scans. Buried under old meteor tracks and shuttle noise, I found a sequence of atmospheric spikes that do not belong to any registered thruster profile, cutting straight across restricted lanes like they owned the sky. Cross-checking the timestamps against patrol rosters gives me a heading and a hull class, and every line points toward a Navy combat ship that was never supposed to be on that circuit at all. Some of the techs back in the dive swear they saw it slip past on a dead transponder; others say it is all barroom exaggeration. Either way, the next piece of this mess is sitting in a silent UC hulk, waiting for someone brave or desperate enough to board it.
zh: 我头发里还抖得出这座碉堡里的灰，这里的控制台比半个巡逻网格都要老，可它们仍然懂得怎么保守秘密。那名逃兵删东西时很马虎；他擦掉了导出路径，却没擦掉缓存的扫描。在旧流星轨迹和穿梭机噪声底下，我找到了一连串大气尖峰，不属于任何登记过的推进器剖面，笔直横切受限航道，仿佛这片天空是它们家的。把时间戳与巡逻名册交叉比对，我得到了一个航向和一个船体级别，每一条线都指向一艘本不该出现在那条航线上的海军战斗舰。潜水区那边的几个技工赌咒说，他们见过它开着死应答器悄悄溜过；另一些人说那全是酒馆里的夸大其词。无论怎样，这摊烂摊子的下一块拼图正躺在一具沉默的联殖船壳里，等着哪个够勇敢或够绝望的人登上去。

#en: This module has a way of hanging onto things it is not supposed to. Old firmware, obsolete protocols, ghost accounts from contractors nobody remembers hiring it is all still here, just pushed one layer deeper every time someone does a "cleanup." I came in thinking I was tracing a straightforward breach, another bored tech moving proprietary routes offsite for a quiet sale. But the deeper I dug, the more I kept finding the same bent curves pressed into different logs, like a bootprint stamped over and over in fresh dust. Someone upstream noticed, tried to wipe it, then stopped halfway through, like they got called away or decided they did not want their name tied to this anymore. This place remembers them anyway. Even with lazy edits and truncated records, the system still clings to their mistakes and to the shape of those impossible paths, faint and overlapping where no sane corridor should ever cross.
zh: 这个模块有一种本事，能留住它本不该留住的东西。旧固件、作废的协议、来自没人记得雇过的承包商的幽灵账户——全都还在，只是每次有人做一次"清理"，就被往下推深一层。我来的时候以为自己只是在追查一次简单的入侵，又一个百无聊赖的技工把专有航线挪到站外去悄悄变卖。可我挖得越深，越是在不同的日志里一遍遍撞见同样那些弯曲的弧线，像一枚靴印被反复盖在新落的灰尘上。上游有人察觉了，想把它擦掉，却在半途停下，像被叫走了，或者打定主意不想再让自己的名字跟这事绑在一起。可这地方照样记着他们。哪怕有偷懒的删改和被截断的记录，系统仍死死攥着他们的错误，攥着那些不可能路径的形状——淡淡的、相互交叠，没有任何理智的走廊会从那里穿过。

#en: I keep telling myself I only take the night shifts in the back corridors because the pay is better, but it is really because no one looks too hard back here. You sign off a crate as medical relief, watch it roll past the scanners, and by the time it hits storage someone has scraped the tags and called it scrap. Lately, though, the routes stamped on the cargo slates do not match the traffic boards upstairs, little course corrections that nudge whole loads away from the usual lanes. Some of the other handlers swear they saw a woman in a battered flight jacket, just standing at the junctions, fingertip tracing invisible paths on the bulkhead, but when I ask for details they laugh it off like bar talk. Maybe it is all exaggeration, but the manifests keep changing after she is supposed to have passed through, and the colony destinations on those shipments have a way of disappearing from the system altogether.
zh: 我一直告诉自己，我只挑后走廊的夜班是因为钱多，其实真正的原因是这里没人会细看。你把一只板条箱签成医疗救济品，看着它滚过扫描仪，等它进到仓库时，已经有人刮掉了标签、管它叫废料。可最近，货板上盖印的航线跟楼上的交通公示板对不上，一些小小的航向修正把整批货从惯常航道推偏。别的几个装卸工赌咒说，他们见过一个穿破旧飞行夹克的女人，就站在岔口那儿，指尖在舱壁上描着看不见的路径；可我一追问细节，他们就当酒吧闲话一笑而过。也许那全是夸大的说法，可每次她该经过之后，清单都会变，而那些货运单上的殖民目的地，总有办法从系统里整个消失。

#en: I spent half the cycle today under New Atlantis instead of in it, sitting in a humming archive room that smells like old ozone and cheaper coffee than they serve upstairs. One junior admin owed someone a favor and let me mirror a set of deprecated traffic models he swore nobody used anymore. The projections looked clean at first, then I started overlaying real freight logs. Tiny manual corrections, always in the same direction, always just enough to miss something the official charts do not admit is there. When I asked who signed off on those edits, every analyst I cornered said the same thing they had only seen the pattern after someone else ran it, and nobody was willing to say whose name was on the original run. There were other gaps too, places in their stories where words should have been and were not, like they had all agreed ahead of time which parts of the night sky did not belong in the conversation.
zh: 今天我大半个周期都待在新亚特兰蒂斯底下，而不是里面，坐在一间嗡嗡作响的档案室里，那地方闻起来是旧臭氧和比楼上供应得还廉价的咖啡味。有个初级管理员欠某人一个人情，让我镜像了一套他赌咒说早没人用的作废交通模型。那些投影起初看着很干净，随后我开始把真实的货运日志叠上去。微小的手动修正，永远朝着同一个方向，永远刚好足以避开官方星图不肯承认存在的东西。我问是谁批准了那些改动，每一个被我堵住的资深分析师都说了同样的话：他们只是照别人跑过的结果才看出来有图案；而没人愿意说出最初那次运行的署名是谁。还有别的空白，他们叙述中的一些地方本该有词却没有，像他们早就一致约定好了，夜空里的哪些部分不该被放进这场谈话里。

#en:
I am writing this down so I can stop replaying it in my head every time the grav drive spins up.

The buoy was supposed to be scrap, just another hazard marker drifting where nobody cares. I cracked it for parts and the data core spilled out a set of routes that should not exist, drift math nudged off by the same fraction every time. When I asked around on the dock, nobody claimed to know anything; they just said they had heard it from a friend, from a cousin, from some pilot who had already shipped out. Same name, different mouths, nobody willing to swear they were the first.

Dock records do not match the departure times. A freighter listed as lost took a path that never appeared on the official chart. Every time I try to trace the origin of those vectors, the line bends back into rumor and shrugs. It feels like catching a voice in the static and being told, over and over, that someone else heard it first.
zh:
我把这个记下来，好让自己不必每次重力驱动一转起来就在脑子里重放它。

那只浮标本该是废料，不过又一个漂在没人管的地方的危险标记。我把它拆了取零件，数据核里却泄出一组本不该存在的航线，漂移算法每次都偏掉同样的一个小分数。我在码头上打听时，没人承认知道什么；他们只说是从一个朋友那儿听来的，从一个表亲那儿，从某个已经出航走了的飞行员那儿。同样的名字，不同的嘴，没人肯起誓说自己是最先知道的那个。

码头记录与离港时间对不上。一艘被列为失事的货船走的是一条从未出现在官方星图上的路径。每次我试图追查那些矢量的源头，线就弯回传闻和耸肩里。感觉就像在静电中逮住一个声音，然后被人一遍又一遍地告知：别人早就先听到了。

#en: I am logging this while the tug's reactor is still warm under my boots, before some supervisor edits the story into something cleaner. We were supposed to mark the derelict and move on, just another piece of junk drifting a few clicks off the lane. Then Nav said its drift did not match the model, Comms swore the beacon was just standard hazard code, and I said we did not have time to argue over scrap. Three different readings, three different priorities, and we split the difference like idiots. By the time we were close enough to see the extra plating and the way the drones orbited it like guard dogs, every channel on the board was full of that same faint, wrong signature. I keep thinking if I had pushed harder, or if Comms had not muted that one warning ping to clear space for a routine check-in, we would not have watched a whole cargo stack vanish off our scopes as if the lane itself opened a door and swallowed it.
zh: 我趁拖船的反应堆在我靴子底下还热乎时记下这段，免得某个主管把这段经过改写成更干净的东西。我们本该给那艘弃船做个标记就走，不过是又一堆漂在航道外几公里处的垃圾。可导航说它的漂移跟模型对不上，通讯赌咒说那信标只是标准危险代码，而我说我们没时间为废料吵架。三种不同的读数，三种不同的优先级，而我们像白痴一样各让一步。等我们靠得够近，看清那多出来的装甲板、看清那些无人机像看门狗一样绕着它转时，控制台上每一个频道都塞满了同样微弱、不对劲的信号。我总在想，要是我当时再坚持一下，或者通讯没有为了腾出例行报到的空档而把那一记警告嗡鸣调成静音，我们就不至于眼睁睁看着一整摞货物从示波器上消失——仿佛那条航道自己开了一扇门，把它吞了进去。

#en: I docked today at what should have been a dead node on the edge of nowhere. Old UC paint, dead beacon, the sort of relay you route around because nobody has maintained it since before you were born. Except the boards down in the well are still listening, running just enough juice to catch a little kick in the traffic a crooked bump in the timing that does not belong to age or dust. Silk Collective types are squatting here, running contraband through the blind spot, muttering about "lucky" jumps and refusing to look too closely at the diagnostics. Every time I ask about the missing convoy, voices drop, conversations thin out, like speaking the details aloud might ping the wrong set of ears. All I have right now is this whisper in the numbers, a relay that was supposed to be cold, and the memory of that analyst on Jemison who said her anomaly folders emptied themselves and then refused to say anything else above a murmur.
zh: 我今天停靠在一个本该是天涯尽头的死节点上。旧联殖涂装、死信标，那种你会绕开的通讯中继——自你出生以前就没人维护过。可下面井里的主板还在听着，耗着刚够的电流，捕捉交通中一点小小的踢动，一处不属于年岁或灰尘的歪斜顿挫。丝绸集体那伙人正赖在这里，把违禁品从盲区里运过，嘟囔着什么"幸运"跃迁，还拒绝细看诊断数据。每次我问起那支失踪的运输队，声音就低下去，谈话就稀薄起来，仿佛把细节说出口会惊动错的耳朵。我现在手里只有这些数字里的低语、一座本该冰冷的通讯中继，以及杰米森星上那位分析师的记忆——她说她的异常文件夹自己清空了，然后就再也不肯把话说得比耳语大声。

#en: I keep telling myself it was just the Aurora talking, but it has been three nights and I still see that symbol when I close my eyes. Not the usual dock scribbles, not some drunk spacer's tally mark, but a clean little arrow cut into the edge of a table in the Astral Lounge, right where the noise is loudest and the cameras always seem to glitch. I watched a hauler trace it with his thumb while he argued over a fuel bonus, swearing a "Kyrgyz map-witch" had shaved whole days off his run. His buddy called it bar fiction, said the only thing getting shaved was his sense. Later, when the lights dimmed and the band took a break, I saw two of Neon's quieter brokers pass a napkin over that same spot. They looked around like they expected someone else to be there, someone who never showed. Next shift, that hauler's ship was still docked, cargo sealed, crew gone. Half the bar swears they saw it leave; the logs say it never undocked.
zh: 我一直告诉自己那只是极光酒在说话，可已经三个晚上了，我一闭眼还是看见那个符号。不是码头那种寻常的涂鸦，也不是哪个喝醉的太空人刻的计数痕，而是一个干净的小箭头，刻在星界酒廊一张桌子的边缘，正好在最吵的地方，也正好是监控老是出故障的位置。我看着一个运货船员一边为燃料奖金争吵，一边用拇指描它，赌咒说有个"吉尔吉斯制图女巫"给他的航次省下了好几天。他的哥们说那是酒吧里的瞎编，说唯一被削掉的是他的脑子。后来灯光暗下、乐队休息时，我看见霓虹城两个最安静的经纪商把一张餐巾传过那个位置。他们四下张望，像在等另一个人出现——而那人始终没来。下一个轮班，那运货船员的飞船还停靠在泊位上，货舱封着，船员不见了。半个酒吧都赌咒说看见它离港了；日志却说它从未解缆。

#en: I am never going to admit this to SysDef, but the deserter was right about one thing the bunker's ears are better than its masters. Half the racks are dead, dust in the fans, but down in the cold storage I found a patrol grid slice nobody ever purged. Atmospheric sweeps, routine passes, then a smear of interference that keeps popping in the same place. Not over a colony, not over a lane. Out past the orbit tracks, right where the scouts say the rock field goes thin.  \n\nThe deserter swore some UC captain called it "the place your scopes forget," and that a certain pilot slipped through that gap more than once. I pulled old buoy chatter from a remote station that heard the same static, and way back on that farm rock I heard a drunk freighter hand mumble about a ship that crossed the sky without leaving a trail. Everyone pretends they are just telling stories, but all the stories point toward the same empty patch of stone.
zh: 我绝不会把这话跟星防队承认，可那名逃兵有一点说对了：碉堡的耳朵比它的主子好使。一半的机架都死了，风扇里积着灰，可我在冷库里找到了一段谁都没清除过的巡逻网格切片。大气扫描、例行通过，然后是一片反复出现在同一位置的干扰涂抹。不在殖民地上空，不在航道之上。而是在轨道轨迹之外，正是侦察兵们说岩场变薄的地方。\n\n那名逃兵赌咒说，某个联殖舰长管那地方叫"你的示波器会遗忘之处"，还说某位飞行员不止一次从那条缝隙里溜过去。我从一座听到同样静电的偏远站点调来了旧浮标通讯，而很久以前在那块农场岩石上，我听过一个喝醉的货船船员含含糊糊地念叨一艘穿过天空却没留下痕迹的飞船。人人都假装自己只是在讲故事，可所有故事都指向同一片空的石头地。

#en: I remember when the Scarrunner still smelled like new sealant and cheap coffee, back when our routing package was supposed to be a "trial build" for some contractor in New Atlantis. We were told the tweaks were temporary, just a test run on a mid-tier hauler. Nobody ever pushed an update to take them back out. Jump after jump, the little corrections stayed, got copied, got baked into our standard when nobody was looking. I only started logging the drift after our last three runs all brushed the same patch of nothing near that debris field, all flagged by the same unseen hand in the telemetry. Now I am sitting in a dead ship, in a cabin that still has two mugs strapped to the bulkhead, watching logs that prove our "temporary" settings nudged us here on purpose, and every line of code points back toward a quiet analyst who decided we were safer as numbers in his model than as people trying to make a living between the lanes.
zh: 我记得疤痕快船还带着新密封胶和廉价咖啡的味道的日子，那时我们的航路数据包还只是给新亚特兰蒂斯某个承包商的"试用版"。他们告诉我们那些调整是临时的，只是在一条中档货船上试跑一下。可从来没人推过一次更新把它们撤掉。一次跃迁接一次跃迁，那些小修正留了下来，被复制、在没人注意时被烤进了我们的标准里。我是直到最近三趟都擦过那片碎片场附近同一块空无、且每次都被遥测里同一只看不见的手标出来，才开始记录这种漂移的。如今我坐在一艘死船里，在这间舱壁上还绑着两只杯子的船舱里，看着证明我们那套"临时"设置是故意把我们推到这里来的日志，而每一行代码都指回一名沉默的分析师——他断定，我们当模型里的数字，比当在航道之间讨生活的人更安全。

#en: Dock master logged this sector as routine hold space again today. Funny word, "hold." Out here it means everything from "waiting on parts" to "don't ask why that hull has not moved in six months." The local tug crews joke that ships come here to be forgotten; the old hands just shrug and say this pocket of orbit is where cargo and secrets both go to overstay their welcome.\n\nI walked past a viewport on break and caught sight of that dark courier, still drifting, still tagged as temporary layover. Nothing about its scorch pattern says temporary. I cannot stop thinking about the stories I have heard, the ones that get softer around the edges every time they are told in the back of the bar. A farm whose harvest turned to dust. A dome where the air went wrong but the paperwork stayed perfect. Now there is a dead ship parked in a zone that never lets go of what it is given, and everyone pretends their gaze just slid past it by accident.
zh: 今天码头主管又把这片区域记成了例行的暂存空间。一个有意思的词，"暂存"。在这外面，它的意思从"等零件"一直到"别问那具船壳为什么六个月没挪窝"。本地的拖船船员开玩笑说，飞船来这儿就是为了被遗忘；老手们只是耸耸肩，说这一小片轨道是货物和秘密都喜欢赖着不走的地方。\n\n休息时我路过一扇观察窗，瞥见那艘深色的快船，仍在漂着，仍被标为临时停泊。可它身上的烧灼纹路没有一点"临时"的样子。我止不住地想我听过的那些故事，那些在酒吧后堂每被讲一次、边缘就变得更柔和一些的故事。一座收成化为尘土农庄。一座空气出了故障、文件却依然完美的穹顶城。如今一艘死船停在一片从不放过任何被交给它的东西的区域里，而人人都假装自己的目光只是不小心从它身上滑了过去。

#en: I spent the afternoon on a busted crate outside Bay 6, pretending to fix a scanner that was not broken, just so I could watch the traffic. Same tugs, same bulk haulers, same bored crane ops running their loops. On paper, nothing wrong. In the air, though, you can feel the skips. Escorts that always seem to find a reason to break formation three klicks out, freighters that never actually touch the deck they are booked for. Nobody talks about it. Foreman changed the subject when I asked, like we had both agreed years ago that some routes just were not to be discussed.\n\nWhat bothers me is how neatly it all fits around that slate I pulled off the derelict last week. Wrong registry there, wrong tonnage here, and now these quiet detours that only show up in smudged grease-pencil on a wall no one admits to updating. Feels less like random error and more like somebody has been drawing a new map over the old one, and the rest of us decided not to see it.
zh: 我一下午都待在 6 号泊位外一只破板条箱上，假装在修一台根本没坏的扫描仪，就为了看交通。同样的拖船、同样的散货船、同样无聊的吊车工跑着他们的圈子。纸面上，什么都没问题。可在空气里，你能感觉到那些顿挫。护航船总是找得到理由在三公里外散开队形，货船从不真正碰上它们预订的那个泊位。没人谈这事。我问的时候，工头就换了话题，像我们多年前就都默认有些航线不该被讨论。\n\n让我不安的是，这一切围着上周我从弃船上取下的那块数据板拼得太齐整了。这里登记号不对，那里吨位不对，现在又是这些只出现在墙上某人涂的油铅笔痕里的安静绕行——而那面墙谁都不承认更新过。感觉不像随机的错误，倒更像有人在旧地图上画着一张新地图，而我们其余人打定主意不去看见它。

#en: I am writing this down because if I say it out loud again, someone will tell me to file it under "routing anomaly" and move on. I have been staring at traffic plots from this dustball for months, half asleep at the console, letting the patterns blur. Today I finally overlaid them with the old LIST settlement requests, the ones that never got a green light but also never got closed. That is when it snapped into place tiny course nudges on ore haulers and research ferries, always just a degree or two off declared vectors, always lining up with cargo that "went missing in transit." No one caught it because each tweak was nothing on its own, buried under years of lazy audits and cut budgets. Now I can trace the arc of those corrections out into an empty patch of sky where no beacon broadcasts and no chartered colony supposedly exists. Whatever she has been feeding lives out there, in the gap between what the records say should happen and what actually did.
zh: 我把这个写下来，因为要是我再说出口，就会有人叫我把归到"航路异常"下面然后翻篇。这几个月我一直在盯着这颗尘球星传来的交通图，半睡半醒地坐在控制台前，任由图案糊成一片。今天我总算把它们和独立盟那些旧的定居申请叠在一起——那些从没拿到绿灯、却也从未被结案的申请。就在那一刻，一切卡到位了：矿石货船和研究渡船上那些微小的航向轻推，永远只偏离申报矢量一两度，永远与那些"在运输途中失踪"的货物对得上。没人发现，是因为每一次微调单拎出来都不算什么，被埋在多年懒惰的审计和被削减的预算底下。如今我能把那些修正的弧线一路追到一片空旷的天空里——那里没有信标广播，据称也不存在任何特许殖民地。她一直在喂养的东西就活在那里，活在记录声称应该发生的事与实际发生的事之间的那道缝隙里。

#en: I have been working this yard long enough to know when a story is supposed to die. Command cashed out the contracts, auditors stamped everything "decommissioned," and the patrols we picked up from the regulars walk like they were told to stop thinking about what happened around that wreck. Still, on long shifts, over cheap coffee and the clank of cutters, the same details leak out in different mouths civilian beacons that should not have been there, targeting orders that arrived a little too late, logs that got "reconciled" between one rotation and the next. Officially, it was all settled years ago. Unofficially, some of us kept scraps of residue, fragments of data, the way you keep a splinter after it works under your skin. They wanted the whole thing to rust away out here, but the whispers will not stay buried, and now someone is following the same trail from that forgotten rock to our piles of Deimos steel, listening harder than anyone has in a long time.
zh: 我在这座船坞干得够久，久到能看出一个故事什么时候是该死的。指挥部把合同套了现，审计员给一切盖上了"已退役"的章，而我们从常客那儿捡来的巡逻任务里，那些人走路的架势像被告知过别再想那场残骸附近发生了什么。可即便如此，在漫长的轮班里，就着廉价咖啡和切割机的哐当声，同样的细节还是从不同的嘴里漏出来：不该出现在那里的民用信标、到得稍晚了一点的瞄准指令、在一个轮换与下一个轮换之间被"整理核对"过的日志。官方说法是，这一切多年前就了结了。非官方地讲，我们有些人留着些残渣碎片、数据断片，就像一根扎进你皮肤底下的刺你会留着它一样。他们想让整件事在这外面锈掉烂掉，可低语不肯被埋住；如今有人正沿着同样的痕迹，从那块被遗忘的岩石一路追到我们这堆火卫二钢材，听得比很久以来任何人都更仔细。

#en: I was supposed to be working border disputes today, not chasing ghosts in the shipping lanes. One wrong routing code hit my console this morning, some clerk in Akila mixing up sectors, and suddenly I am looking at a convoy manifest that should not have passed anywhere near last year's incident. I pinged New Atlantis for clarification, got three different answers and a polite threat to drop it. The more they stumbled over themselves, the more that spiral pattern in the transit logs burned into my eyes. It is in the timing, the way the grav burns stagger just so. Cross-referencing old blackbox echoes with that misfiled manifest pointed to a dirty orbit above a dead-looking world, where the sensors keep flagging "background noise" and then clearing it. I logged it as a routine debris survey; dispatch signed off without reading. A few careless words, a few half-read requests, and now I am pretty sure I have the next breadcrumb to whoever has been rewriting our sky.
zh: 今天我本该处理边界纠纷，而不是在航运航道里追鬼。今早一个错的航路代码打进了我的控制台，阿基拉某个文员把星区搞混了，于是我忽然就在看一份本不该经过去年那起事件附近的运输队清单。我向新亚特兰蒂斯发消息要求澄清，得到三个不同的答复，外加一句客气的"别追究了"的威胁。他们越是互相绊脚，运输日志里那个螺旋图案就越是烧进我的眼睛。问题出在时序上，出在重力点火以那样的方式错开的方式上。把旧的黑匣子回响和那份归错档的清单交叉比对，指向一颗看起来死透的星球上方一条肮脏的轨道——那里的传感器老是标出"背景噪声"，随后又把它清掉。我把它记成一次例行的碎片勘测；调度员看都没看就批了。几个不留心的词、几份只读了一半的请求，如今我相当确定，我已经拿到了下一条通往那个一直在改写我们天空之人的面包屑。

#en: I docked at that rock expecting a routine inspection and a half-decent cup of TerraBrew, nothing more. From up close the facility is just another tired UC contract job, weld scars and patched plating, but the techs walk like they are carrying glass inside their skulls. One of them slipped, called the drive bay "the screaming room" before she caught herself and shut down, eyes on the nearest camera. I have heard three different versions of what happened here already, each one softer than the last, like someone has been sanding the edges off the story. Some say it was a test article that went sideways, some say sabotage, some say the logs were changed after the fact and nobody can remember the original numbers anymore. Whatever the truth was, it is buried under secondhand gossip and redacted files now, and all I have to go on are a falsified report, a slate full of panicked equations, and a whispered name that makes every engineer in this place change the subject.
zh: 我停靠在那块岩石上时，只指望一次例行检查，外加一杯还过得去的地球酿酒，别无他求。凑近了看，这设施不过是又一个疲惫的联殖承包工程，焊缝疤痕和打补丁的装甲板，可那些技工走路的架势像脑袋里揣着玻璃。有个技工说漏了嘴，把驱动舱叫做"尖叫室"，随即意识到不对闭了嘴，眼睛瞟向最近的一个摄像头。关于这里发生过什么，我已经听过三个不同的版本了，一个比一个柔和，像有人在把故事的棱角一点点磨掉。有人说是试验品出了岔子，有人说是蓄意破坏，还有人说是事后改了日志，现在已经没人记得原始数字了。无论真相是什么，它如今都被二手闲话和涂黑的文件压在底下；我手里能抓的，只有一份伪造的报告、一块写满惊慌方程式的数据板，以及一个让人一说出口、这地方每一个工程师都会立刻换话题的名字。

#en: I am writing this from a maintenance cubby three decks below the cargo office, where the walls still sweat dust from the last micrometeor strike. The relay feels wrong tonight. Dock queues are short, ships are holding in shadow, and every terminal I jack into shows the same thing: credits pushed through, then quietly walked back like they were never there. I finally traced the pattern past the forged manifests and dead shell firms the broker has been peddling. All those "corrections" bend toward one dead node off the main grid, a relay station that should have been decommissioned years ago but still drinks a trickle of power and bandwidth it is not supposed to have. Whoever is steering this tide thought the story would sink under paperwork and time, but the whispers from that farm foreclosure, from a frozen LIST rock, from bar gossip in Gagarin kept matching the same invisible signature, and now the route lines all point to that deserted hub waiting in the dark.
zh: 我在货舱办公室下三层的一间维护小间里写下这些，四壁还在往外渗着上次微陨石撞击留下的灰尘。今晚这座中继站感觉不对劲。泊位队列很短，飞船都待在阴影里，而每台我接进去的终端都在显示同样的事：信用币被推过去，然后又悄悄退回来，像是从没出现过。我终于顺着伪造的清单和经纪商一直在兜售的空壳公司，把图案追出了轮廓。所有那些"修正"都朝着主电网之外的一座死节点弯过去——一座多年前就该退役的通讯中继，却仍在啜饮着它本不该拥有的些许电力和带宽。操纵这股潮水的人以为故事会在文书与时间里沉底，可来自那桩农庄查封、来自一块冰封的独立盟岩石、来自加加林酒吧闲谈的低语，一直对得上同一个看不见的签名；如今所有航线都指向黑暗中等待的那座荒废枢纽。

#en: I asked dispatch about the Capitalwing again today and he did that thing with his eyes, looked past me like I was a bulkhead that needed repainting. Nobody forgets an escort that size, not out here, but they talk around it now, like a word you are not supposed to say in front of kids. I keep running into that same look: clerks shuffling printouts, techs suddenly very interested in cable routing, even the bartender wiping the same spot on the counter while I pretend not to notice his hands shaking. The stories do not line up, either. Official feed says grav-drive failure, quick loss, nothing to salvage. Haulers coming through three beers deep swear they heard about a test lane, faster, cleaner, if you did not ask too many questions. And somewhere between those versions there is this hollow in the logs, beacons that should have pings but do not, green ratings that appeared without scans attached. When a secret is that big, it makes people afraid to even meet your eyes.
zh: 今天我又向调度员问起首都之翼，他又用那种眼神，越过我看着某个方向，仿佛我是一面需要重新刷漆的舱壁。那么大的护航船没人会忘，在这外面更不会，可他们现在都绕着它说话，像一个不该在孩子面前说的词。我总是撞见同样的神情：文员翻弄着打印件，技工忽然对电缆布线极感兴趣，连酒保都在擦吧台上同一块地方，而我假装没注意到他的手在抖。那些说法也对不上。官方播报说是重力驱动故障、迅速失事、无可打捞。而喝到第三杯的运货船员赌咒说，他们听说过一条测试航道——更快、更干净，只要你别问太多问题。而在那些版本之间的某处，日志里有一道空洞：本该有信号的浮标却没有，没附扫描记录的绿色评级突然出现。当一个秘密有那么大，它会让人连对上你的眼睛都害怕。

#en: Somebody wiped this place lazy, like they trusted time to finish the job. Half the terminals still think it is three years ago, half the cameras loop blank corridors, and the security daemon is chasing ghosts in its own logs. I was supposed to audit a simple breach trail, tick the boxes, bill whoever hired me. Instead I find a chain of connection requests that never should have routed through a backwater lab like this, all handshakes half completed, then neatly severed just before they reached the main archive. Ran them through my own rig, out of habit, and every one of those broken calls resolves toward the same patch of deep nothing a dead coordinate buried under layers of "temporary" redirects. It feels too clean to be an accident, too convenient to be just fear. Whoever she is, she knew exactly how much to cut so the system would keep limping along, and now I am holding the first clean vector to wherever she sends the people who do not want to wait in line anymore.
zh: 有人把这地方擦得很懒散，像是笃定时间会替他们收尾。一半的终端还以为现在是三年前，一半的摄像头在空走廊里循环播放，安全守护进程在自己的日志里追着鬼跑。我本该审计一条简单的入侵痕迹，勾完表格，然后向雇我的人开账单。可我找到的却是一串本不该经过这么个穷乡实验室的连接请求，握手全都进行到一半就被干净利落地切断，正好在够到主档案之前。出于习惯，我把它们放进自己的机器里跑了一遍，结果那些中断的呼叫每一个都指向同一片深深的虚无——一个被层层"临时"重定向埋住的死坐标。这干净得不像意外，方便得不像单纯的恐惧。不管她是谁，她清楚该切掉多少，好让系统继续一瘸一拐地跑下去；如今我手里攥着第一条干净的矢量，通往她把那些不愿再排队等候的人送去的地方。

#en:
I should not be down here alone.

The pod still thinks it has a purpose. Consoles cycle through the same old sweeps on dead satellites, query beacons that have not answered in years, ping corridors UC stopped admitting existed. Nobody ever shut any of it off; they just stopped looking at the results. That is the only reason I found it. Buried in the rolling diagnostics, under three generations of "do not touch" tags, there is a route offset that repeats whenever one particular transponder pattern passes through the field. Cross-checking it against the fragments I pulled from that hillside cache, and the static-riddled jump data from the freighter that never arrived, it all lines up.  

Somewhere above this rock, between here and that stretch of wreck-strewn dark everyone pretends is just bad luck, the same tiny correction keeps being applied to ships that bought a certain kind of chart. The system is still nudging them, long after the people who set it up walked away.
zh:
我不该一个人待在这下面。

这个舱体还以为自己有用。控制台一遍遍对死去的卫星做着同样老旧的扫描，查询多年没应答过的信标，向联殖早已不再承认存在的航道发延时探测。从没人把这些关掉；他们只是不再看结果了。而这就是我唯一的发现途径。在滚动的诊断数据里，压在三代人留下的"勿动"标签底下，有一处航路偏移——每当某种特定的应答器波形经过这片空域，它就会重复出现。把它和我从山坡缓存里取出的碎片、以及那艘从未抵达的货船上满是静电的跃迁数据交叉比对，全部对得上。

在这块岩石上方的某处，从这里到那片人人都假装只是运气不好的残骸遍布的黑暗之间，同样那点微小的修正一直在被施加给那些买了某种星图的飞船。设置它的人早已离开，可系统仍在轻推着它们。

#en: I am writing this from the Riftblade, and the ship feels like it is trying to forget something. Drives are cold, power throttled down, but every bulkhead has that faint shiver you get after a hard abort, like the metal remembers being somewhere it should not have been. The manifest I am digging for should be routine cargo nonsense, but the routing stamps do not match the stories I heard back on the fringe. Same captain name, different paths. Same ports, different dates. Like someone took a perfectly straight haul and bent it just enough to slip between patrol sweeps. What gets me is how every step that led here was small, harmless on its own: a garbled ping from a monitoring shack, a miner talking about a missing cousin over cheap Erdebrau, a scratched-out line on an old service log. None of it screamed conspiracy, just little scuffs on the paint of reality, and somehow all of those quiet mistakes pushed me toward this dead ship and the name everybody swears they do not know.
zh: 我在裂刃号上写下这些，这艘船感觉像在努力忘记什么。驱动是冷的，功率被压到最低，可每块舱壁都带着那种硬着陆中止后才会有的微弱战栗，像金属记得自己去过本不该去的地方。我要挖的那份清单本该是些例行公事的货物废话，可航路戳记跟我在外缘听说的事对不上。同样的船长名，不同的路径。同样的港口，不同的日期。像是有人把一趟笔直的运输稍微掰弯，刚好够从巡逻扫描的缝隙里滑过去。真正让我在意的是，一路把我引到这里来的每一步都那么小、单看都无害：一座监测棚传来的含糊延时探测、一个矿工就着廉价埃尔德啤酒念叨失踪的表亲、一份旧维修日志上一行被划掉的字。没有一样像是阴谋，只是现实漆面上的小小擦痕；可不知怎的，所有这些安静的错误把我推向了这艘死船，以及那个人人都赌咒说自己不认识的名字。

#en: They say if you stay too long in a dead GalBank hull, you start hearing old transactions whisper in the bulkheads. Sitting in the cold server bay of this vault ship, watching the power flicker over racks nobody is supposed to know about, I almost believe it. The logs do not match the public story; course changes are shaved by fractions, storm alerts delayed by minutes, payouts denied on worlds that should have been safe. I have heard this tale in bars and supply queues, passed around like a ghost story about a nav engineer who tilted the sky, but every retelling trims an edge, blurs a name, makes it sound like bad luck instead of design. Out at that first backwater homestead, all I saw were ruined fields and people who cursed the weather; at the old listening post, I found recordings cut off mid-warning. Now the patterns in these sealed ledgers say none of it was random, and that someone has been very careful about which parts of the truth survive the trip to the next backroom.
zh: 都说你要是在一具死去的盖尔银行船壳里待得太久，就会开始听见旧交易在舱壁里低语。坐在这种金库船的冰冷服务器舱里，看着没人该知道的机架上电力忽明忽暗，我几乎信了。日志与对外的说法对不上；航向被削掉几分之几度，风暴警报被延迟几分钟，本该安全的世界却被拒付赔款。我在酒吧和补给队列里听过这个故事，它被传来传去，像一则关于某个把天空掰斜的导航工程师的鬼故事；可每次转述都会剪掉一个棱角、模糊一个名字，让它听起来像运气不好，而不是精心设计。在那第一座穷乡农庄，我看到的只有毁掉的田地和咒骂天气的人；在旧监听站，我找到的录音在警告中途就被切断。如今这些密封账簿里的图案说明，这一切都不是随机的；有人非常小心地决定，真相的哪些部分才被允许活着走进下一个后堂。

#en:
I picked up that dataslate because Rafi swore Juno swore her cousin had pulled it off a dead hauler out near Narion. That is how it always goes out here. No one ever finds anything themselves, they just pass along someone else's ghosts.

I ran the file on my bunk, lights low, just the hum of the recycler and that cold glow on my hands.

Course data, stamped like it came off a UC console twenty years ago, but nudging jumps by half a degree here, a full degree there.

Nothing dramatic, just a slow drift.

When I asked Rafi where Juno's cousin actually got it, he laughed and said he heard it from a Ranger who heard it from a smuggler who heard it from a Navy washout.

Every name was a step sideways, never forward.

Now I am sitting in a ship that hums the same way, staring at routes that look just a little too clean, and all I can think is that whatever started this never had to show its face.

It just needed people like us, trusting that somebody else checked the math.
zh:
我捡起那块数据板，是因为拉菲赌咒说朱诺赌咒说她表亲从纳里昂附近一艘死货船上弄来的。在这外面事情从来都是这样。没人自己找到过任何东西，大家只是转手传递别人的鬼。

我在铺位上跑那份文件，灯光调暗，只有回收机在嗡鸣，冷光落在手上。

航路数据，戳记像二十年前从联殖控制台上打出来的，却把跃迁一处拧偏半度、一处拧偏整整一度。

没什么戏剧性，只是缓慢的漂移。

我问拉菲，朱诺的表亲到底是从哪儿弄来的，他笑了，说他是从一个游骑兵那儿听来的，游骑兵又是从一个走私贩那儿，走私贩又是从一个海军淘汰兵那儿听来的。

每个名字都是一步横向偏移，从来不是向前。

如今我坐在一条以同样方式嗡鸣的飞船里，盯着那些看起来稍微太干净了一点的航线，满脑子只有一个念头：挑起这一切的东西，从来不必露面。

它只需要我们这样的人，信任别人已经核对过算式。

#en:
I always thought banks were boring, even when they were floating in orbit. Turns out the quiet ones hide the worst rot.  

I have been on this derelict for three hours now, lungs full of recycled dust and old insulation, watching GalBank headers scroll past on dead consoles. The numbers say traffic, insurance, expected loss. Between the lines, I see ships nudged a little off the lanes, like someone was leaning on the galaxy with one finger. Nobody flagged it. Nobody wanted to.  

Out in that first backwater outpost, the locals just shrugged when routes shifted, said the sky changes. Later, that beacon in orbit with its jittery telemetry seemed like a one-off glitch. Now, buried in this courier's belly, I can feel the pattern tightening, realize how long this has been in the system, ignored because it was profitable to look away. Whatever I pull from here points toward Neon, toward high steel where someone has been rewriting how we travel while the rest of us pretend not to notice.
zh:
我一直以为银行很无聊，哪怕它们漂在轨道上。结果发现，安静的那种才藏着最烂的腐坏。

我在这艘弃船上待了三个小时了，肺里灌满再循环的灰尘和旧隔热层，看着盖尔银行的页眉在死控制台上滚过。那些数字说的是交通、保险、预期损失。可我在字里行间看见飞船被轻轻推离航道，像有人用一根手指压着银河。没人标记它。没人想标记。

在那第一座穷乡前哨站，航线一变，本地人只是耸耸肩，说天空会变。后来，轨道上那座遥测抖个不停的信标，看起来像一次性的故障。如今，埋在这艘快船肚子里，我能感觉到那图案正在收紧，意识到它在这套系统里已经存在了多久——一直被忽视，因为别过头去是有利可图的。我从这里挖出的任何东西都指向霓虹城，指向那些高耸的钢铁，那里有人在改写我们出行的方式，而我们其余人假装没看见。

#en: I signed on to Heat Ridge because it was supposed to be simple work. Guard duty, they said. Easy credits babysitting a dead UC husk no one remembered filing the decommission papers for. First few months it really was that dull; same patrol routes on half-lit catwalks, same hum of old scanners sweeping an empty sky out of habit. Felt like we were watching a locked door in a corridor no one walked anymore.\n\nThen the captain started checking the sensor room himself. Not just once, but every shift change. We got told not to touch certain consoles, not to ask why the old arrays were suddenly drawing more power. The logs started filling up with tiny course corrections for ships that, on paper, never passed within a system of us. No alarms, no flags, just little numbers pushed into folders marked routine. Somewhere along the way, standing post on a forgotten station turned into sitting on something someone else did not want found, and none of us could say when that change actually happened.
zh: 我签下热脊的任务，是因为它本该是份简单活儿。他们说是站岗。轻松挣信用币，照看一具没人记得提交过退役文件的联殖死壳。头几个月确实就那么无聊；半亮的天桥上同样的巡逻路线，老扫描仪出于习惯扫着同一片空荡天空，发出同样的嗡鸣。感觉就像我们在看守一条再没人走的走廊里一扇锁着的门。\n\n后来，船长开始亲自检查传感器室。不是一次，而是每个交班都去。我们被告知不许碰某些控制台，不许问为什么那些老旧阵列突然开始耗更多电。日志里开始填满些微小的航向修正，对象是那些纸面上从未经过我们所在星系范围内的飞船。没有警报，没有标记，只有一些小数字被塞进标着"例行"的文件夹。不知不觉间，在一座被遗忘的空间站上站岗，变成了坐守某样别人不愿被找到的东西；而我们谁都说不上来，这变化究竟是什么时候发生的。

#en: I keep replaying that day the crate lists, the loader jams, and suddenly we are staring at seals with medical hazard glyphs instead of processed grain. Trade Authority paperwork said "nutritional supplements." Smelled like antiseptic and metal, the way every battlefield clinic I have ever limped through smells. Jonas cracked a joke, Kira logged it under a different code, Elias just went very, very quiet. No one wanted to say the obvious out loud that somebody was shunting chems to places that do not show up on any of our route maps. Since then, every time some spacer in the dockside bar mutters about a ghost medic patching up people the system forgot, the crew shifts in their seats. They laugh it off, look at their drinks or the wall or anything that is not my face. Manifest says we jumped clean from Gagarin, but the nav buffer shows a burned-in echo of a different vector, a short, dirty hop toward nowhere. The closer I look, the more the gaps line up into a shape that feels like intent.
zh: 那天的事我一直在脑子里重放：货箱清单、装卸机卡住，然后我们忽然盯着一堆印着医疗危险符号的封条，而不是加工好的谷物。贸易管理局的文件上写着"营养补充剂"。那气味像消毒剂和金属，就像我拖着腿进过的每一间战地诊所的味道。乔纳斯说了个笑话，基拉把它记到了另一个代码下，伊莱亚斯只是变得非常、非常安静。没人愿意把显而易见的话说出口——有人正在把药剂转运到任何一个航图上都不显示的地方。从那以后，每当码头酒吧里哪个太空人嘟囔起一个给系统遗忘之人疗伤的幽灵军医，船员们就在座位上挪动身体。他们一笑带过，盯着自己的酒、盯着墙，盯着任何不是我的脸的东西。清单说我们是从加加林干净地跃过来的，可导航缓冲里却留着一道另一条矢量的烙痕，一次朝虚无的短促而肮脏的跳转。我看得越仔细，那些空白就越拼成一个像是"有意为之"的形状。

#en: I keep replaying that intake shift in my head. One overworked Trade Authority clerk, three screens blinking orange, and a cargo ship with a routing anomaly that "looked like a sensor hiccup." Nobody wanted to hold the line over a few mismatched timestamps when there were paying haulers stacked behind it. We cleared Tidewalker TA-7207 with a shrug and a shared joke about phantom paperwork, and I told myself I would circle back to the discrepancy after shift. I did not.\n\nSince then I have watched settlement distress calls pile up from worlds stamped "marginal but viable," watched survey signatures come through with tiny calibration quirks that feel familiar now. The stories all sound the same: storms no model mentioned, groundwater souring overnight, coordinates bought from someone who swore the numbers were solid. One skipped follow-up turned into a corridor nobody questioned, the perfect place for a man who lives in the blind spots between what the data says and what people want to believe.
zh: 那个接收窗口的班我一直在脑子里重放。一个忙不过来的贸易管理局文员，三块屏幕闪着橙色，还有一艘货船的航路异常"看着像传感器打嗝"。后面还排着付了钱的运货船员，谁愿意为几个对不上的时间戳卡住队伍呢。我们耸耸肩，开了个关于幽灵文书工作的玩笑，就把潮行者 TA-7207 放行了，我还告诉自己交班后回头再查那处出入。我没查。\n\n从那以后，我看着盖着"边缘但可行"印章的星球不断累积起定居者的求救呼叫，看着勘测签名带着如今感觉很眼熟的那些微小校准怪癖传进来。那些故事听起来都一样：模型从未提及的风暴、一夜之间变酸的地下水、从某个赌咒说数据可靠的人手里买来的坐标。一次被跳过的跟进，变成了一条无人质疑的走廊——对那种活"数据所说的"与"人们愿意相信的"之间盲区里的人而言，这是完美的藏身处。

#en: I keep telling myself I am not paranoid, just observant. Then I look around this box they call a command post and see how every wall is held up by things no one wants to say out loud. Manifests pinned under other manifests, patrol reports with whole hours missing, hauler complaints tagged "resolved" when I know damn well no one even sent a reply. Today I found three different versions of the same convoy's route, all stamped clean. Only the timing lines did not match. Little delays, a few seconds here, a minute there, always bending the same way. When I traced them on the board they curved into something like a spiral, neat as you please. I asked dispatch about it and got silence, then too much talking about unrelated sectors. Everyone pretended not to understand which files I meant, like we were all suddenly bad at our jobs at the same time. That is when I knew this was bigger than a bad routing algorithm and that whatever is sitting at the center of that spiral is not supposed to have a name.
zh: 我一直告诉自己我不是多疑，只是善于观察。然后我环顾这间他们称作指挥所的盒子，看见每一面墙都是靠没人愿意说出口的东西撑着的。清单压在别的清单底下，巡逻报告整小时整小时地缺失，运货船员的投诉被标成"已解决"，而我他妈的清楚根本没人回过一句。今天我找到同一支运输队路线的三个不同版本，全都盖着干净的章。只有时间线对不上。小小的延迟，这里几秒，那里一分钟，永远朝同一个方向弯。我在图板上把它们描出来，它们就弯成了一个螺旋似的东西，整整齐齐。我去问调度，得到的先是沉默，然后是一大堆关于无关星区的废话。人人都假装听不懂我说的是哪些文件，就像我们忽然同时变得不会干活了。那一刻我就知道，这比一个糟糕的航路算法大得多；而坐在那螺旋中心的东西，本不该有名字。

#en: I have been staring at these screens long enough that the afterimage of the graphs follows me when I close my eyes. No windows down here, just recycled air and the low whine of processors chewing on data no one officially collects anymore. Off the record, half the bureau will tell you they have heard of "those routes" in a bar somewhere between shifts. On duty, those same people swear the charts are clean, the lanes are safe, and any missing tonnage is bad bookkeeping or pirate work. Funny how the stories thin out when the recorder is running.\n\nI pulled a jump log from a small freighter that never arrived, overlaid it with half-erased telemetry from an old survey corridor, and there it was again: that same tiny course correction, like a hand on the rudder just off-center. Someone built that into the system, then everyone agreed not to see it. Whatever this cartographer is doing, it is stitched straight into the gap between what we know in private and what we are allowed to write in the report.
zh: 我盯着这些屏幕太久，一闭眼那些图表的残影就跟着我。这下面没有窗户，只有再循环的空气和处理器低低的呜咽——它们在嚼着官方早已不再收集的数据。私下里，半个局子的人都会告诉你，他们在交班间隙的某个酒吧里听说过"那些航线"。可一到当班时，同样是这些人却赌咒说星图是干净的、航道是安全的，任何失踪的吨位都只是记账太糟或海盗干的。好笑的是，只要录音机一开，那些故事就都变稀薄了。\n\n我调出一艘从未抵达的小货船的跃迁日志，把它和一条旧勘测走廊里擦了一半的遥测叠在一起，它又出现了：同样那点微小的航向修正，像一只手把舵稍稍推离了中心。有人把它建进了系统，然后所有人一致同意不去看见它。不管这位制图师在做什么，它被直接缝进了"我们私下知道什么"与"我们被允许写进报告什么"之间的那道缝隙里。

#en: I met him at the edge of nowhere, where the dust eats boots and the only light is whatever you bring with you. He still had the posture, the haircut, the way of scanning horizons like someone who expects orders to drop into his ear at any second, but his badge never left his pocket. We talked like people who were not supposed to know each other, trading half phrases and old unit slang, and every time I pushed for something concrete his eyes slipped sideways, like there was a list of things he had decided not to remember. Ship names, dates, the exact wording of clearance codes no one uses anymore all brushed past, never quite spoken. I recognized the pattern; I have seen whole patrols swear they never saw the wrong kind of insignia on the wrong kind of corpse. Still, in between the gaps he gave me enough duplicated IDs, ghost cargoes, a flight plan that ends in empty coordinates to know there is a thread running through it all, and that everyone who has touched it is now pretending their hands are clean.
zh: 我在天涯尽头遇见了他，那地方尘土啃靴子，唯一的光就是你自己带的。他还留着那种姿态、那种发型、那种扫视地平线的方式，像个随时等着命令落进耳朵里的人，可他的徽章从未离开过口袋。我们像两个本不该认识的人那样交谈，交换着半截的话和老部队的黑话；每次我逼问具体的东西，他的眼睛就朝旁边滑开，仿佛有一份他决定不再记起的清单。船名、日期、那些早已没人用的通行代码的准确措辞——全都一擦而过，从来说不出口。我认得这个套路；我见过整支巡逻队赌咒说，他们从未在错的尸体上见过错的徽记。尽管如此，在他那些空白之间，他给了我足够多的重复 ID、幽灵货物、一份终点是空坐标的飞行计划，让我知道有一条线贯穿其中，而每个碰过它的人如今都假装自己的手是干净的。

#en: Docked at the relay again, grav low enough that every step feels like walking through someone else's dream. The broker finally talked, after enough credits and a reminder that rival haulers die messy when routes go bad. Under all the fake manifests and shuffled crate IDs, there it was a repeating drift in the routing tables, like someone had taught the system to breathe in a certain rhythm. Every third shipment, no matter the declared destination, nudged one or two degrees off into the same empty patch of sky. Cross it with the queue anomalies from New Atlantis and that half baked jump plan pulled from the dead survey cutter and it lines up with eerie precision. I flagged the coordinates, prepped a shuttle, told Jo I would ping back once I had eyes on whatever is floating out there. She joked I would probably find nothing but another derelict and a bad story. That was three cycles ago. Her berth is still empty, and the route is still there, pulsing quiet in the relay's old nav buffer, waiting for someone else to follow.
zh: 又停靠在中继站，重力低得每一步都像走在别人的梦里。在足够的信用币、外加一句"对手运货船员在航线出事时死得很难看"的提醒之后，那经纪商终于开口了。在所有伪造的清单和打乱的货箱 ID 底下，东西就在那儿——航路表里一处反复出现的漂移，像有人教会了系统按某种节奏呼吸。每逢第三批货，无论申报的目的地是哪里，都会被推偏一两度，滑进同一片空的天空。把它和新亚特兰蒂斯的队列异常、以及从那条死勘测船上扒出来的半吊子跃迁计划交叉比对，吻合得诡异。我标记了坐标，备好一艘穿梭机，告诉乔等我亲眼看到那外面漂着的东西就回她消息。她开玩笑说我多半只会找到又一艘弃船和一个烂故事。那是三个周期前了。她的泊位还是空的，而那条航线还在那儿，在中继站老旧的导航缓冲里安静地脉动着，等着下一个人跟上去。

#en: I have seen a lot of farms on the edge of nowhere, but this one hums wrong. The air smells of soil and synth-fertilizer, sure, but under the tractor chatter there is a steady, artificial rhythm in the power lines, like a heartbeat that forgot it was supposed to stop years ago. Someone bolted an extra antenna into this place and then never turned it off again. What was probably meant as a quick workaround, a temporary relay to skirt some inspection, just kept doing its job until it became part of the scenery.\n\nThe datapad I found on that rock should have been junk, yet its route times did not fit any legal lane. Then I kept hearing freighter crews complain about deliveries that arrived before they were even filed. Now I am watching a tired homestead push more power to its uplink at the exact moments those impossible shipments appear overhead. None of it screams conspiracy; it all just looks like systems that were supposed to be cleared, retired, forgotten  quietly left running until someone clever enough decided to use them.
zh: 天涯尽头的农场我见过不少，可这一座嗡鸣得很不对劲。空气里当然是泥土和合成肥料的味道，但在拖拉机的轰鸣底下，电线里有一种稳定而人造的节律，像一颗忘了自己多年前就该停下的心跳。有人往这地方硬装了一根多余的天线，然后再也没有关掉它。原本大概只是权宜之计，一座用来绕过某次检查的临时中继，结果就一直干活，直到成了风景的一部分。\n\n我在那块岩石上找到的数据板本该是垃圾，可它的航路时间不属于任何合法航道。接着我又不断听到货船船员抱怨货在他们还没提交文件之前就到了。如今我眼看着一座疲惫的农家宅院，在那些不可能的货运出现在头顶的精确时刻往上行链路推更多电。这一切都没有阴谋的味道；看起来只像一些本该被清除、退役、遗忘的系统——被安静地留着运行，直到某个足够聪明的人决定利用它们。

#en: I am writing this from a maintenance alcove that smells like coolant and old paper, which tells you everything about the kind of place this is. Out here, manifests change in the time it takes a bored clerk to look away, and no one notices if a freighter's mass reading is a little off or its route history does not match the stamp. I have been combing through half-burnt logs and ghost entries all shift and I keep seeing the same thing: jumps filed one way, radiation signatures insisting they went somewhere else first.  \n\nFunny thing is, none of this would be on my mind if I had not cut a corner two weeks back, letting a convoy through on a hunch because the queue was long and the supervisor was on my neck about throughput. Tiny decision, gone in a heartbeat. Now I see that same convoy's ID echoed in the dead survey site's data, and in a story a Neon dockhand swears he heard from "somebody who was actually there." It feels like I kicked a stone out of a wall without thinking, and only now do I hear the rocks shifting further in.
zh: 我在一间闻着冷却液和旧纸张味的维护壁龛里写下这些，光这一点就能说明这是个什么样的地方。在这外面，清单在一个百无聊赖的文员移开视线的工夫里就能变，没人会注意一艘货船的质量读数有点不对、或者它的航路历史跟戳记对不上。我整个班都在翻检半烧毁的日志和幽灵条目，反复看到同一件事：跃迁是按一种方式申报的，辐射特征却坚称它们先去别处转过一圈。\n\n好笑的是，要不是两周前我抄了个近路，这些本来都不会在我脑子里——当时队列很长，主管又为吞吐量盯着我，我就凭直觉放行了一支运输队。微不足道的决定，一眨眼就过去了。如今我看见同一支运输队的 ID 回响在那座废弃勘测站的数据里，也回响在一个霓虹城码头工赌咒说从"真在场的人"那儿听来的故事里。感觉就像我无意中从墙上踢落了一块石头，而直到现在才听见里面的石块继续往里移动。

#en:
I am recording this from the quiet end of the module, where the fans drown out most of the guilt.

The Ryujin handler handed me a packet like it was nothing, just a side-channel scrape from an old routing experiment. I burned half a shift combing the telemetry, lining it up with the ghost vectors we pulled from that forgotten relay weeks ago. The same rounding quirks, the same microsecond drift on the time stamps, repeating like a nervous tic. Follow the offsets long enough and they stop looking random; they all curl back to one place, a dead ground station parked in orbit like a bad memory.

Everyone here swears they heard about her from someone else. A cousin on a freighter that jumped late and lived, a broker who paid extra to shave risk off a convoy, a UC analyst who saw their anomaly folder emptied overnight. No one has the whole story, just fragments traded in low voices when the room feels safe. But the traces in this packet all point to the same gap in the network, the same relay where the numbers stop making sense.
zh:
我在模块安静的那一头录下这段话，那里的风扇声盖过了大半的愧疚。

龙神的接头人把一份数据包随手递给我，像那不值一提，不过是从某个旧航路实验里旁路刮来的一点东西。我花了大半个班去梳理遥测，把它和我们几周前从那座被遗忘的中继站扒来的幽灵矢量对齐。同样的舍入怪癖，同样的时间戳微秒漂移，像神经质的抽搐一样反复。顺着那些偏移追得够久，它们就不再显得随机；它们全都卷回同一个地方，一座停在轨道上的死地面站，像一段糟糕的记忆。

这里人人都赌咒说，他们是从别人那儿听说她的。一个在跳晚了却活下来的货船上的表亲、一个额外付钱给一支运输队削去风险的经纪商、一个看到自己的异常文件夹一夜清空的联殖分析师。没人掌握完整的故事，只有碎片，在房间让人觉得安全的时刻以低语交换。可这份数据包里的痕迹全都指向网络里同一道缺口，同一座数字不再讲道理的通讯中继。

#en: I do not usually give a damn what falls onto my table, so long as it weighs out and does not explode. Today felt different. Spacer came in shaking, said he pulled a datapack off a derelict that "went wrong" and wanted it gone, fast. Half the casing is slag, but the core still ticks if you sweet-talk it. I cracked it for parts, like always, and the screen flickered long enough to spit a string of drift coordinates before dying for good. The line it drew on my nav looked too clean for a random trader, too quiet.\n\nI traced the route as far as my old charts would take it. It threads right past that dead ice-world everyone pretends not to remember, skims a relay with missing logs, then sinks out toward a patch of empty system nobody ever files flight plans for. People around here say it is safer not to ask why certain lanes stay empty, that some places are unlucky, some cargo best left lost. I do not know if that is fear talking or just the comfort of not having to care, but the trail is there now, whether anyone wants to see it or not.
zh: 我平时不在乎什么落到我桌上，只要称得出重量、不会炸就行。今天不一样。一个太空人抖着进来了，说他从一艘"出了岔子"的弃船上扒下一个数据包，想赶紧把它处理掉。外壳一半已经熔成渣，可只要你哄一哄它，核心还是会滴答作响。我像往常一样把它拆了取零件，屏幕闪了那么久，吐出一串漂移坐标，然后就彻底死了。它在我的导航上画出的那条线，对随便一个商贩来说太干净了，太安静了。\n\n我顺着我的旧星图能带我去的地方追那条航线。它贴着那颗人人都假装不记得的死冰星掠过，擦过一座日志缺失的中继站，然后朝一片没人会提交飞行计划的空荡星系沉下去。这周围的人说，别问某些航道为什么一直空着会更安全，说有些地方不吉利，有些货最好就当它丢了。我不知道那是恐惧在说话，还是只是"不用去在意"的那份轻松，可那条痕迹如今就在那儿，不管有没有人愿意看见它。

#en:
I am recording this from the old relay pit, the one UC swears was taken off the grid ten years ago. The walls still hum, just enough to rattle your teeth if you lean against them. Funny thing for a dead node, right

The deserter finally cracked after the third cup of bad coffee and a reminder that the Trackers do not file every name they hear. He handed over a slice of the patrol grid logs, the part he copied before his supervisor told him to "correct the anomaly and move on." Nobody here says that word out loud, anomaly. They talk around it, like it is a curse that might ride the comms back to whoever is listening.

I reran the scans on the bunker boards. Same ship signature, same wrong vector, threading through restricted air like it owned the place. The echoes converge on a relay that should not be handling anything but dust, way out past regular traffic. No coordinates in the open records, but the old maintenance tags still point the way. Every time I mention it to anyone, they drop their voice, like the signal itself can hear.
zh:
我在旧中继坑里录下这段，就是联殖赌咒说十年前就移出网络的那座。墙壁还在嗡鸣，你靠上去刚好够震得牙齿发麻。对一座死节点来说，这挺有意思，对吧？

那名逃兵在第三杯烂咖啡之后终于松了口，再加上我提醒他追踪者联盟不会把听到的每个名字都备案。他交出了一段巡逻网格日志，就是他上司叫他"修正异常然后翻篇"之前他抄下来的那部分。这里没人把那两个字说出口——异常。他们都绕着它说话，像那是个可能顺着通讯传回到某个正在监听之人耳中的诅咒。

我在碉堡的主板上重跑了那些扫描。同样的飞船特征，同样错误的矢量，在受限空域里穿行，像那地方是它家的。那些回响汇聚到一座本该只处理灰尘的通讯中继上，远在常规交通之外。公开记录里没有坐标，可旧维护标签仍指着路。每次我向任何人提起，他们都会压低声音，仿佛那信号自己听得见。

#en: I used to think bad jumps were just part of the life, like rust on a bulkhead or dust in the air over Akila; you curse, you patch, you pour one out for whoever did not make it, then you fly the next lane they hand you. Lately the lanes feel like they are flying us. The last contract I ran was on one of those "optimized" routes everyone whispers about, the ones with just enough success stories to drown the wreck reports. Ship handled fine, drives within tolerance, but the timing in the chain itched at me, like a note played half a beat late. When we dropped, there was fresh debris spinning a few thousand klicks off vector and a buoy broadcasting the wrong correction by a hair. That is not random drift; that is a hand on the scale. Now I hear the same alias in spacer bars from Neon to the Stretch, always tied to quiet adjustments, cheap deals, and convoys that do not all come back. None of this started with me, but you can feel how every little cheat and covered-up "accident" bent the map, nudging us all toward this knot we are sitting in now.
zh: 我以前以为糟糕的跃迁不过是这行当的一部分，像舱壁上的锈，或阿基拉上空的尘；你骂一句，补一补，为没活下来的人倒一杯，然后飞他们派给你的下一条航道。可近来这些航道感觉像在飞我们。我上一份合同跑的是那种人人都低声议论的"优化"航线——它们有着刚好够多的成功案例，足以把失事报告淹没。飞船操控正常，驱动都在容差内，可那链式时序让我心里发痒，像一个音符晚了半拍才奏出。我们跃出时，矢量外几千公里处有新鲜碎片在旋转，还有一只浮标把错误的修正只偏差一丝地广播出去。那不是随机的漂移；那是一只手压在天平上。如今，从霓虹城到延伸带，我在太空人的酒吧里都听到同一个化名，总与安静的调整、便宜的买卖、以及那些并非全都回来的运输队绑在一起。这一切都不是从我开始的，可你能感觉到，每一桩小小的作弊和被掩盖的"事故"如何把地图掰弯，把我们都推向此刻所坐的这个结。

#en: Prime Deckhands is the informal name given to a loose fraternity of independent technicians, cargo hands, and systems wranglers who work the insurance and asset-protection routes around ships like GL-7623 Assetguard. They are not formally on GalBank payroll, but the bank's captains rely on them to coax aging vault-ships through decaying orbits, patch sensor arrays no one admits still exist, and negotiate with frontier crews for tug assistance without triggering legal scrutiny. \n\nLocal traders describe Prime Deckhands as quiet, methodical, and unnervingly well-briefed on which derelicts are truly dead and which are merely pretending to be. Recent unlogged course corrections and unexplained telemetry gaps in the region are often attributed to their unseen maintenance runs, or to private salvage operations carried out under the cover of "stabilization work." Rumor has it that on more than one occasion, they arrived at a drifting hull seconds after a catastrophe, as if someone had warned them which ship would start lying to its own instruments.
zh: 精英甲板工是对一群松散同人的非正式叫法——他们是独立技师、货舱工人和系统管理员，在 GL-7623 资产卫士号这类飞船周边的保险与资产保护航线上讨生活。他们并不正式在盖尔银行的编制里，可银行的船长们却仰仗他们把日渐老化的金库船哄过衰减的轨道、修补没人承认还存在的传感器阵列，并与边疆船员就拖船协助讨价还价，还不惊动法律审查。\n\n本地商人形容精英甲板工沉默、有条不紊，而且对哪艘弃船是真的死了、哪艘只是在装死，了解得令人不安。该区域近来那些未入账的航向修正和无法解释的遥测空白，常被归到他们看不见的维护航次上，或是归到打着"稳定作业"名义进行的私人打捞行动上。有传言说，不止一次，他们在灾难发生后几秒就赶到了一具漂流的船壳旁，仿佛有人提前警告过他们，哪艘船即将开始对自己的仪器说谎。

#en: I am logging this from a maintenance crawlway because it feels safer talking to the bulkhead than to anyone else on this module. The air purifiers whine on a half-cycle, lights dimmed to conserve power, but the archive banks are still warm. That is all I needed. Took me most of the night to unwind the rerouted access trails, hidden under old agronomy reports and budget audits. Every time I found another redacted freight route tagged to the same hauler, my hands shook a little more. The last string was buried deep, crosslinked with soil-sample telemetry and crop failure alerts from a nowhere patch of land. Coordinates, property tags, even the irrigation layout point to an abandoned farm that should not matter to anyone anymore. Yet every story about the man in the dust circles back to places like that, and each retelling shifts a little, like the fear is editing the facts. First it was a convoy ghost, then a saboteur, then a protector no one asked for. Now the ledger in my hands says he keeps going back to ground everyone else walked away from.
zh: 我在一条维护爬行通道里记录这些，因为跟舱壁说话比跟这个模块上任何其他人说话都更安全。空气净化器在半周期上呜咽，灯为了省电调暗了，可档案库还是温热的。我要的就这些。我花了大半夜才把那些被改道的访问痕迹解开，它们藏在旧农学报告和预算审计底下。每找到一条被打上涂黑标记、却归属同一艘货船的货运航线，我的手就更抖一点。最后那串埋得很深，与土壤采样遥测和来自一片荒地庄稼歉收警报交叉关联。坐标、产权标签、甚至灌溉布局，都指向一座早该对任何人都不再重要的废弃农场。可每一个关于那个"沙尘中的人"的故事，都绕回到这样的地方；每次转述都略有出入，仿佛恐惧正在修改事实。起初是一个运输队的鬼，然后是一个破坏者，接着是一个没人请求过的保护者。如今我手里的账簿说，他一次次回到别人都已走开的那片土地。

#en: I keep telling myself it is just space junk. Mech armor sloughed off some battle no one logged right, telemetry looping its own last moments until the batteries die. But the numbers in that wreck are too clean where they ought to be scarred, and bent exactly where they ought to be reliable, like someone meant to come back and finish rewriting the story and just never did. It feels like walking into a crime scene where the cleaner got interrupted mid-swipe.\n\nThe more I stare at it, the more it lines up with everything else I have tripped over by accident. A foreclosure on a farm that reversed itself while the owner was still packing. A dataslate half-buried in dust, full of draft entries that almost made it into the system. A jump node whose timing made my teeth itch even though the charts said it was fine. Little things, all of them, the kind you blame on tired clerks and lazy techs. But taken together, they look like someone started pulling on the threads of the Settled Systems a long time ago, and just got used to leaving the ends hanging.
zh: 我一直告诉自己这只是太空垃圾。机甲装甲从某场没人好好记录的战斗中剥落，遥测循环着它自己的最后时刻，直到电池耗尽。可那残骸里的数字，在该有伤痕的地方太干净，在该可靠的地方又恰好弯折，像有人打算回来把故事改写完，却始终没能回来。感觉就像走进一个凶手清理现场清到一半被打断的犯罪现场。\n\n我盯着它越久，它就越和我无意中绊到的其他一切对得上。一桩在主人还在收拾行李时就自我撤销的农场查封。一块半埋在灰尘里的数据板，满是几乎进了系统的草稿条目。一个跃迁节点，它的时序让我牙齿发痒，尽管星图说一切正常。都是些小事，那种你会归咎于疲惫文员和懒惰技工的小事。可合在一起看，就像有人在很久以前就开始拉扯定居星系群的线头，然后只是习惯了把线尾一直那么吊着。

#en: HM-6310 is still out there, hanging between beacons like a bad thought no one wants to finish. I caught its ID in a rundown dockside bar, buried in a spacer s story he swore was just a joke. Dead Navy hull, clean cuts in the comms, no scorch marks from a boarding, no beacon loop. Just silence, and a notation buried three menus deep that says "operational loss" in the kind of language auditors use when they do not want to know more.  \n\nWhat sticks with me is not the ship itself, it is the pattern around it. Convoys rerouted for "efficiency," escorts arriving a little late, patrols shifted one sector over for reasons that sound reasonable until you realize they always leave one lane thin. Then something disappears and everybody shrugs and blames raiders, or equipment, or bad luck. Nobody ever mentions the matching blackout windows or the way records get neater the closer you get to New Atlantis. Every time I bring it up, people laugh it off too fast, like they are afraid if they stop joking the truth will land somewhere between cowardice and calculation.
zh: HM-6310 还在外面，悬在信标之间，像一个没人愿意想完的坏念头。我是在一间破败的码头酒吧里撞见它的 ID 的，埋在一个太空人的故事里——他赌咒说那只是个玩笑。死海军船壳，通讯上有干净的切口，没有登船留下的烧痕，没有信标循环。只有沉默，以及深埋在三级菜单底下的一行备注，写着"作战损失"，用的是审计员在不想知道更多时才会用的那种措辞。\n\n让我挥之不去的不是那艘船本身，而是它周围的图案。运输队为"效率"被改道，护航船稍微来晚一点，巡逻因为一些听起来很合理的原因被挪到旁边的星区——直到你意识到他们总是把某条航道留薄。然后有东西消失了，大家都耸耸肩，怪劫掠者、怪设备、怪运气不好。没人提那些互相吻合的信号盲区窗口，也没人提越靠近新亚特兰蒂斯、记录就变得越整洁这件事。每次我提起，人们都笑得太快，像他们害怕一旦停止开玩笑，真相就会落在懦弱与算计之间的某个地方。

#en: Calen Rourke here, logging this before someone decides it is inconvenient and wipes the drive clean. The module is dead quiet, just fans and my own breathing, but the consoles tell a louder story than most captains ever will. I traced the data forks like any good thief would trace a payout, following the jumps where they should not bend, the packets that detoured through places no contract mentioned. Every time the trail went fuzzy, the same ship ID kept reappearing in scrubbed access notes and half-redacted audit flags from the Trade Authority. Someone thought routing that much traffic through a single cargo hauler was subtle, that if they buried it in routine freight no one would notice. Maybe they were right, for a while. But the broken beacon logs we pulled near the outer marker, the whispers in Neon's lower levels about ghost routes, and that LIST emergency broadcast everyone pretends not to remember, they all point back to the same thing: a cargo ship running too many "lucky" jumps and a pilot whose name keeps getting spoken in a lower voice every time.
